Witch of Vainglory |Previous Occupation = Head of the Saintess Sect |Status = Alive |Relatives = [[Echidna]] (daughter) |Authority = [[Authority#Authority of Vainglory|Authority of Vainglory]] |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 14|Volume 14]] (flashback) |Manga = [[Manga Arc 4 Chapter 57|Arc 4 Chapter 57]] (flashback) |Anime = [[Episode 43]] (flashback) |Japanese Voice = [[Wikipedia:Rie Kugimiya|Kugimiya Rie]] |English Voice = Deneen Melody}} '''Pandora''' (パンドラ) is the '''Saintess'''While Pandora has not been explicitly stated to be the Saintess within the text, at a talk show held on July 26, 2026, the author stated that the Witch Factor of Vainglory was specifically created to suit Pandora, thereby indirectly confirming that she is the Saintess. and the '''[[Witches of Sin#Witch of Vainglory, Pandora|Witch of Vainglory]]'''. A mysterious [[Witch]] regarded as taboo to both the [[Witch Cult]], which she seemingly presides over, as well as the world, she is a [[Witch#Supernumerary Witches|supernumerary Witch]] considered separate from the rest of the Witches. As the Saintess, she was the head of the [[Saintess Sect]], a mysterious group that existed during the era of Witches. She has masterminded several major events throughout history, such as the [[Permafrost of Elior Forest]] and the death of the [[Theresia van Astrea|previous Sword Saint]] during the [[Great Conquest]]. ==Appearance== Pandora has the outward appearance of a young woman with a small, delicate body. She has long, straight platinum hair, which is said to be seemingly transparent, to give off a soft glow akin to the shine of the sun, and to have a radiance that creates the effect of a glistening waterfall that travelled down her slender shoulders and rested slightly below her knee line. She has blue eyes with slit pupils that are framed by long eyelashes. She is described as having inhuman beauty that is terrifying enough to make any person who set their eyes upon her incapable of stopping themselves from trembling. Likewise, it is stated that Pandora's charming facial features are considered the ideal image of the word "beauty" accepted by human beings, that her beauty is enough to make others tremble or rouse happiness within them, and that if it were possible to kill through beauty alone, it would be her radiance that would be capable of doing so. However, it has been declared that it is possible to tell at a glance that Pandora is a dangerous being who can not be allowed to exist. Although she may appear to have a gentle smile and a gaze filled with compassion towards a stranger, suggesting she could feel love for them, that sense of love seemed so distorted and overwhelming to the point that it was terrifying. Pandora's clothing is incredibly simplistic. The only thing the Witch wears was a single sheet of white fabric that covers her torso and traipses over her. The decoration the fabric has a line of deep blue stitches at the top and a matching blue ribbon. Aside from her gown, the other sole piece of material she has is a blue ribbon tied into her hair that is similar to the one that decorated her dress. ==Personality== At first glance, Pandora is dignified and graceful, with a generally calm demeanor. This calm exterior hides an extremely selfish and sociopathic personality, willing to do anything to achieve her goals. She had no problem with manipulating [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti]] into killing his beloved [[Fortuna]] and driving him into insanity, and she even told [[Emilia]] that she would rip up [[Elior Forest]] to open the Seal if she did not comply with her demands. Despite these traits, she never showed anger toward anyone, sending [[Regulus Corneas]] away when he turned on her and speaking calmly toward Emilia despite the latter repeatedly killing her. She had an abject lack of guilt stemming from her actions, showing no form of remorse when she caused someone mental or physical pain or even when she killed innocent people and concocted catastrophes. The Witch only saw the people around her as pawns or pets, not actually viewing them as intelligent creatures worthy of being considered her equals in any way. ==History== More than 400 years ago, Pandora was known as the Saintess. Though it is unknown for what reason she bore this title, she willingly took in the Witch Factor of Vainglory, something which was tailor-made for her usage,''“To begin with, it is inconceivable that you, Petra, would be compatible with the Witch Factor of Melancholy. This Factor and one other, the Factor of Vainglory, are both unenumerated… no, supernumerary is the right word. These have each been fine-tuned to their respectively singular and uniquely compatible persons―― the Valiant and the Saintess. Tailored. They shall never be compatible with any other. Besides.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 5, Section 3. and became counted as a supernumerary Witch Factor holder alongside the Valiant, [[Hector]]. According to Clind, however, despite being compatible with their respective Factors, the Saintess and the Valiant were unable to avoid the mental corruption that came with Witch Factors.''“Even they who were compatible, were unable to escape the corruption of their minds. Disgrace.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 5, Section 3. Pandora and the Warlock of Melancholy, Hector, had a daughter together, that being Echidna.''“You could say it was a warped sense of love, I suppose. But, it wasn't like he was head over heels for Mother, in fact. After all, Hector was Mother's father, I suppose.”'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 31, Section 2.''“A Witch, I suppose. ――The Witch of Vainglory, Pandora, that is Mother’s mother, in fact.”'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 31, Section 2. Pandora and Hector were responsible for her birth, having supposedly produced her with a specific goal in mind, that goal being unknown.''“That is a complexity unique to disorganized opinions. But, there are many holes in that logic. You claim I am off the mark, but my parents produced the existence known as myself for a purpose, and I produced the existence known as yourself for a purpose… in that case, you could say that I, who perpetuated the chain, am more malicious.”'' [[No Stella No Life 4]]. By Echidna's claim, she never learned anything positive from her parents, having only learned negative emotions such as contempt and ridicule from them. However, she believed that, from their perspective, her existence was a failed imitation to them.''“I have hinted at it many times now, but my parents were good-for-nothings. I learned many negative emotions, such as contempt and ridicule, from my parents. Though from their perspective, my very existence would have been a failed imitation, a result that they had not desired.”'' [[No Stella No Life 4]]. Many years after Echidna's birth, Pandora, as the head of the Saintess Sect, was an enemy to the [[Witch Era Party]]. Although according to [[Beatrice]]'s knowledge, Pandora was supposed to have died sometime in the past,''“There’s no need to make a fuss, in fact. You don’t need to worry, Hector… Mother’s father is no longer among us, I suppose. Not just her father, but her mother too, in fact.”'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 31, Section 2. in reality, she remains alive to this day. As such, Pandora was the only Witch who roamed the world freely after the [[Great Calamity]] and the [[Satella|Witch of Envy]]'s subsequent sealing. Over the next four centuries, Pandora sowed various seeds of chaos across the world for reasons currently unknown. At some point, the Witch Cult was effectively subsumed into the Saintess Sect, and due to their preexisting name not being very well known, the Sect switched to operating under the Cult's name, leading to the modern Witch Cult. Although the exact position that Pandora has in the modern Witch Cult remains unknown, the Sin Archbishops that lead the group treated Pandora with respect, indicating she held a position outranking theirs. Furthermore, her existence was a well-kept secret among members of the Witch Cult who neglected to talk about her. ===[[Permafrost of Elior Forest]]=== Approximately 100 years ago, intending to open the Seal in the Great Elior Forest that was guarded by the forest's elves, she instructed Regulus Corneas, the Sin Archbishop of Greed, to accompany her there. Moreover, she used her [[Authority]] to direct the [[Black Serpent]] there. Pandora and Regulus arrived to find Fortuna, the Guardian of the Seal, and Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti, the leader of the moderate faction of the Witch Cult. Pandora explained to the pair her intentions of opening her Seal. After their initial hostile interactions, Petelgeuse ordered Fortuna to escape and make sure Pandora doesn't get the chance to interact with Emilia and use her for her vile plans. After the pair successfully escaped, Petelgeuse then revealed a box containing the Witch Factor of Sloth, and despite being incompatible with the Factor, took it in, gaining the Authority of Sloth. Pandora commended him for his efforts, giving him the title of the Sin Archbishop of Sloth, but the [[spirit]] rejected it, saying he accepted the power only to protect what he loved. Petelgeuse then dueled Regulus, however, Greed easily defeated Sloth, severing off his right arm and utterly destroying his legs, rendering him unable to even move. Just as Regulus was about to stomp Petelgeuse's head, ending the spirit's life forever, Fortuna came back to save him. As Regulus prepared to slaughter the pair, Pandora intervened, stating that she would not allow him to harm him as they held significant importance for her plans. Regulus, enraged, hurled dirt at her, which blew her into bits of gore, however, Pandora brought herself back to life and removed Regulus' presence from the forest which automatically reverted all the damage he had done, including disfiguring Petelgeuse. Pandora then managed to escape from Fortuna and Petelgeuse, and she made her way to the Seal where she met Emilia. Pandora revealed that she had been controlling the lesser spirits that Emilia followed and told her how no one had to be hurt and that all she had to do was open the Seal. To the Witch's disappointment, Emilia told her that she had made a promise to Fortuna not to open the Seal, to which Pandora replied she would tear the forest apart and open the Seal forcefully. Seconds before Pandora succeeded in convincing the child, a heavily injured Fortuna attacked Pandora, killing her time after time after time, but to no avail. As Fortuna yelled at her to stay away from Emilia, Petelgeuse joined the fight. The newly promoted spirit and the Guardian of the Seal then prepared to finish the Witch once and for all however, Pandora used her Authority to confuse Petelgeuse who accidentally used his Unseen Hands to rip a hole into Fortuna's chest, destroying her vital organs and sending her to death's door. With the illusion broken, Petelgeuse realized what he had done, and was subsequently driven completely mad due to the unbearable guilt. Pandora then asked Emilia to open the Seal again. Pandora then revealed she had been controlling the lesser spirits that had played with Emilia and led her to the Seal. Emilia, witnessing these events, unleashed her magic, and continuously killed Pandora in her rage, as Pandora came back repeatedly and attempted to calm her down. Emilia then lost control and froze the entire forest, thus ending Pandora's assault. ===[[Great Conquest]]=== Fourteen years before [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]]'s arrival, Pandora made an appearance during the Great Conquest, the Lugunican army's attempt to slay the [[White Whale]]. She then approached Theresia van Astrea, the former Sword Saint, who had recently lost her [[Divine Protection]]. Theresia attempted to attack Pandora, but with her Authority, she was ultimately unaffected. After Pandora's death was rewritten, Theresia lost consciousness and soon died. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Thus far, as she has yet to show how capable she is in combat, it is unclear just how powerful she is. However, she is still incredibly dangerous, capable of manipulating the likes of Regulus, Petelgeuse, and even the Black Serpent with ease, taking actions that lead to the deaths of the likes of a Sword Saint and the guardian of Elior Forest's seal, as well as easily evading death. ===[[Authority]]=== '''[[Authority#Authority of Vainglory|Authority of Vainglory]]''' (虚飾の権能, ''Kyoshoku no Ken'nō''): Pandora is the current holder of the '''Witch Factor of Vainglory''' and is able to use its Authority, granting her abilities related to the manipulation of natural phenomena. As the Saintess, Pandora is compatible with the Factor of Vainglory, allowing her to unrestrainedly exercise its abilities. Pandora - Phenomenon Manipulation.gif|Pandora removing Regulus' presence from Elior Forest. Pandora - bury into the ground.gif|Pandora burying Regulus into the ground by lightly pushing him down. *'''Phenomenon Manipulation''': Though Pandora's Authority remains largely unexplained, the apparent main application of the Authority of Vainglory is the power to manipulate phenomena at will, although there are conditions in place for the ability to come into effect. One example of Pandora manipulating phenomena was when she first buried Regulus into the ground with no effort, and then removed him from Elior Forest, which effectively made it so that he never entered the forest in the first place, reverting all the damage done by him including him badly wounding Petelgeuse. The moment Pandora used her power, Regulus was no longer in the forest, and instead, he found himself frolicking in his mansion with his wives. As Regulus had never technically attacked, the wounds on both Petelgeuse and Fortuna ceased to exist. Despite the newly forged fact that Regulus had never attacked, however, Petelgeuse, Fortuna, and Pandora all retained memory of the lost event. Likewise, it seems that she can pick and choose which events still take place, as despite removing Regulus, Petelgeuse maintained his hold on the Witch Factor of Sloth. When manipulating phenomena, Pandora would usually state what she wanted to happen similar to a narrator and whatever she said would come to pass. **'''Memory Manipulation''':[[File:Pandora - Memory Manipulation.gif|thumb|250px|Pandora rewriting Emilia's memories]] Using her Authority, Pandora could seemingly manipulate the memories of another person to a certain extent. By making contact with her victim's head, the Witch could erase memories of her choice and also implant fabricated ones. She demonstrated her power of memory manipulation when she made Emilia forget any knowledge of the Witch of Vainglory's existence. However, this aspect of the Authority wasn't all-encompassing, as Emilia in her later years would occasionally remember disjointed fragments of the memories she had lost. **'''Self-Resurrection''':[[File:Pandora - Self Resurrection.gif|thumb|250px|Pandora negating her own death.]] In the event that Pandora was somehow killed, her demise would somehow be rewritten. Ultimately, this application of Vainglory's power that the Witch could evidently use posthumously ensured that Pandora would never be permanently felled by any known physical attack. Her power to self-resurrect was best demonstrated during her attack on Elior Forest. During the assault, she resurrected without a scratch on her after the Regulus used his Authority to turn her into bloody paste. Later, she suffered numerous brutal deaths at the hands of Fortuna and young Emilia, only to instantly return each time. **'''Sense Manipulation''':[[File:Pandora-Sense Manipulation.gif|thumb|250px|Pandora tricking Fortuna into thinking she's holding Emilia while she was actually holding Pandora.]] Pandora was capable of utilizing her ability to seemingly manipulate phenomena to alter her target's senses to potentially perceive things differently to how they were. In this way, Vainglory could manipulate her targets into believing she was somebody else. Similarly, she could also alter people's senses into believing that other people were her. During her attack on Elior Forest, Pandora was able to make Fortuna mistake her as Emilia by making Fortuna perceive Pandora as the young girl. The Witch was also able to trick Petelgeuse into mistaking Fortuna as herself and Emilia as Fortuna, therefore goading him into killing the former. **'''[[Witchbeast]] Manipulation''': Pandora is able to manipulate witchbeasts and bring them to locations of their choosing. In the web novel version of Arc 4, according to one of Petelgeuse's fingers, although she cannot control the Black Serpent with her Authority, she is able to direct it to wherever she wants. ==Trivia== *Like the other Witches (with the exception of Satella), Pandora's namesake matches both an asteroid and a mythological being. [[Wikipedia:55 Pandora|55 Pandora]] is the name of a fairly large asteroid located in the solar system's asteroid belt. The asteroid is relatively bright, a factor reflected in Pandora's god-like radiance. The mythological [[Wikipedia:Pandora|Pandora]] was the first human woman and the one who opened a jar that released all of humanity's evils into the world. **Pandora in Greek means "all gifted" or "all giving." This is either a reference to how Pandora was given a blessing by each Greek God before being sent to Earth or a reference to how she gave all the evils to mankind. The former in particular would be a fairly appropriate name for a Witch associated with Vainglory. *According to one of Petelgeuse's fingers, Pandora is a part of the Witch Cult.''“Her name is Pandora. She is a part of the Witch Cult, the world’s forbidden Witch.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 14]], Chapter 3, Section 3. Both the extremist and moderate factions of the cult which existed at the time never dared to mention her, with Regulus even treating her with respect. *It is highly implied through Fortuna's wording that Pandora was responsible for the deaths of Emilia's parents.''“I’ll make it up to Brother by turning you into a pincushion!!”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 14]], Chapter 3, Section 1. *Pandora's birthday was a fan birthday decided at a talk show held on April 2, 2023. ==Navigation== {{Witch Navbox}} {{Witch Cult Navbox}} [[Category:Unknown Race]] [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Authority Users]] [[Category:Arc 4 Antagonists]] [[Category:Arc 5 Antagonists]]

[[Episode 51]] (actual) |Japanese Voice = [[Wikipedia:Aya Endō|Endō Aya]] |English Voice = Stephanie Southerland}} '''Reala Thompson''' (リアラ・トンプソン), née '''Reshia Tinzel''' (リーシア・ティンゼル), is [[Garfiel Tinzel|Garfiel]] and [[Frederica Baumann|Frederica]]'s mother. First appearing in a flashback in [[Arc 4]], she formally debuted in [[Arc 5]], where she played a pivotal role in Garfiel's character arc. She was believed to have died in a landslide after leaving the [[Sanctuary]], which greatly scarred Garfiel. However, in Arc 5, it is revealed that she survived at the cost of her memories. Afterwards, she moved to [[Priestella]], where she [[Garek Thompson|remarried]] and started a [[Rafiel Thompson|new]] [[Fred Thompson|family]]. ==Appearance== Reala has green eyes and long golden hair which she braids into a ponytail. After reuniting with her son in [[Priestella]], she wears brown and black. She has a glintstone necklace, a plain white shirt, and black shoes. ==Personality== She was considered a rather luckless person by those who knew her due to having lived a life a of much hardship, and despite that, she was known to carry strange but kindly disposition. After surviving in a rock slide, Reala has no memories about Garfiel Tinzel and her past as Reshia, but her affectionate personality did not change. ==History== Reala's family suffered from a crushing debt, which forced her parents to sell her off into an illegal slave trader at a very young age. Not long after, she was kidnapped by a group of demi-human bandits who raided her slaver trader's camp. Several years later, she was abandoned by the [[Demi-Human|demi-human]] bandits after she became pregnant with Frederica, and spent the following years of her life hopping from one slave caravan to another. At an unspecified point in time, she moved to the [[Sanctuary]], where she gave birth to Garfiel, roughly seven years after giving birth to Frederica. Then, roughly 10 years before the start of the main story, she left the Sanctuary in pursuit of Garfiel's father. Almost immediately after departing, she was involved in a rock slide accident, which led her to be found by [[Garek Thompson]] with seemingly no memories of her past. He took care of her and brought her to Priestella. A few years later, they married and had two kids, [[Fred Thompson]] and [[Rafiel Thompson]]. ==Abilities== '''Equipment''': Reala used to carry a necklace of two '''glintstones''' (輝石). However, she took the two stones off the necklace and gave one each to her two children. {{Clear}} ==Trivia== *Before the web novel of [[Arc 5]] revealed Reala's present and original names in a chapter released on November 9, 2014, in response to a comment the author received, he revealed the name of Garfiel and Frederica's mother was '''Muhria Tinzel''' (ムーリア・ティンゼル, ''Mūria Tinzeru'') several months earlier on May 26.Narō impression response on May 26, 2014, at 12:05 JST It is unknown why her name was changed. *Reala has golden hair, which was mistakenly colored as orange in [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 13|Volume 13]]. However, in [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 17|Volume 17]], it was fixed by making her hair golden as intended. *The author considers her to be the most luckless person in Re:Zero.''"In the story, the most luckless woman is Garfiel and Frederica's mother."'' Before the fall of the [[Sanctuary]], the clone was known under the name '''Shima''' (シーマ), one of the original four clones who were tasked with overseeing the Sanctuary. Setting out on a journey following her reincarnation, Omega intends to see how the world has changed in her absence until she reacquires the full extent of her original powers. Accompanied by [[Omega Party#Members|the members of her party]], she was last known to be in [[Gusteko]], having yet to visit [[Kararagi]] and [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]]. ==Appearance== After possessing the body of Ryuzu Shima, Echidna naturally took on the physical form of her host and named herself Omega. In terms of her appearance, Omega is a petite young girl around ten to twelve years of age, though in reality, she's well over four centuries old, predating even the [[Great Calamity]]. Her beautiful yet pale face is adorned with a long, refined nose and almond-shaped cyan eyes. After encountering and killing a group of bandits, she stole what clothes and shoes of theirs could fit her, opting to wear them over her original white robe. As Ryuzu Meyer was a half-elf, Omega's ears are inhumanly pointy. Her long fluffy pink hair flows down her back and is slightly curved outwards. Befitting a girl of her physical age, Omega is rather short, failing to reach even halfway up Subaru's chest. Omega can choose to project her soul as Echidna, temporarily giving her [[Echidna#Appearance|the Witch of Greed's physical appearance]]. However, she shies away from using it for too long to prevent herself from being found by an unknown enemy of herself and the other Witches.''“…There’s someone you don’t want to be found by, right?”'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting]], Section 2.''Typhon anticipated what Echidna was going to say, and spoke them for her innocently. The latter did not bother to deny the point the young Witch had made. She was speaking the truth. All of the Witches here in the Castle of Dreams knew that. It was not just Echidna, after all. This someone was an enemy all of the Witches had in common.'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting]], Section 2. Currently, her appearance has gradually begun shifting over time to match that of her original self, with her pink hair having turned grey while in the process of becoming white. ==Personality== Ryuzu Shima was against freeing the Sanctuary due to seeing the original Ryuzu's memories 10 years in the trial and had partly been manipulating [[Garfiel Tinzel|Garfiel]] behind the scenes to make sure it didn't happen. She entered the grave in an attempt to rescue Garfiel but was forced to take the trial. In the end this meant she broke her contract with Echidna. As punishment Shima was duly stripped of her position as an overseer and was made to live with other mindless clones in the forest, donning the white robe as a result. After being possessed by Echidna's soul, Omega is essentially Echidna from the [[Castle of Dreams]], but in a different body. She retained all of her memories and thoughts, but she was forced to forsake most of her magical power in order to retain her full self. Having been born anew, Omega mostly spends her time observing and adventuring, trying to learn as much as possible about the world she is so unfamiliar with, and she has also retained the clumsiness that Echidna was known for, which has led her accidentally set fire to an entire forest, nearly drown in a river, and almost pass out in the cold snowfields of Gusteko. It should be kept in mind, however, that Omega is in fact the Witch of Greed from the Castle of Dreams, rather than the Witch of Greed who roamed the world before the fall of the [[Witch]]es. After starting her journey, she has shown a rather friendly, if somewhat shrewd side of herself, both getting back at people who have wronged someone she has taken a liking to by giving them nightmares or taking others along with her on her journey after either helping them or being saved by them, stating that it was primarily to ward away a common enemy of the Witches. That said, when she was told to be mindful of causing too many deaths for the sake of the people she travels with, she decided to take that advice to heart, which has led to her preventing the deaths of the people around her and even threaten others to prevent such deaths with their own. ==History== Roughly 10 years before the events of [[Arc 4]], Garfiel ran into the Tomb and challenged the Trials. Out of concern for him, one of the Ryuzu copies–Shima–followed suit and accidentally underwent the first Trial. Seeing this as a good opportunity to yet again kick off her experiments with Soul Transcription, Echidna used that occasion to latch a tiny bit of her soul onto her. For the following ten years, she slowly filled the host with her soul, bit by bit. A decade after kickstarting her new plan, Echidna was finally given an opportunity to escape–and so she did. Toward the end of the [[Sanctuary Incident]], Echidna somehow managed to pour in the last bits of her soul and escape the Sanctuary after four long centuries. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party]]=== After the fall of the Sanctuary, Echidna managed to completely transfer her soul into Shima and renamed herself Omega, which means "the end", based on Subaru's memories of his original world. She then decided to take it slow and first get accustomed to the new body. Following her reincarnation, Omega left the Sanctuary, taking with her a glintstone anchor that housed the souls of [[Typhon]], [[Daphne]], [[Carmilla]], [[Minerva]], and [[Sekhmet]]. She unintentionally burned down a forest when using a fire magic spell to heat herself up. Later, she encountered a group of thieves, killed them with her miasma by projecting her true appearance, and stole their clothes for herself. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Requirements to be a Witch|The Requirements to be a Witch]]=== Sometime later, Omega accidentally fell into a river and was saved by [[Colette]], a young girl who lived by herself just outside of a local village in the forest. The two of them spent several days together, getting to know one another and exchanging stories from their pasts. When Omega decided to take a walk on another day, Colette informed her to not travel to the eastern side of the forest to avoid a [[witchbeast]] that had been attacking people there. Omega went anyways and met [[Palmyra]], who also warned her of a "Beast". That night, she travelled to the eastern side of the forest and attempted to murder the beast herself until Palmyra came and revealed that it was Colette. Learning of the young girl's ostracization as a Witch for being the only survivor caused by a "Beast", Omega came to the conclusion that Colette had accepted the discrimination she faced and decided to try and "become" a Witch by killing the girl she had only recently met. Omega took off a bracelet that Colette had owned since she was very young, the [[Meteor#Beast Protection Bracelet|Beast Protection Bracelet]], the [[meteor]] that was behind her transformation into a beast. Manifesting her true form to Palmyra and an unconscious Colette, Omega set off for the village in hopes of setting things straight with the villagers. However, this only made things worse for Colette, as she was forced to leave the area as a consequence for being acquainted with a "Witch". Seeing as how Colette had nowhere else to go and Palmyra had used up all of her courtesy for the village, the two of them were invited by Omega to join her, officially forming their party. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting|The Witches' Evaluation Meeting]]=== Once the Omega Party was formed, in the Castle of Dreams, the six Witches had a meeting together where they discussed Echidna's reasoning for allowing Colette and Palmyra to travel with her. To avoid being found by an unnamed enemy of the Witches, Echidna chose to blend in with other humans and avoid being discovered by them. As a result of this reasoning, Minerva set a two-year deadline for Echidna to regain her full powers. It was decided by Echidna that they should leave [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Lugunica]]. Believing Gusteko was out of the question, between Vollachia and Kararagi, she set her sights on the latter. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 1|One Wild Night]]=== Ironically, the trio then proceeded to cross over into Gusteko. One day, they were caught in a severe blizzard and rescued by [[Noelle Tuérico]], an Itinerant Preacher of the [[Gustekan Church]], after Omega launched a fire spell into the distance. They wait for Omega to regain her energy in a makeshift snow house Noelle created and speak with her in the meantime, learning about the term Silver Blessing, her position in the Gustekan Church and the nearby church building they can use as a refuge. They visit the church once Omega is rejuvenated and acquaint themselves with [[Podoso]], [[Admonsah]], and [[Maqueena]], each of whom had come to the church to meet the pastor who lives there, [[Coatl]]. The trio learned of Coatl's history of having saved a local town from the effects of an avalanche unintentionally caused by the Ice Thieves and how he took up a position of the town's watcher following his charity towards its people, becoming known by the moniker Saint of the Avalanche. Maqueena and Podoso split off from everyone else to visit another part of the church, and another visitor named [[Trellock]] arrives while they are out. Eventually, Maqueena discovers something and screams, prompting everyone else to follow after her to find what has caused her fear. They all stumble upon Coatl's corpse, prompting Omega to say that there was a cold-blooded killer among them. Omega took charge of the situation, using detective work to determine the killer's identity. She heard from Podoso that there had been a string of serial murders, with Coatl being the eighth known victim. The other victims were peddlers and travelers. Querying him about the seventh victim, Omega then sets her sights on Admonsah, whom she was certain was associated with them. They learn Admonsah was a former slave who unexpectedly killed his owner in self-defense. He was unequivocally forgiven by a majority of the group. Omega tries to ascertain why Coatl would be murdered, searching for any hidden savings. Suddenly, everyone but Maqueena in the room fell asleep to the effects of the Muskrim flower, and she made her getaway with Coatl's collection of magic stones, not wanting to stay and fall victim to his murderer. She was stopped outside by Noelle, who says she could not be affected by such a simple drug and had killed Coatl out of revenge for his former membership of the Ice Thieves and his part in causing the avalanche that devastated Leanotte, her town. Omega arrives to stop Noelle before she could kill Maqueena, outlining that she was only a con artist who perceived Coatl's connection to the Ice Thieves rather than an outright member before giving the ultimatum that she would die if she caused another death, yet again manifesting her true form while saying so. Meanwhile, the culprit responsible for the serial murderers, Trellock, attempted to murder Colette, but her Beast Protection Bracelet activated, severely injuring him. In the end, they pretended that Noelle had apprehended Trellock and left, Podoso decided to take in Admonsah, and Maqueena was forced to stop conning people. With her revenge foiled, Noelle was left aimless. Colette proposed for her to join their group to which she accepted upon Omega's approval. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Extra|One Wild Night Extra]]=== Later, the party decided to head to the town Podoso had told them about. Eventually, they set up camp, and while Colette and Noelle set up the camp, Palmyra decided to talk with Omega about including Noelle in their travels, worried about getting her involved in their troubles, which included Omega being a half-elf Witch and Colette's bracelet. Omega believed that there was nothing to worry about, and shortly after, Noelle, who had heard part of their conversation appeared and said that she already knew about Omega's secret and chose to follow them regardless. Though Palmyra asked if she had a thing for odd people and Noelle's joking reply that she did, just like Palmyra, she claimed to be just as odd, as she was an itinerant preacher from the Gustekan Church who had decided to leave. Though Palmyra thought it wasn't as bad as Omega's secret, Omega told her that she was underestimating the Church and what they bestowed Noelle, and the two claimed that they would not be amicable toward her effectively breaking a contract, something which might end up leading to them falling into her mess. Though Palmyra told Omega to be prepared to fight, when Noelle told her to feel free to kick her from the party if she ever became a burden, to which she replied by saying not to underestimate her and spoke of her own circumstances, basically unintentionally cornering Noelle into staying in the party after saying not to use Colette as an excuse. Colette arrived shortly after, and the group decided not to talk to her about their conversation. Instead, they ate, and Noelle explained repairs that she had made to their equipment and offered her knowledge of how to use their equipment and how to survive in Gusteko, including knowledge on the Gustekan Church, to which Palmyra and Omega realized that they wouldn't be able to survive in Gusteko without Noelle. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland Part 1|Omega in Wonderland]]=== The party continued to trudge to the snows of Gusteko, with Palmyra and Omega becoming exhausted. Attempting to give Palmyra some more energy, Colette attempted to let her use her bracelet, but when Palmyra tried, it left her weak and vomiting. Omega explained the reason for this, claiming she allowed it to happen because she wanted to see the look on her face. Afterward, she had Noelle carry Palmyra while Colette carried her. As the got closer to the town of Sylphoa, Omega dispelled a barrier, and eventually they reached the town, where she and Colette fell subject to the Dream Arts spell that had been cast over the town. Impressed with the size of the space and likening it to her Castle of Dreams, even claiming it as superior to herself, Omega cast Al Shario in order to lure out the caster. The caster, [[Lilac]], appeared shortly after, erasing the star Omega summoned and questioning who they were. After a small dispute, she left convincing her to take down the spell to Colette. Despite her standoffish attitude, Omega claimed that Colette's words were getting through to her. However, upon hearing Omega's use of a loan word, Lilac wanted to know where she heard it, leading to negotiations. Despite becoming frustrated with her and even slapping her, she decided to give Omega a chance to take care of the [[Mikli Yulitô|Temple Knight]] who had come after her, breaking the seal that she'd placed. The fight that followed was short lived as the Witches of Sin quickly dispatched her, much to Lilac's shock. Shortly after, Palmyra entered the dream space with a message from Lilac's partner, [[Shion]]. Following this, after Omega spoke to the [[Zank Metley|other Temple Knight]] who had come to retrieve Mikli and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party. Afterward, Omega realized that they must have skimmed across [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]]'s memories at some point, and she claimed that combing through those memories would be dangerous for them, assuming they could see them after bypassing all six Witches' resistance. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Witch Trials Part 1|Witch Trials]]=== One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a [[Witchbeast#Snow Blight|Snow Blight]]. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of [[Nananna Pezza]] and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches. Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named [[Minor Characters#Piditz|Piditz]] who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find [[Mireille Hetia]] using her [[Magic#Spiritual Arts|spiritual arts]] to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody. Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to [[Edmon Quayle]]. As part of Omega's plan, Noelle persuades Nananna to speak up, and Nananna insists on the town holding a Witch Trial for Omega, and Palmyra declares that if she is a Witch that she would burn with her. While remaining in the prison, she continues to talk to the guards and annoy them, gathering information all the while. The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise. Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an [[Minor Characters#Elderly Healer|elderly healer]], and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch. Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil [[spirit]] accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Since Shima's body was not the most suitable host for Echidna to possess, she was forced to leave out her experience with magic. Despite this, she is still incredibly knowledgeable, and she can still use magic to easily defeat and kill most of her enemies. Furthermore, she could kill most beings with her miasma alone if she so chose, making her dangerous just by being close to her. According to her estimates, it will take her roughly two years to regain all her skills and powers. Furthermore, as she has not exhibited it as of yet, it is unknown if she retains her Authority of Greed. As it is unknown how much time has passed by the time of the Witch Trials side story, it is unclear how much of her power that Omega has recovered. ===[[Magic]]=== Although she is currently limited from using her full capacity of spells, Omega is still familiar with the usage of magic and is capable of using fairly powerful spells without needing incantations and effectively using all affinities to her advantage against an opponent, even retaining her ability to dispel "blessings" placed by a Temple Knight. Although she hasn't shown it off, she is capable of using all six attributes of magic, and at least within a dream realm, she has shown the capacity to use a forbidden art. Presently, she is unable to properly cast the more advanced spells in her arsenal. '''Spells''': *'''Goa''' (ゴーア): Omega is able to manifest a blaze of fire to incinerate foes. *'''Dona''' (ドーナ): Omega can summon one wall of earth, which she uses as a defensive spell. *'''Minya''' (ミーニャ, ''Mīnya''): A basic yin magic spell in which the user creates purple stakes of crystallized mana with light purple flames. The spell can ignore defenses, and when it hits, it can stop time on a part target, crystallize them, and cause them to shatter. Any stakes in the air explode and release smaller stakes that fly in all directions which then rips targets apart. *'''Dream Arts''': Omega is capable of utilizing a lost type of forbidden arts known as dream arts. Though her level of skill with it is not on the same level as someone such as Shion, she still had enough proficiency with it to create the Castle of Dreams. *'''Al Shario''' (アル・シャリオ): Omega was capable of casting a forbidden spell that literally brought stardust down to earth, massacring her opponents. As of right now, she has shown to be able to use this spell within a dream realm, but as it is unknown how much of her full strength has recovered by the time she exhibited this spell, it is unknown if she can presently use it in the real world. ===Intelligence=== '''Vast Intellect''': Omega has retained the knowledge that she had acquired in her life as Echidna. She possessed one of the greatest intellects in the world, and had conducted numerous experiments with magic, creating powerful meteors. Numerous people from every nation used to come to her, seeking her knowledge when she was alive. She possessed vast knowledge about the older era, to the point she could boast there is nothing she didn't know. ===Other=== '''Miasma''': Omega can project the soul of the Witch of Greed, making it appear as if she was physically standing by Omega's side. By doing so, Echidna starts emitting an intense aura of wickedness and madness which is enough to drive people mad and kill them in thirty seconds. It's mentioned by Echidna that a Sage could endure her aura. '''Miasma-Attuned Olfaction''': Shima can smell the Witch's miasma, something that only a few individuals in the series so far are capable of doing. This is likely due to her connection with Echidna before she completely took over Shima's body. ===Equipment=== *'''Glintstone''' (輝石 ''Kiseki''): Omega uses a necklace to carry a glintstone with her. This glintstone is an [[Terminology#Magic Related|anchor]] that contains the five souls of the other witches, Minerva, Carmilla, Typhon, Sekhmet, and Daphne in it. She can freely converse with them, but she is unable to bring them out of the stone and have them materialized in the world. ==Trivia== *Unlike her original name and the names of the rest of the Witches, Omega does not have any connotation to any specific celestial body. **However, "Omega" is commonly used in astronomy and astrology. *Contrary to popular belief, '''Omega cannot use the other Witches' [[Authority|Authorities]]'''. *While it is known that previous wielders of an Authority can retain their Authorities even as souls and even after having lost their Witch Factors, Omega has yet to display the Authority of Greed she wielded as Echidna. It is unknown if, by having a new vessel that is attempting to match the shape of her soul, it means she cannot use her Authority, she has no access to it for some unknown reason, she is choosing not to use it, or other such reasons. *While Garfiel claimed that he could smell the Witch's miasma, it was actually Shima who could smell the miasma off Subaru. *Despite her scene from the end of [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 15|Volume 15]] being omitted in [[Episode 50]], Omega made her debut in [[Episode 49]]. **As Emilia entered Echidna's laboratory and started enquiring about the circumstances and speculating about the identity of Ryuzu encased in the massive glintstone in the middle of the room, the attention is briefly given to Ryuzu Shima, who, with Echidna's distinct voice, states the following: "Unbelievable. To see this, and that's the first thing you can think of?". It's presumed this scene serves as a substitution of the final Volume 15 chapter titled ''Extra: ...The Second Coming'' which was, as mentioned before, omitted from the final episode. *In the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)|web novel]], Echidna named herself Omega because Subaru named her that, implying that Echidna's new vessel is the original Omega copy may have merged with the original Ryuzu sealed within the glintstone, similar to how Shima sacrificed herself by vanishing with the stone and ended up becoming her new vessel in [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 15|Volume 15]]. **Since the Omega copy was removed in the Light Novel, Echidna chose the name Omega on her own at the end of Volume 15. *In [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 10]], Omega was mistakenly drawn with white hair while being described as having the pink hair of Ryuzu Shima's form. This was retroactively explained in [[The Witch's After Tea Party / Witch Trials Part 1|The Witch's After Tea Party / Witch Trials]] as being the result of her body changing to suit her soul, thus gradually transforming her appearance to match that of the Witch of Greed's. *According to the author, Omega only uses "boku" to refer to herself in front of Subaru,''"She uses ‘boku’ only with Subaru."'' AskFM Q&A. which he explains as being akin to trying to get the attention of someone she likes.''"It’s sort of like she’s trying to get the attention of someone she likes."'' AskFM Q&A. The reason she uses "boku" in front of him supposedly has to do with her birth, which will be discussed in the "Witch chapter".''"The answer to that would lead back to Echidna’s birth, so we’ll leave that for the witch chapter."''
