title: Orphe
wikitext:
{{Parent Tab |tab1 = Information |tab2 = Image Gallery}} {{Character |Name = Orphe |Image = Orphe LN design.png |Kanji = オルフェ |Romaji = Orufe |Alias = Six Tongues (六枚舌, ''Roku-mai Jita'') |Race = Human |Gender = Male |Hair Color = Unknown |Eye Color = Unknown |Affiliation = [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]
[[Royal Capital]]
[[Six Tongues]] |Previous Occupation = Con Artist
Director of the Six Tongues |Status = Unknown |Relatives = |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 3|Ex Volume 3]]}} '''Orphe''' (オルフェ) was the former Director of the [[Six Tongues]]. Once a con artist, Orphe met [[Wilhelm van Astrea|Wilhelm Trias]] in the Prison Tower when the latter was arrested. Later, when Wilhelm came to visit him, Orphe gave the Sword Demon advice on how to deal with [[Theresia van Astrea|Theresia]]'s situation after receiving a guarantee that a good word would be put in for him. Upon Orphe's release, at Wilhelm's recommendation, [[Bordeaux Zergev]] began making use of his skills, resulting in the foundation of the Six Tongues. ==Appearance== Orphe is a handsome man with long hair, a neat and tidy appearance, and a pale complexion that suggests a touch of high society. He is described as having a sweet face and voice that could charm anyone regardless of gender. ==Personality== A sharp smooth-talker not above acting on his desires, Orphe gained a reputation as a philanderer as a result of swindling six noble women at once. Despite his habits, he is an intelligent man who is skilled with gathering information in a short period of time. He was trusted and capable enough to be appointed as the leader of the Six Tongues. He spoke highly of his smooth-talking, saying it was the only skill he had in his life, and could use it to navigate the Kingdom and get people to reveal to him things that officials would not be told.''“The only skill I've had in my life is smooth talk. With this tongue, I can navigate through every corner of the Royal Capital… of the Kingdom, rather. Just let me get on their good side and they'll start spilling stuff they wouldn't even tell an official.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 2, Section 2. ==History== In the past, Orphe was seeing six different women in the Noble District of the [[Royal Capital]] and gave each of them different stories, which resulted in him being called Six Tongues because it was as if he used a different tongue with each of them, and eventually being incarcerated and sent to the Prison Tower. When Wilhelm Trias was imprisoned for invading the ceremony commemorating Theresia van Astrea's achievements in the [[Demi-Human War]] at the Royal Castle, Orphe was in the cell directly across from him, and the two briefly spoke before the Sword Demon was released. Sometime later, after speaking with [[Miklotov McMahon]] about Theresia's circumstances as the Sword Saint, Wilhelm returned to meet Orphe, receiving advice on what to do in regard to her situation and promising to put in a good word for him and release him sooner upon his readmittance into the army. After Orphe's release from the Prison Tower, Bordeaux had the conman come under his service at Wilhelm's recommendation. In no time, Orphe proved himself a worthy intelligence gatherer, leading to the foundation of the secret intelligence organization bearing his alias, the Six Tongues, becoming its leader.''“It always helps to have a man with smarts like his at hand. Maybe it wouldn’t hurt to create an organization for him and those alike someday. In that case, I suppose it’d be fitting to name it Six Tongues, after him.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 3]], [[Sword Demon Love Story: Wedding Day Part 1|Sword Demon Love Story: Wedding Day]], Section 3.''Giving him a sidelong glance, Wilhelm remembered the forenamed Six Tongues―― to think that Orphe's organization was now functioning as a part of the Kingdom's intelligence services.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 3, Section 3. With his new position under Bordeaux's supervision, using his tongue as his primary resource, he had been permitted to do a wide range of things throughout the Royal Capital and the Kingdom as a whole, procuring information that officials such as knights would have been unable to. When meeting with Bordeaux and Wilhelm to discuss the Stride Faction after they had begun attacking Lugunica, he requested permission to contact remnants of the Demi-Human Alliance and interrogate them if necessary. Later, he obtained the information that they had been spotted at Abiate, and discovered that those responsible for sheltering them while they were staying hidden from view were thugs, broke mercenaries, or those who bore hostilities towards the Kingdom, the demi-humans from across the country with lingering negative sentiments against it after the Demi-Human War. He relayed [[Cragrell Dawson]]'s request to speak with the Sword Saint to Wilhelm and, with the Six Tongues presided over by him, he continued to keep an eye on the remnants of the Demi-Human Alliance.''Coincidentally, while Theresia collaborated to obtain answers from Cragrell Dawson, the Six Tongues, led by Orphe, had been on the lookout for any remnants of the Demi-Human Alliance lurking throughout the country.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 3, Section 6. In preparation for [[Raizo]]'s attack on [[Gionis Lugunica]]'s life, [[Roswaal J. Mathers]] suggested using [[Clind]] to counter the [[shinobi]], to which Miklotov approved and Orphe arranged the preparations for to ensure his defeat as smoothly as possible. Although Orphe's status is unknown in the present, [[Russell Fellow]] has succeeded his leadership position to become the current Director of the Six Tongues. ==Trivia== *The name of Orphe's epithet, and by extension, the name of the Six Tongues organization, is likely derived from the Japanese phrase ''ni-mai jita'' (二枚舌), an idiomatic expression meaning to lie and contradict oneself, such as in telling someone one version of a story and another a different story. ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Lugunica Navbox}} [[Category:Royal Capital]] [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Six Tongues]] [[Category:Unknown Status]]

[[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33|Volume 33]] (main story) (mentioned)}} '''Raizo''' (ライゾー) was a [[shinobi]] and one of the two “Generals” under the command of [[Stride Vollachia]], a role shared with his younger twin brother [[Shasuke]]. He served as a secondary antagonist of [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6|Sword Demon Battle Ballad]]. Raizo was ultimately killed at the hands of [[Clind]] following a failed attempt to assassinate [[Gionis Lugunica]]. ==Appearance== Raizo was a man with white hair parted to the right, blue eyes, and a single left eyebrow. He was described to always wear a black cloak which covered his entire body. He also wore a mask on his face, and a hachigane on his forehead. ==Personality== Raizo had quite a humble personality, serving his master without complaint. It's presumed he did not feel many emotions, as the training process specifically stripped them from him.  ==History== Shasuke and Raizo were born in [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]]'s shinobi village. The two of them were twins who were subject to the training process of a shinobi. The process was cruel, and involved body modifications using drugs, curse marks, all kinds of magic, and heavy training. It was mentioned that only one in a million could survive this process. Both he and Shasuke survived and reborn as shinobi. However, despite their promise, the two of them were deemed as imperfect by the shinobi for being twins. As a result, they killed the grown-ups who had deprived them of everything, the comrades who followed them, and became runaway shinobi. Before they fully escaped, they had a run-in with the most formidable and deadly shinobi of all, [[Olbart Dunkelkenn]], who decided to let them live on a whim. Eventually, the twin shinobi encountered and devoted their services to Stride, accepting his offer to use and dispose of them in the most extravagant way possible. ==Abilities== '''Shinobi Techniques''' (シノビの術技, ''Shinobi no Jutsugi''): Raizo was apt in the use of kunai, and in fighting using martial arts. In addition to that, it can be expected he had multiple skills that were unnamed; some examples include one which allowed Raizo to escape the Astrea Mansion with Stride despite being heavily injured. *'''Shadow Form''': Raizo could sink into a person's shadows, and become part of it. He could use this ability to carry people into them and transport them to his brother, or to hide. Furthermore he could use this ability to appear in another person's shadow. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Stride Faction]] [[Category:Deceased]] [[Category:Shinobi]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

title: Palmyra
wikitext:
{{Parent Tab |tab1 = Information |tab2 = Image Gallery}} {{Character |Name = Palmyra |Image = Palmyra LN design.png |Kanji = パルミラ |Romaji = Parumira |Race = Human |Gender = Female |Age = |Hair Color = Black |Eye Color = Brown |Affiliation = [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]
[[Omega Party]] |Status = Alive |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 6|Tanpenshuu Volume 6]]}} '''Palmyra''' (パルミラ) is [[Colette]]'s friend. She, alongside Colette, later joined [[Omega]] and formed the [[Omega Party]]. ==Appearance== Palmyra is a teenage girl with long black hair and piercing brown [[Wikipedia:Sanpaku|sanpaku]] eyes. She wears a dark grey coat along with a short black skirt and long dark boots. She and Colette have matching hairpins. ==Personality== A headstrong, sensible girl with a caring nature, Palmyra is loyal to and protective of her younger friend Colette. She is prone to openly, bluntly voicing her frustrations, often briefly bickering or bantering with Omega as a result of her choice of words or actions. While having an aggressive exterior and being wary of strangers, she has a kind heart and behaves mindfully. Despite her usual attitude, Palmyra tends to think ahead, worrying about the future of the party and planning for eventual problems to crop up. She will keep an eye on others who have joined the group and try to talk in secret from them in preparation for how to deal with them. That said, she is still quick to accept newcomers after a brief conversation, and she will feel somewhat guilty for suspecting them. She is also quick to act in events when her friends are in danger, though she will openly express her annoyance when her friends also interfere with her attempts to help. This is usually the case with Omega, leaving Palmyra regularly frustrated. Most prominently, however, she is also willing to keep secrets from Colette in order to keep her innocence intact and not worry her, often colluding with other members of her party to do so. ==History== ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Requirements to be a Witch|The Requirements to be a Witch]]=== Palmyra is Colette's friend who stuck by her side when she was outcast from their village, despite being aware of her past and her identity as a "Beast". When away from her home village, in which she lived within its largest house, she maintained a graveyard for the animals that were mauled by Colette's transformed form. When Palmyra first met Omega, she warned the half-elf girl to leave the forest they were in, or else the "Beast" would eventually tear her apart. Omega did not heed her warning and challenged the "Beast" herself, almost managing to successfully slay it until Palmyra stopped her and revealed that it was Colette, who she wanted to help. She proceeded to explain Colette's history of being ostracized as a Witch due to her connection with a "Witchbeast" which slaughtered everyone that took her in. Omega reveals that Colette had transformed into a beastly form due to the [[Meteor#Beast Protection Bracelet|Beast Protection Bracelet]], a [[meteor]] her parents unknowingly gifted to her when she was young with the effect of enhancing its user's mana and transforming its user in exchange for their sense of reason. Soon after, the Witch unveiled her true appearance to Palmyra and an unconscious Colette, sensing promise in the former for being able to withstand her presence. She then made her way to Colette's village in an attempt to straighten the situation out with them. However, this only made things worse for Colette, as she was forced to leave the area as a consequence for being acquainted with a "Witch". Seeing as how Colette had nowhere else to go and Palmyra had used up all of her courtesy for the village, the two of them were invited by Omega to join her, officially forming their party. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 1|One Wild Night]]=== The trio then proceeded to cross over into [[Gusteko]]. One day, they were caught in a severe blizzard and rescued by [[Noelle Tuérico]], an Itinerant Preacher of the [[Gustekan Church]], after Omega launched a fire spell into the distance. They waited for Omega to regain her energy in a makeshift snow house Noelle created and spoke with her in the meantime, learning about the term Silver Blessing, her position in the Gustekan Church, and the nearby church building they can use as a refuge. They visit the church once Omega is rejuvenated and acquaint themselves with [[Podoso]], [[Admonsah]], and [[Maqueena]], each of whom had come to the church to meet the pastor who lives there, [[Coatl]]. The trio learned of Coatl's history of having saved a local town from the effects of an avalanche unintentionally caused by the Ice Thieves and how he took up a position of the town's watcher following his charity towards its people, becoming known by the moniker Saint of the Avalanche. Maqueena and Podoso split off from everyone else to visit another part of the church, and another visitor named [[Trellock]] arrives while they are out. Eventually, Maqueena discovers something and screams, prompting everyone else to follow after her to find what has caused her fear. They all stumble upon Coatl's corpse, prompting Omega to say that there was a cold-blooded killer among them. Omega took charge of the situation, using detective work to determine the killer's identity. She heard from Podoso that there had been a string of serial murders, with Coatl being the eighth known victim. The other victims were peddlers and travelers. Querying him about the seventh victim, Omega then sets her sights on Admonsah, whom she was certain was associated with them. They learn Admonsah was a former slave who unexpectedly killed his owner in self-defense. He was unequivocally forgiven by a majority of the group. Omega tries to ascertain why Coatl would be murdered, searching for any hidden savings. Suddenly, everyone but Maqueena in the room fell asleep to the effects of the Muskrim flower, and she made her getaway with Coatl's collection of magic stones, not wanting to stay and fall victim to his murderer, and Noelle followed after her. While Omega, who had woken up, took care of them, the culprit responsible for the serial murderers, Trellock, attempted to murder Colette, who Palmyra had wrapped her arms around before falling unconscious in an attempt to protect her, but her Beast Protection Bracelet activated, severely injuring him. In the end, they pretended that Noelle had apprehended Trellock and left, Podoso decided to take in Admonsah, and Maqueena was forced to stop conning people. With her revenge foiled, Noelle was left aimless. Colette proposed for her to join their group to which she accepted upon Omega's approval. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Extra|One Wild Night Extra]]=== Later, the party decided to head to the town Podoso had told them about. Eventually, they set up camp, and while Colette and Noelle set up the camp, Palmyra decided to talk with Omega about including Noelle in their travels, worried about getting her involved in their troubles, which included Omega being a half-elf Witch and Colette's bracelet. Omega believed that there was nothing to worry about, and shortly after, Noelle, who had heard part of their conversation appeared and said that she already knew about Omega's secret and chose to follow them regardless. Though Palmyra asked if she had a thing for odd people and Noelle's joking reply that she did, just like Palmyra, she claimed to be just as odd, as she was an itinerant preacher from the Gustekan Church who had decided to leave. Though Palmyra thought it wasn't as bad as Omega's secret, Omega told her that she was underestimating the Church and what they bestowed Noelle, and the two claimed that they would not be amicable toward her effectively breaking a contract, something which might end up leading to them falling into her mess. Though Palmyra told Omega to be prepared to fight, when Noelle told her to feel free to kick her from the party if she ever became a burden, to which she replied by saying not to underestimate her and spoke of her own circumstances, basically unintentionally cornering Noelle into staying in the party after saying not to use Colette as an excuse. Colette arrived shortly after, and the group decided not to talk to her about their conversation. Instead, they ate, and Noelle explained repairs that she had made to their equipment and offered her knowledge of how to use their equipment and how to survive in Gusteko, including knowledge on the Gustekan Church, to which Palmyra and Omega realized that they wouldn't be able to survive in Gusteko without Noelle. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland Part 1|Omega in Wonderland]]=== The party continued to trudge to the snows of Gusteko, with Palmyra and Omega becoming exhausted. Attempting to give Palmyra some more energy, Colette attempted to let her use her bracelet, but when Palmyra tried, it left her weak and vomiting. Omega explained the reason for this, claiming she allowed it to happen because she wanted to see the look on her face. Afterward, she had Noelle carry Palmyra while Colette carried her. As they got closer to the town of Sylphoa, Omega dispelled a barrier, and eventually they reached the town, where she and Colette fell subject to the Dream Arts spell that had been cast over the town. Meanwhile, Noelle and Palmyra, who were unaffected thanks to Noelle's seal, met with a Temple Knight named [[Zank Metley]], who was there to hunt a heretic. Noelle and Palmyra, carrying the others' unconscious bodies, followed him into an empty tent, where he explained the situation. However, after entering into conflict with Palmyra, who does not follow the Church's teaching, Colette's bracelet senses danger and transformed her body into a beast. After Zank deemed her a heretic, Colette ran away with Omega and Palmyra. Elsewhere in town, she came across the person responsible for the town's predicament, [[Shion]] who, after she introduced herself and explained the situation to her, asked for Palmyra's assistance. Soon after, she used her hypnosis magic to put Palmyra to sleep, giving her a message to pass on to [[Lilac]]. After passing it along to her, she woke up and told Zank, who was in a fight with Noelle, that [[Mikli Yulitô]], the other Temple Knight, was alive. Following this, after Omega spoke to Zank, who had in reality come to retrieve Mikli, and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Witch Trials Part 1|Witch Trials]]=== One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a [[Witchbeast#Snow Blight|Snow Blight]]. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of [[Nananna Pezza]] and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches. Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named [[Minor Characters#Piditz|Piditz]] who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find [[Mireille Hetia]] using her [[Magic#Spiritual Arts|spiritual arts]] to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody. Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to [[Edmon Quayle]]. As part of Omega's plan, Noelle persuades Nananna to speak up, and Nananna insists on the town holding a Witch Trial for Omega, and Palmyra declares that if she is a Witch that she would burn with her. At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started. Likewise, Omega explained this to Palmyra, as she learned it while imprisoned. The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise. Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an [[Minor Characters#Elderly Healer|elderly healer]], and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch. Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil [[spirit]] accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it. ==Abilities== '''Miasma Resistance''': Palmyra seems to have a higher resistance to miasma compared to the average person, as noted by [[Minerva]]. Despite having been exposed to the miasma of Omega, which had previously caused numerous fully grown men to go mad and kill themselves, Palmyra showed no signs of being negatively affected by it. ==Trivia== *In the Comic Alive version of [[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 2|One Wild Night]], Palmyra's age is said to be fifteen.''Faintly drawing her eyebrows together, Palmyra fixed her gaze on Omega. The pleas of this young girl, so brave at only fifteen—the same age as Colette—left Omega with no choice but to surrender.'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 2]], Section 2. The adaptation of One Wild Night in [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 10|Tanpenshuu Volume 10]] changes the sentence to avoid any mention of her age, thus making it unknown if her age is the same in the present. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Lugunica Navbox}} [[Category:Omega Party]]

She was tasked by [[Capella Emerada Lugunica|Mother]] to keep an eye on Salum. ==Appearance== Pooka is a small squirrel whose fur is mostly light brown. She wears blue shoes, a blue scarf, and a yellow flower on her head. When Wolf fed her a large amount of mana with his Evil Eye of Avarice to save her life while she was on the verge of death, she underwent a transformation similar to [[Puck]]'s Star Beastification, becoming enlarged, showing buck teeth, and taking on sharp, red eyes. ==Personality== In contrast to the quiet Salum, Pooka has a cheerful and energetic personality. Sometimes she scolds the less responsive Salum, and sometimes she speaks on his behalf. Though she cares for Salum, she is less kind towards his other personality, Wolf. She respects Puck, who is famous as one of the [[Spirit#Four Great Spirits|Four Great Spirits]] and is often angry with [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]], who treats Puck as usual. She also claims to be Puck's "admirer". ==Trivia== *Pooka shares her name with a shapeshifting spirit in Celtic folklore that is said to bring both good and bad fortune. Ironically, it is also believed that the pooka inspired the character "Puck" in William Shakespeare's ''A Midsummer Night's Dream''. *Pooka's boss design was inspired by Hamsuke from the ''Overlord'' series. *Although currently unconfirmed, in the prologue of [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 46|Volume 46]], there is an unnamed speaker who uses Pooka's Japanese pronoun ''atai'' (アタイ), strongly suggesting that she has been canonized in the main story. ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} {{Non-Canon Navbox}} {{Beloved Children Navbox}} [[Category:Contract Spirits]] [[Category:Great Spirits]] [[Category:Spirit]]

She has short green hair and a matching green-coloured dress. She typically wears various accessories in her hair. ==History== At some point after [[Sithonia Featherrun]] became a Featherrun Sister, Ornea was taken in by [[Holosseo Featherrun]] and made into an imperfect curse doll. Ornea was exceptionally suited to her role as a curse doll, and excelled in regeneration and combat. As a result, she was typically the one chosen among her sisters for missions that required assassination. After the plan to complete a perfect curse doll was set into motion, Ornea's mind broke due to the poison Sithonia had planted in the amulet she'd given her, and was thus sent out to kill [[Elsa Granhiert|Elsa Featherrun]]. However she failed and was crushingly defeated by Elsa. Despite being killed, due to her exceptional powers as a curse doll, Ornea was able to regenerate herself. However the effects of the poison had made it so she'd regressed to an infantile state. After Elsa defeated Sithonia, Elsa entrusted her to [[Oliver Zeppes]] and granted the Featherrun mansion to them. ==Abilities== '''Curse Doll''' (呪い人形): As an imperfect curse doll, Ornea possessed immense regenerative capabilities giving her a pseudo-immortality. From the Featherrun sisters, Ornea was said to be the strongest in both regenerating and combat. [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 28|Volume 28]] (main story)}} '''Olbart Dunkelkenn''' (オルバルト・ダンクルケン) is the previous '''Third ranking [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Divine General]]''' of the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]] and the chieftain of Vollachia's shinobi village. He played an antagonistic role in [[Arc 7]] and a supporting role in [[Arc 8]]. He also played a minor supporting role in [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5|The Tale of the Scarlet Princess]]. A long-time [[shinobi]], having lived in the shadows for his whole life, Olbart played his role as a shinobi with one ambition in mind: to manifest an unbelievably flashy death for himself.''“To be honest, I ain’t that interested in people like ya both. Those guys who got the tables turned on ‘em and got defeated were weak, and that was their fault… oh, me? The reason I’m doin’ this shinobi thingamajig is, ya see. Somewhere, someday, I aspire to have an unthinkably flashy death. Keep that a secret, tho’, eh?”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 8. Becoming a Divine General later in life, the Vicious Old Man decided that, in order to fulfill his ambition, he would assassinate Emperor [[Vincent Vollachia]], thereby leaving his mark on the history of the Empire and bringing down the very concept of the shinobi.''The appeal from his fighting instincts ceased when he realized that it was not Olbart within the grasp of his fingers, but Kafma’s body that the old man had thrown over Garfiel’s head.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 1. Of course, even in spite of the viciousness he is known for, there are some things that Olbart considers being taken too far, one example being the group that used sacrifices to turn [[Arakiya]] into a [[spirit]] eater,''In Olbart’s mind as he spilled those words, an unmatched, unorthodox group who he had dealt with in the past emerged. In order to produce the perfected Spirit Eater known as Arakiya, those criminals had sacrificed an enormous amount of people, and had said that their actions were out of a sense of duty, that it was for the sake of the Empire’s future.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 60, Section 1. while another was the experimentation of souls that led to undead monstrosities born of mutated and mixed souls.''Valuing human life or having mercy towards the weak, that leeway that only people with such room in their hearts possessed, was something that Olbart, who did not have much time left, had already discarded a long time ago. For Olbart, the audience chamber―― no, this experimentation ground of “souls”, had gone too far.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 60, Section 1. In the case of the former, while he was unwilling to dispose of Arakiya, he did bring an end to the group responsible for her,''"Reminds me of the bunch who made Araki, this way of doin’ things. Even tho’ it wasn’t for fun or for revenge, I couldn’t bear ta dispose of it ‘cause they nerve ta do this kinda thing. They were dealt with, tho’."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 60, Section 1. while in the case of the latter, he believed it was better to bring an end to such monstrosities.''"Even so, it was better ta kill it. It’s way too awful if it makes me think that way."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 60, Section 1. By not holding anything precious and refusing to devote his heart to anyone, Olbart has achieved the pinnacle of shinobi techniques, reigning as the indisputable strongest shinobi the Empire has to offer and climbed all the way up to the rank of Third among the Nine Divine Generals.''――Without a doubt, Olbart’s thoughts were dictated by no one. For that reason, this man, Olbart Dunkelkenn, reigned as the strongest shinobi. He was a shinobi who had been perfected with him not holding anything as precious, or having anyone to whom he devoted his heart.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 30]], Chapter 2, Section 1. With his unusually long life spanning over nine decades, Olbart has achieved pretty much everything he wished for. However, despite his being a perfect representation of what a shinobi should be, Olbart has always had his misgivings about how he had lived as a shinobi, and at times, he even attempted pass his teachings and beliefs onto the other shinobi of his village, albeit mostly meeting with failure, and at times, he would openly and brazenly disobey the village's doctrine.''The essence of the shinobi was to obey commands without asking too much, and Yae considered that a preferable trait. The only one who would brazenly disobey was the village chief, and since Yae was not the same as him, she remained obedient.'' [[Arc 9]], Chapter 51, Section 4. For example, Olbart does not believe that it is good for the shinobi to specialize in one technique and must be capable of exploiting their targets' weaknesses, and thus, the shinobi must be capable of using multiple techniques.''Prior to Olbart becoming the chieftain, the shinobi were generally encouraged to specialize in a singular technique. However, the idealized conception of single-skill specialization was only for the privileged few like Cecilus and Arakiya, who possessed a single technique that could be effective against anyone, while those with ordinary abilities must be adaptable or they would simply die. Thus, when Olbart became the chieftain, he immediately abandoned the doctrine of single-technique specialization.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7.''A battle, in essence, was about imposing one’s strengths upon the weaknesses of the other. This was the basis of Olbart’s fighting style as a shinobi. To strike according to the weaknesses of all sorts of opponents, Olbart had avoided honing any specialized skills.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7. Though, he failed to cultivate shinobi toward this direction, and with the supposed death of one of the village's most talented shinobi, [[Yae Tenzen]], he came to believe the idea a lost cause.''Rather than blindly honing one’s own special skill, they would thoroughly forge a combat style that thwarted the opponent’s strong points, and learn techniques to bring about that situation. But then again, this change did not readily bear fruit.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7.''Those who had been properly shaped by it were few, with the last being a genius girl who had appeared in the village four or five years prior. It seemed like that genius girl had also died, so the cultivation of talented individuals was nothing more than a lost cause.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7. He also believes that, despite the teachings of the shinobi, living without finding something that one could hold precious holds back the true potential of the shinobi. Like Yae, because he is capable of doing almost anything without a second thought, most of life loses its spark, making it so that the idea of keeping something precious becomes more desireable. In fact, he has even pestered Yae regularly about such issues, claiming that she should also go against the shinobi's teachings.''“Hey, yer like that, ain’t’cha? Same as me, ya can do just about anythin’ without so much as a second thought, ‘n so life kinda loses its spark, don’t it? Wouldn’t it be fine ta keep at least a single somethin’ in yer heart, then?”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 1.''“Ya don’t wanna? Listen, I’ve been there myself. Remarkable folk like the two of us end up livin’ longer than most ordinary shinobi without even realizin’ it, ‘n we end up seein’ tons’a things. So occasionally, there’ll be times. Times when you’ll hafta end up breakin’ the ironclad law of the shinobi.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 10. In particular, although he is aware that living as a shinobi means living in the shadows without the chance for fame, he holds the ambition of making his own death glamorous so that he can have posthumous fame, thus leaving a mark on the Empire's history and uprooting the very concept of shinobi. This is mainly because he believes that dying as a shinobi would leave their death as empty.''“Old age is not enough for your ambition to dry up. ――The shinobi push their bodies and minds to the extreme, and merely a scant few can reach such a state. Even if the day of your death arrives, you shall never be complete.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 2, Section 1. Knowing that he was close to death in his old age, he decided to follow this strong ambition and decided to set his sights on murdering Emperor Vincent Vollachia, who he has regarded as the greatest emperor of all time. ==History== Olbart hails from the shinobi village located in the Sacred Vollachia Empire. Having been seemingly raised by the shinobi, Olbart has lived the life of one ever since an early age. He did not believe in the doctrine of specializing in only a single technique, instead training in using strategies that thwarted an opponent's strong points and learning techniques to guide a battle to a favorable result. By the time he reached middle-age, he had gained a reputation as the most formidable and deadly shinobi of all. When [[Shasuke]] and [[Raizo]] became runaway shinobi and fled from the village, he permitted them to escape on a whim, and revealed to them his secret, the ambition that led him to becoming a shinobi: to die an unimaginably flashy death. Eventually, Olbart became the chieftain of the shinobi, abandoning the single-technique doctrine in favor of his own philosophy.''“Oh, that Halibel guy’s here. Tha only shinobi in tha world stronger than me, really hate that guy.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 3, Section 1. At another point in time, Olbart also came into contact and dealt with the people responsible for turning Arakiya into a spirit eater. ===[[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5|The Tale of the Scarlet Princess]]=== Shortly after Vincent Vollachia's coronation as the seventy-seventh emperor of the Sacred Vollachia Empire roughly 7 years before the start of the main story, a large [[Ginunhive Armed Rebellion|uprising]] took place on the [[Ginunhive|Gladiator Island Ginunhive]], with the gladiators led by [[Ubilk]] wanting to become independent from the mainland. In order to squash the rebellion, Vincent had dispatched a regiment of the [[Imperial Army]] led by the Divine General Olbart and Arakiya, who had yet to be indicted as one of the generals. While Arakiya infiltrated the island in order to lower the bridge and let the main force inside the island, Olbart patiently waited outside the island. After Arakiya and a gladiator named [[Al]] took back the Gladiator Island, Olbart offered a reward to the gladiator, but he denied it. ===Years during Vincent's rule=== There were few who were properly molded by Olbart's ideology, the most recent of them being Yae Tenzen, a girl who gained a reputation as a genius prodigy who blossomed as a shinobi from childhood. She became Olbart's most valued pupil, earning unreserved praise from him. Often, Olbart would speak to her, giving her advice that he had learned over the course of his long life while also tempting her to go against the very teachings that the village espoused. Having caught wind of her talents, [[Chisha Gold]] tasked her with infiltrating the Barielle Manor in the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]] to observe, and later, to assassinate [[Priscilla Barielle]], which she ultimately failed, seemingly resulting in her purported death. Although Olbart referred ten more shinobi to the White Spider for him to deploy to Lugunica and fulfill the same task with, all ten of them failed at their tasks and met their ends, and no more shinobi were sent after her once one of the shinobi's techniques was turned against Chisha. In the aftermath of the situation, believing that Yae had truly died, Olbart felt regret that the cultivation of capable shinobi had seemed to end up a lost cause. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Olbart is a tremendously powerful man with an incredibly long lifetime of surviving impossible odds and opponents more powerful than himself. His skills are such that he has been considered one of the most dangerous warriors in the Vollachia Empire. More than that, however, he is considered to be the pinnacle of being a shinobi, and he is the second most powerful shinobi in the world behind the Admirer, Halibel. Among Vollachian generals, if one did not include Cecilus's overwhelming strength and Arakiya's sheer firepower, Olbart, alongside one other general, are considered to be among the most dangerous elements in the event that a nation was to enter war with Vollachia. ===Physical Traits/Flow Method=== '''Skilled Martial Artist''': As the leader of Vollachia's shinobi village and its strongest member, Olbart has mastered the art of being a shinobi. He can masterfully bend his body to his own will, perform attacks seemingly impossible for an aged man, and dish out monstrous damage to his surroundings and enemies. His speed, strength, and accuracy are nigh unmatched among all Nine Divine Generals of the Empire. Even while missing an arm, he seemed rather unaffected by it and even used it to his advantage while in combat. Olbart is shown to use misdirection while in combat, making his opponent think that he is ducking or attacking from one direction while in reality, his attack is coming from elsewhere.''As his eyes followed Olbart, who should have slipped below, an impact struck the top of his head. Even though Olbart should have crouched down, something had hit him from above.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 1.''Garfiel’s fist, swinging downwards, whiffed, and struck the ground with a tremendous impact. Instead, the voice of Olbart, who disappeared in an instant, was heard from directly above.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 1. He is also particularly knowledgeable of the weaknesses of the human body and can accurately target those spots; even should he be forced to fight without killing his opponents, he can strike at pressure points to instantly incapacitate them.''By precisely striking the weak spots of the human body that were known as pressure points, the body could be robbed of its freedom, becoming powerless like the undead that had been buried in the wall earlier. In that manner, the undead stuffed into the wall by Olbart numbered about fifty―― he was relieved that their pressure points still functioned as weak spots, even though the construction and interior of their bodies were a sham.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 58, Section 1. Even ignoring that, he has enough physical might that his hand is capable of piercing straight through his enemy's chest,''The flying debris had split her forehead, kunai had been thrust into her neck and femur, and her chest had been pierced through the middle by Olbart’s hand. Even then, the Witch had not moved an inch.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 68, Section 2. and a kick from him holds enough power that it could not only send someone as strong as Garfiel flying away, but it could easily behead the average soldier.''Garfiel, breathing heavily, was then struck square on the nose by a kick from Olbart. His head snapped back from the astonishingly powerful kick of the puny-looking old man, his nose was broken, and Garfiel was blown off his feet. With that, he tumbled and flipped across the rough ground, then coming to lie with his whole body stretched out, spread-eagled. Were it not for Garfiel’s sturdy neck, the kick would have detached his head and sent it flying.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 100, Section 3. '''Superhuman Speed''': As a master shinobi, Olbart can move at insane speeds, seemingly teleporting and flying around the battlespace. During his fight with [[Yorna Mishigure]], his speed is described as that of a fighter jet, moving around at speeds surpassing that which can be followed by a normal human eye. His speed, in application with his mastery of primarily shinobi-used martial arts and deadly precision achieved only by a select few individuals around the world, make him one of the most deadly and efficient fighters hailing from the Empire. ===Techniques=== '''Shinobi Techniques''' (シノビの術技, ''Shinobi no Jutsugi''): Over the course of his long life, Olbart has become the pinnacle of the Empire's shinobi, making him the second strongest shinobi in the world, inferior only to Halibel, and one of the country's strongest living fighters, able to easily overpower most people facing him. By holding nothing precious to him, Olbart has managed to achieve the peak of shinobi techniques, and due to his belief that a shinobi should not specialize in merely one technique and must be capable of exploiting their opponents' weaknesses, Olbart has achieved mastery over many techniques, which, when combined with his vast experience, has allowed him to survive to the present day while able to overcome nearly every kind of opponent.''"That was entirely yer own punch. I just let it pass through my body, and returned it to ya."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 1.''However, an attack that resonated throughout the core of his body could not be negated.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 1.''"Incredible, isn’t it? I just released the power of yer attack onto the ground."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 1. *'''Unnamed Earth Diving Technique''': Through an unknown method, Olbart is capable of sinking into the ground and appearing elsewhere on the battlefield.''With five fingers of his outstretched, the old man’s face sank into the ground and disappeared, leaving behind his ridicule.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 100, Section 3. He is also capable of taking things from the environment and flinging them at his enemy from beneath the ground.''Looking at it, it appeared to be one of the corpses on the battlefield, which the old man had flung out from the sunken ground. By the time he realized that he had been successfully duped, it was already too late.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 100, Section 3. *'''Unnamed Poisoning Technique''': Through an unknown method, Olbart is capable of leaving behind poison with little more than a handprint. Those afflicted bleed, and their skin, flesh, and bone face being burned while steaming.''The moment his thoughts turned red-hot, an even greater heat arose on his right shoulder, where he had been touched. Taking a glance, Olbart’s handprint stood out, having been stamped in red upon his shoulder. From the handprint blood seeped and smoke was emitted, as it attempted to burn skin, flesh, and bone. Immediately after determining it to be poison, there was no hesitation.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 100, Section 3. It is unknown if this poison can spread to the rest of the body, as Garfiel, who was once hit with the technique, tore out the affected area before it could deal too much damage. *'''Unnamed Burial Technique''': By giving a tap to a solid surface, he can make said surface ripple like water, softening it to the point that he can hide bodies within it, and afterward, the surface hardens again.''Saying that, the white-haired, white-eyebrowed old man―― Olbart, carried the collapsed enemy with his lone left arm, using the tips of his toes to give a light strike to the defensive wall beside. As he did so, the surface of the wall rippled as if it were water, and stuffing the enemy’s body inside, it was swallowed, after which the wall’s surface filled back in.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 58, Section 1. ===Other=== '''Stealth''': As a shinobi, Olbart is a master of stealth. He is able to completely erase his presence if he so wishes, to the point that others will forget that he is in the same room, and he can remain hidden until he has either killed everyone nearby or purposefully makes his presence known. Though it is unclear if his statement is true, he has claimed himself to be able to go invisible.''"――Oh, so ya can see through my invisibility. Isn’t that a bit dangerous?"'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 1. Likewise, by keeping his presence hidden, he can also bypass the effects of specific [[curse]]s, such as [[Eugard Vollachia]]'s [[Curse#Curse of Thorns|Curse of Thorns]], which covers a relatively large radius.''The invisibility that eliminated the shinobi’s presence, rather than serving as a precaution against the castle’s guards, was a countermeasure to elude being counted as a target of the Curse of Thorns, which had been dispersed across a wide area in the Imperial Capital.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 1. '''Keen Battle Experience''': Due to his long lifespan, Olbart has seen many fights and toppled countless opponents. This allowed him to become quite proficient at figuring out his opponents' tricks and tactics, allowing him to form destructive counters to incoming attacks. Olbart immediately recognized Al's use of his unknown Authority, noting he had some strange tricks up his sleeve,''"That's an opinion that rebounds back onto you, you know? And I didn't cut corners too much either. That youngster with the helmet has got some strange tricks up his sleeve."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 39, Section 1 something that completely flew over Kafma Irulux's head, and after seeing Rui use Leaper once, he was able to determine how it worked. Likewise, he used this experience to expertly target his enemies’ weaknesses while on the battlefield, something that allowed him to even wipe out an army by himself. It was this habit and viciousness that earned him the moniker Vicious Old Man, and it is thanks to this that he has managed to survive fighting against even opponents who were stronger than himself.''“That’s the thing, even I’ve ended up on the verge of death many times quarrellin’ wit’ those above myself, ya see? But, I’m the one who’s still kickin’ when all’s said ‘n done, so it means we gotta get sneaky ‘n bridge the gap between us ‘n those monsters bit by bit ta succeed in life. If ya can rob yer opponent of their ability ta perform flawlessly, the opportunity ta chop off the heads of those above ya will come around. ――And it goes both ways, y’see? Kakakakka!”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 1, Section 2. '''Keen Orientation''': Olbart has mastered the ability to grasp a scene by looking at a map and never forget a location upon a single visit.''Being able to perfectly grasp a scene simply by looking at a map, and absolutely never forgetting a location upon a single visit, were fundamental skills of the shinobi, and for Olbart, the Crystal Palace was a place of work that he visited frequently.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 58, Section 1. It is thanks to this ability that he was able to traverse the Crystal Palace, which he had visited many times prior, with ease, despite its hallways and rooms being distorted. ===Equipment=== As a shinobi, Olbart carries many traditional weapons associated with them, such as kunai and shuriken, as well as compressed spirit stone bombs, keeping them stored away safely inside his sleeves: *'''Kunai & Shuriken''': Olbart can use his kunai knives and shuriken with terrifying speed and precision, killing very skilled opponents without them even realizing it. It is not uncommon for him to flood the area around him with his weapons in order to cut off his opponent's movements, and he can use shinobi techniques to disguise when he threw them.''The next instant, an endless deluge of shuriken rained upon Yorna in the air from all directions. The shinobi technique made it impossible to discern when he had thrown them. The rotating blades drew a different trajectory each as they closed in on Yorna, threatening to brutally lacerate her maidenly skin in their wake.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 6, Section 1. He also has his shuriken coated in poison that is capable of exploding even if the target dodges.''"Garfiel, that’s a shuriken. It’s coated with poison. Even if you avoid it, it’ll explode. What is the right move?"'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 109, Section 1. *'''Ration Balls''': Olbart keeps ration balls, small balls filled with nutrients without regard for taste, on his person. Despite their awful taste, by Olbart's words, they are capable of keeping a person going for an entire day.''“It’s called a ration ball, it’s part of a shinobi’s essentials. One of these’ll last’cha a day and keep yer head and body in shape. But lemme tell ya, it tastes awful.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 6, Section 1. *'''Compressed Fire Stone Bombs''': During his fight with Yorna, Olbart demonstrated a deadly and brutal weapon; compressed fire stone bombs. Taking a similar shape to his emergency food rations, Olbart is equipped with small black balls which have chunks of fire stones embedded inside of them.''“Ngh, looks like that, right? But, things’d get messy if ya ate ‘em. ——For ya see, chunks of Fire Magic Stones are tightly stuffed in ‘em.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 6, Section 3. Though their size is miniscule, the potential damage dealt by their explosions is no laughing matter. By simply throwing them in the air and forcing Yorna to try and destroy them in order to prevent a bombardment of the city below, Olbart managed to catch Subaru in a brutal death loop with there being no seeming way to avoid the blast and having his eyes and ears destroyed. *'''Book of Techniques''': Olbart has a book which he uses to keep track of and record as many different combat techniques and skills as possible. ==Trivia== *Olbart's birthday, which was decided at the April 6, 2025 talk show, is September 15, which in Japan is Respect for the Aged Day. *It is said that the types of people that Olbart has killed the most were scouts and messengers.''Olbart, the head honcho of the shinobi, was more than aware of how important it was to have accurate and recent information within warfare. It was to the extent that the enemies Olbart had killed the most within his lifetime were either scouts or messengers.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 58, Section 1. *According to Vincent, Olbart is knowledgeable of curse arts.''"Excluding Groovy Gumlet, the only one with knowledge of Curse Arts is Olbart Dunkelkenn."'' Gladiator |Status = Alive |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 31|Volume 31]]}} '''Null''' (ヌル), commonly known as '''Old Man Null''' (ヌル爺さん), is a healer who previously resided at the [[Ginunhive|Gladiator Island Ginunhive]] for many years. He later became a member of the Pleiades Battalion. ==Appearance== Null is an elderly man with a thin and wrinkly body. He has protruding white hair near his ears, and a circular symbol above his right ear, and an elongated head. He wears a light vest and a long scarf wrapped around his neck. ==Personality== Prior to leaving Ginunhive, Null often cooped himself up in the island's healing room, where he had the free time to occasionally doze off when he was not working. He also dislikes when others use his medicine for harm, befitting his position as a healer. ==History== Many years ago, Null was sent to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive for unknown reasons at a time when the island was much more deadly. One day, his life would change when he put a cloth over the wound of a gladiator who lost their arm.''It had all began when he did nothing more but to apply a dirty cloth to stop the bleeding on an open wound of a gladiator who had lost their arm.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 31]], Chapter 3, Section 5. This would lead to more instances where he would be called to heal people. Null was consequently ordered to work as a healer in Ginunhive's healing room, and he would become more acquainted with bloody scenes over the years. While Null lived peacefully as a healer, [[Al|a gladiator]] would escape the Gladiator Island and the Chief at that time was promptly fired. To fill up the new position, Emperor [[Vincent Vollachia]] would appoint [[Gustav Morello]] as the new Island Chief. Under Gustav's leadership, the Gladiator Island was remade from its previous lawlessness into a more orderly place where there were less unnecessary deaths. As a result, the number of people who died from injuries or illnesses decreased. ==Abilities== '''Amateur Healing Skills''': Although Null was formerly a healer at Ginunhive, he lacks the skills to properly treat other people, effectively making him a healer in name. Null can stitch wounds and concoct simple medicinal drugs. However, because he was not allowed to use effective drugs by the Gladiator Island's administrators, he couldn't create anything more than adverse concoctions, such as the poison he made for [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]]. ==Trivia== *Null's name is likely based on the German word "null", meaning "zero". *Although Null is described to have a beard in [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 31|Volume 31]],''The old man with a thin body, an untended long beard, and the impression of a cotton swab was Old Man Null, the healer cooped up in the healing room.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 31]], Chapter 3, Section 3. he lacks one in any official illustration. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Ginunhive]] [[Category:Gladiators]] [[Category:Slaves]] [[Category:Pleiades Battalion]]

[[Omega Party]] |Previous Affiliation = Leanotte
[[Gustekan Church]] |Previous Occupation = Itinerant Preacher |Status = Alive |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 10|Tanpenshuu Volume 10]]}} '''Noelle Tuérico''' (ノエル・トゥエリコ) is a former Itinerant Preacher of the [[Gustekan Church]]. She later deserted from her position to join the [[Omega Party]]. ==Appearance== Noelle is a fair-skinned woman with a curved body and plump chest. She has long, braided gold hair that reaches down past her shoulders, clear blue eyes, and wears a thick, black church vestment. ==Personality== Noelle is a friendly and cheerful girl who is willing to help those in need. That said, she is also smart and is properly wary of the people she is around, especially when it comes to fellow members of the Gustekan Church. Furthermore, she also has a vengeful side, born the day her village was crushed. She is patient and diligent enough to wait for years so that she can find her target. Likewise, she can also be rather brutal towards her enemies, and she is quick to resort to violence if anyone she deems her enemy doesn't meet her demands. ==History== ===Early Life=== When she was young, Noelle lived in the village of Leanotte in [[Gusteko]]. However, after an avalanche caused by the Ice Thieves, many of the village's people died, including her family, her friends, and her neighbors. As a result, Noelle joined the Gustekan Church, seeking to use her induction into the faith as a means to pursue revenge against those responsible for the avalanche. For twelve years, she awaited the day she could exact her revenge, and she eventually managed to become an Itinerant Preacher. At one point, she was saved by [[Nananna Pezza]]'s medicinal knowledge, and she later assisted her in regard to Leanotte. One day, Noelle was forwarded a letter from Coatl, a pastor who used his savings to restore Leanotte in the aftermath of its avalanche and took up residence at a nearby church on a mountain, by the Gustekan Church. In the letter, he confessed that he had belonged to the Ice Thieves and had been among those who caused Leanotte's avalanche. When Noelle arrived at the church he resided in, Coatl welcomed her, affirming the sins he had committed, and requesting that retribution be limited only to his life. However, Noelle, whose reason for joining the Gustekan Church had been to seek payback on all of the Ice Thieves, refused to accept the result. She tortured Coatl in an attempt to force him to divulge the identities of his peers, but he refused, leading Noelle to murder him by dealing a killing blow to his head with her gloves. She then fled from Coatl's church, travelling down the mountain despite an ongoing blizzard until she caught a glimpse of a fire spell. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 1|One Wild Night]]=== After having seen a fire spell in the distance, Noelle found a [[Omega|party]] [[Colette|of]] [[Palmyra|girls]] in the snow, with one of them, Omega, passing out from the cold of the active blizzard. They waited for Omega to regain her energy in a makeshift snow house Noelle created and spoke with her in the meantime, learning about the term Silver Blessing, her position in the Gustekan Church, and the nearby church building they can use as a refuge. They visit the church once Omega is rejuvenated and acquaint themselves with [[Podoso]], [[Admonsah]], and [[Maqueena]], each of whom had come to the church to meet the pastor who lives there, [[Coatl]]. The trio learns of Coatl's history of having saved a local town from the effects of an avalanche unintentionally caused by the Ice Thieves and how he took up a position of the town's watcher following his charity towards its people, becoming known by the moniker Saint of the Avalanche. Maqueena and Podoso split off from everyone else to visit another part of the church, and another visitor named [[Trellock]] arrived while they were out. Eventually, Maqueena discovered something and screams, prompting everyone else to follow after her to find what has caused her fear. They all stumbled upon Coatl's corpse, prompting Omega to say that there was a cold-blooded killer among them. Omega took charge of the situation, using detective work to determine the killer's identity. She heard from Podoso that there had been a string of serial murders, with Coatl being the eighth known victim. The other victims were peddlers and travelers. Querying him about the seventh victim, Omega then sets her sights on Admonsah, whom she was certain was associated with them. They learn Admonsah was a former slave who unexpectedly killed his owner in self-defense. He was unequivocally forgiven by a majority of the group. Omega tries to ascertain why Coatl would be murdered, searching for any hidden savings. Suddenly, everyone but Maqueena in the room fell asleep to the effects of the Muskrim flower, and she made her getaway with Coatl's collection of magic stones, not wanting to stay and fall victim to his murderer. She was stopped outside by Noelle, who says she could not be affected by such a simple drug and had killed Coatl out of revenge for his former membership of the Ice Thieves and his part in causing the avalanche that devastated Leanotte, her town. Omega arrives to stop Noelle before she could kill Maqueena, outlining that she was only a con artist who perceived Coatl's connection to the Ice Thieves rather than an outright member before giving the ultimatum that she would die if she caused another death, yet again manifesting her true form while saying so. Meanwhile, the culprit responsible for the serial murderers, Trellock, attempted to murder Colette, but her Beast Protection Bracelet activated, severely injuring him. In the end, they pretended that Noelle had apprehended Trellock and left, Podoso decided to take in Admonsah, and Maqueena was forced to stop conning people. With her revenge foiled, Noelle was left aimless. Colette proposed for her to join their group to which she accepted upon Omega's approval. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Extra|One Wild Night Extra]]=== Later, the party decided to head to the town Podoso had told them about. Eventually, they set up camp, and while Colette and Noelle set up the camp, Palmyra decided to talk with Omega about including Noelle in their travels, worried about getting her involved in their troubles, which included Omega being a half-elf Witch and Colette's bracelet. Omega believed that there was nothing to worry about, and shortly after, Noelle, who had heard part of their conversation appeared and said that she already knew about Omega's secret and chose to follow them regardless. Though Palmyra asked if she had a thing for odd people and Noelle's joking reply that she did, just like Palmyra, she claimed to be just as odd, as she was an itinerant preacher from the Gustekan Church who had decided to leave. Though Palmyra thought it wasn't as bad as Omega's secret, Omega told her that she was underestimating the Church and what they bestowed Noelle, and the two claimed that they would not be amicable toward her effectively breaking a contract, something which might end up leading to them falling into her mess. Though Palmyra told Omega to be prepared to fight, when Noelle told her to feel free to kick her from the party if she ever became a burden, to which she replied by saying not to underestimate her and spoke of her own circumstances, basically unintentionally cornering Noelle into staying in the party after saying not to use Colette as an excuse. Colette arrived shortly after, and the group decided not to talk to her about their conversation. Instead, they ate, and Noelle explained repairs that she had made to their equipment and offered her knowledge of how to use their equipment and how to survive in Gusteko, including knowledge on the Gustekan Church, to which Palmyra and Omega realized that they wouldn't be able to survive in Gusteko without Noelle. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland Part 1|Omega in Wonderland]]=== The party continued to trudge through the snows of Gusteko, with Palmyra and Omega becoming exhausted. Attempting to give Palmyra some more energy, Colette attempted to let her use her bracelet, but when Palmyra tried, it left her weak and vomiting. Omega explained the reason for this, claiming she allowed it to happen because she wanted to see the look on her face. Afterward, she had Noelle carry Palmyra while Colette carried her. As they got closer to the town of Sylphoa, Omega dispelled a barrier, and eventually they reached the town, where she and Colette fell subject to the Dream Arts spell that had been cast over the town. Meanwhile, Noelle and Palmyra, who were unaffected thanks to Noelle's seal, met with a Temple Knight named [[Zank Metley]], who was there to hunt a heretic. Noelle and Palmyra, carrying the others' unconscious bodies, followed him into an empty tent, where he explained the situation. However, after entering into conflict with Palmyra, who does not follow the Church's teaching, Colette's bracelet senses danger and transformed her body into a beast. After Zank deemed her a heretic, Colette ran away with Omega and Palmyra, Noelle stood in his way and negotiated working with him to take care of the problem at hand, to which he complied. Soon after, Noelle encountered [[Shion]] who had just put Palmyra to sleep. Not listening to her, Noelle threatened Shion with violence, only to be warned that Zank had killed his allies. Shortly after, alongside the beastified Colette, she had a small fight with Zank, until Palmyra awoke and claimed that the other Temple Knight, [[Mikli Yulitô]], was alive. Following this, after Omega spoke to Zank, who had in reality come to retrieve Mikli, and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, [[Lilac]], Shion's phantom, released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Witch Trials Part 1|Witch Trials]]=== One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a [[Witchbeast#Snow Blight|Snow Blight]]. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of Nananna and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches. Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named [[Minor Characters#Piditz|Piditz]] who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find [[Mireille Hetia]] using her [[Magic#Spiritual Arts|spiritual arts]] to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody. Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to [[Edmon Quayle]]. As part of Omega's plan, Noelle persuades Nananna to speak up, and Nananna insists on the town holding a Witch Trial for Omega, and Palmyra declares that if she is a Witch that she would burn with her. At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started. Likewise, Omega explained this to Palmyra, as she learned it while imprisoned. As for Noelle, she joined Nananna, who had been speaking with Edmon about finding Piditz. As she is intent on finding out about the real culprit, Nananna knocks her out and hides her in a pit where all the bodies of the dead "Witches" were dumped. Meanwhile, Shion used her dream arts to peer into the minds of the townsfolk, and she warns Lilac that the "Witch" is just a conspiracy by the council to get rid of political enemies. After learning of this, Lilac informs the Colette and Palmyra, and the elves suggest sowing division in the people to uproot the conspiracy. Though wanting to talk to Noelle, she does not come back that night, and Lilac and Shion decide to use their dream arts to nudge the townsfolk to attend the upcoming. The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise. Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an [[Minor Characters#Elderly Healer|elderly healer]], and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch. Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it. ==Abilities== ===Physical Traits/Flow Method=== Noelle has received training from the Gustekan Church, and by her own claim, although she has not received a Blessing, her strength is supposedly on par with a Temple Knight. '''Melee Fighter''': As a former Itinerant Preacher, Noelle is skilled in combat. She has enough physical strength to smash a person’s head in, and she can momentarily clash with a Temple Knight like Zank Metley. '''Stimulant Resistance''': Although Noelle has not been bestowed with a Blessing, as an Itinerant Preacher, she can resist drugs and poison. ===Other=== '''Seal''': As a part of her training, she was given a seal that makes her resistant to external [[magic]] and [[Curse|curse arts]], and it can even do the same for anyone she carries. With it, she was able to complete ignore the effects of Shion and Lilac's Dream Arts that affected an entire town. It is unclear if this seal has been born of magic or some other method. ===Equipment=== *'''Steel Gloves''': Noelle wears a pair of black steel gloves. They are a type of holy tool that harden when mana is transmitted through them, allowing them to easily be used to smash a person’s head in. ==Trivia== *When Noelle was initially introduced in the Monthly Comic Alive release of One Wild Night, her name was '''Lysa Conwell''' (ライサ・コンウェル, ''Raisa Konueru''). However, with the release of [[The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland Part 1|Omega in Wonderland Part 1]], the author permanently altered her name to Noelle Tuérico in her future appearances. ==Navigation== {{Gusteko Navbox}} [[Category:Gustekan Church]] [[Category:Omega Party]]
