[[Ryuzu Meyer (original)|Ryuzu Meyer]] (basis)
[[Garfiel Tinzel]] (ward/grandson figure) |Status = Alive |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 10|Volume 10]] |Manga = [[Daiyonshou Chapter 3|Arc 3 Chapter 3]] |Anime = [[Episode 27]] |Japanese Voice = [[Wikipedia:Aimi Tanaka|Tanaka Aimi]] |English Voice = [[Wikipedia:Lizzie Freeman|Lizzie Freeman]]}} '''Ryuzu Meyer''' (リューズ・メイエル) is the name of the [[Ryuzu Meyer (original)|original Ryuzu Meyer]], whom her copies are based on. They played supporting roles throughout [[Arc 4]]. Originally created by [[Echidna]] during her immortality experiments, the Ryuzu clones were tasked with protecting the [[Sanctuary]] and its residents for 400 years. Following the [[Sanctuary Incident|events]] of Arc 4, the Ryuzu clones now live in a village near the new [[Roswaal Manor]] and are part of the [[Emilia Camp]], and they can also be seen wandering around on the new Roswaal Manor's grounds. ==Appearance== Like the original Ryuzu Meyer, all of the copies look the same. Ryuzu is a petite girl with long, fluffy pink hair that curves outward at the ends. She wears a large black robe (white for Shima) that drags along the ground and is too big for her hands to show completely through the sleeves. The bodies of the copies are revealed to have been created with an artificial "Od" that is surrounded and bound together with mana, forcing them to change places in order to recharge once they reach their daily limit. Following the Sanctuary Incident, [[Garfiel Tinzel|Garfiel]] and [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]] have begun styling each Ryuzu's hair differently in order to tell each of them apart, with the exceptions of the main three Ryuzus. ==Personality== Out of all of the clones, only four have an actual personality, as a necessity to perform their duties as main managers of Sanctuary. Although they share the first name with the original they are given different last names as part of their roles, personality quirks, hobbies and interests. The rest of the copies are devoid of any ego and act as simple workers who obey the 4 main Ryuzu or take care of other duties. Those that are recognized to be an Apostle of Greed by Echidna are allowed to gain command over the clones if they touch the crystal the original Ryuzu resides in. Each of the four main Ryuzu take on the role as Ryuzu every four days. '''[[Ryuzu Meyer (original)|Ryuzu Meyer]]''' (original): By her own will, she sacrificed her life to enact the Sanctuary's Barrier by using her own Od which sealed her body in a crystal in order to stop the [[Hector|Warlock of Melancholy]] from destroying the Sanctuary. She also agreed to be a part of Echidna's experiment as long as the witch promised to maintain the Sanctuary. *'''Ryuzu Alma''' (リューズ・アルマ, ''Ryuuzu Aruma''): Alma was in favor of freeing the Sanctuary. She was the one who clarified Subaru over various aspects of the conflict within the Sanctuary. *'''Ryuzu Bilma''' (リューズ・ビルマ, ''Ryuuzu Biruma''): Like Alma, Bilma was also in favor of freeing the Sanctuary. She is the 2nd clone Subaru meets and speaks the most with. Bilma also has the most playful disposition among the main overseers. *'''Ryuzu Shima''' (リューズ・シーマ, ''Ryuuzu Shīma''): Shima was against freeing the Sanctuary due to seeing the original Ryuzu's memories 10 years prior to the start of the story in the trial, and she had been partly manipulating Garfiel behind the scenes to make sure it didn't happen. She entered the grave in an attempt to rescue Garfiel but was forced into taking the trial. In the end, this meant that she had broken her contract with Echidna. As punishment, Shima was duly stripped from her position as overseer, and she was made to live with the other childlike clones in the forest, donning the white robe as a result. After the Sanctuary's fall, it is revealed after that incident from a decade prior, Echidna had been planning to use her to escape once the barrier had been lifted, and to that end, she had been slowly latching more and more of her soul onto Shima, until eventually, she successfully hijacked her body. Echidna, now in Shima's body, calls herself [[Omega]]. *'''Ryuzu Delma''' (リューズ・デルマ, ''Ryuuzu Deruma''): One of the copies with an actual personality. She was also in favor of lifting the barrier. She acted as Shima's support when the latter was telling the story of the Sanctuary's past. *'''Pico''' (ピコ, ''Piko''): Pico is a copy that Subaru named when he first discovered the original Ryuzu's body. She is able to follow simple orders, but other than that, she is like a baby. She was the clone most oddly attached to Subaru throughout the arc. *'''Others''': The other copies don't have knowledge or experience, and they can only obey broad orders. The copies act as eyes and use their telepathy to relay messages if needed. They need others to order them to eat food once in a while and curl up when they reach their limit in the forest. Following the events in Arc 4, the main clones, alongside Subaru and Garfiel, have been giving names and new hairstyles to the numerous clones in order to help them gain a proper sense of self. The same goes for Pico. *'''[[Sphinx]]''' (スピンクス, ''Supinkusu''): The first clone created. Due to the imperfect method of Soul Transcription, she could not inherit all of Echidna's memories, personality, and power, which left her with a fragmented mind, and as a result, she was discarded. Centuries after her creation, she became a leading figure in the [[Demi-Human War]] and the instigator of the [[Great Disaster]]. She ultimately perished by the hands of [[Cecilus Segmunt]], [[Priscilla Barielle]], Subaru, and [[Spica]]. ==History== The Ryuzu copies were created by Echidna in an experiment to research immortality. She copied her memories and knowledge to the copies. However, her experiment was never completed because of her death. The main copies took over in order to manage the other copies in Echidna's place and to take on Ryuzu's role within the Sanctuary when the Mathers family supported them. ==Abilities== ''Note: This section will only detail the abilities shared by the clones. For the individual abilities of characters like Sphinx or Omega, see their respective pages.'' ---- '''Telepathy''': The Ryuzu copies are able to transmit their thoughts to each other. '''Self Destruction''': If ordered to do so, the clones can blow themselves up and inflict magical bomb-like damage on their enemies. ==Trivia== *In the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)|web novel]], the main Ryuzu copies did not have already individual names, leaving Subaru to give them random Greek alphanumeric names instead. There were also 5 main Ryuzu copies instead of 4, each named Alpha, Beta, Sigma, Theta, and Omega by Subaru. *In the light novel, it is revealed that Echidna was slowly hijacking Shima's body, ever since she accidentally underwent the first trial roughly a decade before the events of Arc 4. **In the web novel, Echidna renamed herself as Omega, stating that this is how Subaru named her, which implies Echidna's new vessel is the original Omega Ryuzu copy who may have merged with the real Ryuzu Meyer sealed in the crystal, similar to how Shima sacrificed herself by vanishing with the crystal and became her new body in [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 15|Volume 15]]. *[[Wikipedia:Aimi Tanaka|Tanaka Aimi]], the Japanese voice actress of the original Ryuzu and her copies, also voices [[Plum Risch]]. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Royal Selection Navbox}} {{Lugunica Navbox}} [[Category:Sanctuary]] [[Category:Emilia Camp]] [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[de:Ryuzu Meyer (Kopie)]] [[es:Ryuzu Meyer (copia)]] [[fr:Lewes Meyer (copie)]] [[pl:Ryuzu Meyer]] [[pt-br:Ryuzu Meyer (Cópia)]] [[ru:Рюдзу Мейер (копия)]] [[uk:Льюїс Мейєр (копія)]] [[zh:角色:琉兹（复制体）]]

52 unnamed former co-wives |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 18|Volume 18]] |Anime = [[Episode 55]] |Japanese Voice = [[Wikipedia:Aoi Koga|Koga Aoi]]}} '''Sylphy Elmart''' (シルフィ・エルマート) is a maid working at [[Roswaal Manor]] and the former 184th wife of [[Regulus Corneas]]. Introduced in [[Arc 5]] as '''Number 184''', one of Regulus's wives, she effectively acted as a leader amongst the wives and played a small hand in aiding [[Natsuki Subaru]], [[Emilia]], and [[Reinhard van Astrea]] with taking down the Sin Archbishop of Greed. Following Regulus's death, she and the other former wives were hired as maids for the Roswaal Manor by [[Annerose Miload]]. ==Appearance== Sylphy is a woman with golden blonde hair and dark blue eyes. She has similar hair to that of Emilia and noticeable cute features. She wore a dress with a similar design to the one most of Regulus's other wives wore, but with features distinguishing it from the others. When employed as a maid, she starts to wear a maid uniform. ==Personality== Due to years and years of having to live in fear of being killed for even smiling in front of Regulus, Sylphy developed a cold and emotionless facade which made her look like apathetic and uncaring. However, Sylphy does care about the others who were forcefully taken by Regulus, and she does not want to see them end up like many of his previous wives. This led her to taking the position of the representative of the other wives, willing to take his brutal punishment in place of the others. Likewise, she also believed that anyone who was able to escape from him should never come back, regardless of herself and the other wives, as she displayed to Emilia after she returned following her own “escape”. She even showed determination to end her own life if necessary in order to assist Emilia in defeating the man when she learned about the weakness of Regulus’s Authority. In the aftermath of Regulus's defeat, she developed profound feelings of loyalty to Emilia, dedicating herself to serving the [[Royal Selection]] Candidate upon her employment as a maid in the Roswaal Manor. ==History== At some point in the past, Sylphy lived in a small village in a mountain valley. However, when Regulus came and decided to take her as his 184th wife, he slaughtered her family, friends, and other villagers, just for knowing her face and name, leaving her to take on the emotionless facade that she and the other wives were forced to wear. ==Trivia== *Sylphy's birthday was decided at a talk show held on April 5, 2026. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Lugunica Navbox}} [[Category:Maids]] [[Category:Servants]] [[Category:House Miload]]

[[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33|Volume 33]] (mentioned)}} '''Stride Vollachia''' (ストライド・ヴォラキア) was a former prince of the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]] and a [[Witch Cult#Sin Archbishops|Sin Archbishop]] of the [[Witch Cult]], representing '''Pride'''. He was a younger [[Wilhelm van Astrea]]'s mortal enemy. He was the main antagonist of [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 3|Sword Demon Love Story]] and [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6|Sword Demon Battle Ballad]]. Born a sickly prince who was expected to die under the harsh tutelage of [[Kurgan|Eight Arms Kurgan]], he was a man who came to bear hostility toward the Observers. Following his failure to become the emperor, he obtained a Witch Factor and become one of the Witch Cult's Sin Archbishops, and with his [[Melinda|wife]], Kurgan, and [[shinobi]] subordinates, the [[Raizo|Twin]] [[Shasuke|Shura]], he began generating strife within the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]. In his final campaign against the Kingdom, in an event that has come to be remembered as the [[Subjugation of the Blight Dragon]], Stride assaulted the [[Picoutatte|Commercial City of Picoutatte]], summoning and manipulating the Blight Dragon [[Valgren]] with his [[Authority]]. However, in the end, he, alongside his wife, were devoured by that very [[Dragon]], and because of his actions, his name was stricken from the Empire's records.''"No, your studies are not to blame. In fact, your life would be at risk if you knew that information. That man’s existence has been long erased from the records of the Imperial Family of Vollachia, after all."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 3. ==Appearance== From a mere glance, Stride Vollachia could easily be recognized as a man of status around thirty years of age. His features, which helped distinguished his importance, were uncommonly sharp and noble. He had grey eyes and long, rich deep-purple hair that had a silky look to it and reached past his shoulders. His slim body had, ever since his youth, been riddled by illness that made even the simplest of physical activities grueling for him. His voice betrayed his imperialism and thus also his connection to the meritocratic Sacred Vollachia Empire. In reflection of his physical appearance and noble carriage, Stride wore clothing of princely refinement. His outfit, that was primarily black, consisted of black trousers, black shoes, a light grey shirt, a black cravat, a white waistcoat over the shirt, and a black long coat over the waistcoat that had notched lapels and rolled cuffs. Some of his clothing had purple lining that matched the color of Stride's hair. On his left shoulder, similarly to what future emperor [[Vincent Vollachia]] would come to bear, Stride had many large feathers with purple tips, denoting his remaining connections to the Imperial Family. On each of his ten fingers, Stride wore his rings, the Hubristic Ten Commandments, that he could use to afflict [[curse]]-like effects on his enemies. ==Personality== As the Sin Archbishop of Pride, Stride was vain and prideful, disliking being told what to do by others, as shown when he rebuked [[Yaktol Suwen]] for trying to restrict his actions or doing the same to Kurgan for talking back to him. He was openly rude to those he viewed to be lower than himself, and [[Theresia van Astrea|Theresia]] noted that he fluently insulted others. He seemed to underestimate fighters that aren't well known, as when Wilhelm and Kurgan first fought, he didn't think the former would stand a chance. Despite this, he was a quick thinker and praised things he found to be satisfactory. He was willing to ignore formalities to stop Wilhelm and Kurgan's first duel in order to prevent himself from potentially losing a valuable pawn. He plotted against the Kingdom of Lugunica knowing full well the power of [[Volcanica]]'s protection, earning him his alias, the Destruction Wish. Stride bears a powerful hatred of the Observers, as he has written in his journal. Likewise, many of his actions were done in accordance with this hatred. Stride spoke in a very archaic, regal and scornful manner. He favored using the pronoun '''mine venerable self '''(余, ''yo'') when speaking, which is a pronoun used only by kings or emperors. He also referred to people using '''thou '''(貴様, ''kisama'') with it having connotations of Stride treating everyone he spoke to as an inferior. ==History== ===Early Life=== Stride Vollachia was born as one of the sons of the emperor. However, he was born sick, and his family quickly proposed to offer the renunciation of his inheritance rights to another family, exchanging him for a suitable recompense. On the surface, Stride was sent to train under the strongest warrior in Vollachia, Kurgan, in order to improve his strength in mind and body, however, he was fully expected to die under Kurgan's harsh training regime. Luckily for Stride, though, Kurgan grew strangely attached to the bottomless darkness that was cultivating inside of the young boy's eyes, quickly taking a liking to Stride. Against all odds, he grew into adulthood under Kurgan's supervision. With strong ambition and insight, Stride had the potential to rise to a position where he could compete for the imperial throne. However, he had no backers for the Imperial Selection Ceremony. Shortly after, an unknown culprit poisoned Stride with a powerful poison, which caused Stride to drift between life and death for three arduous and agonizing months. The illness utterly destroyed him, to the point he more resembled a walking corpse, than a man. However, his eyes shone with newly-found determination–as he had found the very truth of the world, in the midst of his battle for life. On that day, Stride relayed to Kurgan what he saw: that there were entities called "Observers" who sit in the heavens, toying with everyone as if they were mere pieces upon a board. With Kurgan at Stride's side, wanting to support his "son", the Destruction Wish began carving his path forward. He met and recruited the runaway shinobi Shasuke and Raizo, the Twin Shura, appointing them as his "Generals". Not long after, he encountered his future wife, the Ashen Bride, Melinda, a survivor of the Evil Eye Tribe, a people nearly erased from existence due to their Evil Eye abilities. At some point in this timeframe, he acquired a Witch Factor, joined the Witch Cult, and received his Gospel from a [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti|diligent knave]] who introduced himself as a Sin Archbishop and assisted Stride with the handling of his Hubristic Ten Commandments.''“It is not like I hold any foolish beliefs towards that Witch, but emulating the diligent knave who handed this book to me and contributed in the way of handling my Authority… the Hubristic Ten Commandments, I shall say this.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 4. At an unknown time, he hid his journal within the Crystal Palace. ===[[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 3|Sword Demon Love Story]]=== Approximately forty years prior to the start of the story, aiming for Sword Saint, Stride used the gift of [[Veltol Astrea]] as an excuse to meet with him in the Suwen Company in Picoutatte, where he openly insulted him and his daughter. With Veltol challenging him to a duel, he claimed to be unable to fight due to his illness, which Theresia had noticed, and he decided to have Kurgan act as his champion. Further antagonizing the two with insults to them and Theresia's husband, Veltol struck him, leading to his brutal beating by Kurgan and being cursed by Stride. Leaving Yaktol Suwen with a message that he would be waiting at a great bridge in the city's west district with the source of the curse, he left. The next morning, he met with Theresia and Wilhelm, who challenged him to a duel. Despite being irritated that the rumors he heard regarding her award ceremony were true and that Wilhelm had equivalent battle aura to Kurgan, the duel ensued. Despite this, both sides took great damage, and seeing that he was in danger of losing his pawn, he stopped the duel and claimed it their loss, tossing his ring to them, and using another to turn the bridge beneath them into sand, allowing him and Kurgan to escape. ===[[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6|Sword Demon Battle Ballad]]=== In the following months, he conducted a series of attacks, targeting seemingly random locations across the Kingdom, such as the Astrea Manor, where he had his wife Melinda ensnare Wilhelm with her [[Melinda#Abilities|Evil Eye of Vainglory]] through a Conversation Mirror and bound [[Carol Remendis]] to the curse of the Amethyst Thumb on his left hand. During this period, he went to [[Sphinx]]'s refuge in Shamrock Valley to retrieve a forbidden art of hers that disabled people's [[Divine Protection]]s and nullified the covenant between the Kingdom and the Divine Dragon. Roughly eight months into Theresia's pregnancy, Stride delivered a swift blow to the Kingdom by invading the [[Royal Capital#Royal Castle|Royal Lugunica Castle]] and killing Veltol by forcing Carol, who he had cursed before, into doing his every bidding with the Amethyst Thumb. Carol kidnapped Theresia and Stride, after cursing the surviving [[Tishua Astrea]] with his remaining Scarlet Pinky Finger, took the both of them back to Picoutatte, where he would begin an incident that later became known as the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon. There, Stride set the forbidden art he previously retrieved across Picoutatte, situated himself in the city's main tower, and began collecting sacrifices, including a great deal of [[Demi-Human|demi-humans]] with a grudge against Lugunica who volunteered their lives in an attempt to aid Stride in bringing the nation's ruin. Using the skull of a deceased dragonkin, which drunk the blood of the sacrificed people he forced Carol to slay, he was able to summon the dragonkin's parent, the Black Dragon Valgren, through its survival instincts, binding its will to his with the Jade Index Finger, Amber Middle Finger, and Azure Ring Finger on his left hand. He ordered Melinda to use her Evil Eye of Vainglory on the city's guards, sending them to the Subjugation Force and pinning them down, allowing Kurgan to attack the knights. Shasuke then brought forth [[Roswaal J. Mathers]] and [[Grimm Fauzen]], the latter of whom arrived by error. Grimm had an arduous battle with Carol, who was still under Stride's curse, and Shasuke, one of Stride's shinobi. Roswaal, at the cost of her life, sacrificed herself to save the pair of Grimm and Carol from Shasuke. After attempting to defend himself from Grimm's attack by summoning the [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword]], it rejected him and began the process of burning his body, but he was quickly saved by Shasuke, who cut off his left arm, to stop the spread of the sword's flames. With the rings on his left hand reduced to ash, terminating their effects and leaving him with only the four rings on his right hand, Stride revealed his Gospel and his position as the Witch Cult's Sin Archbishop of Pride.''Holding that black evil book―― the Gospel, Stride gave a wicked smile, and said.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 4.''“Sin Archbishop of the Witch Cult, representing Pride―― Stride Vollachia.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 4. Due to his left arm being scorched to nothingness and five of his nine remaining rings being destroyed, however, Valgren regained its senses and promptly attacked the four people on the top of the tower. Barely being saved by Shasuke, Stride jumped in the air while being carried by his "General" but was intercepted by Carol. A duel between her and the shinobi followed, resulting in Carol bisecting Shasuke, leaving Stride unprotected. Realizing he had lost, Stride fell off of the Dragon's back, towards the streets of the city below. Before he could hit the ground, the Black Dragon sprung towards him. Just before it could swallow Stride, Melinda, utterly burnt due to being scorched by one of Valgren's previous attacks, lunged towards her husband, embracing him. Seconds later, Valgren's heads chewed their two bodies into chunks and swallowed the pair. However, even after his body was devoured, Stride's rings continued to influence Valgren. The Dragon was confronted by Wilhelm and Grimm, who both dealt a great deal of damage to the Dragon. During combat, Grimm and Wilhelm were both seriously wounded and could barely continue the fight. Just as the battle was about to close on a disastrous end, the fortieth King of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica, [[Gionis Lugunica]], appeared in the city, and with him, the Divine Dragon descended from the skies above. In a couple of minutes, Volcanica scorched Valgren's body away, effectively marking the end of Stride Vollachia's influence over the world. After this, Vollachia erased him from their history, with his sole remaining physical legacy, the journal he concealed in the Crystal Palace's library, being discovered by Vincent Abellux as a child. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Due to his weak physical condition from childhood, Stride's physical power is effectively non-existent. He primarily binds people to his will by employing his Authority in order to face off with his opponents, using this power to turn the swordswoman Carol Remendis against her friends. He also uses the skills of his four subordinates, including the combat prowess of his surrogate father, the Eight Arms, Kurgan, the Evil Eyes of Pride and Vainglory belonging to his wife, Melinda, and shinobi techniques of the Twin Shura, Shasuke and Raizo, having them fight and use their powers for his sake when his condition prevents him from engaging in a duels or he does not apply the effects of his Authority onto an opponent. ===[[Authority]]=== According to himself, Stride “obtained a Witch Factor and the manifestation of an Authority” despite proclaiming himself a “sham” and there being no recognizable inheritor to the Witch Factor of Pride after his death.''“Unfortunately though, I am just a sham that managed to obtain a Witch Factor and a manifestation of an Authority.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 4. He was assisted in handling his Authority by the same diligent knave who provided him with his Gospel. '''[[Authority#Authority of Pride|Hubristic Ten Commandments]]''' (傲れし十戒, ''Ogoreshi Jikkai''): Stride is the previous wielder of the '''Witch Factor of Pride''' and could use its respective Authority. Stride’s Authority produced a set of ten different rings that could “curse” any targets of Stride’s choosing. There were five unique rings, each corresponding to the five fingers on Stride's hand and having their own color assigned to them, as well as two copies of each unique ring for use on both hands. The rings shared the curse of binding a target's soul to adhere to Stride’s will, effectively turning them into a puppet that abode by his every whim. The eyes of a target changed change to the color corresponding with the ring Stride cursed them with. Furthermore, the rings had a last-resort technique that allowed Stride to manipulate a target’s body in such a way that their maximum potential was drawn out, but the burden this placed on their body was so immense, it could destroy the target if it was not terminated as soon as possible. It is unknown if Stride had a means to manufacture more rings or if the Authority could only manifest a total of ten rings. Similarly, it is unclear if the curses he could produce were related to those cast by curse arts or are otherwise entirely separate. *The '''Scarlet Pinky Finger''' (朱色の小指, ''Akeiro no Koyubi''), the ring variety on Stride's pinky fingers, had the secondary effect of casting a limb-rotting curse on its target. It exhausted the gate and rotted the limbs of the target it was placed on, and eventually led to death.''“――His gate is seriously exhausted. Unnaturally so. I should think it’s curse arts.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 3]], [[Sword Demon Love Story: The Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte Part 2|Sword Demon Love Story: The Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte]], Section 10.''“The normal course of things would have been for all four of my limbs to rot away, but that healer managed to force the decay into just one spot.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 3]], [[Sword Demon Love Story: The Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte Part 2|Sword Demon Love Story: The Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte]], Section 14. Its curses were cast on Veltol and Tishua Astrea. The Scarlet Pinky Finger on his right hand was sliced in half by Wilhelm at the conclusion of the Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte, leaving Stride with a total of nine remaining rings. *The '''Amethyst Thumb''' (紫紺の親指, ''Shikon no Oyayubi''), the ring variety on Stride's thumbs, had the secondary effect of casting an asphyxiation curse on its target. This curse activated when the cursed target touched a loved one, at which moment a dark red bruise left on their chest would begin to strangle them, hindering their capacity to breathe. Its curses were cast on Carol Remendis and an unborn Heinkel Astrea. *The '''Jade Index Finger''' (翡翠の真指, ''Hisui no Mayubi''), the '''Amber Middle Finger''' (琥珀の中指, ''Kohaku no Nakayubi''), and the '''Azure Ring Finger''' (空色の環指, ''Sorairo no Kanyubi''), each corresponding to their respective fingers, were not observed to have any secondary effects. The three rings on Stride's left hand were used to bind the Black Dragon Valgren, which required three rings for its three souls, to his will. Its curses were also cast on the Twin Shura, Shasuke and Raizo, and assumedly on an unnamed member of the Safeguarding Chamber. ===Equipment=== *'''[[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword Vollachia]]''' (陽剣ヴォラキア, ''Youken Vorakia''): As a member of the Imperial Family of Vollachia, Stride was capable of summoning and using the Yang Sword Vollachia, otherwise known as the Yang Sword, an ornate crimson sword with light that shines like the sun. However, Stride was unworthy of summoning the Yang Sword, and shortly after materializing the blade, Stride's left arm began to burn, incinerating his left hand and all five rings on it, prompting Shasuke to cut it off in order to save his life. *'''Gospel''' (福音): As a member of the Witch Cult, Stride was the owner of a copy of a Gospel. Each Gospel was a replica of the Book of Wisdom, a book that had been in the possession of the Witch of Greed, [[Echidna]]. The [[Terminology#Story Specific|Book of Wisdom]] would provide exact details of future events concerning the Witch of Greed, essentially bestowing Echidna with a form of precognition. Unlike the original Book of Wisdom, the Gospels of the Witch Cult were imperfect replicas, meaning that, although they detailed the future of its owner, the events conveyed were subject to change and the information provided was often up for interpretation. The Gospels took the form of small black books that could only be read by their owners. *'''Conversation Mirror''' (対話鏡, ''Taiwa-kyō''): A meteor that allows its user to communicate with others over a long distance by connecting with a separate Conversation Mirror, similar to a cell phone. Stride used a pair of Conversation Mirrors with his wife, Melinda, to have her ensnare Wilhelm with her Evil Eye of Vainglory over a long distance. ==Trivia== *In Sword Demon Love Story, Stride Vollachia referred to his rings, which bore the ability to curse their targets, as curse tools, claiming that they would be referred to as meteors in Lugunica.''“This is the Scarlet Pinky Finger. A curse tool of considerable age… I believe in this Kingdom, you call them meteors?”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 3]], [[Sword Demon Love Story: The Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte Part 2|Sword Demon Love Story: The Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte]], Section 11. In future content, however, curse tools were not only differentiated from meteors, but the status of Stride's rings as curse tools was contradicted in Sword Demon Battle Ballad, with them becoming the manifestation of his Authority, the Hubristic Ten Commandments. **Furthermore, in the Comic Alive version of Sword Demon Battle Ballad, in order to harness the power of the curse tools and unrestrainedly cast curses, he was forced to pay compensation in the form of offering a part of his body to them, causing a part of his body to sustain everlasting damage.''“Each ring causes everlasting damage to a part of your body. That is how they work.”'' [[Sword Demon Battle Ballad: Act 7]], Section 3. In his years of owning the ten ring curse tools and casting curses with them, Stride's body was rendered to a near corpse-like state. *Much of Stride's history from his depiction in the Comic Alive version of Sword Demon Battle Ballad was expanded on and altered between [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33|Volume 33]] and the Ex version of the aforementioned story. **According to Vincent Vollachia in Volume 33, Stride was likely a Stargazer, was expelled from the Imperial Family, and erased from Vollachia's historical records. The only trace left of him was a journal found by Vincent in the Crystal Palace's library. Vincent also states the journal contained delusions of the Observers and future information about the [[Great Disaster]], knowledge only privy to Stargazers. **To compensate for the particulars of the Imperial Selection Ceremony in Stride's original backstory in Comic Alive differing from the aspects of it introduced in [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5|The Tale of the Scarlet Princess]], his father, the emperor, was no longer the culprit behind his poisoning, and the identity of the perpetrator was made unknown. His infertility and connection to an unidentified “criminal” with whom he made an oath were cut from the story altogether. Moreover, he voiced that the Observers were averse to a gazer deviating from their commandment,''“…Indeed, you do not find it to your liking when a gazer deviates from their commandment, accursed Observers!”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 5, Section 2. implying that he was not adhering to his own commandment. **Although Stride was a Sin Archbishop in both the Monthly Comic Alive and Ex 6 versions of the story, presenting a Gospel that served as proof of his alignment with the Witch Cult, in the Comic Alive version of events, he called himself “a sham that managed to obtain the Authority and position”,''“Unfortunately though, I am just a sham that managed to obtain the Authority and position.”'' [[Sword Demon Battle Ballad: Act 7]], Section 3. referring to that which comes with being a Sin Archbishop. However, he did not use the Authority he claimed to have, instead opting to use his curse tool rings. *Like the [[Satella|Witch of Envy]], Stride is the only few individuals to possess a Witch Factor who isn't named after a celestial body. *Throughout real-world history, many societies and cultures revered the color purple as something that denoted royalty and refinement. In fact, in some societies, it was forbidden for ordinary citizens to wear the color. The use of the color purple in Stride's design may therefore be used to highlight him as someone of nobility and high standing. ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} {{Witch Cult Navbox}} [[Category:Sin Archbishops]] [[Category:Stride Faction]] [[Category:Imperial Family]] [[Category:Deceased]] [[Category:Nobles]] [[Category:Royalty]] [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Stargazer]] [[Category:Authority Users]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

'''Sergei''' (セルゲイ) was one of the [[Witch Cult]]ists that attacked [[Ram]] and [[Rem]]'s village. After his defeat, he was killed by the sisters.

==Appearance==
Sergei was a young man with a frivolous and innocent appearance.<ref name="calm">''While holding onto Rem, the young man kept laughing with a frivolous and innocent look. It wasn’t like he’d completely changed. He was extremely calm, extremely composed. That was dreadful.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref>

==Personality==
Sergei was almost always shown to be calm and composed.<ref name="calm /> He was also sadistic, believing it to be fun to strangle his victims, whether or not they were children.<ref>''“Now then, what’s left is the fun of choking you out and retrieving you with your sister. I’ll be expecting you to act honorably as a descendant of the prideful Oni clan.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref>

==History==
===[[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village|The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]]===
Around ten years before [[Natsuki Subaru]]'s arrival into the world, [[Faust]], [[Sado]], Sergei, and [[Fogg]] attacked the [[Oni]] Village. Three months later, Sergei ambushed and murdered [[Dudley Miload]] on his way home from [[Costuul]]. Afterward, he left for the Miload Manor to lure away [[Roswaal L. Mathers]] and one of the sisters. After the group arrived, he showed Rem the brutalized corpses on the convoy and tricked her into using her horn, effectively incapacitating her with his mana poisoning. After then unleashing an explosion on the carriage Roswaal was in, he summoned the other nearby cultists, and he tried to strangle Rem. However, Roswaal attacked with magic and retrieved Rem. After sending her off to the Miload Manor to save Ram and Grace, he faced off with the cultists, effectively slaying them all and breaking all of Sergei's limbs. Sergei was presumably killed by the sisters a short while later.

==Abilities==
'''Mana Poisoning''': Sergei was born with a nature that randomly interferes with and poisons the atmospheric mana around him. This makes him the natural enemy of the Onis, and it is the primary reason why they were able to be so easily defeated.<ref>''“…is being interfered with, yes. I was born with this nature. I randomly contaminate the mana around me. If it’s in my surroundings, the mana turns into poison. That’s why it was easy to take control of your village.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref> This trait makes it troublesome for [[magic]] users to use magic, capable of reducing the power of high-powered spells of someone like Roswaal and reducing the freedom to use it in general.<ref>''“The mana around turns into poison. In other words, the space becomes very troubling for magic users. To think that Ul magic can actually repress power to such an extent…”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref><ref>''“…Usually you wouldn’t be able to cast magic freely either and yet you pulled it off. I’ll have to give you props for that. But this place has to feel uncomfortable for you, huh?”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref>

'''Explosion Technique''' (爆裂術式): Sergei was able to use the Explosion Technique; however, he admits that he's terrible at it.

'''Sado''' (サド) was one of the [[Witch Cult]]ists that attacked [[Ram]] and [[Rem]]'s village. He was later killed by [[Ram]].

==Appearance==
Sado was a sluggy, short, and somewhat fat man. Neither his appearance nor his clothes were unique; they appeared so normal that if he slipped into a crowd, it would be easy to lose sight of him.<ref>''He was a sluggy, short, and somewhat fat man. His face and clothes weren’t unique at all; he was so ordinary that if he slipped into a crowd, you’d lose sight of him instantly. Even that was probably part of what the man wanted.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref>

==Personality==
Sado was shown to be extremely careful person who does not work on his own, willing to abandon any plan the moment things look bad for him, even being willing to leave the country he is in,<ref>''Rem understood it. In the short time she confronted that man, she understood his traits and mentality. That man who realized that he was being targeted would never show up before Rem again. It was quite obvious that if he got away now, he would immediately try to flee out of the country.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref> something which has allowed him to stay alive.<ref>''When the man saw how dangerous the wind was, he decided to abandon his whole plan. He gave up on it so quickly, but this decisiveness was also an ability that allowed the man to live up to this point.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 4.</ref> To him, everything that the wind tells him is most important, and he will act according to the way the wind blows.<ref name="wind">''One could say that the wind was the most important factor to the man. To know which direction the wind created by nature was blowing from the hardest, he always had to carefully determine the level of humidity and the temperature. Otherwise, it would significantly affect his goals and actions. Even a large fire that burns everything starts as just a mere spark. A supporting wind is needed to burst it into big, intense flames. And that was his exact role.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 4.</ref> Sado was not very expressive,<ref>''The small man, who had an expressionless look on his face, stood face to face with the small Oni and large cat while they showed him hostility. He wasn’t expressionless because he gave up or because he wasn’t regretful; he was expressionless because emotions did not come out in waves for him.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref> and as he was dying, he did not beg for his life, merely pitying his enemy and offering his name in his final moments.

==History==
===[[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village|The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]]===
Around ten years ago, [[Faust]], Sado, [[Sergei]], and [[Fogg]] attacked the [[Oni]] Village. Three months later, he set upon a scheme to cause mayhem in the [[Royal Capital]] involving the use of magical miasma stones. However, when the wind turned bad for him, he decided to abandon his plan, only to be confronted by Rem and [[Frederica Baumann]]. Deciding to leave other cultists to hold him off, he avoided the girls' attacks and rode the wind to escape. As he was escaping, however, Ram was able to shoot him down with her magic, severing his limbs. As he was bleeding out on the ground, Rem and Frederica found him, and Rem began interrogating him. However, he merely claimed to pity Rem, and he gave her his name before he died.

==Abilities==
'''Wind Reading''': Sado was taught how to read the wind by Faust, something which allows him to determine if good or bad things are coming his way. Because of this, he has an extremely sharp intuition.<ref name="wind" />

'''Wind Riding''': Sado was able to float and ride on the wind at high speeds. However, it is not flight [[magic]], and it is unclear if this ability is related to magic.<ref>''“…Sorry to disappoint, but this isn’t that sort of high-class magic. It’s wind riding that’s just for show.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref><ref>''The man that got away from Rem’s attack jumped and was floating in the air. The man sighed at Frederica, who raised her voice upon seeing that unexpected scene.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref> Due to its nature, he can only move windward and downwind, giving him less freedom to maneuver himself.<ref>''The small man riding the wind, practically swimming in the sky, was going as fast as the wind itself, but he could only move from the windward and the downwind. If he was going in a fixed direction, even if there was distance between them, he wouldn’t escape.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref>

'''Equipment''': Sado kept magical miasma stones on his person to use in a certain scheme. It is unknown if he had any other uses for them.

wikitext:
{{Character |Name = Safis |Kanji = サーフィス |Romaji = Saafisu |Alias = Snake Eyes (蛇目, ''Janome'') |Race = Human |Gender = Male |Hair Color = Dark Green |Affiliation = [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]

Black Silver Coin |Occupation = Aide |Status = Alive |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4|Tanpenshuu Volume 4]]}} '''Safis''' (サーフィス) is [[Doltero Amule|Doltero]]'s aide. ==Appearance== Safis is a slender man with dark green hair and eyes reminiscent of a snake's. ==Personality== Safis is absolutely loyal to Doltero and his organization, the Black Silver Coin. He will do anything to ensure the livelihood and power of his boss, even if it means offering his own life or having the lives of his Doltero's family murdered so as to ensure that he has no weaknesses. ==History== ===[[Royal Selection Life from Zero: The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint Part 1|The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint]]=== Upon learning about the existence of his boss's mistress, [[Kalifa]], and daughter, [[Ilya]], from Doltero himself, Safis took it into his own hands to have them killed out of loyalty to his boss, having the desire to remove his "vulnerabilities". As a result, Kalifa was attacked by an assailant Safis sent and had her larynx destroyed, inhibiting her from ever being able to speak again. She and her daughter both survived, and she entrusted Ilya to the Astrea Manor for protection. Doltero sent one of his men after the two, but he was discovered by [[Felt]] and [[Reinhard van Astrea|Reinhard]] and revealed his affiliation with the Black Silver Coin once the candidate threatened with the Sword Saint. Shortly afterwards, [[Gaston]], [[Rachins Hoffman|Rachins]], and [[Camberley]] located Kalifa and brought her back to the mansion, where they discovered that Doltero was Ilya's father. Deciding to visit Doltero in Flanders, Rom used his connection to Doltero to hold a meeting with him. When Felt, Reinhard, and Rom, alongside Kalifa and Ilya, met with Doltero, he discovered that Safis was responsible for ordering the attack on his mistress and daughter. Safis revealed his intentions, preparing to commit suicide to atone for his misdeeds, only for Doltero to suddenly assault him to keep him alive and demote him to a simple lackey position in the Black Silver Coin unless he could work to regain the Pig King's trust. Understanding Safis's argument, he decided to disown his mistress and his daughter, much to the displeasure of Felt and Rom. Following the incident, Safis was stripped of his executive position in the organization, but was allowed the chance to prove his loyalty and regain Doltero's trust. ===[[The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint, Riot in Flanders 1|Riot in Flanders]]=== Two months later, Doltero had a meeting with [[Toto]] and [[Manfred Madison]], the other heads of the Big Three, and [[Helaine Gatness]], the leader of the [[Flanders]] branch of the Golden Beetle. The meeting concerned a series of murders that had been committed against members of the Big Three organizations, as well as the Golden Beetle, with Helaine proposing that Felt was responsible, having received reports that she contacted Doltero and the Black Silver Coin before. As a result, Manfred and Toto went on to seek courtesy visits from her as a means to verify her intentions, with Doltero sending Safis to inform her of their wishes. Meeting Felt and Reinhard in Hakuchuri, he told them of the circumstances in Flanders and relayed Doltero's message that the Flower Prison Garden and the Balance were awaiting courtesy visits from her. Several days after Felt's courtesy visits, the Big Three started began pursuing [[Ezzo Cadner]], who was framed for burning down a brothel in the red-light district and killing members of the Big Three, including a veteran of the Black Silver Coin and [[Mimosa]], a prostitute from the Flower Prison Garden. Once Felt discovered his location at an abandoned mansion and heard his side of the story and Reinhard defeated a hundred members of the Black Silver Coin who had gathered at the mansion to catch the dwarf while using the name of the Masked Knight Veltol, the candidate and the Sword Saint proceeded to Doltero's mansion. Reinhard defeated another hundred men from Doltero's group, and him and Felt met with the Pig King and Safis. Felt suspected that the Black Silver Coin was responsible for the strife in Flanders, having learned that Kalifa and Ilya were targeted again. Neither Doltero nor Safis claimed responsibility, and nobody else in the organization had realized the truth about their relation to the Pig King. However, Safis mentioned that the veteran of the group who died on the night of the brothel's arson had been present when Kalifa and Ilya visited Doltero with Felt, and had revealed this information to Mimosa, who then relayed it to someone else. Ultimately, the incident's mastermind attempted to pit Felt and her group and the Black Silver Coin against each other, and succeeded in guiding her faction's actions. Despite that, Felt maintained confidence and relied on her comrade's approach to resolve the strife in Flanders. In the end, the true culprits were discovered and the incident was resolved, and the Black Silver Coin continued operation. ==Navigation== {{Lugunica Navbox}} [[Category:Flanders]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

[[Kararagi Reaper Incident 4]] (canon side story)}} '''Reize''' (レーゼ) is a resident of Kararagi who stole the Light Sphere of the Slasher, [[Zarestia]]. Though she has yet to appear in the main story, she first appears in the [[Kararagi Reaper Incident 6|Kararagi Reaper Incident side story]]. ==Appearance== After taking part of the Light Sphere, Reize's appearance would mirror Zarestia's. Reize has milky-white shaggy hair with a magenta strand, white eyebrows, and sharp almond-shaped eyes with a bright yellow color. She wears an immaculate pure black kimono with a magenta sphere and the right side over the left, giving the impression of burial clothes, but with the skirt shortened to the mid-thigh and freely exposing her long, slender legs. In [[Re:IF]], Reize was a young woman who had short, dark brown hair, and light blue eyes. Upon being exposed to alcohol, she was reverted to her true appearance, having dark circles around her eyes and bearing a physique smaller than that of Zarestia's. ==Personality== After taking part of the Light Sphere, Reize gained the desire to murder people akin to how Zarestia had. While her true form and age have not been stated in the main canon, due to her impulsive behavior, it is suggested that she could be on the younger side. She was also intent on killing Anastasia's longtime companion, the artificial spirit Echidna, for unknown reasons, until the former convinced "Black Tia" that she could help her. In Re:IF, she was easily angered by members of the [[Witch Cult]] as they were the ones that destroyed her village. This consequentially made her extremely vengeful and ruthless towards anyone who emits miasma. Moreover, she showed an envy towards someone for living a positive life that she could not have. She also acquired Zarestia's aversion to alcohol. ==History== Reize lived with her mother within a village for outcasts that lay in a remote area near the city of Azamiki. However, the peaceful life she had in her village was brought to an end when it was attacked by [[Capella Emerada Lugunica]]. By some chance, she survived and sought the power to take revenge. Sometime later, Reize received a part of Zarestia's Light Sphere and is currently seeking revenge. ===[[Kararagi Reaper Incident 5|Kararagi Reaper Incident]]=== At some point after taking a part of Zarestia's Light Sphere, she unleashed a black tornado toward [[Banan]], which the [[Anastasia Camp]], [[Halibel]], and Zarestia all fought off. However, the moment they overcame the tornado, Reize kidnapped [[Anastasia Hoshin]] and [[Eridna|Echidna]]. When Anastasia later woke up, she found herself in Zarestia’s Bed, and Echidna had left her side to ensure her safety, as she was the main target behind their enemy’s actions. Anastasia spoke with Reize, who looked effectively identical to Zarestia, and after a one-sided conversation, Anastasia promised to help her, as otherwise, everyone who would come to find Echidna, Reize, and Anastasia herself would find themselves likely killing each other. Not long after, Echidna appeared after realizing Anastasia would be safe, and despite her concerns, Anastasia convinced her that everything would be fine. After this, Anastasia learned Reize's name, history, and goals, chose to help her achieve them, and returned a full day later to Banan, where Reize allowed herself to quietly sit in a cell. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== When using Zarestia's Light Sphere, Reize's power becomes immense, capable of easily destroying towns. However, it is unclear just how much power Reize is capable of or is proficient in utilizing, making the full extent of her capabilities unknown. Similarly, it is unknown whether or not she is capable of combat without the Light Sphere. ===[[Magic]]/[[Magic#Spiritual Arts|Spiritual Arts]]=== Although it is unknown what attribute that Reize has an affinity for, with Zarestia's Light Sphere, Reize can utilize the Slasher's immensely powerful wind magic. However, it is unclear if she is capable of using ordinary magic or if the Light Sphere enables Reize to naturally use spiritual arts. ===Physical Traits=== '''Miasma Attuned Olfaction''': On the night her village was destroyed, Reize was approached by a mysterious figure, who poured "something" into her ear. Following that incident, Reize was able to smell the miasma. With this ability, Reize can easily locate people who are emitting a strong miasma, similarly to how Rem can smell Subaru's miasma after the latter Returns by Death. It is revealed by [[Echidna]] in [[Re:IF Kasaneru]] that this is a natural ability of the Oni tribe as well as their purpose for existing. '''However, as her race in the main canon is unknown and it is unclear if Capella has done anything to her, it is unknown whether Reize retains this ability.''' ===Equipment=== *'''Light Sphere''' (光珠, ''Mi Tama''): Reize received a part of Zarestia's power from the Light Sphere, a gem that serves as Zarestia's anchor, the source and store of her power. For unknown reasons, after acquiring it, she assumed Zarestia's appearance. This effect could be reverted, however. ==Trivia== *Before her debut in the Kararagi Reaper Incident side story, Reize first debuted in the Kararagi IF side story. *The reason why Zarestia mistook Rem for the culprit of the Light Sphere's theft in Re:IF was due to her similar smell to Reize, who was also an oni. As Zarestia has mistaken Ricardo and Halibel for the culprit behind the Light Sphere's theft, it is possible that, rather than being an oni like she was in Re:IF, Reize is a wolf person or a werewolf in the main canon. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Kararagi Navbox}} [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[Category:Unknown Race]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

[[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33|Volume 33]] (main story) (mentioned)}} '''Shasuke''' (シャスケ) was a [[shinobi]] and one of the two “Generals” under the command of [[Stride Vollachia]], a role shared with his older twin brother [[Raizo]]. He served as a secondary antagonist of [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6|Sword Demon Battle Ballad]]. Shasuke was ultimately cut in two by [[Carol Remendis]]. ==Appearance== Shasuke was a man with white hair parted to the left, blue eyes, and a single right eyebrow. He was described to always wear a black cloak that covered his entire body. He also wore a mask on his face, and a hachigane on his forehead. When he took off his cloak, his body was described to be quite pale, with an eerie blue mottled pattern covering his torso. ==Personality== Shasuke had quite a humble personality, serving his master without complaint. He did not feel any emotions until the very end due to the Shinobi training process stripping them from him. Just before his death, he was described to have finally been happy, and was finally able to laugh louder than he ever had in his life. ==History== Raizo and Shasuke were born in [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]]'s shinobi village. The two of them were twins who were subject to the training process of a shinobi. The process was cruel, and involved body modifications using drugs, curse marks, all kinds of magic, and heavy training. It was mentioned that only one in a million could survive this process. Both he and Raizo survived and reborn as shinobi. However, despite their promise, the two of them were deemed as imperfect by the shinobi for being twins. As a result, they killed the grown-ups who had deprived them of everything, the comrades who followed them, and became runaway shinobi. Before they fully escaped, they had a run-in with the most formidable and deadly shinobi of all, [[Olbart Dunkelkenn]], who decided to let them live on a whim. Eventually, the twin shinobi encountered and devoted their services to Stride, accepting his offer to use and dispose of them in the most extravagant way possible. ==Abilities== '''Shinobi Techniques''' (シノビの術技, ''Shinobi no Jutsugi''): Shasuke was apt in the use of kunai, and in fighting using martial arts. In addition to that, it can be expected he had multiple skills that were unnamed; some examples include one which allowed Shasuke to attempt to transform his body into steel, before it was interrupted by [[Carol Remendis|Carol]]. *'''Shadow Form''': Shasuke could sink into a person's shadows, and become part of it. He could use this ability to carry people into them and transport them to his brother, or to hide. Furthermore, he could use this ability to appear in another person's shadow. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Stride Faction]] [[Category:Deceased]] [[Category:Shinobi]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

Following the unexpected death of his mother, Karl was possessed by the original Roswaal, and inherited the Roswaal estate, along with its assets. At some point, Karl began researching numerous things regarding magic. He’d come up with a theory to imbue objects with Yang Magic, and he created numerous magic dolls which he used to guard his home. [[Capella Emerada Lugunica|Mother]] |Previous Affiliation = Slave Trading Company |Previous Occupation = Slave |Status = Unknown |Weapon = |Equipment = Void Garb |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 5|Tanpenshuu Volume 5]] |Manga = |Anime = |Japanese Voice = |English Voice =}} '''Reisel''' (ライゼル) was one of [[Ricardo Welkin]]’s colleagues back when he was a slave. ==Appearance== Reisel is a brown Tanuki-human who wears traditional Japanese-style clothing. ==History== Reisel was originally a slave who was forced to work in the mines doing hard labor. He met Ricardo there, forming a friendship with him. Reisel organized numerous slave rebellions, and in one of them, he and some others escaped, though Ricardo was not invited to it.  Five years after that, in [[Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye Part 1|Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye]], Reisel entered a bar and met with Ricardo. He requested Ricardo to do him a favor by stealing from a cargo full of goods. Ricardo asked what his aim was, and Reisel replied that he intended to steal a Meteor from it.  On a mountainside outside of [[Banan]], both Ricardo and Reisel tried to ambush the cargo, [[Shiroro Tonerico|Shiroro]] emerged from the cart and attempted to cut off Ricardo's head. Whilst that happened, Reisel stole the cart, leaving Ricardo behind as he battled against Shiroro. However, the cargo had been switched with empty boxes, thus Reisel wasn't able to recover the [[meteor]] he was looking for. In rage, he used his own meteor that [[Capella Emerada Lugunica|Mother]] had given him to create shadows to locate the real shipment and kill those who stole them. His plan was thwarted by the combined efforts of [[Anastasia Hoshin]], [[Eridna|Echidna]], and Ricardo. As a result of his defeat, Reisel destroyed the meteor that was given to him by Mother. She came to the scene, where the weak and sprawling Reisel was in front of her. He begged that he wanted a second chance, but she did not tolerate his failure. She touched his forehead, causing Reisel to lose all of his limbs, his eyes, nose, mouth, ears, and transformed him into something inhuman. ==Abilities== ===Equipment=== *'''Void Garb''' (虚影装 ''Kyokagesou''): A meteor that was loaned to Reisel by Mother. It allows the user to create shadowy humanoid figures using their hair that can be controlled. The user shares in the shadows' senses, including in their sense of sight and pain. The Void Garb was destroyed by Reisel to prevent his death from the recoil of the destruction of its shadows. ==Navigation== {{Kararagi Navbox}} {{Beloved Children Navbox}} [[Category:Slaves]] [[Category:Unknown Status]] [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

She, alongside [[Lilac]], later joined the [[Omega Party]]. ==Appearance== Shion has orange eyes with blue pupils, and as an elf, she also has pointed ears. She has long green hair with a ponytail on her right side. Her attire consists of a short white cloak with a green diamond-shaped pattern in the inside, a white and brown dress that is like a huntress wears, and white high-end boots. She also adorns an orange rose on her left shoulder, a dagger wrapped around on her hips, and a small gold locket around her neck. Since Shion shares the same physical vessel as Lilac, whenever her personality manifests in their vessel, its appearance instantly shifts to match hers. ==Personality== Shion is a rather friendly person who is easy to talk to, and she does not like dragging others into her messes if she can help it, even going as far as to ask a [[Palmyra|stranger]] to help her speak to her other half, Lilac. Due to being a Dream Arts User, however, her sense of self is somewhat fuzzy, and because she is so synchronized with others, she can find herself becoming influenced by other people's memories, including taking on their speech quirks. It is because of this that she can often be heard speaking with numerous loan words, having picked them up from passing memories of a person who uses them. She is somewhat driven by her goal to find the person who uses these words, even being willing to follow [[Omega]] as part of her party for the chance to learn of the person who uses them. ==History== At an unknown point in time and for unknown reasons, two separate souls, Shion and Lilac, came to possess the same vessel. When the two souls first confronted each other, they were in conflict and fought for control over their shared body. However, one day, that changed, and they now share their body peacefully, speculating that, having entered another person’s dream, they were deeply affected. As time passed, they came across the dream of a man who spoke with English loan words, and ever since, they have been searching for the person whose dream they entered in order to fill the void that lingered in their hearts. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland Part 1|Omega in Wonderland]]=== At some point, she and Lilac appeared in [[Gusteko]]. However, they were deemed heretics by the [[Gustekan Church]], causing them to send a [[Mikli Yulitô|Temple Knight]] after them. At some point after entering the town of Sylphoa, they confronted Mikli, and Lilac, having had no time to aim, used her Dream Arts to put her, and accidentally, the entire town, to sleep. Unable to contact Lilac after this, Shion remained in Sylphoa, where eventually, [[Zank Metley|another Temple Knight]] and his cohorts arrived. However, shortly after arriving, she felt her connections to them start to vanish, despite attempting to bring them into the dream world. Sometime later, after having witnessed a [[Colette|beast]] escaping with two girls, Shion spoke with one of them, Palmyra, and while introducing herself, she asked for Palmyra's assistance. After explaining the situation to her, she used her hypnosis magic to put Palmyra to sleep, giving her a message to pass along to Lilac. Shortly after, she came face to face with [[Noelle Tuérico]], who was making hostile remarks and threatening violence toward her if she didn't undo her spell, not listening to anything Shion would say. Just before Noelle flew into violence, however, she warned Noelle that the person she was working with, the other Temple Knight, killed his allies and might do the same to her. This led to a fight immediately afterward between said Temple Knight and Noelle and the beastified Colette. However, this did not last, as Palmyra awoke and told the man that his fiancée Mikli, the other Temple Knight, was still alive. Following this, after Omega spoke to the man and had him leave with Mikli and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party. ===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Witch Trials Part 1|Witch Trials]]=== One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a [[Witchbeast#Snow Blight|Snow Blight]]. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of [[Nananna Pezza]] and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches. Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named [[Minor Characters#Piditz|Piditz]] who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find [[Mireille Hetia]] using her [[Magic#Spiritual Arts|spiritual arts]] to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody. At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started. Likewise, Omega explained this to Palmyra, as she learned it while imprisoned. As for Noelle, she joined Nananna, who had been speaking with Edmon about finding Piditz. Shion used her dream arts to peer into the minds of the townsfolk, and she warns Lilac that the "Witch" is just a conspiracy by the council to get rid of political enemies. After learning of this, Lilac informs the Colette and Palmyra, and the elves suggest sowing division in the people to uproot the conspiracy. Though wanting to talk to Noelle, she does not come back that night, and Lilac and Shion decide to use their dream arts to nudge the townsfolk to attend the upcoming. The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, [[Edmon Quayle]] counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise. Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an [[Minor Characters#Elderly Healer|elderly healer]], and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch. Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it. ==Abilities== '''[[Magic]]''' (魔法, ''Mahō''): Shion is skilled at using dream arts. *'''Dream Arts''': A type of forbidden art that is all but lost from the world in the present that allows its user to meddle with the mind.''"Magic that uses dreams as intermediary to meddle with the opponent’s mind, in fact. On top of that, it is a kind of forbidden art, and its users were almost entirely eradicated, I suppose."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 4, Section 1. It is trained by using people as test subjects. After the person falls asleep, the practitioner must learn to sense and attune themselves to the person's Od before they die. Her proficiency with Dream Arts is considered impressive by Omega, who herself can use Dream Arts, and even surpasses her, being able to put an entire town to sleep for long periods of time and create a dream space larger than the [[Castle of Dreams]]. According to Omega, due to her talent, lifespan, and dedication to the art, she has the potential to be called a [[Witch]]. **'''Hypnosis Magic''': A form of magic that temporarily stops mana from flowing into the target's Od, severing their consciousness from reality. Hypnosis Magic is considered the specialty of Dream Arts Users. **'''Thought Implantation''': Using Dream Arts, it is possible to place a thought into another person's head and leave them to act on it, such as making a person think of the user as an ally and making them stop any pursuers chasing after them. **'''Memory Scouring''': As a Dream Arts user, Shion is attuned to other people and is influenced by their memories. Likewise, if she chooses to, she can look into another person's memories to extract specific information. However, their target may show resistance, preventing her from reaching the memory she is looking for. '''Equipment''': Shion carries a dagger around on her hip. However proficient she is with it is unknown. ==Trivia== *Both Shion and Lilac initially debuted in the non-canon video game [[Re:Zero Lost in Memories]]. However, they were later written to be canon characters in [[The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland Part 1|The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland]]. **In Lost in Memories, [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]] found Shion in the Remembrance Village, a world created from his memory. She was the navigator who helped him recover his lost memories. In addition, the name Shion was given to her by Subaru; she was previously nameless. *Shion and Lilac have a shared birthday on September 9, which is the anniversary of the Lost in Memories game's release. *Like Lilac, whose name shares a similar origin, Shion's name comes from a flower called [[Wikipedia:Aster tataricus|Aster Tataricus]], also known as Shion (紫苑). The flower has a meaning in Hanakotoba, the Japanese language of flowers, which corresponds to "I won't forget you." It is reference to the theme of Lost in Memories and was a name that was given to Shion by Subaru within the game itself. ==References== [[Category:Omega Party]] [[Category:Demi-Human]]

Kai Jordan (Wolf)}} '''Salum Pristis''' (サルム・プリスティス) is [[Melty Pristis]]'s older brother. As his alternative personality, '''Wolf''' (ウォルフ), he was an assassin who attempted to dispatch the five Royal Selection Candidates other than Melty. After Wolf and [[Pooka]]'s defeat, Salum, Wolf, and Pooka joined Melty and [[Tiga Rauleon|Tiga]] in fleeing from the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]], intending to pay a visit to Tiga's old group of travelling entertainers. ==Appearance== Salum wears a Middle Eastern-inspired uniform with a black, short shirt, gold eyes-like belts around his chest waist, a blue bandana on his head, and bandages on his hands, covering the Evil Eyes engraved on his hands. As Wolf, he dons a yellow uniform with a black overcoat that touches the ground, black gloves and boots, and switches between several masks with different expressions. However, as opposed to the two sharing the same vessel but having different appearances, Wolf's body is the same as Salum's, and thus without the uniform that obscures his appearance, the two appear identical, with only their voices changing. Initially, Salum puts a black robe over himself as a ritual of sorts to give control of his body to Wolf, but after the two of them came to terms with one another, they could switch between each other at will without the use of the robe. ==Personality== Serious and humorless, Salum is a man of few words. He is a vagabond on a journey, traveling around the world with his [[spirit]] partner Pooka. He is an unsophisticated yet kind-hearted person who steps forward and takes on danger in place of others. Although Pooka describes him as a man of common sense, he has trouble communicating with other people. He has a soft spot for younger people and always carries sweets with him to distribute to younger children. Because of his intimidating appearance and quiet nature, people sometimes react with suspicion. As opposed to Salum, Wolf is significantly more talkative, has a haughty temperament, and enjoys toying with his opponents. His mercilessness towards targets and his capacity to be cold-hearted in order to fulfill a task distinguish him from Salum. Wolf frequently admonishes his other half for his weakness, and is far more powerful than Salum when he is in control. While he still covered his body with a black robe, he showed off his emotions by wearing one of his eight masks to express himself. Due to his purpose to act in Salum's place, he convinced himself that he had to play the role of a villainous evildoer, hurting himself in the process. Unlike Salum, he lacked a bond with and did not care for Pooka, though in spite of this, he panicked as she approached death and refused to let her die. After Wolf's defeat, he was recognized by Melty and Salum as their other sibling, and changed his ways, calling himself Pooka's friend and declaring that he would spoil his little sister. ==History== Salum hailed from Faradar, the village of the Evil Eye Tribe, which was home to him and his younger sister, Melty. When it came time for Melty to undergo an exam to determine her power's strength, she was found to have the Evil Eye of Bewitchment and unintentionally caused the people at the exam to fight each other until they collapsed. Although nobody died, as a result of this, she was separated from the rest of the village, and Salum was told to never visit her. However, he frequently slipped by the tribe's adults to meet with her, bringing her information about her Evil Eye, such as that someone else from hundreds of years ago had possessed the same power as her, for her sake. Salum also happened to meet Melty shortly after her first encounter with Tiga. While initially wary of Tiga's presence, he accepted the young boy's assertion that he was Melty's friend and would never leave her side. Following an attack on Faradar, Salum was separated from his sister. Desperate to reunite with her, Salum joined with Mother's faction, working to ensure his sister's safety. Around this time, he met and formed a contract with Pooka, who was tasked by Mother to keep an eye on him. However, Salum could not fully embrace the power of his Evil Eye, which made him fail at even the simplest of jobs. As a result of his weakness and his inability to fulfill his role, the personality of Wolf was born. Wolf made a deal with Salum to perform the dirty work in his place. Salum accepted this and deferred control of his body to Wolf in order to accomplish the work he was tasked with. ==Abilities== [[File:Salum Evil Eye Design.png|thumb|150px|Salum Evil Eye Design.png|Salum's Evil Eye]] '''Evil Eye''' (魔眼, ''Magan''): Salum has the '''Evil Eye of Avarice''' (貪欲の魔眼, ''Donyoku no Magan'') on both of his hands. It allows him to drain mana from an individual or the area around him. So long as the world continues to exist, the supply of mana he can absorb from his surroundings is limitless. If he steals too much mana from someone, he can kill the individual. He can also drain mana from [[magic]], rendering it virtually ineffective. According to Wolf, Salum is unable to embrace the power his Evil Eyes have. '''Spirit User''' (精霊使い, ''Seirei Tsukai''): Salum is currently contracted with Pooka. '''[[Magic#Spiritual Arts|Spiritual Arts]]''' (精霊術): Salum is capable of using his spiritual arts with Pooka and his other spirits. '''Equipment''': Salum wields a shamshir with jagged blades close to the hilt. ==Trivia== *The way Wolf changes his masks is based off of [[wikipedia:Bian_lian|Bian Lian]], meaning the Art of Mask Changing, which is a subculture of Chinese Sichuan Opera. ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} {{Non-Canon Navbox}} {{Beloved Children Navbox}} [[Category:Bodyguards]] [[Category:Assassins]] [[Category:Demi-Human]]
