He has orange cat ears along with a tail and wears a white robe. Unlike his siblings, he wears a monocle on his left eye, making him give off an intellectual and calculating aura. ==Personality== Tivey tends to let [[Mimi Pearlbaton|Mimi]] and [[Hetaro Pearlbaton|Hetaro]] do whatever they want unless it involves him and acts like a straight man to his siblings' actions. Contrary to their love of the outdoors, he prefers to stay indoors and gain knowledge, such as reading books in the corner, though even then he is bothered by Mimi. He is in charge of the Iron Fang's clerical duties, which he excels at to the point where it's said that the mercenary group wouldn't function correctly without him. Because of this, he sometimes helps Anastasia with her business, however he refuses her offers to have him permanently move to her company. ==History== ===Early Life=== Sometime in the past, Mimi, Hetaro, and Tivey were abandoned by their parents. When they were two, Tivey was about to be kidnapped. Mimi attempted to fight off the kidnappers, but she was stabbed four times in the process, and Hetaro was also injured.As Mimi recalls, Tivey was about to get caught by the kidnappers and Mimi somehow stopped it but got stabbed in the belly by Mimi’s opponent. Mimi got stabbed four times, and Mimi was still two years old, so Mimi was only at the beginning stage of being the strenghtiest, so even Mimi was in a near death situation. [[Mimi Pearlbaton's Chomp of Love and Passion]], Section 2. As they were running away, they ran into [[Roshi Pearlbaton]], who healed them,''While they were running for their lives while Hetaro was dealing with a stomach wound as bad as Mimi’s, an old man suddenly appeared in front of Mimi when her wound started to feel better.'' [[Mimi Pearlbaton's Chomp of Love and Passion]], Section 2. and after taking them in, he taught them how to survive.''Roshi, who had picked up Mimi and her siblings, laughed with his dirty clothes and his ugly face with a chipped tooth. After that, the three cat’s and Roshi’s life began somehow. The three of them didn’t know anything, as they were just kittens. The three kitten siblings were taught the means to survive by Roshi, who was very knowledgeable. The energetic Mimi was taught how to fight. The kind Hetaro was taught how to live cautiously. And the wise Tivey was taught knowledge regarding various things. Roshi had always said that it would help the three of them in the future.'' [[Mimi Pearlbaton's Chomp of Love and Passion]], Section 2. ===[[Kararagi Girl Meets Cats Part 1|Kararagi Girl Meets Cats]] and [[Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye Part 1|Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye]]=== As he tried to find help, he met with [[Ricardo Welkin|Ricardo]] with a plan to rescue Anastasia and the siblings. After the defeat of [[Reisel]], Anastasia vowed that if anything happened to Roshi, she would take the Pearlbatons under her care. Eventually, Roshi made a kamikaze attack while on a mission, blowing up with an enemy in the process. Ever since, the siblings have lived with the Iron Fang under Anastasia and Ricardo's care. ===[[Joshua Juukulius's Careful Encyclopedia]]=== As Mimi, Hetaro, and Tivey had entered his room the moment they realized that there was food, [[Joshua Juukulius]], who was honored to have finally been chosen to do something for Anastasia, was concerned that he had to act as a messenger to invite [[Emilia]] to [[Priestella]], nervous and somewhat fearful of her due to her race and the rumors of her appearance being a match for the [[Satella|Witch of Envy]]. However, Mimi declared that Emilia wasn't scary, and recalling that Hetaro and Tivey had interacted with the [[Emilia Camp]] for the [[Subjugation of the White Whale]] and the [[Subjugation of Sloth]], he asked for their opinions. While Tivey claimed that Emilia didn't seem to be scary, Hetaro declared that he only ever talked with her knight, [[Natsuki Subaru]], someone else that Joshua had heard rumors and was wary of, as his origins were unknown and he had no known power. He also recalled the other worrisome rumors about the camp, which only increased his worries, and then, he went ask Anastasia about her intentions directly. ===[[Kararagi Reaper Incident 2|Kararagi Reaper Incident]]=== Sometime after the [[Battle for Priestella]], the Pearlbatons returned to [[Banan]] in [[Kararagi]]. However, at some point after the events of the [[Great Disaster]], the Slasher, [[Zarestia]] set a windstorm on the town, destroying half of it and raising everyone in town sans Ricardo into the sky - an event that would be remembered as the Shinigami Disaster. Believing Ricardo to have stolen her Light Sphere, the two confronted each other, worrying the Pearlbatons. However, after withstanding all of her attacks, she stopped attacking him, made the windstorm dissipate, and lowered everyone to the ground. Later, everyone went to counter a black tornado that had started to assail Banan, and though they managed to quell it, Anastasia and [[Eridna|Echidna]] had gone missing. ==Abilities== ===[[Divine Protection]]=== '''[[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of Trisection|Divine Protection of Trisection]]''' (三分の加護 ''Sanbun no Kago''): This Divine Protection enables Tivey and his siblings to bear each other's physical and emotional burdens and can also be used to split damage between them such as to block death blows. However, as Mimi is the strongest out of the three, her brothers are often stuck with bearing her burdens. In addition, they can launch a destructive interference wave using the Divine Protection and the other siblings, though Mimi is limited to five times and Hetaro and Tivey are limited to two times, so the maximum usage per day is four times. ===[[Magic]]=== Tivey has the capacity to use fire magic. ===Other=== [[File:Tivey & Mimi - Resonance Wave.gif.gif|thumb|250px|Tivey uses the '''Roaring Wave''' against a finger of [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti|Petelgeuse]].]] '''Roaring Wave''' (咆哮波, ''Hōkōha''): The triplets unleash burst of a violent destructive [[mana]] from their mouths together. Only two of the three of them can do it at a time. This ability was learned from Ricardo as he is the originator of that ability. {{Clear}} ==Trivia== *Because Mimi is full of energy, the author decided to make her, Tivey, and Hetaro's birthday fall on Children's Day in Japan. *Tivey is the smartest of the three siblings. ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Royal Selection Navbox}} {{Kararagi Navbox}} [[Category:Banan]] [[Category:Anastasia Camp]] [[Category:Iron Fang]] [[Category:Mercenaries]] [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Treasurers]] [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[Category:Beast Human]] [[Category:Divine Protection Holders]] [[de:Tivey Pearlbaton]] [[es:Tivey Pearlbaton]] [[fr:Tivey Pearlbaton]] [[pl:Tivey Pearlbaton]] [[pt-br:Tivey Pearlbaton]] [[ru:Тиви Перлбатон]] [[zh:角色:缇碧]]

title: Witch Cult
wikitext:
{{Parent Tab |tab1 = Information |tab2 = Image Gallery}}
[[File:Witch Cult Symbol Episode 59.png|300px|right]]
The '''Witch Cult''' (魔女教, ''Majo Kyō'') is an organization that allegedly worships the [[Satella|Witch of Envy]]. It was co-founded by [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti]], alongside either one or multiple unknown individuals.

==Information==
===Overview===
[[File:20200812_095808.jpg|thumb|right]]
The Witch Cult is a secret organization active throughout the [[world]], shrouded in utmost secrecy and ambiguity. It has existed for well over 400 years, originating from the times when the [[Witch]]es were freely roaming around the world. The cult is made up of '''Witch Cultists''' (魔女教徒, ''Majo Kyōto'') at the bottom and a group of members at the top known as '''Sin Archbishops''' (大罪司教, ''Taizai Shikyō''). The Sin Archbishops each govern over one of the Seven Deadly Sins other than Envy, just like how, centuries and centuries ago, individuals known as [[Witch#Witches of Sin|Witches of Sin]] were said to represent the Seven Deadly Sins, and they are selected based on whether they are compatible with Witch Factors. Currently, the representatives for Pride, Sloth, and Greed are vacant. Also, each member of the Witch Cult owns a book known as the '''Gospel''' (福音, ''Fukuin''), which shows them a route to a future they desire through vague details. These books can only be read by the holder and appear to be incomprehensible to others, though it should be mentioned that, in the web novel, Subaru was able to read Petelgeuse's Gospel after his first meeting with the [[Echidna|Witch of Greed]] (the scene was ultimately omitted from the Light Novels, rendering it non-canon). Despite their recent appearances in the [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica]], the Witch Cult is active throughout the world, with members spread out across various countries. According to Petelgeuse, during the events of Arc 3, Wrath was situated in another country, hence she was unable to support him. Their numbers are unknown; however, according to the author, the Witch Cultists that served under Petelgeuse did not even make up ten percent of their numbers, implying that the cult's numbers are quite large. The symbol of the Witch Cult is what appears to be a large red eye, which can be seen both on their flags and on the triangular hoods of the black clerical robes worn by the cult's members,<ref>''The flag had some kind of strange symbol traced on it using red dye. The eye pattern pricked at an unpleasant part of Subaru’s memories.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 17]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref><ref>''“That is the symbol of the Witch Cult.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 17]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> and their coat of arms appears to be crossed twin gold swords surrounded by a gold circle, which can be seen worn around the cultists' necks. The Witch Cult follows that which is written within the Gospels that are given to its members upon joining the cult.

Uniquely, the Witch Cult's Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, [[Lye Batenkaitos]], was capable of commanding the [[White Whale]]. Thanks to this, they were able to have use the whale's reputation and threatening presence to act as a sort of roadblock in order to prevent anyone from interfering with the cult's activities. It was at one point speculated that the whale was somehow involved with the cult due to disasters taking place around the times when the whale was sighted, but it was not confirmed to be so until the [[Subjugation of the White Whale]] helped to expose the cult's activities.

The ultimate goal of the Witch Cult is unknown, and according to the observations of [[Sphinx]], during the time in which they began erasing the history of the Witches of Sin, they seemingly started to stray from their original objective. However, according to the Witch of Vainglory, [[Pandora]], the seal within [[Elior Forest]] is connected to it. It is for this reason that she led an attack on the elves prior to the [[Permafrost of Elior Forest]].

===Regular Cultists===
[[File:Witch Cult Members 2.png|thumb|left|250px]]
Witch Cultists tend to live normal lives, but when the writ of their Gospels provides them with new instructions, they will disappear to complete them. Because their Gospels provide them with their instructions seemingly at random, the cult also seems to operate at random. While taking on a new mission, they rarely speak and show just the bare minimum of movements, effectively giving off a sense of distortion and abnormality, almost like a group of walking dolls. To those they attack, they seemingly appear out of thin air and cause damage of catastrophic proportions. Once they complete their objective, they will return to their normal life like nothing ever happened, making it difficult for anyone to learn of the cult's members' identities. They leave nothing behind, whether they are the assailants or the victims, making it impossible to locate them.<ref>''“Whether they are the assailants or the victims, that’s how it is. They won’t leave anything behind at the devastated scene. Soooo, it’s the same deal with you guys’ village.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref><ref>''When the Witch Cult decides on their target, the place, people, and soil are extirpated. Even if the Witch Cult is repelled, the driven off Witch Cultists wouldn’t leave behind anything and they’d hold their tongues. Therefore, even though the Witch Cult was detested everywhere, for hundreds of years they acted as they pleased.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref>

[[File:Witch Cult Members.png|thumb|right|250px]]
When the Cultists launch attacks, they do so in smaller groups, resorting to ambushes rather than outright announcing their attacks, which allows them to quickly dispatch several times larger and more skilled groups than theirs with relative ease and minimum casualties. Additionally, there were some cases when regular members of the cult made their appearances as normal citizens or merchants, such as what was observed in the case of [[Ketty Muttart]]. With that being said, normal members of the Witch Cult are expendable, and even if one person dies, it will have no affect at all on fellow cultists, who will continue to attack their enemies to the very last man.<ref>''The Witch Cultists appearing one after another as if swarming from the shadows─ None of them were as strong as the two of them, but it seemed like they weren’t even disturbed by their comrades' deaths, and it was the most insane thing to the two people facing each other.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref> They often employ suicidal tactics, lunging themselves toward an enemy so they can manage to avoid the incoming attacks and land a single killing blow. Furthermore, in the face of captivity, regular cultists will commit suicide without fail by using magic stones embedded in their bodies to trigger poisons in order to keep information about the cult from leaking out. Petelgeuse's fingers are an exception, as they have an explosion ritual embedded in their bodies instead that only activates when they kill themselves to take out all nearby enemies with them when Petelgeuse needs to swap to a different body. 

As opposed to their leaders, the Sin Archbishops, regular members also don't appear to be as mentally damaged and unstable, in some cases even showing some prejudice and fear when being subjected to tantrums and outbursts of anger from the likes of Sloth and Greed. This being said, the Cultists following Sloth were shown to obey every and all commands given to them by the madman and, at times, they even mimicked his behavior, as could be seen when the entire group started banging their hands on solid stone, shattering their bones, just like Petelgeuse did in one of [[Natsuki Subaru]]'s failed loops of [[Arc 3]]. While it is unknown if designated groups are working under each of the Sin Archbishops (apart from Sloth), they do acknowledge them with the highest level of respect and are very often employed by them, most often by Petelgeuse and [[Capella Emerada Lugunica|Capella]], expressing a willingness to even be used as sacrificial pawns. [[Faust]] asserts that the Witch Cult's deviousness is comfortable to evildoers and that they are desperate to “enlighten” people and convert those with no interest in them into “believers”.<ref>''“Even the Witch Cult is desperate to enlighten people. Lately, there’s been no hesitation to convert those with no interest at all in their ideas into believers. Their deviousness is comfortable to evildoers.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 5, Section 6.</ref>

===Petelgeuse's Fingers===
As mentioned above, Petelgeuse was the only known Sin Archbishop who organized and led a larger force, totaling up to a couple hundred members. To keep their element of surprise, the Cultists were split into ten groups, each harboring about twelve members with '''finger''' or ringleader being put in charge of the group. These so-called fingers were physically stronger than normal Witch Cult members, being capable of taking on [[Rem]] single-handedly and fighting on pretty much equal grounds. The fingers' main purpose, however, was to serve as spare bodies for Sloth, in case his main body was slain. Accordingly, all 10 fingers had to be [[Magic#Spiritual Arts|spiritual arts]] users and were given a small part of the Witch Factor of Sloth through a complex ritual that allowed Petelgeuse to continue using his Authority of Sloth when in their bodies. After the events of Arc 3, all surviving fingers were either killed or captured during the [[Subjugation of Sloth]], or they were slaughtered and "opened up" by [[Sirius Romanée-Conti|Sirius]], who was searching for Petelgeuse's spirit, effectively marking the end of Petelgeuse's faction.

===Factions===
As recent as one century ago, the Witch Cult was divided between the moderate and radical factions, each led respectively by Petelgeuse and [[Regulus Corneas]]. The exact reason for the divide is unknown, but it seemed that the two sides did not often interfere with the other, often taking on their own objectives. However, this came to an end after the two sides officially clashed in Elior Forest. Although it is unknown just what happened to the rest of the moderate faction, after Petelgeuse started acting without abandon like the radical faction, the Witch Cult's activity and violence skyrocketed.

===External Factions===
Aside from ordinary Witch Cultists, the Sin Archbishops are known to create their own groups and factions that serve them. Although they are technically separate from the Witch Cult, they still are forced to serve the Sin Archbishops for their own purposes, some of which might align with the Witch Cult without their being aware. One such group is composed of the brides of Regulus, which is made up of women who unknowingly act as vessels for Regulus's heart while his Authority is active. There are times when Witch Cultists are taken as one of his brides as well.<ref>''"Some are cultists, some aren’t, there’s all types."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref> Another such faction is the [[Beloved Children]], who are forced to obey the commands of Capella Emerada Lugunica as her "children" mostly out of fear. The last known group known to play a similar role are the hundreds of people who were previously "overeaten" by [[Leilani Alnair]]'s Authority. Because they were effectively brainwashed, they would willingly follow her every command, even if it meant their deaths.

===Taboos===
Although it is unknown why, the Witch Cult does not tolerate the existence of the other Witches. It is unknown if it was always like this, but as recent as between 250-150 years ago, the Witch Cult began erasing any and all history related to the other Witches of Sin.<ref name="erase">''So, in order to learn about the Witch of Greed who had already been dead for a long time, she set out on a journey to follow the legends and books in various places, but there was an organization known as the Witch Cult that was attempting to erase the Witches from history―― that did not seem to be the original objective of its founding, but their activities served as hindrances, so results were very slow to come by. [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 7.</ref> Ever since, the Witch Cult has been ruthless towards anyone who even so much as mentions Witches other than the Witch of Envy, going as far as to destroy entire cities in response. Likewise, if there something connected to a Witch happens to be found anywhere in the world, the Witch Cult will come to rob it.<ref>''"On top of that, I’ve also heard from Otto before. No matter what part of the world, if there’s something that’s happened to be found with a connection to the Witch, then the Witch Cult would come to rob it… that sorta thing."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref>

==History==
The Witch Cult has existed for over 400 years since the times when the Witches were alive and active. According to Regulus Corneas, Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti was one of its founders.<ref>''“You might have been one of the founders of the Witch Cult, and you may have your seat because of a few past services you contributed, but if the question of who deserves it more was to come up now, that seat would be mine!”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 14]], Chapter 3, Section 1.</ref> According to the author, Geuse and the others created the Witch Cult to aid a persecuted Witch, engaging in good activities. 

At some point in time, the Witch Cult was effectively subsumed into the [[Saintess Sect]], and due to their preexisting name not being very well known, the Sect switched to operating under the Cult's name, leading to the modern Witch Cult. In its current state, the Witch Cult is shrouded in secrecy and mystery, thus little is known of the organizational structure and other specifics, like their doctrine beyond rumors, as a result. They are evil enough that knights are ordered to annihilate them immediately should they appear. The followers are elusive. Their means of hiding are unknown, allowing them to survive until the present day. Their purpose is rumored to be the resurrection of the Witch of Envy. However, some Sin Archbishops have disputed that notion.

According to Sphinx's observations, between 250 to 150 years ago, the Witch Cult was seemingly straying away from the original objective of its founding through erasing the old Witches of Sin from history, making it difficult to acquire information on them.<ref name="erase" />

The moderate faction often visited Elior Forest and had many interactions with the Elves that lived there. However, just 100 years ago, the moderate and radical factions engaged in all-out combat during the latter's attack on the Elior Forest. Although this battle ultimately resulted in the forest being completely frozen, Petelgeuse became the official Sin Archbishop of Sloth after taking in the Witch Factor of Sloth and being brainwashed by the Cult's associate, Pandora.

Around forty years ago, [[Stride Vollachia]], the Sin Archbishop of Pride at the time and an apparent [[Stargazer]], led several campaigns in the Kingdom of Lugunica. During his final campaign on the city of [[Picoutatte]], he met his end after being torn apart in the jaws of the [[Dragon]] that he summoned, [[Valgren]]. The incident became widely known as the [[Subjugation of the Blight Dragon]].

As of at least thirty years ago, Capella Emerada Lugunica formed an organization separate and independent from the Witch Cult composed of numerous talented people she forced under her command called the Beloved Children.<ref>''"Is that, so… is the nuance something like a squad detached from the Witch Cultists, or a private army that includes the Sin Archbishop? Either way, calling them something like her beloved children just rubs me the wrong way."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> With them, Capella began targeting the Kingdom and replacing people of importance with her children, resulting in her entering a silent war with the Kingdom intelligence agency, the [[Six Tongues]], a war that would progress quietly over decades.

Several decades later, the [[Great Conquest]] was waged on the White Whale, led by the Sword Saint of the time, [[Theresia van Astrea]], which ultimately ended in failure and the Sword Saint's death. For reasons unknown, Pandora made an appearance during the failed subjugation. Afterward, Theresia's body was collected by the Witch Cult and turned into a corpse soldier for their use. At some point over the next few years, Regulus made an appearance at [[Garkla]]. This resulted in the Fortified City being leveled single-handedly by the man, as well as the death of [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]]'s strongest warrior, [[Kurgan]]. Like with Theresia, Kurgan's body was taken and turned into a corpse soldier by the Witch Cult.

Around this time, Leilani Alnair attempted to reach the [[Pleiades Watchtower]] with her captivated followers, who were all killed on the way. [[Shaula]] found her and brought her to the tower, and she attempted to take over her memories with her Authority. However, once she thought that it had taken her over and attempted to act on it, Shaula shot her since it did not take over the memories and devotion toward [[Flugel]]. After being tossed out of the tower, because her will to be saved over her unborn children was misunderstood by passing travelers, Leilani's two remaining children survived while she perished.

Ten years ago, the Witch Cult also led an assault on the [[Oni|Oni Clan]], slaughtering the vast majority of them, with the exceptions of [[Ram]] and Rem. Just a year later, they led an attack on Miload Manor in another attempt to kill the Oni girls. Though they failed in their objective and were killed in the end, they were still responsible for the deaths of [[Dudley Miload]] and his wife [[Grace Miload|Grace]]. Later, while searching for traces of the Witches, [[Al|Aldebaran]] lured out Petelgeuse, who mentioned that Al did not appear in his Gospel. After using his Authority to gather information from Petelgeuse, Al escaped, much to the spirit's displeasure.

When the [[Royal Selection]] began, Petelgeuse set out to attack [[Arlam Village]] and [[Roswaal Manor]] in order to test if [[Emilia]], a Royal Selection candidate and mirror image of Satella, was worthy by presenting her with the "trials". What the trials entail is unknown. In this effort, the White Whale was left to guard the road between the village and the [[Royal Capital]], the Lifaus Highway. However, thanks to the efforts of Subaru, an attack was led on the White Whale with the assistance of the [[Wilhelm van Astrea|Sword Demon]] and [[Crusch Karsten]]. This attack, now dubbed the Subjugation of the White Whale, was a great success. Shortly afterward, Subaru led about half of the soldiers, members of the [[Iron Fang]], Wilhelm, [[Ferris]], and [[Julius Juukulius]] to slay Petelgeuse in the Subjugation of Sloth, which also led to the deaths of Petelgeuse and numerous cultists, and the capture of his fingers. Unfortunately, the Witch Cult struck back at around the same time, slaughtering many members of the subjugation unit in an attack. Shortly after, Regulus and one of the Sin Archbishops of Gluttony, Lye Batenkaitos, defeated Crusch and Rem, leaving the former without her memories and the latter in the Sleeping Beauty state. Thanks to the subjugations, Capella started to panic, leading to two of her children defecting to the Six Tongues, leading her to plan an attack a year later.

A year later, the Witch Cult led a siege on the [[Priestella|Watergate City of Priestella]], demanding the remains of the [[Typhon|Witch]], the Book of Wisdom, an artificial spirit, and to not interfere with Regulus's marriage to Emilia. In the following [[Battle for Priestella]], the Witch Cult was successfully repelled, with Regulus being slain and the Sin Archbishop of Wrath, Sirius Romanée-Conti, being arrested. The corpse soldiers of Theresia and Kurgan was also defeated, returning to death. However, thanks the Sin Archbishops of Gluttony and Lust, they left behind many casualties of their respective Authorities. Thanks to this battle, Capella started using decoys to lure the Six Tongues away while she started acting on more of her plans.

Approximately two months later, the Sin Archbishops of Gluttony led an attack on the Pleiades Watchtower after Subaru's encounter with [[Rui Arneb]]. This, however, backfired, and Rui was left in an unknown predicament in the [[Od Lagna#Corridor of Memories|Corridor of Memories]], Lye was killed by Ram, and [[Roy Alphard]] was sealed, and soon after, confined to the Prison Tower.

Several months later, after Subaru was forced to seal away Al after his [[Pleiades Sealing Conflict|failed attempt to fulfill his role]], he, [[Beatrice]], and [[Reinhard van Astrea]] visited the Prison Tower in order to negotiate with Roy about spitting up all of the names and memories he and his siblings devoured. However, upon arriving, they have found his unsealed body, torn apart and seemingly deceased. A mere few days later, Capella's plan started to come to fruition as the government, many of which had been replaced by the Beloved Children, had begun targeting the Royal Selection camps.

==Sin Archbishops==
The Witch Cult is led by the Sin Archbishops, who each represent one of the seven deadly sins except for Envy itself,<ref>''“…I have heard that those in the Witch Cult acting as leaders have taken the names of those deadly sins in place of the lost Witches. Satella is the symbol of Envy, which is what they worship. In other words, besides that, there are six—six Sin Archbishops.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 7]], Chapter 6, Section 6.</ref> though the sin of Pride, among the six sins, remained unrepresented by an Archbishop at the time of Subaru's arrival.<ref>''“Among the six Sin Archbishops, only the seeeat of Pride is currently vacant!”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 8]], Chapter 1, Section 5.</ref> Interestingly, most of the Sin Archbishops didn't feel any fealty towards the Witch of Envy, instead possessing their own reasons for working with the Witch Cult. Following Petelgeuse's death, no Sin Archbishop exists that would prioritize the resurrection of the Witch over their personal goals. Each Sin Archbishop possesses a mysterious source of power known as a Witch Factor that correlates to their respective sin. The Witch Factor would eventually blossom into a powerful ability known as an [[Authority]], which allows its wielder to do various things depending on their ideals, goals, and personalities.

For the most part, the Sin Archbishops despise one another and rarely, if ever, work together. Each Archbishop is allowed to command lesser members of the Cult, although most of them choose to operate without support instead relying on their Authorities in battle. The membership of the rank of Sin Archbishops includes Capella Emerada Lugunica representing Lust, Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti representing Sloth, Regulus Corneas representing Greed, and Sirius Romanée-Conti representing Wrath. Gluttony was represented by three siblings who each took on a different aspect of Gluttony: Rui Arneb represented Satiation, Lye Batenkaitos represented Gourmet, and Roy Alphard represented Bizarre Eating. Pride was possessed by a member of the Sacred Vollachia Empire's imperial family named Stride Vollachia, and he perished around forty years ago at the hands of the Blight Dragon Valgren.

At present, most of the Sin Archbishops have either been killed or captured.

===Current===
====Sin Archbishop of Wrath, Sirius Romanée-Conti====
{{Main|Sirius Romanée-Conti}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 16 11.png|thumb|225px|Sirius Romanée-Conti using her Authority of Wrath.]]
The current Sin Archbishop of Wrath is the most physically formidable of the Sin Archbishops. Her Authority of Wrath allows her to manipulate the emotions and sensations of others, meaning she can amplify a person's hostility level and distribute damage dealt across multiple people. Alongside Petelgeuse and Regulus, Sirius is one of the three Sin Archbishops to have inhuman longevity. Although her past is wrapped in mystery, Sirius claimed that her hometown was destroyed by Witch Hunters. She was obsessively infatuated with Petelgeuse, making her the only known Sin Archbishop to view another amicably (with the exception of the Gluttony siblings). She spent a large part of her time stalking Petelgeuse and trying to earn his affection, although he seemed to never reciprocate her feelings. Like Petelgeuse, Sirius appeared to be completely insane and barely held a grasp on reality. She viewed the Witch of Envy as a hated love rival rather than a deific figure.

During the Battle for Priestella, Sirius met Subaru after he had killed Petelgeuse and absorbed the Witch Factor of Sloth. As she knew of Petelgeuse's nature as a [[spirit]], Sirius presumed Subaru was her beloved's latest body and refused to accept his attempts to deny her claim. She was later captured by [[Priscilla Barielle]] and [[Liliana Masquerade]] during the attack. During a subsequent interrogation with Subaru, Sirius finally understood that he was not Petelgeuse, although she still believed that Sloth lived within Subaru and was waiting to emerge. After a two-month long journey, she was jailed within the Prison Tower in the Royal Capital with Evil Sealing Stones.

====Sin Archbishop of Lust, Capella Emerada Lugunica====
{{Main|Capella Emerada Lugunica}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 17 13.png|thumb|225px|left|Capella Emerada Lugunica taunting Subaru with an unconscious Crusch.]]
The current Sin Archbishop of Lust and the holder of the Witch Factor of Lust. Her Authority of Lust allows her to transform herself into seemingly any creature or being – she has used this power to transform into a giant black dragon with golden horns, a small girl, a well-endowed woman, an honest-looking village girl, a multitude of field mice, an innocent looking young girl with a lewd smile, and she even morphed into Emilia with a crazed smile. She can also use this power defensively to regenerate by transforming the parts of her that are damaged into undamaged parts. She was able to heal during her battle with Al, despite him "cutting off her head" and "crushing her heart". Furthermore, her Authority can be used offensively by turning anyone she touches into what she desires. Capella has used this ability to transform people into various creatures and, at worst, nothing but unrecognizable lumps of flesh with no consciousness. Similarly to most of the other Archbishops, her past is clouded with mystery and there is very little information about her. Although she has a popular standard appearance, with signature gold hair and red eyes, there is no confirmation that this is her actual form due to the nature of her Authority, meaning there is no hint towards her age, height, or other key characteristics. Capella is shown to have the worst personality among the Sin Archbishops and even responds to her fellow cultists with insults and degrading nicknames. Capella permanently speaks in an insulting tone to all of those around her and believes that all of the love in the world should be directed towards her and her alone.

Capella is also known as "Mother" and controls people she calls her "children" to do various tasks across the Four Great Nations. She appeared alongside her fellow Sin Archbishops during the Battle for Priestella, causing havoc in her black dragon form until she ultimately dueled Al and fled after the Witch Cult's defeat. However, she caused severe damage with the use of her Authority before leaving, causing many civilians to be stuck in the forms of giant flies, chunks of meat or worse. One has been seemingly permanently transformed into a giant black dragon.

===Former===
====Sin Archbishop of Pride, Stride Vollachia====
{{Main|Stride Vollachia}}
[[File:Re Zero Ex Volume 3 10.png|thumb|225px|left|Stride Vollachia threatening to gouge Yaktol Suwen's eyes out.]]
The most recent Sin Archbishop of Pride, Stride Vollachia was a man hailing from the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He tended to fight using his self-proclaimed Authority, the Hubristic Ten Commandments, a set of ten rings that he used to inflict curses on people, and often utilized his subordinates: the Vollachian War God Kurgan, the twin [[shinobi]] [[Shasuke]] and [[Raizo]], and his wife, [[Melinda]], a surviving member of the Evil Eye Tribe. Stride was the son of the Emperor of the Vollachia Empire and was supposed to succeed him on the throne. However, he was betrayed and poisoned by his own father. He survived the assassination and eventually joined the Witch Cult. Befitting his identity as the Sin Archbishop of Pride, Stride held excessive pride in himself and always looked down on others. Like most Archbishops, he didn't care about the Witch of Envy, only joining the Witch Cult to further his own goals.

Four decades before Natsuki Subaru was transported to the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica, Stride led several campaigns in the heart of the Kingdom, wanting to destroy its covenant with the Divine Dragon [[Volcanica]] and topple the entire country. During these attacks, Stride found an archenemy in the Sword Demon Wilhelm van Astrea, a nigh-unparalleled warrior and the strongest swordsman of his era. Eventually, Stride summoned Valgren in Picoutatte, hoping that the dreadful beast would decimate the entire Kingdom. However, in the end, Valgren devoured Stride. Since his death, the seat of Pride has been vacant for many years. The status of the Witch Factor of Pride that presumably resided within Stride remains unknown.

====Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, Leilani Alnair====
{{Main|Leilani Alnair}}
One of the previous Sin Archbishops of Gluttony, Leilani was the self-proclaimed most pitiful woman in the world. Her pitifulness and self-deprecation manifested itself through her Authority, which allowed her to sway the hearts and minds of her enemies, and replace their dearest memories with herself in order to have them follow and protect her. It is unclear what accomplishments she provided to the Witch Cult, but her existence was still responsible for bringing an end to the lives of hundreds of people in her time.

One day, more than a decade before the events of the main story, Leilani, who had willed herself not to give birth to her children over the course of three years, crossed the [[Augria Sand Dunes]] and attempted to reach the Pleiades Watchtower with her captivated followers. In the end, however, her followers died, and when she attempted to act upon her Authority after she presumed that it had fully taken over the mind and heart of Shaula, she was instead shot and tossed out of the tower, where she was found by travelers who misunderstood her wishes to save her as a wish to save her two surviving unborn children, and she lost her life.

====Sin Archbishop of Sloth, Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti====
{{Main|Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 8 4.png|thumb|225px|Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti introducing himself before Subaru.]]
The most recent Sin Archbishop of Sloth, one of the founders of the Witch Cult, and the Leader of the Moderate Faction. As a co-founder of the Witch Cult, Petelgeuse spent four centuries acting as one of its highest-ranking members and worked tirelessly to fulfil the goals of the Witch Cult and was even appointed the title of an Archbishop, despite not occupying any of the Seats until three centuries following the supposed creation of the Witch Cult. Dubbed as "Geuse" by his friends and people dear to him, Petelgeuse was a kind-hearted spirit, well respected by everyone save for the other Sin Archbishops. It was stated that he was even acquainted with the Witch of Greed and acted as Beatrice's teacher when Echidna was too busy.

His contributions to the Cult led to him being given the title of an Archbishop, though not entrusted with a Sin as he was incompatible with the one he was entrusted with by [[Flugel]]–the Witch Factor of Sloth. Roughly a century before the start of the main story, Petelgeuse carried out different tasks relating to the elves located in the Elior Forest–something that was very dear to him, as the [[Fortuna|Guardian of the Seal]], who he was regularly sent to monitor, was someone he was deeply familiar with and cherished above anyone else. Not long after, however, the forest was suddenly besieged by another two Witch Cult members: Regulus and Pandora, the former leading the Radical Faction of the Cult and the latter leading one of the Three Great Witchbeasts, the [[Black Serpent]]. As push came to shove, Petelgeuse was forced to forcefully take in the Witch Factor of Sloth, gaining the Authority of Sloth in the process, which allowed him to stall the intruders, though to not much avail, as he was overpowered relatively quickly. In the following events of the fight, the Witch of Vainglory used her Authority of Vainglory to influence Petelgeuse into slaughtering Fortuna, the very woman he loved. The unbearable pain caused by his actions caused Petelgeuse's mind to completely shatter, leaving him in a permanent state of madness.

In the following century, Petelgeuse had accepted the seat of Sloth and joined the Radical Faction of the Cult. He became notorious for his cruelty, frequently slaughtering entire towns and villages, acting strictly according to his Gospel's writing. He was finally countered and defeated by the Sloth Subjugation Force consisting of Natsuki Subaru, Sword Demon Wilhelm van Astrea, knights Julius Juukulius and Ferris, and the Iron Fang. After Julius destroyed his body, Subaru later destroyed his spirit, marking the end of Sloth. The Witch Factor of Sloth was inherited by Natsuki Subaru.

His remains were later collected by Wrath, who cremated them in an unknown location. After meeting Subaru, Sirius suspects Petelgeuse is attached to him, though the spirit was overshadowed by Subaru’s soul.

====Sin Archbishop of Greed, Regulus Corneas====
{{Main|Regulus Corneas}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 17 7.png|thumb|225px|left|Regulus Corneas kidnapping Emilia to be his 79th wife.]]
The most recent Sin Archbishop of Greed was considered the most powerful known Sin Archbishop and one of the most powerful characters from the entire series. His Authority of Greed, which he gained after absorbing the Witch Factor of Greed from a box similar to Petelgeuse's, allowed him to stop time in and around his body, making him utterly invincible against any kind of physical attack regardless of its raw strength. Because his body was in a sort of permanent temporal stasis, Regulus never aged and lived over a hundred years. 

Regulus was a man who cared little for people around him and firmly believed that he was in the right no matter what he did. He rarely tolerated people acting in contradiction to his twisted will, often murdering or mutilating innocent people as soon as they dissatisfied him in the slightest. Despite his egotistical attitude, Regulus followed the commands of the Gospel unquestionably. He also showed respect towards Pandora and followed her orders if they didn't contradict his own will too much. Of the Sin Archbishops, Regulus was the most infamous alongside Sloth for the sheer magnitude of the few atrocities he committed. Among his attacks were the incursion into the elven village of Elior Forest that led to the freezing of the entire area and the desolation of the Vollachian Fortress City of Garkla that resulted in the deaths of thousands of soldiers and the Vollachian War God Kurgan. It was Regulus' actions in Garkla that single-handedly taught the world to fear the Witch Cult. 

During the attack on Elior Forest, Regulus acted as the Leader of a Radical Faction that existed within the Witch Cult. He led the Cult and the Witch of Vainglory to the forest, despite making a mutual agreement with Petelgeuse, that the latter would be the only one to have access to the elven village and the seal they were guarding. Having made short work of Petelgeuse, Regulus – after the situations gravely escalated due to things not going the way he would have liked – turned his back on the Witch, killing her. However, due to her Authority of Vainglory, she was able to erase the time of her death and erase his existence from the forest, making it so that he effectively never visited Elior Forest in the first place, reverting all of his damage done to the surrounding nature and Petelgeuse's body.

Roughly a month after Subaru's arrival, Regulus made his appearance at the Lifaus Highway, intercepting the dragon carriage convoy transporting the wounded, Crusch Karsten, and Rem. After decimating a good portion of the convoy and crippling Crusch by cutting her arm off, Regulus – now accompanied by the fellow Sin Archbishop of Gluttony Lye Batenkaitos – introduced himself and, in the following short battle, helped defeat Rem.

Regulus was finally defeated a bit over a year following his initial debut in the story during the events of [[Arc 5]]. After arriving in the Watergate City of Priestella, causing havoc in the city streets, and kidnapping Emilia, Regulus was confronted by the Greed Subjugation Force consisting of Natsuki Subaru and Reinhard van Astrea. After a tough and arduous battle, the team managed to decipher his Authority and give Reinhard a chance to deliver the finishing blow. By lunging him high above the city and batting him down into the streets, Regulus – whose invincibility now had a five-second timer – was utterly shredded by the sheer speed and force of his body digging through dirt and rocks underground. After his hole was flooded by a nearby water canal, Regulus drowned deep underneath the city streets. The Witch Factor of Greed was inherited by Natsuki Subaru.

====Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, Lye Batenkaitos====
{{Main|Lye Batenkaitos}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 24 11.png|thumb|225px|Lye Batenkaitos using Lunar Eclipse.]]
One of the three Sin Archbishops who were jointly the most recent representatives of Gluttony, with Lye representing the gourmet aspect. Like his little sister, Rui, Lye was addicted to the consumption of human names and memories and cared little about the people his Authority hurt. His Authority of Gluttony functioned identically to his sister's and, although he wasn't incredibly powerful like Regulus Corneas, Lye made up for his shortcomings with his versatile fighting style and unpredictable arsenal. He was, at one point, noted by the Author as the most skilled martial artist among all the Sin Archbishops. Until his swan song, Lye was hesitant to use the aspect of his Authority that allowed him to transform into his victims and use their skills to their fullest capacity, as he believed doing so harmed his individuality. Upon finally overcoming his fear, Lye started morphing his body into an amalgamation of numerous victims he had eaten, which greatly amplified his stolen skills' strength, effectively making him the ultimate martial artist, the likes of the world had never seen and will never see. With his Authority, Gluttony could control one of the Three Great Witchbeasts known as the White Whale and occasionally used it in his schemes. He was fond enough of the Whale to consider it a pet. Out of the three Sin Archbishops, Lye was the one who cared the most for his siblings. Although not too fond of Roy, he cared deeply for his younger sister, Rui, whom he genuinely sought to protect from harm.

Although his exact age and the amount of time he spent as a Sin Archbishop are unknown, Lye had the appearance and immature attitude of a youth in his mid-teens. After devouring the name and memories of Rem, Lye garnered an obsession with the man she loved, Natsuki Subaru, hoping to one day devour his name and memories as well. On the other hand, Subaru saw Lye as a mortal foe due to his actions against Rem. However, Lye was never able to experience the feast he sought. During an [[Pleiades Watchtower Expedition|incursion]] into the Pleiades Watchtower, Lye was confronted by Rem's elder twin sister, Ram, who proceeded to face him in a desperate and brutal battle. Eventually, Lye threw up some of the names and memories he devoured up to that day in hopes of taking Ram’s alone and, soon after, he was beheaded by Ram. The states of his victims at present, besides Rem and Emilia, are unknown.

====Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, Roy Alphard====
{{Main|Roy Alphard}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 40 12.png|thumb|225px|Roy Alphard freed from his seal.]]
One of the three Sin Archbishops who were jointly the most recent representatives of Gluttony, with Roy representing the bizarre eating aspect. Unlike his brother, Lye, Roy doesn't care about what he eats, nor does he place any special emphasis on who he eats with, like his sister, Rui. As bizarre eating, his approach towards his meals is much more casual when compared to that of his older brother and younger sister, emphasizing quantity over quality, such as when he ate Julius Juukulius, despite admitting he had a bland taste. As described by his brother, he simply wants to eat without any thought or preparation put into it, for which he was repeatedly criticized by his siblings. He isn't as close to Rui as Lye is, but he is nonetheless devoted and caring towards her. 

In combat, Roy strives to exploit his opponents' weaknesses, unlike his brother, who likes to give his opponents a chance to compete with him. He views combat as nothing more than a violent way of getting his meals. 

During the Battle for Priestella, he ate Julius' name, causing everyone but Subaru to forget about him. During the Pleiades Watchtower Expedition, however, when he tried to devour [[Reid Astrea]], his body was unable to withstand it and was instead taken over. While he regained control of his body after Reid's soul was shattered due to it being incompatible with Roy's body, the fatal wound rendered him unconscious, and he was sealed away with the usage of Yin Magic and escorted to the Kingdom's Prison Tower. However, as his supposed corpse was later discovered in the Prison Tower, it is unclear whether or not Roy is dead or alive.

===Unknown===
====Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, Rui Arneb====
{{Main|Rui Arneb}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 20 5.png|thumb|225px|left|Rui Arneb hijacking Lye Batenkaitos' body.]]
One of the three Sin Archbishops who were jointly the most recent representatives of Gluttony, with Rui representing the satiation aspect. She is a spiritual being who died at birth and, as a result and for unknown reasons, became trapped inside the Corridor of Memories. Like her big brother, Lye, Rui was addicted to the consumption of human names and memories and cared little about the people her Authority hurt. Her Authority of Gluttony functioned identically to her brothers, Lye's and Roy's. Rui didn't care much about what she ate, putting more emphasis on who she ate with. Similar to the [[Great Rabbit]], Rui could split and create a copy of herself whenever she separated her Witch Factor of Gluttony into multiple pieces, often using this ability to keep her original self within the Corridor of Memories while her copy inhabited the body of someone else. 

Being the youngest sibling, Rui initially​ gave off the impression of being respectful and loving towards her brothers, but she later revealed that she found them idiotic for blindly eating lives for her just because she was unable to exit the Corridor of Memories. Rui believed that life is unfair and is like a conveyor belt without having the ability to choose the family, environment, and future to be born into. Advocating her actions and beliefs as a way to search for happiness, she mentioned that she is making an effort to find the life that will satisfy her and let her live with her head held high and believed that Subaru's​ life will provide her that fulfilment, as he is able to Return by Death, which would effectively render her the only living being who would have experience of death itself.

Learning of Return by Death, she ate Subaru's memories and latched onto him to gain the knowledge and "taste" of death. However, Subaru ultimately managed to defeat her and left her for dead, though she is later revealed to have survived, but now has amnesia herself. After experiencing Return by Death, the Rui that had entered Subaru's soul as a Witch Factor became traumatized and got into a fight with the Rui within the Corridor of Memories, who retained her original personality. The end result of this confrontation was that Rui became mind-broken, regressing into an infant-like state. She was transported along with Rem and Subaru to Vollachia and is currently accompanying Subaru around the Empire as she's strangely attached to him. Though her original personality has seemingly vanished, Rui, now recognized as [[Spica]], retains her Authority, making her relation to the cult currently unclear.

[[Episode 34]] (actual) |Japanese Voice = [[Wikipedia:Misaki Kuno|Kuno Misaki]] |English Voice = Kimberley Anne Campbell}} '''Typhon''' (テュフォン) was the '''[[Witch#Witch of Pride, Typhon|Witch of Pride]]'''. Mentioned throughout the series, she formally debuted in [[Arc 4]] as a supporting character. In life, Typhon, with her Authority of Pride, judged those she encountered, leaving behind countless bodies in her wake. Though she met her end, drowning in the trap that was the [[Priestella|Watergate City of Priestella]], her soul was preserved by the [[Echidna|Witch of Greed]] in the [[Castle of Dreams]] placed within the [[Sanctuary]]. Following the events of Arc 4, her soul was taken into a glintstone necklace that [[Omega]] wears on her travels. ==Appearance== Typhon was a young girl who looked as though she was around ten years of age. She had large round red eyes that brimmed with curiosity and short messy dark green hair that fell down to her chin, stylized into a bob-cut of sorts. Her skin was dark and her face possessed an adorability expected in a girl of her age. She gives off an aura of a lovely young girl. Contrary to her true nature as the Witch of Pride, she evoked images of youth, innocence, and purity to those that met her. She does not give off the impression of being a witch. Typhon's lovely clothing helped complement her youthful disposition. Her ensemble included a wreath of blue flowers of different shades decorating the top of her head, a blue armband on each arm, matching light blue scrunchies worn on both of her wrists, a pair of pieces of white material that covered her ankles and had a matching pair of blue flowers attached to them, and a white sundress with light blue lining and a row of blue flowers as its bottom hem. The dress was translucent below its hemline, as Typhon's bare legs could partially be seen under the fabric. The Witch of Pride was never seen wearing anything on her feet. ==Personality== Typhon acted very childlike, which reflected on her actual age, often doing things on impulse, not reading the mood properly and rarely listening to other people. She had trouble understanding heavier, philosophical topics, as seen when she didn't understand Subaru's view on "good" and "bad" people, though, her replies sometimes tended to be different from what one would expect from a 10-year-old child. She showed heavy interest in people's "sins", more often than not disregarding topics and entire conversations (often important) just so she could figure out if a person is an "evildoer" or not. Despite her young age, Typhon had a strong sense of justice and showed no remorse to those she considered guilty. Instead of judging people off of their actions, Typhon condemned those she came across over their feelings of guilt. She showed the capacity for manipulation, as she used her adorable charm to her advantage when getting [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]] to hold her hand so she could test his guilt. She showed little to no compassion for people who she regards as evildoers. However, she felt solicitude towards people who weren't evildoers but had a guilty conscience, even though she was perfectly capable of killing them. She was said to have judged criminals with the innocence and ruthlessness of a child, which stemmed from her past of watching her father execute people, in order to find an answer about the concept of good and evil. This later resulted in her killing her own father, alongside other members of her village. In time, it was not uncommon for her to go on sprees of "judgment", often needing the [[Sekhmet|Witch of Sloth]] to stop her. Her view on the world was described as easygoing and bizarre, completely different from what one would expect from a 10-year-old girl. ==History== It is unclear when exactly in her childhood she absorbed the Witch Factor of Pride. When Typhon was a young girl, she was troubled with the concept of good and evil, and she tended to watch her [[Minor Characters#Typhon's Father|father]] execute people as a part of his job to find an answer. One day, she broke his wine cup, prompting her to confess her deed to him while fearing execution, though fortunately he accepted her apology, leading her to believe that the scale that measured a person's sin was inside of their own heart. Because of this, during one of the executions his father was performing, she had unveiled her Authority for the first time, asking the criminal, her father, and the people in the plaza around her if they were guilty, resulting in all of them shattering. Ever since then, Typhon began asking people if they were sinners and brought down punishment to those that were guilty. Because of her actions, Typhon came to be known as the Witch of Pride, feared as one of the [[Witch#Witches of Sin|Witches of Sin]], and her campaigns to unleash judgment on sinners often led to her and Sekhmet confronting each other. Over 400 years ago, Typhon went to Priestella where she drowned in the city's trap. Echidna later proceeded to collect and preserve her soul in her tomb in the Sanctuary, alongside the other Witches of Sin. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Typhon is considered to be an incredibly powerful Witch, and her strength was such that it required the Witch of Sloth, the strongest Witch outside of Envy, to stop her, and even then, the clashes would lead to massive damages. The full extent of her strength is presently unknown. ===[[Authority]]=== '''[[Authority#Authority of Pride|Authority of Pride]]''' (傲慢の権能, ''Gōman no Ken'nō''): As the Witch of Pride, Typhon was a user of the Authority of Pride and was a compatible holder of its corresponding Witch Factor.''This phenomenon had a precedent; for instance, having once been compatible with Witch Factors and possessed Authorities, the Witches of Sin still retained the same powers even after being reduced to souls post-mortem.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 4, Section 9. Her Authority gave her abilities relating to passing judgment and perceiving the guilt and sins that a person bears. Typhon using her Authority to shatter people.gif|Typhon using her Authority to shatter a group of spectators in the plaza. Typhon - Authority of Pride.gif|Typhon ripping Subaru's arm off due to his feelings of guilt. Typhon's Authority of Pride.gif|Typhon using her Authority of Pride to shatter Subaru's body into pieces. Typhon activate her Authority destroy.gif|Typhon shattering Minerva's hand with her Authority. *'''Dichotomy/Guilt Perception''': After obtaining the Authority, Typhon was able to sense whether an individual was good or bad merely by touching them. Furthermore, she could also tell whether the person in question felt any guilt for any past actions. If a person felt guilt, regardless of the size and context of the guilt or whether or not they were a good or a bad person, Typhon's Authority would have an effect on them. *'''Body Shattering''': The power of the Authority allowed Typhon to telekinetically shatter the bodies of perceived "sinners". Under Typhon's gaze, the target would simply collapse into a collection of shards of themselves. If a guilty person had a good heart, they would feel no pain when Typhon obliterated them. The first time Typhon was seen using the power was on Subaru in Echidna's Castle of Dreams, who failed to feel pain from the Authority thanks to his good heart. However, as they were only in a dreamscape, Subaru didn't die when the Witch of Pride shattered his body, though if Wrath hadn’t healed him, his fate would've been sealed then and there. She has also been shown to use this on a large number of people at once, merely looking at them and asking if they were guilty, and moments later, causing them all to shatter. It even works on someone who physically attacks her, though it will not nullify damage inflicted on her by the strike. **It is implied that Typhon takes the sinner's body parts as "compensation for their sins". **It also has no effect on living things that possess limited or no capacity to think, like [[Daphne]]'s Centipede Coffin. ==Trivia== *Like the other Witches (with the exception of Satella), Typhon's namesake matches both an asteroid and a mythological being. [[Wikipedia:42355 Typhon|42355 Typhon]] is the name of a scattered disc found in the Solar System. The mythological [[Wikipedia:Typhon|Typhon]] was a male serpentine giant and one of the deadliest monsters in Greek mythology. **The day of the asteroid's discovery is February 5, the same day as Typhon's birthday. *Of the Witches of Sin, Typhon is the only member confirmed to be deceased whose Witch Factor doesn't have a clear current owner. Following the Witch Factor of Pride's inheritance by [[Stride Vollachia]], the former Sin Archbishop of Pride, the Witch Factor has seemingly vanished. However, [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti|Petelgeuse]] believed that Pride reached a new holder. *Her remains are still located in the Watergate city of Priestella, where she had died. After the Priestellan Council of Ten were slaughtered, [[Kiritaka Muse]] is the only person who knows how to access the Great Temple, where her remains are said to be kept. Following the events of Arc 5, a group consisting of [[Garfiel Tinzel]], [[Ezzo Cadner]], [[Liliana Masquerade]] and [[Ricardo Welkin]] retrieved her remains: a single withered arm. *She condemned and killed her own father, implying he felt guilty for executing so many people. *Her father's design, (half black and half white) along with the fact that he's an executioner, may be a reference to the character Monokuma from the Danganronpa franchise. *She's stated to be the 3rd strongest Witch, right behind Satella and Sekhmet. Sekhmet was also the one who was repeatedly sent to calm Typhon down when she went on her rampages, although Sekhmet wasn't that effective either. *Typhon often bathed Sekhmet since the latter Witch was too lazy to wash herself. *An underground organization known as The Balance runs the gambling districts in each of Lugunica's Five Great Cities, including [[Flanders]]. Members of The Balance are known to revere Typhon, who is dubbed “the bearer of the balance”.''“Your crimes must be accounted for, in the name of Typhon, the bearer of the balance.”'' [[The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint, Riot in Flanders 5]], Section 6. *In 2014, the author stated that Typhon was among nine known characters introduced in the story up to that point who had the highest capacity for holding [[mana]]. However, he chose to not rank Typhon or any of the other listed characters in order.''“Emilia, Roswaal, Echidna, Typhon, Carmilla, Daphne, Ferris, Priscilla, and Mimi have a large capacity. It’s scary to rank them, considering the future, so I will stop…”'' [https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/499581653728378880 2014 AskFM Q&A] It is unknown if the list has changed since then. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Witch Navbox}} [[Category:Deceased]] [[Category:Witches of Sin]] [[Category:Authority Users]] [[de:Typhon]] [[es:Typhon]] [[fr:Typhon]] [[it:Typhon]] [[nl:Typhon]] [[pl:Typhon]] [[pt-br:Typhon]] [[ru:Тифон]] [[zh:角色:堤丰]]

title: Witch
wikitext:
[[File:Witches.jpg|thumb|300px|right]]
'''Witches''' (魔女, ''Majo'') are individuals from the past who possessed a Witch Factor of the Seven Deadly Sins and an [[Authority]] that manifested from a it.

Currently, most known information about Witches is limited to individuals who were the last ones associated with the said term: the seven women known as the '''Witches of Sin''' (大罪の魔女, ''Taizai no Majo'') who governed over '''Greed''' (強欲, ''Gōyoku''), '''Pride''' (傲慢, ''Gouman''), '''Wrath''' (憤怒, ''Fundo''), '''Gluttony''' (暴食, ''Bōshoku''), '''Sloth''' (怠惰, ''Taida''), '''Lust''' (色欲, ''Shikiyoku''), and '''Envy''' (嫉妬, ''Shitto''). There are also two individuals who govern over '''Vainglory''' (虚飾, ''Kyoshoku'') and '''Melancholy''' (憂鬱, ''Yū'utsu''), the two archaic sins.

==Information==
===Overview===
A Witch in the past was someone who was chosen by a Witch Factor and bore a reality manipulating Authority,<ref>''“The Factors choose those who are qualified. Had she been found by them, the path to being a Witch would have opened… Unfortunately though, it seems like the Witch Factors of this era have already found qualified individuals. Well, I suppose this is a Witch-lacking era, thanks to that kid who’s keeping a bunch of them on their own.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 6]], [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Requirements to be a Witch]], Section 7.</ref> and the male equivalent was a '''Warlock''' (魔人, ''Majin'').<ref>''"Of course, there are no confirmed Warlocks other than this Hector of "Melancholy."'' [https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/1362050031558164483 Season 2 Episode 20 Commentary]</ref> However, due to the lack of knowledge of the method of becoming a Witch, people had the idea that anyone could become a Witch, leading to strange and typically gruesome rituals being made in an effort to become one,<ref>''“In fact, similar things to this happened everywhere 400 years ago. Back in those days, the requirements you needed to become a “Witch” were rather unclear. That’s why, to put it in other words, some thought that maybe anyone could become a Witch, provided they fulfilled the minimum requirements. Thus, weird rituals became widespread.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 6]], [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Requirements to be a Witch]], Section 7.</ref> and according to [[Al|Aldebaran]], the title of Witch is not given so lightly.<ref>''Though the Witch’s appearance was certainly identical to Echidna, the title of the Witch of Greed was not something that could be bestowed upon someone who merely resembled her. This was not limited to just the Witch of Greed. ――The title of Witch, was not something to be bestowed so lightly.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 65, Section 2.</ref> In the present day, though they are known to the world as Sin Archbishops who lead the [[Witch Cult]], these Witch Factor bearers are the equivalent of the Witches of the past; regardless of the change in titles over the different eras, any such being was regarded quite the same.<ref>''For starters, in this era, they called those with Witch Factors names like Sin Archbishops, rather than Witches. Quite rightly, the way they were treated didn’t change, no matter how they were called.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 6]], [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Requirements to be a Witch]], Section 7.</ref><ref>''“That goes without saying. We may call ourselves Sin Archbishops, but we’re just a gathering of people loathed by this world. There’s just a difference in what we’re called, but we’re the same as the Witch.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 24]], Chapter 3, Section 1.</ref><ref>''“As one would expect, the nature of the Witch of Envy is worse than even us, so we don’t want to be lumped together, you know. The rest is the same. Both Witches and Sin Archbishops are the same thing, just called differently. Good-for-nothings compatible with the Witch Factors, we’re just called something else due to different eras and viewpoints.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 24]], Chapter 3, Section 1.</ref>

Although the most famous of Witches or Sin Archbishops exist in the Witches of Sin or the present-day leaders of the Witch Cult, in the past, according to the author, before even the ancient Witches of Sin, there had been other existing Witches.<ref>[https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/497758069007609857 August 8, 2014 AskFM Q&A]</ref> However, it is not known who the previous Witches were, when they lived, what their personalities were, what their legacies are, or when and how they perished.

Witches tend to exude a type of contaminated mana known as '''Miasma''' (瘴気, ''Shōki'') that is not safe for a regular person to take into the body. Should a person be overexposed to miasma, it has detrimental effects to one's psyche. They become paranoid and murderous, and at worst, it can lead to those exposed to madness and self-harm, ultimately leading them to ripping into their bodies, tearing out their eyes and committing suicide. When "scavengers" were once exposed to [[Omega]]'s miasma, within thirty seconds, they had all descended into madness and took their own lives. Not even animals like earth dragons or artificial beings like artificial [[Spirit|spirits]] are immune. Food can also become contaminated, plant life will die, and [[witchbeast]]s will thrive. However, Sages and Sage Candidates are able to stand unaffected by their miasma. Sages are considered the only ones who are capable of reigning over the Witches,<ref>''Unfortunately, there had not been any among them who could endure the thirty seconds of hell and qualify to be the Sage that could reign over the six Witches.'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party]], Section 2.</ref> and when she was informed of the term "Demon King" by Al, [[Echidna]] surmised that it would not be a bad idea to proclaim a figure who could force the Witches into submission and rule over them a "Demon King".<ref>''“With how it is written, it would be a King of Evil… it would make sense for such a figure to be one who rules over Witches. If you can bend me and the other Witches into submission, it does not seem like it would be such a bad idea to proclaim yourself the Demon King.”'' [[No Stella No Life 3]].</ref>

===Public Response to Witches===
Although in the present day the only thing associated with Witches is the infamous [[Satella|Witch of Envy]], people have always feared even the concept of Witches. This is primarily due to the fact that Witches are very commonly associated with widespread death and destruction. Because of this, it was not an uncommon occurrence for people to be labelled a Witch if such things followed a person around. [[Colette]], for example, was labelled a Witch due to the mysterious deaths of the people around her. Likewise, if one is considered to be friendly with a Witch, then they will immediately become an outcast. When it was recognized that Colette was not a Witch but instead was a friend with one, she was immediately cast out of the area of the village she resided by. Uniquely, there is even a case where a person was labelled a Witch due to their appearance alone. [[Emilia]], who is a half-elf who resembles the Witch of Envy rather closely, was dubbed the Witch of Frost, something which resulted in her losing access to the right to enter a village.

According to [[Wilhelm van Astrea]], the term "Witch" was used for certain individuals in the four centuries following the demises of last batch of the Witches of Sin. In particular, magic users who sided with the Demi-Human Alliance during the [[Demi-Human War]] were often called Witches out of convenience.<ref>''"There are beings besides the Witch of Envy who we call witches as a term of convenience. During the Demi-Human War, magic users cooperating with the Demi-Human Alliance were often called witches as well, and they were greatly feared."'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 17]] Chapter 3; Section 3</ref> This being said, there were some individuals that were dangerous enough that they were officially recognized by governments as a Witch. The most notable of these Witches was [[Sphinx]], and thus far, she is the only “Witch” besides the Witch of Envy whose name is engraved in the Kingdom of Lugunica's history,<ref>''“The Witch, Sphinx. A being most foul who caused an ocean of blood to be spilled by both humans and demi-humans alike without even batting an eye. The one and only Witch other than the Witch of Envy who left her bloody name in the Kingdom’s history.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 18]], Chapter 4, Section 4.</ref> as well as the only known Witch to have been recognized in such a manner. It is unknown if there were other such individuals in the other nations.

In the past, due to the confusion surrounding how a Witch was born, if someone exhibited a strange ability or was accused of strange acts, they would be accused of being a Witch, and if there was no way to refute the accusations, said person was killed. The excuses for such accusations can vary: if someone managed to kill a witchbeast using the Minya spell, in which the body would crystallize; being found near a body; being responsible for a string of murders; if someone was accused of starting a plague in order to heal everyone with their own methods and in turn gain everyone's favor, even if that was not the case. Persistent problems that occurred commonly in the past were '''Witch Hunts''' (魔女狩り, ''Majogari''), in which accusations would be cast on someone and everyone in a settlement would hunt down that person to kill them, hoping to stop strange happenings within their respective settlement. Such hunts have led to the destruction of entire settlements, such as the home of [[Sirius Romanée-Conti]].<ref>''"It was harder to live back then compared to now, way tougher... My hometown was destroyed by a Witch Hunt. Back then, I was still really young..."'' [[The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint: The Lion's Ferocity Chronicle 1]], Section 2.</ref> Other than that, there were also '''Witch Trials''' (魔女裁判, ''Majo Saiban''), which were held to determine whether or not a person was a Witch. The main problem with this sort of trial, regardless of the neutral witness that would ordinarily be present, is that there has rarely if ever been a case in which the accused was acquitted of being a Witch. Although they have rarely occurred following the demise of the Witches of Sin, in the present day, [[Gusteko]] still has villages and towns that perform these hunts and trials, and during the trials, Itinerant Preachers would ordinarily be called to act as neutral judges.

This being said, due to the dubious and violent nature of Witch Hunts and Witch Trials, people who hold positions of authority are not against using them to cover up conspiracies, and they could even use these hunts and trials in an effort to rid themselves of political opponents, people they didn't like, or the families of important people. If a settlement experiences repeated hunts and trials in order to cover up their messes and avoid blame, then said settlement is very likely to face collapse. Because the people would continue to hunt each other down, the population would continuously reduce, whether via executions or attempting to escape from the settlement out of fear. In the present day, Omega has speculated that the Gustekan town of Limbus is likely to meet its end this way after the conspiracies in the town were uncovered.

===Witches Accepted by Society===
Despite the fact that Witches are generally despised and that the term is generally used as an insult, slander, or even an omen, there are occasions where people who have been labeled as a Witch manage to turn public view in their favor. Even if the original negative label of Witch sticks with them or they actively refer to themselves as a Witch, people like this have managed to become seen as positive forces that can be favorable to the public. One such example of a Witch accepted by society is Echidna, who, before she devolved into the Witch of Greed, was recognized as the Witch of Wisdom, and many important figures sought her out to receive her knowledge for their own gain. Another example is Emilia, who, as stated before, was labeled the Witch of Frost due to her appearance and her connection to the frozen [[Elior Forest]]. Although initially publicly looked down on and feared, after making a name for herself in the [[Royal Selection]] and proving herself a force of good rather than a force of evil, the people have come to recognize her as her own person, and Emilia is even proud and willing to call herself the Witch of Frost. At present, however, beyond these two figures, it is unknown whether or not there have been other such Witches.

===Erasure From History===
Despite their heavy presence in the past, for centuries, the Witch Cult or other related parties have been doing what they could to erase any history related to the Witches excluding the most infamous Witch of Envy.<ref>''So, in order to learn about the Witch of Greed who had already been dead for a long time, she set out on a journey to follow the legends and books in various places, but there was an organization known as the Witch Cult that was attempting to erase the Witches from history―― that did not seem to be the original objective of its founding, but their activities served as hindrances, so results were very slow to come by.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 7.</ref> According to Sphinx, as time passed, information on the Witches became more and more scarce, to the point that she could not find any information on them, including the Witch who made her. Likewise, any mention of Witches besides the Witch of Envy or public knowledge of Witch-related artifacts is to be kept mum, else the Witch Cult will provide painful and often fatal judgment. Even if the public is aware of the Witches or their names, mentioning them, so much as saying their name, is considered taboo in order to avoid a bloody fate. The most well-known example of a violation of this taboo is the fall of the [[Vollachia Empire]]'s [[Garkla|Fortified City of Garkla]], in which a Witch-related artifact was rumored to be up for auction, resulting in the [[Regulus Corneas|Sin Archbishop of Greed]] coming to destroy the entire city and killing one of their most powerful assets and war hero, [[Kurgan]]. This incident served as a warning to the Four Great Nations to avoid breaking the taboo again.

Despite the existence of this taboo and the near complete erasure of the Witches from history, there are still quite a number of organizations and cities that are in some way connected to past Witches, and their legacies still exist in the present day in some way or another. The underground organization known as the Balance, which has had a history across the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]], seems to worship the Witch of Pride, [[Typhon]], who delivered her own justice in the past, and Aldebaran considered one of its members, [[Manfred Madison]], as Typhon's Apostle. In the [[Priestella|Watergate City of Priestella]], which was originally made to trap a Witch, Typhon's remains acted as an integral part of the city's infrastructure. The Witch of Greed's legacy, which includes [[meteor]]s; [[Puck|still-living]] [[Eridna|artificial]] [[Beatrice|spirits]]; the Taygeta Library in the [[Pleiades Watchtower]]; [[Ryuzu Meyer (copy)|results]] of her immortality experiments; failed Books of Wisdom recreations currently held by the Witch Cult; her students, [[Roswaal L. Mathers|Roswaal A. Mathers]] and Aldebaran; and even the entire country of [[Kararagi]], which was said to have been made with her assistance, all still exist and have a relatively heavy presence in the present. The witchbeasts, once created by the Witch of Gluttony, [[Daphne]], still roam around the world, and the Three Great Witchbeasts in particular have terrorized the world for centuries.

==History==
When the existence of Witches were first identified in the world, each of the inheritors of the Witch Factors happened to be women by chance. Thus, the Factors came to be known as Witch Factors, and their holders went on to be collectively deemed Witches throughout history.<ref>''“Previously, I had also wondered about it and decided to investigate, but the reason was nothing too major. When Witch Factors were first perceived in this world… that is, when the first Witches were identified, all those in possession of a Factor just happened to be women.”'' [[No Stella No Life 3]].</ref>
