Despite the existence of previous generations of Witches, the last known Witches of the world were the Witches of Sin, who all existed four centuries ago. Two of the Witches, Echidna and Satella, traveled with the party of [[Farsale Lugunica]] on a journey to apparently save the world. At one point during their travels, while within the country of [[Magrizza]], Farsale declared his own name, resulting in a noble discovering them and inviting them to a banquet of nobles. However, the nation's [[Minor Characters#Magrizza's Crown Prince|crown prince]], who was also in attendance at the banquet, became enamored by Echidna and went behind the scenes to arrange a marriage between the two of them, with Echidna's party going along with them after they were split from their capable fighters. However, at some point, for reasons yet to be explained, [[Reid Astrea]] and [[Volcanica]] went on a rampage, ultimately resulting in the marriage being cancelled and them being driven from the nation. It was a short time later that they learned that the [[Black Serpent]] destroyed Magrizza. According to Echidna, the Black Serpent was likely following after them.

At some point, five of the Witches of Sin perished in different areas of the Kingdom of Lugunica around the time of the Great Calamity, their deaths caused either directly or indirectly by Satella for reasons unknown. Echidna, who seemed to have separated from her group, gathered the souls of the deceased Witches and started training Aldebaran how to use his Authority, magic, and various other things. With their goal to defeat Satella, the two eventually set off to fight her, ultimately resulting in their loss, Al's loss of his arm, and Echidna being heavily injured while protecting him. Believing that they needed to rely on [[Flugel]] at the time and that she could handle secondary damages, she sealed Al away for the next four centuries. At some point after this, Echidna sacrificed her love and devolved from the Witch to the Witch of Greed, and later, she died, and her body and soul were connected to the [[Sanctuary]] via the magic of Mathers.

The Witch of Envy, after confronting the Sage, first Sword Saint, and Divine Dragon, was sealed away near the Great Waterfall in the [[Augria Sand Dunes]]. Sometime after her defeat, the Pleiades Watchtower, which was left in the care of the Sage's [[Shaula|apprentice]], was made to watch over her shrine. There were also two other supernumerary Witches who existed in this era, those being the Warlock of Melancholy, [[Hector]], and the Witch of Vainglory, [[Pandora]]. The Warlock of Melancholy vanished completely for unknown reasons after an attack on Echidna's Sanctuary, having never been seen again, though it is implied that Roswaal and [[Clind]] defeated him and took his Witch Factor. The Witch of Vainglory, despite being practically erased from history, became associated with the Witch Cult. Aside from the sealed Satella, Pandora is the only known Witch who is active in the present, and she continues to wander the world in pursuit of her own goals.

Approximately 100 years ago, when the radical faction of the Witch Cult led an attack on the Elves of Elior Forest, Pandora also became involved, leading the Black Serpent there with her Authority. Because of her interference alongside Regulus, not only did [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti|Petelgeuse]] take in the Witch Factor of Sloth, her usage of her Authority of Vainglory to cause [[Fortuna]]'s death unintentionally led to the [[Permafrost of Elior Forest]] by Emilia's hands. Unable to open the seal there, she erased Emilia's memories, left the girl to freeze, and she brought Petelgeuse alongside her.

During the Demi-Human War, Sphinx, a failed creation of Echidna, became infamously regarded as the only other Witch to go down in the history of the Kingdom of Lugunica due to her widespread use of the Sacrament of the Immortal King to raise the dead as [[Undead#Corpse Soldiers|corpse soldiers]]. After her defeat at the hands of [[Roswaal J. Mathers]], [[Carol Remendis]], and [[Grimm Fauzen]], she was captured by [[Leip Barielle]] and left imprisoned for decades.

Approximately fourteen years prior to the events of [[Arc 1]], Pandora was seen by the previous generation Sword Saint, [[Theresia van Astrea]], during the [[Great Conquest]]. After her Divine Protection of the Sword Saint was transferred to her grandson, [[Reinhard van Astrea|Reinhard]], Theresia lost consciousness as a result of Pandora's interference, and died at the scene, with the [[White Whale]] being attributed as her cause of death.

About ten years prior to the events of Arc 1, when [[Ryuzu Meyer (copy)|Ryuzu Shima]] chased [[Garfiel Tinzel]] to pull him out of the Witch's Graveyard, Echidna, whose soul was still active, decided to prepare Shima's body for the day that she would eventually take over with her Soul Transcription. Within the following years, Aldebaran met again with Echidna without entering the tomb, but he discovered that Echidna had devolved into the Witch of Greed. After failing to defeat her, she gave him a task that would help to deal with "secondary damages".

One day, in the [[Royal Capital]] of Lugunica, a young man, [[Natsuki Subaru]], is summoned to the world. In her love and wish for him not to die, Satella granted him the power of Return by Death, giving him the chance to challenge fate.

During the [[Sanctuary Incident|events]] of [[Arc 4]], the Witches of Sin who, despite their deaths, were residing within Echidna's [[Castle of Dreams]], were heavily involved with Subaru and Emilia's path toward unsealing the Sanctuary, despite Echidna herself providing to be an obstacle due to her own Greed and desires. After the Sanctuary was liberated, Echidna, who had taken over Shima's body and renamed herself Omega. Keeping the souls of the other Witches of Sin within a glintstone, she left the area. On her journey, she met Colette and [[Palmyra]] in the Kingdom and met with the Witches afterwards, deciding to head to Kararagi, which she claimed to have helped [[Alec Hoshin]] create, in order to avoid the Witches' mutual enemy. Ironically, she crossed over into Gusteko instead, and met [[Noelle Tuérico]], [[Shion]], and [[Lilac]], who each joined her [[Omega Party|party]].

Despite her imprisonment, Sphinx continued with her [[Undead|undead]] experimentation once she learned of Leip's death, and upon her tests to create undead in the Barielle Domain being foiled at the hands of [[Priscilla Barielle]], she escaped her confinement. Afterward, she left for Kararagi to continue her experiments, and later, Vollachia. During the events of [[Arc 6]], Satella made her appearance for the first time in four centuries. Using her shadow to take Subaru, [[Rem]], and [[Spica|Rui]] and then taking a hit from the Divine Dragon, she dropped the three in Vollachia. A few months later, towards the end of the [[Imperial Civil War]]'s [[Battle for the Imperial Capital]], Sphinx started the [[Great Disaster]], using the undead as her army. Despite the long and drawn-out battle and her success in taking on the vessel of her creator, she was ultimately brought down by Subaru and Rui, renamed Spica.

==Witches of Sin==
Roughly four hundred years ago, the seven last known Witches of Sin, including [[Sekhmet]], [[Typhon]], [[Daphne]], [[Carmilla]], [[Minerva]], Echidna, and Satella roamed the world. They were considered calamities due to their actions and their consequences: Typhon went around different towns and cities killing everyone who her Authority deemed a sinner, Carmilla was the cause of countless unnecessary deaths of people who accidentally laid eyes on her, and with every usage of Minerva's Authority of Wrath, a natural disaster hit a random location in the world. While not necessarily evil at heart, they were directly or indirectly the cause for many hardships and catastrophes. Perhaps the least calamitous Witches were Echidna and Sekhmet, as Echidna spent her days satisfying her Greed, learning new things and acting as an all-knowing encyclopedia for people all around the world, Sekhmet spent her days in languid Sloth, not moving a muscle and not causing any disasters despite her being the second strongest of the witches.

The Witches of Sin shared a rather intricate and at times wholesome relationship. Typhon regarded Sekhmet as her "mommy" and often bathed her since the latter couldn't bother with such trivial chores. At least once per year, all seven Witches got together and had a calming tea party hosted by Echidna, which always took place in a different location in the world. It goes without saying that the area usually suffered a huge disaster and all the people in the large vicinity had to evacuate for safety reasons. 

Occasionally, a Witch would go on a rampage, destroying entire towns and areas, killing hundreds or thousands of innocent people, directly or indirectly. Typhon was the most prone to such behavior since her childish view of the world and her values often conflicted with the common mindset. Sekhmet was usually sent to calm her down, but she usually did more harm than good, more often than not doubling or tripling the damage and number of deaths. Daphne often went on rampages, eating everything in existence similar to the [[Great Rabbit]]. With her [[Authority#Authority of Lust|Authority of Lust]] clouding everyone's minds to the point of creating instant chaos and/or killing them in a matter of minutes, Carmilla inadvertently turned peaceful areas into devastated war zones with many casualties in their wake, toppling larger cities one after another.

Each of the six Witches met their end in the Kingdom of Lugunica.<ref>''“Well, for now, I’d like to leave Lugunica. Many of you met your ends here in this country; it depresses me a bit.”'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting]], Section 2.</ref><ref>''“W-We… We actually all… ended up dying here…”'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting]], Section 2.</ref> They died in various ways, with some of them being unrelated to Satella's rampage:
*Typhon drowned when she was trapped within Priestella's defenses.
*Sekhmet fell off the Great Waterfall while fighting the Divine Dragon.
*Daphne starved to death in a "sand sea".
*Minerva was lured into a trap by a group of elves that were sent by an unnamed person. She ended up going insane and subsequently died at the hands of Satella, during the Great Calamity.
*Carmilla burned to death in an unspecified location.
*Echidna collected the other Witches' souls, and she eventually went to the Sanctuary. According to the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)|web novel]], at Volcanica's instruction, Echidna's soul was bound to the Sanctuary by the [[magic]] of Mathers,<ref>''“More accurately, it was at Volcanica’s instruction, that the magic of Mathers bound me here.”'' [[Arc 4]], Chapter 12.</ref> with the faint hope that, if the Witch of Envy were to ever return, she could be deterred.<ref>''“Even now, the Witch of Envy is imprisoned in the Sealing Stones, but her seal is not unbreakable. Nor is Volcanica’s lifespan eternal, and there is no guarantee that the seal won’t be undone if given the chance. There are also quite a few who believe that there is no knowing whether every great change in the heavens and the earth might not be chipping away at the Sealing Stones―― That, is why Volcanica left my existence behind.”'' [[Arc 4]], Chapter 12.</ref><ref>''“Myself, the Witch, and the Divine Dragon Volcanica. With the Sword Saint and… the Sage? For the time being, even if the Witch of Envy was resurrected, we should be able to oppose her. At least, that is Volcanica’s faint hope. So, there you have it, the context behind why I am now in this disgrace, after my death.”'' [[Arc 4]], Chapter 12.</ref> In the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (light novel)|light novel]], Echidna claimed that she gathered the souls of the other Witches before her body was destroyed, and she was sealed away by Volcanica later.<ref>''“――The souls of they who passed on reside alongside me in this Castle of Dreams. So that I would not lose them, I gathered them myself before my body was destroyed and I was sealed away by Volcanica.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 11]], Chapter 5, Section 4.</ref>

Currently, only the locations of Typhon and Echidna's remains are known. Typhon's remains are located in the Great Temple under the Watergate City of Priestella and Echidna's resting place is located in the Witch of Greed's Tomb located in the Sanctuary.

Despite their status as calamities, the Witches of Sin left quite a legacy after their deaths, with three in particular having the most influence. Echidna created meteors that are used to the current day, namely by people who are unable to channel magic. Daphne's legacy is perhaps the most destructive and negative as she was directly responsible for the creation of all witchbeasts. Despite her good intentions, Daphne failed to understand or even consider common mindset and morals, creating a plethora of monsters that would go on to do everything other than what they were created for. Instead of solving famine and hunger, the beasts have destroyed towns and larger cities, leaving many areas uninhabitable. The [[Witchbeast#The Three Great Witchbeasts|Three Great Witchbeasts]] have proven the most disruptive by far, ravaging the lands of the known world for centuries. Typhon, on the other hand, seems to be rather notable in the modern era, as she has a cult following from a criminal organization known as The Balance, which operates in each of Lugunica's Five Great Cities.

Throughout the years, people developed some common misconceptions regarding the Witches, specifically regarding the Witch of Envy. Perhaps the most common mistake people make is contributing the creation of the witchbeasts to the aforementioned Witch, common belief being that she created them in order to clean the world and get rid of humanity, which is untrue as Daphne is the true creator of the witchbeasts with an entirely different purpose in mind. Rumors like these spawn further questions of just what other false information is circling around the world regarding the Witches. According to Subaru, he suspects the reason for these misconceptions lies with the Witch Cult's campaigns to erase the Witches from the world, pinning the blame of all Witch-related disasters on Satella.<ref>''"Not “If you want to hide a tree, put it in a forest”, but if you want to hide a Witch then put it in the Witch of Envy episode, huh…? But, if that’s the case, then the one who created the Witch Cult would be…"'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref>

===Current===
====Witch of Envy, Satella====
{{Main|Satella}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 13 5.png|thumb|left|225px]]
The Witch of Envy, Satella, was easily the most powerful among the Witches of Sin. Despite taking in the Witch Factor of Envy and developing an Authority of Envy, she was actually incompatible with the Witch Factor, which resulted in the creation a separate personality known as the Witch of Envy, following her absorbing the Witch Factor. Whereas one personality was fairly approachable, her alternate personality was the embodiment of Envy - possessive and remorseless, capable of easily slaughtering people en masse without a shred of regret. The capabilities of her Authority of Envy remain unclear, although she was also noted as a capable Yin Magic caster, able to control shadows in terrifying manners of both amazing offense and dense to the point of being able to manifest two thousand shadow hands at once, and having immortality that was so seemingly-flawless that not even the Great Sage Flugel could not conceive a method to bring about Satella's death. Furthermore, it's been heavily implied she can turn back time as well as seemingly freeze time.

One day, the Witch began a ceaseless destructive rampage that resulted in the decimation of half of the world. As she could not be killed, Satella was imprisoned in a shrine at the edge of the world for all eternity. Her actions changed the course of history forever, and she was considered the most evil individual to have ever been born. Four hundred years later, in the present day, a boy named Natsuki Subaru was summoned to the new world and Satella bestowed a power on him that prevents him from dying. Though it is currently unknown who exactly summoned Subaru, it is heavily implied to be the Witch of Envy herself. Although her motives remain unclear, Satella claims she gave Subaru the ability to Return by Death because she loves him.<br />

===Former===
====Witch of Greed, Echidna====
{{Main|Echidna}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 12 13.png|thumb|225px]]
The Witch of Greed, Echidna, had a thirst for knowledge that was never quenched regardless of how much she learned. Born as the daughter of the Warlock of Melancholy, Hector, and the Witch of Vainglory, Pandora,<ref name="hectorfather">''“You could say it was a warped sense of love, I suppose. But, it wasn't like he was head over heels for Mother, in fact. After all, Hector was Mother's father, I suppose.”'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 31, Section 2.</ref><ref name="pandoramother">''“A Witch, I suppose. ――The Witch of Vainglory, Pandora, that is Mother’s mother, in fact.”'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 31, Section 2.</ref> she is the only person in history to have been a Witch by birth.

In life, the bountiful wisdom she offered attracted many great men and women to earn her favor. She created the Artificial Spirits Puck, Beatrice, and Echidna for an unknown purpose (however, Puck was made to watch over Emilia), and she made a vow with Puck that forbade him from forming a contract with Emilia on his own. Echidna created the Ryuzu copies (such as Omega and Sphinx) by using the original [[Ryuzu Meyer (original)|Ryuzu Meyer]] as a basis for the clones in an experiment to research immortality, with her copying her memories and knowledge to the copies. Her experiment, however, was never completed because she died before she could ever finish it. In her life, Echidna also created some meteors, which are used to the current day.

Although the exact specifications of her Authority of Greed remain unclear, her mastery of all six magical elements was unparalleled save for possibly Roswaal L. Mathers. The abilities of her Authority of Greed have yet to be revealed, however, it is implied that the [[Terminology#Story Specific|Book of Wisdom]] is tied to it, having created two copies of it for her apprentice Roswaal and her creation Beatrice. Echidna located, collected and preserved the souls of the five other Witches of Sin after their deaths inside her tomb, allowing them to manifest in her Castle of Dreams. Her body was eventually sealed by the Divine Dragon Volcanica within the Sanctuary inside her tomb, although her death has yet to be stated, the Witch of Greed herself claims that Satella devoured her. Her Witch Factor was inherited by Regulus Corneas, then later inherited by Natsuki Subaru.<br />

====Witch of Wrath, Minerva====
{{Main|Minerva}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 11 12.png|thumb|left|225px]]
The Witch of Wrath, Minerva, cared about nothing more than healing the physical ailments of wounded or sick people she encountered in her travels. Excluding Satella, Minerva was the most dangerous out of the Witches of Sin and caused the most damage, although she never actually sought to. Despite her reputation, Minerva was caring and fairly compassionate towards normal people.

In the past, people in the world around Minerva were constantly fighting, causing her to cry. Eventually, she realized that crying wouldn't solve anything and decided to train herself in order to gain enough power to be a deterrent to fighting, though that still didn't change anything. As she fought, she came to understand that she'd been crying out of rage and not sorrow, causing her to start punching people, resulting in their wounds being healed. From that moment on, she traveled the world to heal people wherever she found people in need. Many nations sent troops after her, trying to capture and/or defeat her, but no one was able to successfully catch her. Minerva also has some kind of history with elves as she cared deeply about Emilia and the other elves.

Her Authority of Wrath allowed her to heal a person's wounds by striking them with a part of her body. However, the damage healed would be distributed randomly somewhere else in the world. In other words, for every person she saved another random person in the world would die. Minerva was aware of this, but as she only cared about the wounds she could see in front of her, she never ceased her crusade. She was eventually trapped by a group of elves and driven mad and killed by the Witch of Envy, although another claim suggests Satella devoured her. Her Witch Factor was inherited by Sirius Romanée-Conti.<br />

====Witch of Sloth, Sekhmet====
{{Main|Sekhmet}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 13 4.png|thumb|225px]]
The Witch of Sloth, Sekhmet, was the very embodiment of the sin of Sloth. She was so lazy that she rarely did anything other than relaxing. She was considered the second most powerful Witch after Satella, and was apparently capable of defeating every weaker Witch simultaneously with ease. She was also the least dangerous to encounter by far and possessed the most common sense out of any of her comrades. Sekhmet was rather protective of the young Witch of Pride Typhon. 

Before she was born, Sekhmet's clan, the [[Demi-Human#Types of Demi-Humans|Giants]], expected things from her, wanting to bring back their founder known as God. However, after she was born, she disappointed them, causing them to hold her in disdain and abandon her as punishment. Many years later, upon hearing of a wild woman in the mountains, men came and captured her, taking her down to the city. While there, she gained knowledge, a way of life, and emotions. Eventually, not understanding at the time that what she felt was gratitude and obligation, she snapped the necks of the men in the place she lived in and left. Returning to her homeland, she proceeded to kill her entire clan, not understanding at the time that what she felt was hatred and a desire for revenge. She then returned back to her previous home to give the men she killed a proper burial, and once she was alone, she felt a peace of mind, which she felt happy about.

The Authority of Sloth allowed her to produce an invisible force field of sorts that was capable of crushing almost anything that stood in her way. She eventually fell from the Great Waterfalls to her death while fighting the Divine Dragon Volcanica, although another claim suggests Satella devoured her. Her Witch Factor was inherited by Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti, then later inherited by Natsuki Subaru.<br/ />

====Witch of Gluttony, Daphne====
{{Main|Daphne}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 11 13.png|thumb|left|225px]]
The Witch of Gluttony, Daphne, had a bottomless stomach that always craved substance. It didn't matter what she ate, whether it was animals, furniture, or even people. She was a strong believer in survival of the fittest, citing that every life should have a fair chance at surviving, not just the sentient ones like humans. With her power, she was responsible for creating the man-eating monsters known as witchbeasts so as to end world hunger, although the claim of creating such monsters became known as the Witch of Envy's own accomplishment so as to destroy the world.

A long time ago, a man was afflicted with an incurable disease, and, as he was afraid of dying, he began using various methods to try and prolong his life. Daphne was one of the many people he used in his experiments, and eventually he succeeded in achieving his goal by using her body. In his joy, he forcibly undid her binds, and when she came to her senses, she found herself all alone in the man's castle, suffering from hunger. To satisfy her hunger, she began eating everything in the castle, including things like the throne and the carpets, and resorted to eating what she threw up when necessary. As she was immortal, she couldn't die, however she felt like she was going to die from hunger. Eventually, she somehow began creating witchbeasts in the castle, which she considered to be illusions at the time, and started to use them as a food source. After a while, her binds broke from the fighting between her and the beasts, allowing her to leave the castle. The witchbeasts also left and spread across the world.

Aside from her ability to create witchbeasts, the exact abilities bestowed by Daphne's Authority of Gluttony remain ambiguous. With the possible exception of the Witch of Envy, Daphne was presumably the most morally ambiguous of the Witches as her form of logic is incomparable to that of other humans. She eventually starved to death in the Auguria Dunes, although another claim suggests Satella devoured her. Her Witch Factor was inherited by [[Leilani Alnair]], her children [[Rui Arneb]], [[Lye Batenkaitos]], and [[Roy Alphard]] after she perished, and later, Spica.

====Witch of Pride, Typhon====
{{Main|Typhon}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 11 11.png|thumb|225px]]
The Witch of Pride, Typhon, was a young girl with a naïve outlook on the world. The daughter of an executioner, Typhon judged and delivered lethal punishment upon those she deemed guilty. However, her youthful outlook on justice led her astray, as she judged people as guilty even if they felt only a shred of guilt over something in their past that wasn't worth punishing. As judge, jury, and executioner, Typhon would conduct many massacres.

The Authority of Pride allowed her to sense who felt guilty and completely shatter the bodies of those who did. With her power, Typhon was considered the third most powerful Witch after Satella and Sekhmet. She was eventually trapped in the Watergate City of Priestella and drowned by a flood, although another claim suggests Satella devoured her. Her Witch Factor was inherited by [[Stride Vollachia]]. Pride's current holder is unknown.

====Witch of Lust, Carmilla====
{{Main|Carmilla}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 12 11.png|thumb|left|225px]]
The Witch of Lust, Carmilla, was a timid young woman who despite representing the sin of Lust had a complete disinterest in love. That being said, she recognized the importance that love had on life and would help people realize the love that others had for them if they couldn't notice it themselves. Her captivating beauty was the catalyst for many conflicts where whole factions or even nations would war for the right to possess her. According to Echidna, Carmilla only cares for herself and holds deep grudges if you were to harm or trick her in any way regardless of if she's in the wrong. In the past, Carmilla was the reason why her village, the neighboring villages and cities and even the great country she lived in, were engulfed in the flames of war. Everyone desired and loved her, but she desired none of it, hence she left everything and everyone behind in search of the love she lost.

A long time ago, Carmilla was a normal girl who was loved by the people in her village and even had a fiancé. However, one day a man of power came to the village and desired her. Angered by the man's actions, the villagers rose up in defiance and fought against him, eventually burning him with his mansion. The cities and villages around theirs began to regard them as dangerous, causing the fighting to spread, and soon their force was toppling countries, all the while claiming that it was for her sake. Carmilla began to be regarded as a heavenly maiden, nevertheless, she didn't desire such a thing and saw that they were being misled by their own fantasies and manipulated by their ideals. After they had toppled a large country, her fiancé proposed to her at the top of the castle, though she ignored him and left everything behind, despairing that what she originally wanted had no longer existed.

The Authority of Lust, which was dubbed the "Faceless Bride," allowed Lust to manipulate the minds of others so that they saw her as whoever they loved. Additionally, anyone who laid eyes on her would be completely captivated by her to the point that they would forget anything else. Most people who met her would die as they would forget to breathe in her presence, although the Witch was hardly perturbed by this. She was eventually burned at the stake, although another claim suggests Satella devoured her. Her Witch Factor was inherited by [[Capella Emerada Lugunica]].<br/ />

==Supernumerary Witches==
The Witch Factors of Melancholy and Vainglory are, according to Clind, supernumerary to the Witch Factors, and they were each tailor-made to be compatible with specific individuals, those who bore the titles of '''Valiant''' (勇者, ''Yūsha'') and '''Saintess''' (聖女, ''Seijo'').<ref>''“To begin with, it is inconceivable that you, Petra, would be compatible with the Witch Factor of Melancholy. This Factor and one other, the Factor of Vainglory, are both unenumerated… no, supernumerary is the right word. These have each been fine-tuned to their respectively singular and uniquely compatible persons―― the Valiant and the Saintess. Tailored. They shall never be compatible with any other. Besides.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref> Because of this, though others might be able to bear them and exhibit their respective Authorities, they will never be compatible with another person, always requiring compensation from any users besides who they were made for, as is the case with Clind himself.<ref>''“No. Refutation. I am not compatible with the Witch Factor of Melancholy. Consequently, I necessitate compensation in order to draw out the Authority of Melancholy. Inadequate. By nature, those compatible with a Witch Factor do not require compensation in order to exercise the Authority. It is the right to rewrite the world, as recognized by Od Lagna. Official.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref> This being said, even the people they were specifically made for were incapable of warding away the corruption of their minds brought about by their Witch Factors.<ref>''“Even they who were compatible, were unable to escape the corruption of their minds. Disgrace.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref>

While Clind has inherited the Witch Factor of Melancholy, he does not consider himself a Warlock, and has said that even if he had been compatible, he could not have been counted among the Witches or the Sin Archbishops.<ref>''“Albeit Meili’s misgivings are a matter of course, I am not a Sin Archbishop. Refutation. To begin with, the Witch Factor of Melancholy is an article of an exceptional kind. Anomalous. Even were I one compatible with this Factor, I would not be enlisted among the ranks of the Witches or the Sin Archbishops. Outcast.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref> The previous holder of the Factor, the Valiant, was not attached to any form of address, but his wife believed it would be suitable to dub him the Warlock of Melancholy.<ref>''“The erstwhile owner… the one compatible with the Witch Factor of Melancholy, named himself as the Warlock of Melancholy. Self-named… no, named by another. That individual had no fixations towards any manner of address, but his wife simply deemed it would be suitable to call him as such and named him. Pet name.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 5, Section 3.</ref> They were each considered by Echidna to be especially good-for-nothing people who became deviants reduced to the roles of Warlock and Witch. Compared to the other Witches, who were chosen by their Witch Factors, the Valiant and the Saintess took in Factors of their own volition, attempting to obtain power that defied reality.<ref>''“It does not happen very often that someone takes in a Witch Factor of their own volition. The only ones who fit that description would be the Valiant and the Saintess, who attempted to obtain power that defied reality.”'' [[No Stella No Life 3]].</ref><ref>''“They are especially good-for-nothing. We were all discovered by our Witch Factors to become Witches. Whereas those two are different. They took in Factors of their own volition, pure aberrants reduced to Witch and Warlock.”'' [[No Stella No Life 3]].</ref> While the main seven sins are remembered to some extent in historical record, even though their names have become taboo due to the Witch Cult's influence, the sins of Vainglory and Melancholy seem to be completely absent from memory.

===Current===
====Witch of Vainglory, Pandora====
{{Main|Pandora}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 14 8.png|thumb|225px]]
The Saintess and the Witch of Vainglory, Pandora, represented one of the two "archaic" Deadly Sins, namely the sin of Vainglory. She had a distinct lack of empathy and was rarely seen to lose her composure. With her serene nature and unmatched otherworldly beauty, the Witch of Vainglory was comparable to a figure of divine origin. Like Hector of Melancholy, Pandora's role in the past was unrecorded, and with the exception of her familial relationship with her daughter, Echidna,<ref name="pandoramother" /> her history with the majority of the final members of the Witches of Sin remains ambiguous.

Her Authority of Vainglory allowed her to 'rewrite' events to her liking. With this tremendous power, Pandora could resurrect herself, manipulate the memories and senses of other people, and teleport people to distant locations among many other things. Out of the Witches, Pandora was the only one confirmed to have survived the Great Calamity, and she has since been involved with the Witch Cult that is claimed to worship Satella.

===Unknown===
====Warlock of Melancholy, Hector====
{{Main|Hector}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 14 6.png|thumb|left|225px]]
The Valiant and the Warlock of Melancholy, Hector, was one of the two "archaic" Deadly Sins and is currently the only known Warlock. Befitting the sin of Melancholy that he represented, Hector had a gloomy outlook on the world and disdained to work in a similar way to Sekhmet. He detested many things, including violence and exerting himself, although he wasn't above committing himself to either if it furthered his goals. Hector's role in history has been nearly forgotten, with only a handful of individuals remembering his existence.

The Authority of Melancholy seemed to give Hector the capability to manipulate gravitational fields, allowing him to apply a crush on anyone or anything that he wanted to. As the father of Echidna,<ref name="hectorfather" /> he felt a warped sense of love towards his daughter, which eventually caused him to start pursuing her. The Warlock of Melancholy and the Witch of Greed had a faceoff at the Sanctuary, sometime before the Great Calamity, with the result of it remaining unknown. Later on, Hector engaged in a battle with Roswaal and Clind, and in the end, his Witch Factor was inherited by the latter of the two, and it is implied that the Warlock of Melancholy died after the fight.

==Publicly Accepted Witches==
Those who fall under this category are people who have been publicly labeled or refer to themselves as a Witch, and yet they are accepted by public opinion. Those listed here may or may not have an Authority, but they have still received the label of Witch nonetheless.

===Current===
====Witch of Frost, Emilia====
{{Main|Emilia}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 8 12.png|thumb|225px]]
Although not fitting the proper criteria to become a Witch, Emilia has been dubbed the Witch of Frost, a nickname she later claimed for herself. Bearing neither a Witch Factor nor their Authorities, Emilia has been infamously reviled as a silver-haired half elf who bears an immense resemblance to the Witch of Envy. Her existence has caused many major factions no shortage of trouble; a century ago, when she was young, the Witch Cult attacked her home, with their associate, Pandora, intent on having Emilia use the key to the seal within Elior Forest. She awoke nearly a century later, being given the nickname her by a village man who she once sold glintstones to until an incident forced her to never visit the village again, at which point she showed her face to the man, and was called the Witch of Frost by him as she walked away. During the Royal Selection, the Witch Cult became active, intent on attacking Emilia at some points, whereas other times, she has been used to further certain people's schemes.

Despite the adversity against her, Emilia is a strong-willed, if naive, woman who is participating in the Royal Selection, not only for her own gain, but also to erase discrimination and bring equality to the people within Lugunica. In her efforts, she has been recognized as a major figure in quelling several disasters, which included events like the [[Battle for Priestella]], and she has even managed to accomplish feats said to be nigh impossible alongside her knight Natsuki Subaru, such as creating a temporary alliance between Lugunica and Vollachia.

Emilia's origins are murky, as are her connections to the Witches and the Witch Cult. However, not only is she beloved by spirits, but she is also immeasurably powerful. Furthermore, in the eyes of Pandora, the Witch of Vainglory, Emilia is the "Witch's daughter". As a young child, she unintentionally froze the entirety of Elior Forest and its residents, permanently changing the landscape. Alongside her immense power, she has charisma to match a monarch candidate, causing people of wildly different backgrounds and values to follow her.

===Former===
====Witch of Wisdom, Echidna====
{{Main|Echidna}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 15 11.png|thumb|left|225px]]
Before losing herself to become compatible with her Witch Factor and devolving into the Witch of Greed, Echidna, born to the Witch of Vainglory and the Warlock of Melancholy, was called the Witch of Wisdom, and she was so sought out be people to seek her knowledge that many attempted to earn her favor. A master of magic and a creator of many magical devices and spells, Echidna became responsible for creating many different legacies that remained in the world even centuries later, and she constantly researched the soul and the path to immortality.

A member of the [[Witch Era Party]], Echidna once traveled to save the world, putting her at odds with her parents, the [[Saintess Sect]], the Black Serpent, and other such factions and organizations. However, for unclear reasons, she separated from the party, going on to create Aldebaran in an attempt to fight and overcome Satella, who had become the Witch of Envy. However, as this ended in disaster and Echidna's near death, after sealing Aldebaran away, Echidna somehow devolved into the Witch of Greed and had become attached to the Castle of Dreams, where she resided over the trials of the Sanctuary.

==Other Witches==
Those who fall under this category are people who have been semi-recognized as Witches and Warlocks, yet have an ambiguous or nontraditional position among them due to their lack of a Witch Factor or Authority, their lack of a Witch-like reputation, how they are given their titles, whether or not they proclaim themselves as such, or other similar circumstances. Although, by extension, every user of an Authority can be considered a Witch or Warlock, there are those who do not identify with those titles, such as the Sin Archbishops and Clind, and accordingly, they are not considered as either.

===Current===
====Omega====
{{Main|Omega}}
[[File:Re Zero Witch's After Tea Party SS.png|thumb|225px]]
Following her unspecified demise four centuries ago, the Witch of Greed's soul was imprisoned to her tomb, where she had been resting for the past four centuries. Despite being dead, however, Echidna was still able to converse and interact with people from the world of the living, as long as they had entered the tomb and possessed the qualifications necessary for entering her "Tea Party". Roughly 10 years before Subaru's arrival to the new world, however, Echidna successfully managed to latch a part of her soul onto Ryuzu Shima, and she continued to pour more and more of her soul into the half-elf for the entirety of the following decade. On the day of the Sanctuary's fall, Echidna successfully managed to possess Shima's body, and thus the Witch was once against unleashed to the world, alongside the remaining deceased Witches' souls stored away in a glintstone. As Omega does not have a Witch Factor, she does not possess an Authority and is therefore only a Witch in name. In spite of that, she has the ability to project her soul, which emanates miasma. Furthermore, for unknown reasons, this version of Echidna is considered to be a different individual altogether from the historical Witch of Greed.

She claims to be on an aimless journey,<ref>''“I’ve told you this many times, but my journey is an aimless one. I cannot promise you that it’ll be a spectacular all-action grand adventure like you both desire.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 6]], [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Requirements to be a Witch]], Section 8.</ref> though in reality, Omega has decided to travel alongside others to prevent herself from being discovered by a currently unknown individual who is a shared enemy of the Witches in hopes of not standing out,<ref>''All of the Witches here in the Castle of Dreams knew that. It was not just Echidna after all. This someone was an enemy all of the Witches had in common.'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting]], Section 2.</ref><ref>''“Anyways, that’s why I don’t want to stand out. So rather than wandering around on my own and bringing about modern Witch-related legends, I’ll…”'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting]], Section 2.</ref> at the cost of this approach bringing other risks.<ref>''“There’s a chance I’m inviting different kinds of dangers, but there’s no way anyone would think that a Witch would be moving about with other people.”'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Witches's Evaluation Meeting]], Section 2.</ref> While travelling, Omega met Colette and her friend Palmyra. The two girls decided to travel with Omega, forming the Omega Party. They left to visit Gusteko, where they met Noelle Tuérico, and later on, Lilac and Shion, who all joined them.

===Former===
====Witch of Greed, Sphinx====
{{Main|Sphinx}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 34 8.png|thumb|left|225px]]
Sphinx was an artificial creation of Echidna, the Witch of Greed, in her immortality experiments before the Great Calamity. She is known to history as a leading figure in the Demi-Human War, where she used a spell known as the Sacrament of the Immortal King in order to raise the dead and turn them into corpse soldiers that fought against the [[Royal Army]]. Despite not owning a Witch Factor, she, like Omega, was a Witch in name who possessed parts of the Witch of Greed's soul within her.

After an incident with the Warlock of Melancholy at the Sanctuary, Ryuzu Meyer became encased in a magic crystal. The Witch of Greed began experimenting with immortality and attempted to create copies of Ryuzu in order to replicate her own existence. She constructed a replicant of Ryuzu Meyer with a similar mechanism for the Artificial Spirits she had already created. After she created the first replicant, she attempted to replicate her soul within it. However, the vessel was insufficient, and it could not completely inherit Echidna's full soul. As a result, the failure, named Sphinx, was left with a defective personality, an emotionless disposition, a fragment of Echidna's abilities, and miasma. Many years later, in the Kingdom of Lugunica, she became a member of the Demi-Human Alliance during the Demi-Human War and was responsible for the end of innumerable lives, causing her to be remembered as the only Witch besides Satella whose name was engraved into the Kingdom's history.

In the Sacred Vollachia Empire, Sphinx started a cataclysm known as the Great Disaster, an event foretold by the Empire's [[Stargazer]]s. Through unknown means involving [[Muspel]], she was able to turn Vollachia's deceased populace into [[Undead#Corebug-Based Zombies|zombies]] by using an application of restoration magic and the Sacrament of the Immortal King in tandem with insect-like creatures dubbed corebugs, which reside in every living corpse, act as their cores, and create new soldiers for Sphinx to use. She was killed by [[Cecilus Segmunt]] and became a zombie herself. During the Conquest of the Undead Capital, Sphinx was burned by [[Vincent Vollachia]]'s [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword]], almost burning her soul entirely until she pooled all of her knowledge together and analyzed it, resulting in her soul becoming complete and transforming her appearance into Echidna's. From then on, she used the mantle of the "Witch of Greed" as a substitute for a name, doing so because of the complexity of which name would be correct to use for herself. She continued to her attempt to destroy Vollachia until she was stopped by Natsuki Subaru and Spica, realizing her identity as Sphinx in the process, though not before indirectly forcing Priscilla Barielle to become a zombie to end the Great Disaster.

====Witch of Melancholy, Petra Leyte====
{{Main|Petra Leyte}}
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 42 7.png|thumb|225px]]
Born a young village girl in Arlam Village, her life was turned upside down when she met and had her life saved by Natsuki Subaru. In her love for him, she ended up becoming a maid for [[Roswaal Manor]], and she began learning maid duties, politics, and even magic in order to assist him. An intelligent girl, she took everything she learned and bravely used that knowledge to assist the entire [[Emilia Camp]] during the Royal Selection.

Before they were undone by Return by Death, during the events of the Arc 9 loop, when Aldebaran set upon his scheme to rid the world of Subaru, Petra read his Book of the Dead, intending to discover what Al's goal was. Despite the overwhelming risk that the book could cause her, she witnessed Return by Death, and after waking up, her will was greatly amplified in order to save and help Subaru. She spoke with Clind, the custodian of the Witch Factor of Melancholy who is acquainted with its function and unique qualities, learning of the existence of Witch Factors and what made people a Witch or Warlock, and gave up the possibility of becoming Subaru's bride as compensation for him to use the Authority. Although Petra initially did not take the Factor, she eventually decided to willingly use it for herself, intent on becoming a Witch and fighting alongside Subaru, who she recognized as a Warlock. By her own claim, will, and actions, Petra became the next Witch of Melancholy, willing to sacrifice what she felt was necessary to bear its Authority and resisting its "attraction".

Although she had only been a Witch for a short time, Petra used her Authority in very adaptable and ingenious ways. However, like other people, she was not compatible with the Witch Factor of Melancholy. Similarly, like Clind before her, she did not seem to have the Witch Factor inside of her body; instead, she seemed to be able to use its Authority from within the box it was sealed in. In the end, because of her intention to force Subaru to use Return by Death, the events that led to her becoming the Witch of Melancholy were entirely undone, and she no longer bears the Witch Factor or Authority of Melancholy.

==Trivia==
*The only person in history to have been a Witch by birth is Echidna.
*Nearly all of the Witches' names are related to asteroids and mythological beings, excluding Omega, whose namesake comes from the final letter of the Greek alphabet, and Satella, whose name is scheduled to be explained in the [[Arc 12|final arc]].<ref>[https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/476712575561125888 2014 AskFM Q&A]</ref>
**Despite this, "Omega" is commonly used in astronomy and astrology, while Satella's name bears a similarity with "Stella", the Latin word for star.
*As stated by the author, all of the Witches will reappear in the final arc.<ref>[https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/476340962403581952 2014 AskFM Q&A]</ref>
*According to the author, in terms of common sense, the Witches of Sin are ranked as follows: Sekhmet > Carmilla > Daphne > Echidna > Minerva > Typhon; Satella isn't included because she doesn't even have a word like that in her dictionary.<ref>Narō impression response on June 1, 2013, at 18:45 JST</ref>
*According to the author, in terms of how much of a schemer the Witches of Sin (excluding Satella) are, they can be ranked as follows: Echidna >>>>> Carmilla >> Sekhmet = Daphne >>> Typhon >>>>> Minerva.<ref>Narō impression response on June 3, 2013, at 13:55 JST</ref>
*According to the author, the strength ranking of the seven Witches of Sin is as follows: Satella >> Sekhmet >>> Typhon > Daphne >> Echidna > Carmilla >>>>> Minerva (Minerva being by far the weakest in offense due to her healing abilities).<ref>Narō impression response on June 3, 2013, at 22:16 JST</ref>
*According to the author, the scale of being a danger to the world among the Witches of Sin (excluding Satella) is as follows: Minerva >> Daphne > Carmilla > Typhon > Echidna >>>>>> Sekhmet.<ref>[https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/422402886002159616 2014 Author's Comment]</ref>
*In the [[Re:Zero EX#Re:Zero Academy|Re:Zero School EX chapter]], the ages of the Witches of Sin (excluding Satella) from oldest to youngest were as follows: Sekhmet, Minerva, Echidna, Carmilla, Daphne, and Typhon.
*Beatrice and Echidna initially states that she (Echidna) and the other Witches were killed by the Witch of Envy, but later it is revealed that most of their deaths (with the exception of Minerva, who is the only one actually stated to have been killed by the Witch of Envy) had no involvement from the Witch of Envy.
*Originally, each Witch had two image colors that represented them; Echidna's were white and black, Minerva's were blue and white, Sekhmet's were black and grey, Daphne's were black and purple, Typhon's were blue and green, Carmilla's were red and pink, Pandora's are gold and white, and Hector's are gold and brown.
*The Sacrament of the Immortal King is an ancient and incredibly powerful spell and forbidden art created by an unknown Witch long ago.<ref>''"It was one of the exceptional magics, supposedly created by a witch who held the world in thrall, before the knowledge was lost."'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], Felix Argyle's Curse, Section 8.</ref> Originally, the spell was thought to be capable of fully reviving a dead person, and there are legends of the aforementioned Witch being supposedly capable of bringing back people exactly as they were before their demise.<ref>''The Witch who invented the spell had been said to be able to bring the dead back, looking exactly as they had in life, but that part of the spell had not been passed down.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], Felix Argyle's Curse, Section 8.</ref>
*The Spirit Eaters (which [[Arakiya]] descends from) were created in the distant past to oppose an unnamed Witch who charmed all. The [[Oni|Oni Tribe]] and their ability to sense miasma is implied to play a similar role.<ref>''Created in ancient times to oppose a lone Witch who charmed all, whom even the wordless great spirit obeyed, they were beings devised for the purpose of fighting, much like the Oni Clan that could sense miasma.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 2, Section 5.</ref>
*Despite Sages and Sage Candidates being supposedly immune to or unaffected by a Witch's miasma, Subaru, someone recognized by two different Witches as a Sage Candidate, though he was able to stand in the center of several Witches all at once while being unaffected by their miasma, when he was later exposed to the miasma in one of the paths beneath the Pleiades Watchtower, he was affected and driven into a murderous frenzy alongside his companions. Whether this means that the miasma there is different from what is exuded from the Witches is unknown.
**There are also types of minerals called [[Mana#Mana-Related Natural Resources|Magical Miasma Stones]] that also emit miasma. Whether this is different or the same as the miasma generated by Witches is unknown.
*According to Omega, Shion and Lilac have the potential to be called a Witch due to their talent in Dream Arts, dedication to the art, and their lifespans.
*The forbidden art Ol Shamak, which was made by Echidna, was specifically made to counter Witch Factor bearers like the Witches.
*In the game [[Re:Zero Witch’s Re:surrection]], the character [[Isolde]] was set to be a Witch who represented an unknown sin. The other game-original character, [[Belka]], was of the unique profession of researching Witches.
*One of the Four Mass-Scale Disasters said to hit the Four Great Nations is called the Witch(es) of the Kingdom. However, it is unclear which specific Witch this refers to or how many Witches will be involved.
**Sphinx, before becoming the Great Disaster, had originally set her sights on becoming the Witch of the Kingdom.
*Before she became the Witch of Greed in the truest sense, Echidna was already referred to as a Witch.
*Exclusively to the Sasageru IF, Petra remained the Witch of Melancholy for 400 years, and she became feared to a similar extent to Satella.
*According to the author among all of the Witches besides Satella, Carmilla would be the most difficult to capture both ability- and personality-wise.<ref>''"If, by abilities, you mean combat, you’re likely to die just from approaching both Typhon and Carmilla, so in terms of abilities, their difficulty would be high. In terms of personality, I think the hateful Carmilla that everyone adores would be the most difficult woman to capture. You’d fall for her right away."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref>
*According to the author, the Witch of Sin were not aimlessly going around killing people. Most of their kills happened to be a matter of circumstance or coincidence, such as being hungry, seeing a bad person, or as a side effect of their Authority.<ref>''"Nah, I don’t think that would happen, why do you think that? The witches aren’t really aimlessly hurting people, you know? They just eating because they’re hungry, twisting someone’s arm because they look like a bad person, and when they go walking, nearby people’s hearts just happen to stop."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref>
