Six unnamed younger sisters |Magic = |Divine Protection = |Authority = |Weapon = |Equipment = |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 27|Volume 27]] |Manga = |Anime = |Game = |Japanese Voice = |English Voice = }} '''Zikr Osman''' (ズィクル・オスマン) is a Second-Class General of the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire's]] [[Imperial Army]]. Though his initial role in his debut was as the general sent to quell the People of Shudrak, he ended up playing a supporting role in [[Arc 7]] and [[Arc 8]]. Having grown up in a family full of women, he is a man famous for his respect and love for women. As a general, however, he is commonly referred to as the Coward, often finding ways to find victory with as little direct confrontation as possible, even going so far as to retreat to keep his soldiers from throwing their lives away, earning the respect of those beneath him. ==Appearance== Zikr is a short, plump, and rather frail-looking man. He has a thick moustache, bushy eyebrows, and a hairstyle that would best be described as an afro. He wears a decorated military uniform and has a sword to his side. ==Personality== While he is a lustful, kind, and very respectful man when talking to women, or even those dressed as women, Zikr is also a very tactful individual who thinks about his problems whilst acting accordingly instead of throwing everything at a problem. Unlike other generals, Zikr takes time to bond with his troops and gets to know them. Zikr is very devoted to the emperor, and upon learning that the dancer Bianca is actually [[Vincent Vollachia|Vincent]], he surrendered himself and his troops immediately and pledged loyalty to him. He is also shown to be rather caring towards his allies, as shown when he shielded [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]] from [[Arakiya]]’s attack. Also, though he originally despised being called the Coward and was willing to take up the moniker of the Womanizer to wash away that name, after being praised by the emperor for the reason he was called the Coward, he has taken to referring to himself as such and doing so proudly. Although Zikr himself is also a man of the Empire and is willing to take up arms for his country, despite his own lacking skill with the sword,''It was not that he lamented that. Of course, Zikr was a man of the Empire. Due to that, he swung his sword on the front lines, and the first time he swung it, his heart yearned for him to exist in a way reminiscent of the Nine Divine Generals, who would be able to alter the war situation.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 96, Section 3. he also sympathizes with those who are afraid or unable to bring themselves to fight, such as [[Heinkel Astrea]]. In fact, he even believes it to be too cruel to impose the imperial way onto people like that, especially when they were not a part of the Empire.''When he overtook the red-haired swordsman, who bent his knee on the battlefield and hung his head as if his fighting spirit was disheartened, what flashed through the mind of Zikr Osman was sympathy for following the natural course of life. The brave woman of crimson who introduced herself as Priscilla Barielle had boldly taken part in this rebellion. The swordsman, participating in the war as her follower, was probably not even a person of the Vollachian Empire. It was far too cruel to impose the Empire’s way of being that the people of the Empire must be strong on a guy like him.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 96, Section 3. ==History== Zikr was born into House Osman, which was a household that produced a lineage of soldiers for many generations. However, due to a blood imbalance in his generation, he was the only male born in his family.''The Osman household had produced a lineage of soldiers for generations, but in Zikr’s generation the blood had been unbalanced, and, for some reason, the family had only sired females.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 21, Section 1. Due to this, he was raised in an environment with four older sisters and six younger sisters. He soon joined the Imperial Army at a young age, and from there, he began to desire giving kindness to women whilst receiving kindness from then in return. Eventually, Zikr became a general, and he began employing skillful and steady tactics while making sure that his allies took few casualties. Although he was initially known as the "Coward" for his methods, Zikr's tastes in women gave him many opportunities to speak with other soldiers and officers, and in combination with his threatening prowess as a commander, he soon became known in the army as the "Womanizer". During [[Gaoran Peitiet]]’s rebellion, Zikr was still a Third-Class General. He was promoted to become a Second-Class General at some point before his appearance in Arc 7. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Despite his rank within the Imperial Army, Zikr is not a very strong man. Instead, the danger lies within his mind and leadership skills which has allowed him to ascend in a power-worshipping nation. ===Intelligence=== '''Keen Intellect''': Zikr became a General Second-Class, not for his physical strength, but for his strategical mind. He often finds manners of taking victory with as little direct confrontation as possible, something which has left him dubbed as the Coward, a title that even his emperor respects. It is because of this that he was entrusted with handling the Shudrakians in Buddheim Jungle and defending [[Guaral]]. ===Equipment=== *'''Sword''': Zikr carries a sword with him. However, he does not have much skill with the blade, so it is more of an ornament for him or something he uses while leading and rallying his troops. ==Trivia== *Zikr has his own named chapter in the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)#Arc 7: The Land of Wolves|web novel]], while in the [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 27|light novel]], it was adapted as an interlude that was not listed in the table of contents. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Soldiers]] [[Category:Generals]] [[Category:Imperial Army]]

[[Medium O'Connell]] (sister-in-law) |Magic = |Divine Protection = |Authority = |Weapon = Bow and Arrow |Equipment = |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 26|Volume 26]] |Manga = |Anime = |Game = |Japanese Voice = |English Voice = }} '''Taritta Shudrak''' (タリッタ・シュドラク) is a member and former Chieftain of the [[Terminology#Races and Clans/Tribes|People of Shudrak]] who live in the depths of the Buddheim Jungle in the [[Vollachia Empire]]. She played a supporting role in [[Arc 7]]. Born to the People of Shudrak as the younger sister of [[Mizelda Shudrak|Mizelda]], she spent her youth feeling inferior to her prodigal sister. Following the demise of her soul sister, the [[Stargazer]] [[Mariuli Shudrak|Mariuli]], she lived while awaiting the day to complete Mariuli's commandment. However, after temporarily taking up the mantle of Chieftain she shed herself of both her inferiority and the commandment. In the aftermath of the [[Great Disaster]], Taritta, with Mizelda and the other Shudraks' approval, relinquished the role of Chieftain to her older sister in order to stay with [[Flop O'Connell]]. ==Appearance== Taritta is a tall woman with brown skin and black hair, which has been dyed blue at the tips. Like her Shudrak counterparts, she wears revealing clothing with big round golden earrings. During the [[Fall of Guaral|siege]] of [[Guaral]], she dressed to appear as an exotic dancer. On the road to [[Chaosflame]], she wore a white dress shirt with a bow tie under a purple blazer and purple dress jeans. ==Personality== Unlike most of her people, Taritta is reserved and highly unconfident about her abilities despite being a warrior. She feels disappointment for perceiving herself to have inferior abilities to her older sister, so she consequentially allows herself to be ordered around by other people. She even confided in [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]] about her inferiority complex and that she didn't feel like she would be able to effectively lead her people like her sister could, and she even claimed to be jealous over how Subaru was able to be so confident while he was in his role as "Natsumi Schwartz". However, when she is hunting, Taritta is calm and efficient in executing techniques to finish a prey off. Her lack of confidence stems from guilt for the death of her soul sister, Mariuli, as Taritta holds herself responsible for her death and believes that she let Mariuli die. She shows hatred to the stars that changed Mariuli by choosing her as a Stargazer. Believing they contributed to her early death, she would disobey their will and break her promise with Mariuli if she judged it to be the right thing. ==History== Taritta was born on the same day as Mariuli, her soul sister. The two were inseparable while growing up. Unlike her soul sister, Taritta was able to become a hunter like her most of the other Shudraks, while Mariuli took care of the children due to her frail constitution. Eventually, Mariuli became a Stargazer and soon became very sick, almost reaching her demise. Before her death, she told Taritta of her "commandment", being a mission to kill a traveler with black hair and black eyes in order to prevent them from triggering the "[[Great Disaster]]", which would spell the end for the Empire. After relaying her commandment, Mariuli plunged Taritta's knife into her chest and died as a result, with [[Utakata Shudrak|Utakata]] witnessing this event. Due to the circumstances of having her knife found in Mariuli's chest, Taritta was initially suspected of murdering Mariuli, but Utakata defended her innocence. After the incident was settled, Taritta resolved day after day to carrying out Mariuli's commandment on her behalf, and she waited patiently like a hunter for the "traveler" foretold by the commandment to appear. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Taritta is a powerful warrior capable of handling herself against numerous physically enhanced enemies at once, and she is such a prodigy that even her sister acknowledges her. This being said, her strength is still such that she cannot contend with truly powerful people. ===Physical Traits/Flow Method=== '''Skilled Markswoman''': Just like her fellow Shudrakians, Taritta is very skilled with her bow. She can easily dispatch her targets from afar. Even amongst the Shudrak, her marksmanship is exceptional, as she is able to locate weak spots and accurately aim at them with relative ease while others struggled to do the same,''Before the struggling duo, Taritta quickly fired three arrows from her bow. As three stone golems approached Mizelda’s back in the distance, the arrows pierced the three bodies through their back, head, and thigh, killing them.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 93, Section 1.''Apparently, she really did not do much more than look closely. Taritta was indeed Mizelda’s sister, although her personality was so opposite to hers that it was difficult to tell.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 93, Section 1. as well as easily shoot [[Dragon#Flying Dragons|flying dragons]] out of the sky with headshots after no more than a mere glance.''Taritta blinked once, then twice, and nodded, and the next moment, with blinding speed, she drew and nocked an arrow, and shot it right over their heads. Immediately afterward, Frederica looked up hearing cries of pain high in the sky, and saw a flying dragon spinning and falling to the ground a short distance away from the three of them. The arrow that hit the flying dragon under its chin pierced all the way through to the top of its head, killing it.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 91, Section 1. '''Enhanced Eyesight''': Taritta has excellent eyesight that can easily surpass a beastified [[Frederica Baumann]]'s, allowing her to see across a battlefield with ease.''Frederica was struck speechless at the sisters that conversed nonchalantly as they gazed at the rampart in the distance. As a half-beast, Frederica currently had better eyesight than usual in her beast form. Even so, she could see nothing other than the cloud of dust that hung over the wall the pair were gazing at.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 91, Section 1. ===Other=== '''Excellent Stealth''': As a hunter, being able to hide herself from her prey is a common tactic. She was easily able to find and hide from Subaru when he first arrived in Buddheim Jungle, and though she just barely failed in the main timeline, she was responsible for Subaru's first death in Vollachia. ===Equipment=== *'''Bow and Arrow''': Like most Shudrakians, she wields a bow for combat. ==Trivia== *Taritta has her own named chapter in Arc 7, in both the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)#Arc 7: The Land of the Wolves|web novel]] and [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 30|light novels]]. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:People of Shudrak]] [[Category:Leaders]]

[[Reinhard van Astrea]] (descendant) |Weapon = Old sword |Equipment = Satchel |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]] (side story)}} '''Toska Astrea''' (トスカ・アストレア) is one of the main supporting characters in [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], a side story released with [[Re:Zero 2nd Season BD 5]]. He lived during the era of the [[Witch]]es, predating even the [[Great Calamity]]. When he was around 15 years old, Toska ventured to find the Witch of Greed, [[Echidna]], to request her help in repelling a [[Dragon|Blight Dragon]] attack and saving the life of his childhood friend, [[Minor Characters#Remina|Remina]]. He died some time beyond the age of 150. ==Appearance== Throughout most of Loving the Days Gone By, Toska was around 15 years of age. He was a relatively tall and handsome young boy with flaming red hair and sky-blue eyes, characteristics that indicate a person's connection to [[House Astrea]]. He was usually seen dressed in rough clothes befitting of his family's profession as farmers and was equipped with a rough satchel made out of fur. Around his waist, Toska wore a tawdry sword which was noted to look rather old and borderline useless. ==Personality== Toska had a rather timid personality, but he was ultimately a very brave man. When his childhood friend Remina was set up as a sacrifice for the Blight Dragons, he wasted no time and darted towards the Palace of the Witch, overcoming numerous trials and obstacles just to reach it. When faced with two Artificial Spirits, he was able to retain his composure and voice his wishes, which in turn prompted both [[Beatrice]] and [[Puck]] to help him. Despite him being a meager 15 years old, he displayed immense courage, despite facing powerful beings such as [[Spirit|Great Spirits]], Witches, and Dragons themselves. He was also shown to be rather high-spirited and fun to be around with, once he got more familiar with the other party. He was even capable of cracking jokes and pranks on Beatrice, despite her being the daughter of the Witch. His personality was rather in-tone with Puck's, resulting in them forming a rather friendly bond. Toska is also shown to be easily influenced by others, as seen when he retold the story about his older brother telling him how he'll become stronger if he ate stronger beings. This resulted in him being prepared to eat an entire Guiltylowe, despite it tasting horribly and even being toxic for consumption.''"It's not that I'm hungry...... It's just that, big brother had once earlier said that I'd get stronger if I ate strong creatures, so just out of habit."'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1. Furthermore, Toska was shown to be rather humble. Despite possessing inhuman strength, speed, agility, and skills with the sword, he considered himself normal. Whenever the two Artificial Spirits complimented him, Toska's replies were always that of embarrassment and denial, stating he's slightly better than average at best. One could easily surmise this self-dejection came from growing up in the shadow of the first Sword Saint Reid Astrea. This also led him to underestimate his achievements, as shown when he called an aquatic [[Witchbeast|witchbeast]] that had terrorized a nearby town for a while, "a fish".''"When I'm eating nothing but witchbeasts, you two have a grim look in your eyes at the time of campfire, so I tried catching fish in the river today..."'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1. ==History== Toska was born in a secluded and tiny village called Carnattse, to a family of farmers. When he was about 15 years of age, Toska's childhood friend Remina was chosen as a sacrifice for the Blight Dragons, due to them wanting to take revenge on Toska's brother's family, as his older brother had slaughtered their leader, [[Minor Characters#Amangam|Amangam]]. As running away with her would result in the destruction of the village, Toska opted for a different kind of salvation–seeking the Witch of Greed to have his wish granted. Toska then started his journey, successfully managed to reach the Witch's palace at the top of a mountain, thanks to his powerful body and sharp determination fueled by his mighty wish. To his surprise, he was welcomed by the Witch of Greed's daughter, Beatrice, who back then had the task of acting as a proxy instead of her absent mother. Toska's wish having been accepted by Beatrice, him, her and Puck then started their 9 days long journey to Carnattse in order to save Remina from the Blight Dragon. Once the trio arrived at the village, Beatrice quickly made a plan after noticing that the villagers had no intent of fighting the Dragon. The plan ended up in Beatrice successfully killing the Blight Dragon by surprise, but unfortunately for them, the Dragon they killed was actually under the orders of [[Minor Characters#Fargall|Fargall]]: the Dragon behind the sacrifice. Fargall was in fact scheming to slaughter all villagers of Carnattse in reprisal due to Toska's brother having killed a Dragon leader. This led to a fight between Puck in his Star Beastification form, Beatrice, and Toska and Fargall. With the help of the villagers, Toska's group emerged victorious. However, as they were thinking they finally saved Remina and the village, an army of one hundred Silver Dragons appeared in the sky, determined to kill Toska and his kin. Toska, Beatrice, and Puck, refusing to give up, were ready to fight the Dragons with all their might, until the Witch of Greed suddenly arrived, and with one single spell, managed to annihilate the Dragons as stars were falling down onto them. After Echidna's attack, only four Dragons remained alive, Fargall being one of them, and they finally surrendered and complied. Sometime after Fargall's defeat, Toska and Remina's wedding was held, in which Echidna, Beatrice, and Puck took part in. Once Puck left to start his journey, Toska made a vow with Beatrice, promising that he shall one day repay his debt to her. Later on, Toska and Remina had many children, who also had children, who then had children too. More than a century after the trio's journey to Carnattse, Toska, now an old man, heard about Beatrice's everlasting solitude and decided to repay his debt by helping her. [[Roswaal L. Mathers|Roswaal D. Mathers]] then brought Toska to the Forbidden Library, in which he begged Beatrice to take his hand; he wanted her to leave so that she wouldn't feel lonely anymore. Unfortunately for him, Beatrice refused to give up on the contract and duty given by her mother, which resulted in her kicking Toska out of the library. After being kicked out, Toska lied on the ground, started to wail and cry while pleading for someone to save the kindhearted girl from solitude as he was wishing for her happiness. Toska then died of old age an unknown amount of time later. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Toska's strength could only be described as inhuman. He was easily able to defeat a Guiltylowe and even compete with a Dragon. Furthermore, having grown up with Reid, he became accustomed to being punched by him and was even capable of catching his strikes.April 5, 2026 Talk Show. Despite that, it's worth noting that Toska is still vastly weaker to his older brother.''"Yes. I have an elder brother who is slightly older than me...... though he is so strong, you wouldn't believe he belongs to this world"'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1. According to him, during their duels, he could not stop shaking out of fear, a feeling he'd later experience when facing off Blight Dragons.''"Please stop, Puck-sama. You'll know once you see any actual Dragons... They're, not like this stupid dog. For my body to tremble non-stop during a confrontation, has happened for the first time ever since with big brother."'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1. ===Physical Traits/Flow Method=== '''Inhuman Speed''': Toska was shown to easily be able to sprint at the speed of gale. He traversed the path down the mountain in mere half a day when it would take over a day for a normal person to get back down to the Witch's Forest. To a bystander observing him run, it would appear as if Toska's legs were invisible.''His sprint was so excessively swift that, to a bystander, Toska’s legs would appear as invisible, and any witchbeasts or stray dogs that attempted to pounce and halt him were all deserted behind, their opportunity galloping past them.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1. '''Inhuman Swordsmanship''': Toska was very skilled with his sword. According to Puck, his abilities were nothing short of monstrous.''"Half a day since their departure from the Palace of the Witch, Toska's swordsmanship had exemplarily exited the montane forest, and they had successfully escaped the mountain as well as the forest of the Witch. Nothing existed for Beatrice to draw a comparison with, but by Puck's word his accomplishment was akin to monstrous."'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1. He was easily able to cut down multiple Guiltylowe and even referred to them as "stupid dogs". ==Trivia== *At a talk show held on April 6, 2026, it was confirmed that Toska's name was Toska Astrea and that he was Reid's brother. *It's been heavily hinted that the current members of House Astrea are in fact direct descendants of Toska rather than of Reid. ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Lugunica Navbox}} [[Category:Deceased]]

[[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 28|Volume 28]] (main story) |Manga = |Anime = |Game = |Japanese Voice = |English Voice =}} '''Ubilk''' (ウビルク) is a former [[Stargazer]] in the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]]. He worked for Vollachia's emperor, [[Vincent Vollachia]]. He played an antagonistic role in [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]] and a supporting role in [[Arc 7]] and [[Arc 8]]. A member of the endangered Evil Eye Tribe, Ubilk found himself enslaved on [[Ginunhive]], where he became a male prostitute to survive. Coming to be the mastermind of the [[Ginunhive Armed Rebellion|rebellion]] five years after his enslavement, he managed to escape the island, his goals unknown. At some point, however, he became a Stargazer and became a valuable asset to the emperor, going on to pass on knowledge of the [[Great Disaster]] to Vincent. He eventually fulfilled his commandment and lost his status as a Stargazer,''Sensing that the fog which had always occupied a corner of his mind had cleared up, his thoughts were suddenly free from the influence of the fog, and Ubilk became aware that he no longer was a Stargazer.'' [[Arc 8]], Interlude, Section 1. and afterward, he settled on travelling the world. ==Appearance== Ubilk is a handsome young man with rather long grey hair and livid grey eyes. Roughly 7 years ago, he was seen wearing tattered clothing consisting of an oversized dark long-sleeved robe and pants of the same color as well as a white-striped, purple undershirt. In the present, his robe is fixed of its tears and has an added hood. Furthermore, Ubilk can be seen sporting a necklace with a green crystal and twin bows tying his long hair in place. On the center of his chest is a burn scar where his Evil Eye once laid. and after prophesizing [[Gaoran Peitiet]]'s rebellion, he was allowed by Vincent to be a unique personage who had access to enter the Crystal Palace in order to deliver prophecies to him. ===[[Sword Identity Part 1|Sword Identity]]=== Two to three months after the death of [[Balleroy Temeglyph]], Ubilk attended a meeting centered around the topic of Balleroy's replacement, only to be unwelcomed due to his sudden appearance and his failure to predict events concerning the previous rebellion. While there, Ubilk prophesized [[Yorna Mishigure|Yorna]]'s rebellion by using his power and suggested using the revolt as a way to determine who would take Balleroy's place. ===Pre-[[Imperial Civil War#Imperial Coup|Imperial Coup]]=== During one of Ubilk's visits to the castle, he spoke with Chisha and Vincent, saying that the Great Disaster had been foretold by the stars,''"――The coming of the Great Disaster has been passed down in a commandment. It is regrettable, Your Excellency."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 6. something that he brought up with the intention of informing Chisha about.''"I know, I know. Buuut~, if His Excellency has trouble speaking about the matter, I thought it’d be better if I did. That’s why I’m present together with General First-Class Chisha, isn’t that so?"'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 6. When Chisha began questioning him, having not heard of this Great Disaster, Ubilk claimed that it would bring ruin, also mentioning Yang Sword's glow, implying he knew about what went down with Prisca and resulting in Chisha nearly killing him for it. Afterward, he claimed that it would be the death of Vincent Vollachia that would trigger the Great Disaster.''"――The death of His Excellency Vincent Vollachia, that will be the signal for the beginning of the commandment."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 6. A few days later, having come to realize that he had no way to directly reject Vincent's thoughts, Chisha cornered Ubilk, intent on getting answers out of him. Despite the threats of Ubilk's inevitable death because of Vincent's possible death, Ubilk was undeterred and merely claimed that his role was to prevent the destruction that was to follow the Great Disaster,''"More important than my own destruction, is the fulfillment and realization of the commandment. My purpose, is to ward off the destruction due to follow the Great Disaster."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 8. and if the Great Disaster didn't occur, since he would need to fulfill his commandment, he would become one of the causes to trigger the Great Disaster.''"If the Great Disaster doesn’t actually happen, my commandment won’t be fulfilled. For that reason, even if all the factors that’d cause the Great Disaster are destroyed, I’d become said factor."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 8. Though Chisha was tempted to kill him to prevent that, Ubilk merely claimed another [[Stargazer]] would appear in his place. Afterward, he mentioned that four disasters would occur to destroy the world and that the time to stop one of them has come.''"Four major disasters will destroy the world. The opportunity to stop one of them has come. We are terminals of self-purification and self-defense brought about by the stars, and there are infinite substitutes."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 8. As he thought about what to do, he asked how the commandment was conveyed to Ubilk, and when Ubilk said he would have dreams, Chisha claimed to wonder which Vincent it was he saw in his dream, using his Noh to paint over himself and become "Vincent Vollachia".''"――The Vincent Vollachia that dies there, which one is it, I wondeeer?"'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 8. ==Abilities== '''Evil Eye''' (魔眼 ''Magan''): Ubilk is a member of the Evil Eye Tribe, and like the other members of his tribe, he was born with an Evil Eye which, in his case, was situated in the middle of his chest. Although the power itself was never outright stated, according to Ubilk and Priscilla, it was what allowed him to start his rebellion on Ginunhive in the first place. Priscilla came to the idea that it could have had an ability related to sensing the emotions of others, though Ubilk denied his Evil Eye was that convenient and claimed it would not have worked on her anyway, suggesting that there were requirements for it to work on someone. He later burned it off of his body, leaving nothing but a scar. '''[[Stargazer]]''' (星詠み, ''Hoshiyomi''): Ubilk was a Stargazer who used his power of peering into the future in order to preserve the Vollachia Empire's stability,''“It's not too far from your perception. The power of the Stargazer is to peer into tomorrow, in order to preserve the Empire.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 34, Section 1. namely with things such as larger-scale rebellions or conflicts.''“Your Excellency, there's no need to get upset. Even if I sense a rebellion incoming, I'd prefer to have it their way and let it break out first, then mow the seedling down before it grows further. And that's because I agree with your thoughts.”'' [[The Land of Wolves / Death unto the Weak, No Mercy ZERO Vincent]] Section 3. However, Ubilk seemingly worked for the greater benefit of the nation, and not solely for the emperor's good, which is why he allowed for Vincent to be dethroned and exiled.''“I told you, the power of the Stargazer is for the preservation of the Empire. I think it'd also be cool It's not necessarily compatible with my safety.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 34, Section 1. He has claimed that the stars guide him, even when crossing a battlefield. Berstetz had once seen this in action, as Ubilk managed to leisurely cross a literal storm of projectiles and forest of swords without so much as getting a single scratch.''Ubilk had once leisurely walked through a literal rainstorm of projectiles and a forest of swords without suffering a single scratch. Ubilk claimed to follow the whisperings of the stars, but Berstetz could not determine whether him possessing superhuman fighting skills was true or false. If one thing could be said for certain, then it was that he was enveloped by a power beyond human understanding, be it the whispering of the stars or Ubilk’s own abilities.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 106, Section 1. '''Excellent Tactician''': Though he doesn't show this side of himself after becoming a Stargazer, Ubilk is a remarkable tactician, which he displayed when he began the revolt in Ginunhive and gathered supporters to his cause. ==Trivia== *Ubilk has his own named interlude in Arc 8 in both the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)#Arc 8: Vincent Vollachia|web novel]] and [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36|light novels]]. ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Lupugana]] [[Category:Ginunhive]] [[Category:Evil Eye Tribe]] [[Category:Slaves]] [[Category:Gladiators]] [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Prostitutes]] [[Category:Stargazer]] [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[Category:Arc 7 Antagonists]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

[[Eugard Vollachia]] (former lover) (as Iris) |Equipment = Kiseru |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 28|Volume 28]]}} '''Yorna Mishigure''' (ヨルナ・ミシグレ) is the '''Third ranking [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Divine General]]''' of the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]] and the ruler of the [[Chaosflame|Demon City of Chaosflame]]. She plays a major supporting role in [[Arc 7]] and [[Arc 8]], and she is one of the main characters in the [[Re:Zero EX#Iris and the King of Thorns|Iris and the King of Thorns]] EX chapter. Originally born as '''Iris''', a village girl and former lover of [[Eugard Vollachia]], she was killed by a [[Volcas|former ally]] of hers, and her story with Eugard was immortalized in the tale of Iris and the King of Thorns. She was cursed to reincarnate with her memories for the next 300 years by Eugard. One of those lives included the woman named '''Sandra Benedict''', who gave birth to [[Priscilla Barielle|Prisca Benedict]]. ==Appearance== Yorna is a beautiful and tall fox woman with a thin and alluring physique. Perhaps her most striking facial feature is her slit blue eyes that give off a languid yet sharp look that can captivate anyone with whom she crosses sight. Her hair is neatly arranged, primarily white in color but slowly shifts to orange towards its tips. Furthermore, Yorna adorns her head in a variety of animal bones, horns, teeth, scales and other ornaments, making her appearance majestic and somewhat mythical. As a fox human, she has a pair of sharp orange fox ears and, uniquely, nine white and orange fox tails. Adorning herself in a richly colored kimono that vaguely exposes her thin white shoulders, Yorna gives off an incredibly languid and relaxed air. Her attire consists of a primarily blue kimono with a floral pattern, that has its sleeve edges and its collar's colors in bright green. She keeps it all together with a green belt that has a black floral pattern adorning it. In addition, Yorna can usually be seen smoking from her purple and golden kiseru. As Iris, she was a human who had flax hair tied in a braid and blue eyes. She wore a red dress with orange and black around the ends of the sleeves and the hem, a blue hood, and she wore red shoes. She was described as having a plain face and plain features. ==Personality== Yorna can best be described as problematic and hard to deal with, having even been described by [[Zikr Osman]] as someone with a desire for destruction, and according to [[Kafma Irulux]], she represents a danger to the emperor. Despite bearing the rank of "Seventh", she frequently starts revolts which have forced Vincent to dispatch the [[Imperial Army]] and the Divine Generals more than once, though he considers her too necessary for Chaosflame, to have her be executed for treason, effectively making her some sort of a trouble-child of the Nine Divine Generals. Furthermore, despite her hatred for the Empire and the Imperial Way that governs it,''"Do you happen to hate this country?"'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 47, Section 1.''"I do, too."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 47, Section 1. Yorna's goal was connected to the position of the emperor of Vollachia, and though [[Vincent Vollachia]] could only speculate that her wishes were to be the emperor's favorite mistress due to the vagueness of her goal,''"She won't divulge the details, but I'm fairly certain that's how she sees it. What she wants is the top of the Empire… to be the favorite mistress of the Emperor of Vollachia. It doesn’t have to be me."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 39, Section 3 she wanted desperately to repeal the extinction decree put on the wolf and mole humans that was put in place centuries ago by her lover Eugard Vollachia, both for their sake and her own, as repealing the decree would also result in her soul being free from her curse.''"――. It is in regards to the shackles upon my soul, endlessly invoking its reincarnation."'' [[Arc 8]], Curtain's Close, Section 3.''"――I wish to repeal it. To annul the decree of extinction put out by the Empire in regards to the wolfpeople and the molepeople."'' [[Arc 8]], Curtain's Close, Section 3. She was ultimately able to achieve her goal following the [[Great Disaster]], successfully convincing Eugard to have the decree repealed. When conversing and interacting with others, Yorna tends to act in an extremely relaxed and almost spoiled manner, appearing somewhat arrogant which can be seen with her often taking her time to answer even to the very emperor of the Vollachian Empire. Furthermore, her words are often provoking or teasing, which often tends to anger people with shorter tempers, such as the aforementioned Kafma. She is not above spinning a situation into a conflict for her own amusement, with [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]] initially noting that she was far more vicious and terrible than he had imagined her from hearing everything Vincent and Zikr had to say about her after seeing how she handled both Vincent's and his enemies' envoys during a meeting. In some ways, she's remarkably similar to Priscilla Barielle, but with next to no verbal abuse and a much more languid tone. This being said, she primarily showed this while speaking towards people who were intent on dragging her into their affairs, and when speaking with other people, she has shown to be rather friendly and easy to speak to. Yorna also has a very soft spot for children and [[Demi-Human|demi-humans]], and after becoming a Divine General, despite her overall goal, she prioritized making a safe haven for demi-humans.''"All along, such had been my desire… Though, when I became a Divine General, I had prioritized acquiring the Demon City, so as to have a location to welcome my beloved children."'' [[Arc 8]], Curtain's Close, Section 3. Because of her love for her people, those very people treasure her, offering her various gifts made from parts of themselves, which Yorna treasures, to the point that she finds it loathsome that those precious gifts act as substitutes for her life during battle.''"Needless to say, to treat the gifts of my beloved children as a mere number of substitutes for my life is utterly loathsome."'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 101, Section 2. She is willing to go to extreme lengths in order to protect her people, and whenever she started a rebellion against the Empire, it was always for another person's sake.''Whenever the Flamboyant, Yorna Mishigure, rose in rebellion against the Empire, it had always been for the sake of another.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 2, Section 6. When [[Tanza]]'s sister, [[Zoey]], was tortured and killed by imperial soldiers, she shared her grief and rage with Tanza before declaring her rebellion until the heads of the soldiers responsible were brought to her. Likewise, during the [[Destruction of Chaosflame|fake "Great Disaster"]] in Chaosflame, she went directly against Vincent's orders to flee the city and put her all on the line in order to protect it and ensure a safe haven for those persecuted by the Empire for their blood lineage. Likewise, though she is able to take the life of her enemies, she does not like to do so, and she can only do so after much resignation and significant anguish to her heart. It is for this reason that Yorna manifested the Soul Marriage Technique, which could not be mastered without compassion for others.''However, in most cases, the act of destroying the human form, the receptacle of life, was something that took great resolve and determination, or perhaps accustomation or resignation, in order to be possible. Iris could be said to be the latter case, in extreme form. Even now, she could not kill a being without feeling any anguish in her heart, even supposing it was an opponent displaying hostility towards her. For that reason, Iris had manifested the Soul Marriage Technique, a power that could not be mastered without compassion for others.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 46, Section 2. ==History== {{Construction|Iris and the King of Thorns history to be added}} Around 300 years before the present era, a village girl named '''Iris''' (アイリス, ''Airisu'') met and sheltered Eugard Vollachia, an emperor of Vollachia who was ousted from his throne. The two fell in love and Iris sheltered and supported Eugard's path to return to his position. However, when they were to meet one day, they were betrayed, and Iris was killed by the wolf human and mole human races. After the emperor lost Iris, he descended into madness. He resultingly chose to eradicate all wolf humans and mole humans who remained in the Empire. However, his madness was not quelled, and Eugard chose to cast a curse on Iris, using the slain wolf and mole humans as the core for it. This curse, the Soul Marriage Curse, brought her back to life at the cost of experiencing endless reincarnation. ===Post-Reincarnations=== Beginning the cycle of reincarnation, Iris sought to dispel the Soul Marriage Curse to free herself from its effects, and it became her dearest wish to reunite with Eugard. The genesis of this fervent wish was related to the existence of the [[Stargazer]]s, which she believes is one of the Vollachia Empire's evil practices.''Yorna could not help but feel some bitterness inside as the word “Stargazer” echoed, spoken by his mouth in such a confident tone. The existence of the Stargazer was one of Vollachia's evil practices. At least, that was the only way Yorna could describe it. The genesis of Yorna’s strong, fervent wish was not unrelated to the Stargazers.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 30]], Chapter 1, Section 4. She also learned how to use the ancient Soul Marriage Technique. Many years later, Iris was reincarnated as a human with the name '''Sandra Benedict''' (サンドラ・ベネディクト, ''Sandora Benedikuto''). As Sandra, she had a child with the seventy-sixth emperor of Vollachia, [[Drizen Vollachia]]. Their child was named Prisca Benedict. However, Sandra perished to give birth to Prisca,''For Iris, who had unwillingly continued to live on for a long, long time; for Sandra Benedict, who had tragically lost her life giving birth to Prisca; for Yorna Mishigure, who had been shaken by a beloved reunion after hundreds of years, this was an unknown state of mind――, "――Ah."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 46, Section 2. and she reincarnated into a fox human under a new name: Yorna Mishigure. She became the Demon City of Chaosflame's “Mistress” because of her lineage and lived through the Imperial Selection Ceremony as Yorna, not knowing that her child had been spared and took the name Priscilla. Sometime after Vincent Vollachia was coronated as the seventy-seventh emperor of Vollachia, Yorna was appointed as the Imperial Army's Seventh ranked Divine General once the Nine Divine General system was reestablished. ===[[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 7|Sword Identity]]=== Around two to three months before the main story, Yorna launched a rebellion against the Empire upon discovering that Tanza's older sister, Zoey, was murdered for sport by soldiers stationed at a fortress close to Chaosflame. After Tanza's audience with her, Yorna began by attacking the fortress and killing most of the soldiers there; however, a few soldiers escaped.''After the rebellion that clashed directly against the Imperial Capital when Zoey lost her life, Yorna had gotten revenge for Tanza’s older sister, and Tanza had requested to serve in her sister’s place. It was a request akin to the height of impudence, and she was extremely insufficient for the role, but Yorna had accepted it with pleasure.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 47, Section 3. Soon, she was confronted by [[Madelyn Eschart]], but their battle came to a standstill. Ending their battle, Yorna told Madelyn of the soldiers who left the fortress, asking that they be sent to her in return for stopping her rebellion. Sometime after Madelyn relayed her message, Yorna came face to face with [[Cecilus Segmunt]] and [[Arakiya]] when the Imperial Army's generals assaulted Chaosflame. Despite the power that the Blue Lightning and the Spirit Eater both had as two of the strongest combatants in the Empire, they were unable to defeat Yorna due to her usage of Soul Marriage. In the end, Yorna's demands were met, and the emperor himself personally ordered the escaped soldiers to be sent to Chaosflame, ending the rebellion. ===[[The Land of Nascent Wolves / Undead Busters 4|Undead Busters]]=== With the Great Disaster over, Yorna and the citizens of Chaosflame sought to rebuild the city even greater than it was before. After [[Medium O'Connell]] became Vincent's empress consort, she sought marital advice from her, [[Serena Dracroy]], and Madelyn to visit her. Before long, Cecilus's party returned to [[Garkla]], intending to speak with Vincent about how to handle Volcas. Upon reaching the location that the emperor and the Nine Divine Generals were staying at, Yorna met with Volcas, and they engaged in combat. However, he did not make any attempt to fight back during their battle, and he stated that she smelled like Iris, to which she affirmed that she had gotten stronger since they last met. Although her appearance, expressions, voice, and presentation were completely different to Volcas, he recognized her laughter, which was the same as it was 300 years ago. Following the events of the battle, Volcas sought to be executed by the emperor with the [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword]], whereas Yorna obstinately did not want to accept that outcome. Realizing that there was a possibility Yorna could revolt again, Medium suggested to Vincent that Volcas should be chosen to fill the vacancy in the Nine Divine Generals. She believed her proposal would not only cater to Yorna and fill the vacancy left by [[Chisha Gold]], but with Volcas being the direct cause behind Eugard's decree to execute the wolf people and mole people, forgiving him and having him join their side would show that Vincent was serious about keeping the decree rescinded. After hearing Medium out, Vincent proceeded to meet with Volcas in person to discuss her proposal with him. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Despite being among the lower end of the Nine Divine Generals, Yorna has centuries of experience, and she is capable of drawing out enough power that she can prevent any of her people from dying from an attack. Moreover, she can fight against even the top three of the Nine Divine Generals, not be killed while fighting them, and even push them back. Although her strength scales with her emotions, at their peak, they make Yorna an immeasurably powerful force, especially in terms of home defense. ===Techniques=== '''Soul Marriage Technique''' (魂婚術, ''Konkon-jutsu''): Soul Marriage is a long-lost secret technique of the old world that has been forgotten by most people that requires compassion for others to master. By dividing her own Od and bestowing it onto someone of her choosing, Yorna imbues them with power more or less reflective of her own, granting them the physical might to throw house-sized boulders like cannonballs,''――Each one of them housed a red flame in one of their eyes, and housed within was their high morale, that could be said to be what they had in common. This was also quite literally, a group whose fighting spirit burned within their eyes, and several of them were able to lift up the unbelievably big boulders, and were able to throw them across an outrageous distance.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 96, Section 2. and she greatly boosts their healing capabilities to the point someone acting under her Soul Marriage can receive multiple fatal wounds and be healed completely in a few short moments. However, in order for Soul Marriage to work, Yorna must not only love the receiver of this ability, but she must also be loved by that person in return. If this condition is not met, Soul Marriage will not work. Furthermore, as long as Yorna feels self-love and has a strong affirmation that what she is doing is right, the technique can give her extraordinary power. However, if her own sense of self-love and of her actions being right begins to wane, her strength will drop dramatically, to the point that someone the caliber of [[Rowan Segmunt]] could come close to killing her.''The effects would also apply to Yorna herself, due to the logic of self-love―― the feelings of affirmation towards oneself, which could even be called a manifestation of the belief that one’s actions were right. As long as she sincerely believed that she was correct, extraordinary power would surge within Yorna Mishigure. But, if she did not believe that was the case, what would happen then? Though she was one of the Nine Divine Generals, an apex of the Vollachian Empire’s military, if Yorna could not affirm her own deeds, she would rapidly lose strength. And unmistakably, that very phenomenon had occurred, to the extent that the sword of the Undead Swordmaster, who had parted ways with life, had surpassed her in strength.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 47, Section 3. Likewise, if someone whom she loves wholly affirms and believes that they are loved, the effects of the technique will also be tremendous for them.''――Yorna’s Soul Marriage Technique distributed power to those she loved. If one believed that they were correct, and there was no doubt that they were loved, if they selfishly believed that from the bottom of their heart, its effects would be tremendous.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 2, Section 6. The effects of the Soul Marriage Technique may also create a flame in the eye of someone who is under its effects.''Pressing down on the wrist that had been gripped so tightly, Yorna looked at Tanza’s face in front of her; there was no proof of “love” as great as the flame housed therein, and she stared at it as if it were unbelievable.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 2, Section 6. *'''Damage Substitution''': By imbuing the technique into personal beloved objects given to her, said objects can take damage in her place, preventing Yorna from taking injuries.''Most of the items that Yorna wore were gifts. Her kimono, footwear, and even her hair ornaments, be they woven, carved or molded, the inhabitants of the Demon City had gone to great lengths to craft these beautiful items with their own hands, which became imbued with the souls of their creators. The ones that received Yorna’s love received the capability to be crushed on her behalf to protect her in return.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 2. *'''Environment Manipulation''': By applying this technique to inanimate objects, such as her golden kiseru, the Crimson Lapis Castle, and the Demon City of Chaosflame itself, she is able to manipulate or strengthen everything in her environment; this being said, the same restrictions that apply to the people under the technique's effect apply to inanimate objects as well: she must be able to love the objects that she uses the technique on and spend time and devotion into them, and if that love, time, and devotion is lacking, it can reduce the effectiveness of the technique on said objects or land.''Yorna’s Soul Marriage Technique also worked on inorganic objects. However, it was a system in which the strength of its efficacy was proportional to the amount of time and devotion she had put into it. Therefore, she had an apprehension. ――How much could she really love the land where she had spent time with the man she loved?'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 2. She has applied this technique by manipulating a roof's tiles to form steps in thin air, which she can use to freely jump around on, or create pathways from the ground beneath. During the Destruction of Chaosflame, Yorna cast Soul Marriage upon all of the city, allowing her to attack the shadows by manipulating nearby buildings and throwing them at the incoming tendrils. She is even capable of manipulating something as minuscule as dust and use it as a defense,''In an instant, Yorna gathered the fine pieces of whirled up dirt by the previous gale, and clad herself and Priscilla in a cloud of dust. Rather than “cladding” them in clothing that stuck to the body, it was a delicate technique that circulated around one’s figure at high speed to repel attacks.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 2. or intangible substances like her kiseru's smoke, which she can use as a shield against strikes as powerful as Olbart's, or to repair damage done to her environment.''As the fluttering tobacco smoke reached the large hole, it created a surprising change. As if it were merely an illusion, the broken wall was slowly being repaired. The wood used in the damaged area of the collapsed wall of the Red Lapis Castle wriggled, and the wall was mended like the wounds of a living creature healing. Although it was a building repair, it was a strange and unearthly thing that gave the impression of a living being rather than inorganic matter.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 39, Section 1. *'''Detonation''': Anything under the effects of the Soul Marriage Technique is capable of creating an explosion. Of course, this ordinarily comes with the cost of said objects being destroyed in the process. She demonstrated this ability when she not only blew up the Crimson Lapis Castle but also Chaosflame itself to repel the shadow during the Destruction of Chaosflame. This is also capable of being used by any person imbued with the technique. Tanza, who was under its effects, was able to trigger such an explosion from her body, which managed to fully repel the remnants of said shadow. However, while it is unknown if it was solely unique to Tanza or something that would happen with any other person imbued by the technique, Tanza survived the explosion without injury, and instead, she and the one at the center of her target, Subaru, were instead sent flying to the other side of the country. ===[[Curse]]=== '''[[Curse#Soul Marriage Curse|Soul Marriage Curse]]''' (魂婚呪, ''Konkon Noroi''): The Soul Marriage Curse, also called the '''Binding of Thorns''' (茨の縛め, ''Ibara no Imashime'') by Priscilla Barielle, is a curse that drags a lost soul back without handing it over to [[Od Lagna]].''Indifferent to those doubts of Emilia’s, Priscilla spoke of the curse’s details. That was――, “――The secret art of dragging a lost soul back, without handing it over to Od Lagna.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 32]], Chapter 2, Section 4. It was cast onto Yorna by Eugard Vollachia. Because Yorna's soul cannot go to Od Lagna upon death, it instead fails to receive the proper treatment of a soul after its death, goes into the earth, and repetitively reincarnates her into another vessel.''“If the soul does not return to Od Lagna, it will return to the earth, and without receiving the proper treatment, it will enter its next vessel. ――You could call it resurrection, or even reincarnation.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 32]], Chapter 2, Section 4.''“So long as the curse is not undone, so long as the Binding of Thorns that entangles them is not undone, the departed soul shall continue to rise again. Again and again it will repeat itself, piling up the lives and deaths over and over again.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 32]], Chapter 2, Section 4. It is unknown if the curse has any relation with the Soul Marriage Technique. Thus far, she has been stated to have lived more than ten lives.''Between Prisca, the Empire, the Demon City, Tanza―― and Eugard, her mind was in its greatest state of turmoil throughout all of her lifetimes, numbering greater than ten.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 62, Section 2. Yorna's curse seems to be catalyzed through the deaths of the wolf and mole humans, and with the decree for their deaths being removed, the curse is likely to eventually subside.''"――I see. In order to bind your soul, Dear Mother, the two races that are the wolfpeople and the molepeople, their bodies and lives, which have been piled up since times of yore, were being utilized, and if that supply were to be severed, the curse would disappear naturally."'' [[Arc 8]], Curtain's Close, Section 3. ===Equipment=== *'''Golden Kiseru''': Yorna can usually be seen walking around with her golden kiseru, taking in rainbow puffs of smoke at her own leisure. When in battle, though, she can be seen frequently using it as a weapon, as it has been strengthened by the Soul Marriage Technique to the point that it can shatter a kunai used by Olbart. *'''Numerous Beloved Articles''': Yorna wears various accessories, jewelries, and even articles of clothing that were made by those who love her. Imbued with her Soul Marriage Technique, the various objects can receive any fatal or severely injuring attacks meant for Yorna, though at the cost of the articles themselves. ==Trivia== *Before Yorna was introduced and revealed to be Iris, the story of Iris and the King of Thorns was first mentioned by [[Sirius Romanée-Conti|Sirius]] in [[Arc 5]]. *Yorna's birthday was decided at a talk show held on April 5, 2026. *In the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)|web novel]], Yorna's Soul Marriage Technique was originally claimed to have been derived from her curse. However, this was removed in the light novel. ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Imperial Army]] [[Category:Generals]] [[Category:Nine Divine Generals]] [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Lupugana]] [[Category:Chaosflame]] [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]] [[ru:Йорна Миссигр]]

Gladiator |Status = Alive |Weapon = Hammer |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 31|Volume 31]]}} '''Weitz Rogen''' (ヴァイツ・ログン) is a former gladiator at the [[Ginunhive|Gladiator Island Ginunhive]] and a member of [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]]'s Unit during the latter's stay on the island who later joined the Pleiades Battalion. He made his debut in [[Arc 7]]. ==Appearance== Weitz is a well-built bald man with black eyes. Most of his body, including his arms, legs, chest, and head are covered with blue tattoos. ==Personality== Weitz is an antisocial and cowardly man who talks in a low, hushed voice. His treatment towards others is blunt and often accompanied with threats. Weitz wishes to be treated normally, but since he never had the opportunity to be trusted by those around him, he began to act how he was perceived. However, under the surface, Weitz is a loyal and trusting individual. In return for being kind towards him, Weitz offers genuine help and shows respect to those who extend him a hand. His loyalty is so strong, in fact, that he has a tendency to forget common sense due to his wish to assist the one he is loyal to. When he wanted to follow Subaru to assist him in the [[Conquest of the Undead Capital]], he was willing to latch onto the bottom of the carriage they were using, paying no attention to the fact that he would eventually tire out and be forced to let go, not only subverting his intentions, but also putting himself at risk of great harm. ==History== Weitz was born in Glarasia, a city where the Empire's arms are primarily manufactured. As an orphan, he started working at city's workshops in return for food. Weitz aimed to be normal, but due to his introverted nature, he never talked to anyone. As time passed, people started regarding him as mysterious and creepy. One day, when some stocked materials from a workshop he frequently worked at went missing, Weitz was falsely accused of illegally stealing and selling the materials. Unable to disprove the allegations, a tattoo was inked onto Weitz's body, which branded him as a criminal. After he was no longer accepted into working, Weitz was ironically forced to steal materials from workshops in order to stay alive, fully embracing his status as a criminal. As a result of this, Weitz quit trying to be normal and instead chose to become someone who would be viewed as dangerous. To achieve this goal, he voluntarily covered himself in them from head to toe in more tattoos. Eventually, Weitz had heard a rumor over a drink, and he discovered the identity of the man who had initially falsely accused him through it. Weitz would later retaliate by beating him and biting his ear off. Intending to leave the man beside him crying, shouting, and bleeding, he suddenly found himself surrounded by guards. After being forced to surrender, he quickly spit the man's ear before being apprehended and sent to jail. Weitz was consequentially sent to the Gladiator Island as his punishment. ==Abilities== '''Equipment''': Weitz has wielded a large two-handed hammer and was somewhat well-trained with it despite having amateur movements while using it.''The man who Gudda had seen strike him as he let out a “Gah” donned tattoos all over his body and wielded a large two-handed hammer. He was well-trained. But with his physique and amateurish movements, how could he have―― No, the correct thing to question was not merely what had happened to his own body.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 98, Section 3. ==Trivia== *Weitz has his own named chapter in Arc 7, in both the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)#Arc 7: The Land of Wolves|web novel]] and [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 31|light novels]]. *Weitz's name is likely based on the German word "zwei", meaning "two". *Weitz's birthday was decided at a talk show held on July 26, 2026. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Ginunhive]] [[Category:Gladiators]] [[Category:Slaves]] [[Category:Pleiades Battalion]]

'''Trellock''' (トレロコ) is a serial killer from [[Gusteko]].

==Appearance==
Trellock appeared as a skinny young man in his early twenties with moderately long ashen-colored hair. 

==Personality==
Trellock is a serial killer who targets people whose faces he yearns, destroys their faces, and removes the mask of their “persona”. He uses them to “become” like his victims and employ their personalities.<ref>''Not even he chose to harm people at random. He only destroyed the faces of those he yearned for. By stripping them of their face, by removing the mask of their persona, he could become anyone he wanted to be.'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 2]], Section 7.</ref> The personality he was last known to have employed was that of a sociable yet wary peddler. 

==History==
===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 1|One Wild Night]]===
For a few weeks, Trellock was responsible for a string of six recognized serial murders where each victim had their faces damaged. He eventually crossed paths with a peddler but failed to tear his face off. Trellock got caught in a snowstorm sometime later and visited a church on the mountains overlooking Leanotte. Upon entering, he was greeted by [[Noelle Tuérico]], [[Admonsah]], and [[Omega]] and her group. He proceeded to participate in the discussions revolving around [[Coatl|Pastor Coatl]]'s murder while continuing to simulate the peddler’s personality, up until [[Maqueena]] used Muskrim to make nearly everyone fall asleep. Trellock did not fall completely unconscious, however, but his movement was temporary limited by the effects of the sleeping flower.When Trellock could move his body again, he attempted to remove [[Colette]]'s face, which activated her [[Meteor#Beast Protection Bracelet|Beast Protection Bracelet]]. His body vanished, leaving nothing but bloodstains behind in the basement and church, making it unknown whether or not he survived the ordeal.<ref>''They never found his body, but the bloodstains in the basement and church suggested that it was unlikely he’d survive fleeing down the mountain. But if by some chance he did, there was no doubt he would refrain from meddling with Omega’s group a second time.'' [[The Witch's After Tea Party / One Wild Night Part 2]], Section 8.</ref>

==Abilities==
'''Equipment''': Trellock uses a glove with attached razor blades to peel off the faces of his victims.
