title: Undead
wikitext:
{{Parent Tab |tab1 = Information |tab2 = Image Gallery}}
'''Undead''' (屍人, ''Shibito'') is a general name for reanimated corpses that are raised by a caster and follow their bidding. They are also known as '''corpse soldiers''' (屍兵, ''shikabane-hei'') and '''zombies''' (ゾンビ, ''zonbi'').

==Information==
An undead can be made by the '''Sacrament of the Immortal King''' (不死王の秘蹟, ''Fushiō no Hiseki''), a type of [[magic]] classified as a forbidden art that returns a soul to the body it left.<ref>''“A kind of magic that, upon death, returns the soul to the body from which it has left… a forbidden art, I suppose.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 34]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> The forbidden technique was developed by a Witch who could completely resurrect the dead, making them look exactly as they had in life, though the spell has mostly faded from living memory and it is impossible to realize without a caster who has an innate aptitude for it.<ref>''The Witch who invented the spell had been said to be able to bring the dead back looking exactly as they had in life, but that part of the spell had not been passed down. Most of the ritual had faded from living memory; it was impossible to replicate any of the spell’s effects except moving corpses.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], Felix Argyle's Curse, Section 8.</ref><ref>''Even a basic manifestation was impossible to realize without a innate aptitude for this magic.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], Felix Argyle's Curse, Section 8.</ref> However, if the spell were to be successfully replicated, it could allow the deceased to be resurrected.<ref>''A secret spell developed by a Witch that could resurrect the dead, granting corpses the power to walk again―― his father had not been able to replicate the spell successfully, but if it could be done, even those who were gone could be saved.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], The Dream the Lion King Saw, Section 4.</ref> It is only possible for a caster of the Sacrament of the Immortal King or a person given authority by the caster to control undead.<ref>''Only the spell caster, or someone given authority by the spell caster, could control the corpse soldiers.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], Felix Argyle's Curse, Section 13.</ref>

The Sacrament of the Immortal King is the only known technique that can create undead. [[Wilhelm van Astrea]] believed that the forbidden art, which was used in the [[Demi-Human War]], was the same spell used to resurrect his wife, [[Theresia van Astrea|Theresia]].<ref>''“Corpse soldiers, that is what they were commonly called at the time. In all likelihood, it is the same forbidden art, it seems.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 18]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref> Furthermore, as explained by the author, the forbidden art used to resurrect Theresia revives the dead while returning them to their prime state,<ref> [https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/1899835282402271685 Re:Zero Episode 64 Commentary]</ref> though he did not specify if the forbidden art in question was the Sacrament of the Immortal King. [[Eugard Vollachia]], who was resurrected with the Sacrament of the Immortal King, appeared to be around the same age he had been while he knew [[Yorna Mishigure|Iris]], but it is unclear how long he lived for before his death and if he was of a similar age to what had been when he was with her. Thus, it is unknown if he was also reverted to his prime.

There are two main undead variants that have been presented in the overall story thus far; they are usually differentiated from one another by name. Basic lifeless undead that lack souls in their reanimated bodies are called '''corpse soldiers''', whereas undead with abnormal vitality are dubbed '''zombies'''. Each were made with different applications of the Sacrament of the Immortal King. 

==Corpse Soldiers==
[[File:Re Zero Ex Volume 1 2.png|thumb|250px|[[Crusch Karsten|Crusch]] attacking corpse soldiers with her One Blow, One Hundred Felled technique.]]
Corpse soldiers are an undead variant that are manufactured with an incomplete version of the Sacrament of the Immortal King, and for that reason, their souls do not reside within their reanimated bodies.<ref>''The soul did not actually reside in the resurrected corpse, but perhaps the pain of it remained.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], Felix Argyle's Curse, Section 13.</ref><ref>''“Though the flesh is revived, the soul does not reside within it. Reconstructing the Sacrament of the Immortal King is difficult indeed.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 2]], Fifth Stanza, Section 3.</ref> They are limited with the capability to only follow simple commands.<ref>''But he was a corpse soldier now, capable of following only simple commands.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 2]], Fifth Stanza, Section 3.</ref> A corpse soldier can be resurrected as a rotting corpse, be resurrected after having their bodies preserved with healing magic like what was done for [[Minor Characters#Hannah Regret|Hannah Regret]], or, as seen with Theresia, may even seemingly have their age reverted to a younger version of themselves. When a corpse soldier receives fatal damage and is unable to maintain its form, it is reduced to ash. However, some corpse soldiers have been observed to fulfill a lingering impulse or converse with other people before fully perishing.

Despite the great power that they may have had in life, an average corpse soldier's martial capabilities are lessened from their original levels.<ref>''The corpse soldiers were not stout fighters. However capable they might have been as soldiers in life, as corpses, none of them had much martial ability to speak of.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 2]], Second Stanza, Section 5.</ref><ref>''It was hard to believe that this was how he fought, even with his lessened capabilities as a corpse soldier.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 2]], Sixth Stanza, Section 5.</ref> They are also unable to feel pain,<ref>''He did not show any signs of feeling pain, either. That was only natural. He was already a corpse. Pain was for the living, a lifeline to confirm and protect the flame of life. The dead had no need of it. Because of that, Kurgan completely missed the effect on his right arm.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 20]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> and can even survive what would typically be a mortal wound for a living person or function without vital body parts like the head.<ref>''Yet, despite what was obviously a mortal wound, he flailed his body, working the spear out, and then, apparently unbothered by his shattered skull, stretched out his arms and attempted to attach himself to the next soldier he saw.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1]], Felix Argyle's Curse, Section 9.</ref><ref>''A huge corpse with an enormous sword was advancing on Wilhelm, along with another body that had its arms outstretched, despite having no hands and no head.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 2]], Second Stanza, Section 5.</ref> This was also true for the two corpse soldiers in Priestella, Theresia and [[Kurgan]], who were regarded by Wilhelm to have not been at their prime fighting capacity while clashing against him and [[Garfiel Tinzel|Garfiel]].<ref>''“Before that moment, the skill of her sword was false… were it not, if I had truly fought my wife in her prime, there would be no way that I at my age would have returned alive. And I can say the same for Kurgan.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 21]], Interlude, Section 4.</ref><ref>''“Neither you nor I. I would be a corpse, and you would be naught but hunks of flesh scattered about. That is the truth.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 21]], Interlude, Section 4.</ref> However, with Theresia, who was revived in her prime, her latent strength was drawn out once [[Reinhard van Astrea|Reinhard]] became her opponent,<ref>''The strength of one’s opponent could draw out the latent strength lurking inside even a sword master. And Wilhelm might have felt jealous that it was not him who managed to draw out every last bit of the hidden strength inside Theresia.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 20]], Chapter 4, Section 2.</ref> returning to a level equal to her peak in the era when she had clashed with Wilhelm.<ref>[https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/1899832236666749163 Re:Zero Episode 64 Commentary]</ref>

==Zombies==
Zombies are an undead variant with abnormal vitality. On two separate occasions, [[Al|Aldebaran]] and [[Natsuki Subaru]] used their Earth knowledge to describe this type of irregular fauna as “zombies”. There are two types of undead known as zombies, both of which were created by [[Sphinx]].

===Parasite-Based Zombies===
The first type of zombies were moving corpses that had irregular energy, having the capability to move after a normal body's weak points, such as their heart or the neck, were destroyed.<ref>''Yae’s style of fighting consisted of attacking vital spots after ambushing the opponent, which was completely ineffective against zombies, as neither their heads nor hearts served as proper weak points.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 4.</ref><ref>''The villagers that were turned into undead had an abnormal amount of vitality, and they were moving around freely even after their weak points, such as their necks and hearts, were crushed.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 5.</ref> Their bodies were bloodless<ref>''“I’m just moving around in a bloodless body.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 8.</ref> and due to the flaws in their creation, decomposed over time.<ref>''“They were trying to stick their rotting arms and feet back on to their bodies, trying to restore it to the way it was before.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 3.</ref><ref>''“That means, the fact that undead don’t last for long is a flaw. If it’s like this, then the undead business will probably not succeed.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 9.</ref> These zombies were created from contaminated water containing parasites that turned people into undead.<ref name="substance">''“The villages that surround the Tenrill River have been dirtied by the asinine poison that you have sprinkled into it. Perhaps the liquor over here is tainted by the same substance, am I correct?”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 10.</ref><ref>''Thinking about the villages that used the water from the Tenrill River, as well as the grave situation where the villagers from said villages turned into undead one by one, there was no room left to doubt the idea that the parasites―― the cause of the fiasco, entered the body through water that had been ingested from the river.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 10.</ref> Once they were ingested, the parasites gradually took control of the brains of men and eventually gained full control over their bodies.<ref>''In other words, the parasitic creatures took root in the brains of the men, and had gradually obtained control over their bodies. Since their brains were the first thing that would be taken over, their memories and actions would become more vague and unclear as time passed.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 5.</ref> When the parasites completely manifested in a body, they appeared as tentacle-like appendages which displayed the capability to move, and they acted as if they had a will to survive.<ref>''Squirming around at the man’s wound, were tentacles that resembled the countless roots of a plant. Like weeds that danced around underwater, the writhing appendages prevented Al from making a move, and lunged at him―― not before combusting.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 4.</ref><ref>''With one strike, the tentacle that appeared as thick as the roots of a tree was halved without difficulty, and it started wildly tossing around on the ground. Like a fish out of water, it seemed as if the tentacle was desperately struggling to survive.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 5.</ref> Peculiarly, the parasites could not control children and most women despite residing in their bodies,<ref>''“Or, simpler than that, maybe they just can’t control the bodies of women and children?”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 5.</ref> with the exception of one undead woman who acted as the queen of the parasites.<ref>''“――Apparently, you hideous parasites are able to establish the logic of a queen, despite there being no life in your bodies.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 10.</ref>

The zombies made from these parasites themselves had differences. Some were unintelligent and acted similarly to corpse soldiers, yet others could speak.<ref>''In front of him, multiple silhouettes came into sight. They stuck their hands out, staggering on their feet in the orthodox style of zombies. Thinking that perhaps the speaking zombies he saw back at Coffleton were a rare type, Al ground his teeth upon seeing the unintelligent zombies make their entry.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 9.</ref> Regardless of their inequalities, both the conscious and mindless undead could meld together into one form. They could assemble into a singular inhuman entity that was effectively a lump of rolling zombies,<ref>''――Masses of human bodies that far exceeded the numbers of ten and twenty melded into each other, forming a single entity that was grotesque to the point that it no longer looked like a human. Having assembled into a huge lump of undead, it started rolling towards Al.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 9.</ref> or one zombie could assimilate others into itself.<ref>''That, was an aggregation of multiple undead that Edda had taken into her heavy build. Hands and feet were sticking out all over her body in an unnatural fashion, and the faces of the dead that were letting out silent screams were attached to places such as her stomach and back.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 12.</ref> According to the parasite controlling the body of [[Edda Rayfast]], the speed of the parasites' growth was fast; they were corpses that could only move once their hosts' brains were rotted at first, but over time, as the hosts' intellect and thought processes remained intact, it was believed that they could control hosts when they were completely alive and eventually create natural-born zombies.<ref>''“The speed of our growth is very fast. At first, we may be corpses that are only able to move once the brains are rotted, but that leaves hosts that have their intellect and thought process intact… If that goes on, we’ll be able to attain control over our hosts while they’re fully alive.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 10.</ref><ref>''“Are you saying that sometime in the future, you would create natural-born ‘zombees’?”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 10.</ref> Furthermore, they were tasked with the mission to create a paradise where their creator could be at peace.<ref>''“Well, that’s because our creator is our creator. Our real parent… to be exact, our creator is the incentive that allowed us to be reborn. To make a paradise where our creator could be at peace―― that is the mission that has been bestowed upon us.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 2]], Section 10.</ref> In a village of the Barielle Domain with men controlled by these parasites, the self-aware zombies tried taking the place of the men and appeared to be replacing their lives entirely.<ref>''That was the difference between the zombies that Al knew, and the villagers that were controlled by the parasitic creatures. They were not trying to initiate violence, but they were trying to take the place of the original villagers, and were attempting to protect their own territory. It was as if they were not after the bodies of their victims, but their entire lives instead.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1]], Section 5.</ref> A similar zombie type appeared in Nanou, a smaller city in [[Kararagi]] that borders [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]].<ref>''“Puttin’ it simply, the zombies I happened across had entirely replaced all the people in the city, ‘n were livin’ the same lifestyle as if they were still alive. Seemed like they didn’t want us ta know that they had swapped places.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref>

===Corebug-Based Zombies===
[[File:Re Zero Volume 33 Inside Cover.png|thumb|right|180x|Sphinx leading the zombies of the Great Disaster in Lupugana.]]
The second type of zombies were reproductions of deceased people with the memories they had up until their deaths, but rather than having their original bodies, the zombies' vessels were made of earth.<ref>''“But, this enemy chose earth for their vessels; are they not bothered if the contents overflow?”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> Despite these vessels' poor quality of skin, they were in as much shape and had the same level of strength as the original body that a given undead had, but they were unable to surpass the limits that their old bodies reached.<ref>''This resurrected body was in great shape despite the poor quality of its skin, and Eugard even harbored the misapprehension that he could move inexhaustibly. Of course, that was not the case in reality. This body was not something that could surpass his strength in life, and he ought not to desire anything more excessive than the restoration capabilities whenever the body was broken.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 3, Section 8.</ref> Each zombie possessed pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that run across their bodies, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises. When a zombie's vessel was damaged, they lacked blood to flow from their wounds.<ref>''No jest nor metaphor in that expression, it had been spoken in its truest sense. There had been no blood flowing from the wounds, the crushed parts wriggled and combined together like ice filling out a lake.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 5, Section 5.</ref> According to [[Lamia Godwin]], her body did not seem to feel pain upon being damaged;<ref>''“Well, this body… it does not seem to feel any pain, so I guess that is a relief.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 5, Section 5.</ref> however, this was not true for the undead who came into contact with Eugard Vollachia and experienced the pain of [[Eugard Vollachia#Abilities|his Curse of Thorns]].<ref>''Even the bodies of the undead still felt pain all the same. Ergo, Eugard stood here alone as the guardian of this location. Even if the others were undead, so long as they entered the range of the curse, they would still be tormented by the binding. For even if they were undead, Eugard had no intention of indiscriminately inflicting pain upon the peoples of his country.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 3, Section 8.</ref> Although a zombie could be broken apart into various fragments, if its core was not destroyed, it began the process of regenerating itself by unnaturally wriggling and fusing the fragments together until the vessel was once again whole.<ref>''Beneath her feet, the fragments of the ‘enemies’ she had ground to a fine powder wriggled unnaturally, the wriggling different from how it would occur when caused by the wind or an earthquake.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 5, Section 10.</ref><ref>''Turning around, Rem and Flop witnessed the supposedly-beaten ‘enemies’ regenerating. The broken pieces of pottery fused together as if time had been reversed; though fissures with the appearance very much as if they were seams were visible, they had been restored to their original state.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 5, Section 10.</ref> If grasped, a zombie even had the potential create more vessels and fill their soul with them to create multiple copies of themselves,<ref>''“If I can be resurrected after being shattered, then I can certainly resurrect myself back before being shattered. Receptacles can be made endlessly, so all I need to do is dilute the source and fill them all.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 6, Section 8.</ref> though there was a limit to the amount of vessels that can be duplicated with this technique.<ref>''“There is a limit to your numbers.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 6, Section 11.</ref> Of the four main magic attributes, the most effective one that could be utilized to defeat zombies was fire; wind magic did badly against them, the effect of earth magic was no more than a physical strike, and freezing them was inefficient due to its mana consumption.<ref>''“As it was reported, it’s the fire attribute that works the most effeeectively~. Wind did poorly, and earth is treated no differently than a physical strike. Freezing seems to be inefficient with its mana consumption.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> In addition, yin magic is highly effective in defeating zombies, to the point that it is one of their greatest weaknesses.<ref>''The particular effectiveness of yin magic against zombies―― that was the greatest weakness of the enemy as was currently understood.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 34]], Chapter 1, Section 10.</ref>

The zombies were revived by a combination of the Sacrament of the Immortal King to utilize souls and restoration magic to create vessels,<ref>''“Your judgement is correct. The fact that the zombies can be resurrected without their original corpse means that Restoration Magic is being utilized. With that as a hypothesis, the Sacrament of the Immortal King also ought to be being used in order to call down the souls.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> with the soul being used first and the vessel coming second, changing form to fit the soul.<ref>''“…The basis is the same, but the approach is different, in fact. For the Sacrament of the Immortal King, the vessel comes first, and the soul second, I suppose. However, as for these zombies…”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref><ref>''“The soul comes first, and the vessel after. ――The body changes form to suit the soul.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> The source of the mana that recreated the zombies was [[Muspel]], the [[Spirit|great spirit]] that governs the earth affinity.<ref>''“If anything, the existence of the Stone is being put to use by the opponent… by the Great Disaster.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> Its extraordinary large supply of mana was utilized to inexhaustibly revive the undead.<ref>''“Is in the palm of the enemy’s hand. Likely, in order for the Great Disaster to inexhaustibly give rise to the undead from the grave, it is utilizing that extraordinary amount of mana. Henceforth, they continue to appear in perpetuity.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> The cores that kept zombies intact and created them were called '''corebugs''' (核虫, ''kaku mushi''), which were small, round red bugs that appeared similar to caterpillars.<ref>''As he stated this, in Roswaal’s hand was a small block of ice being pinched between his fingers, about the size of a coin; inside, there was a red, round object. Upon closer inspection, he understood that it was a small round bug that looked like a caterpillar――.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref><ref>''“This corebug is lurking within the body of every zombie. And, this worm is the zombie’s lifeline… in other words, it is undoubtedly their core.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> A corebug acquired the data of a deceased person to turn them into a zombie, and reproduced the victim's original form with a vessel of earth.<ref>''“We will be working to unravel more about the technique, but this corebug acquires the data of the target that is to turn into a zombie, and then reproduces the original form by making a vessel out of earth…”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> This process could be finished near instantaneously, meaning that someone who died could immediately become a zombie following their own demise,<ref name="reborn">''“It seems that when a soldier who was fighting with them died, that same soldier would immediately turn into a zombie and attack them, I suppose.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> though the body of the zombie was separate from the body of the corpse. The corebug, which could be located in a variety of body parts, impacted the durability of a zombie; they could be impervious to damage if stricken in areas that the corebug was not present in,<ref>''It did not seem like the difference in toughness was based on where the arrows pierced them, either. There were some undead that were fine even when pierced in the eye, and some that would shatter when pierced in the shoulder.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> but if the corebug itself was destroyed, the zombie broke apart and was immediately destroyed.<ref>''“So, the true nature of Garfiel’s perceived discrepancy was the difference in the points at which an arrow killed the corebug within the zombie’s body.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref><ref>''An undead’s weak point was neither their heart, nor their cranium. Operating within the vessels of earth, were the corebugs discovered by Beatrice and Roswaal. As long as that remained intact, the activity of an undead would not come to a halt.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 7, Section 3.</ref> This, however, did not exclude the soul of the destroyed zombie from being reused and turned into a zombie over and over again. Once revived, a destroyed zombie could remember their past experiences and the circumstances that caused their destruction,<ref>''“Perhaps making it even worse, the next resurrected zombie could be aware of her previous death and the circumstances that caused it.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 3, Section 1.</ref><ref>''Even if this body were to perish, she would simply regenerate, just like her other selves. Moreover, the advantage of this regeneration was not just the fact that death did not mean the end. The next Lamia to rise would inherit all of this Lamia’s experiences.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 6, Section 9.</ref> allowing them to utilize the information to their advantage.

According to Lamia Godwin and [[Balleroy Temeglyph]] respectively, it seems that people who were satisfied at death are not resurrected,<ref>''“It seems that neither father, nor Barthroy-niisama, have come back. Those two were satisfied.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 7, Section 3.</ref> and the desire of the undead is to resolve any of the grudges or resentment they had in life.<ref>''“The desires of the undead have been fixed since the dawn of time; it’s to clear up any remaining grudges or pent-up resentment.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 7, Section 6.</ref> Their aggressive feelings towards the Vollachia Empire were implanted or amplified upon becoming zombies,<ref>''“We should assume that the aggressive sentiment toward His Excellency Vincent and the Vollachia Empire was implanted or amplified in the process of being resurrected as zombies.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> evidenced by the fact that deceased zombies have attacked their former comrades despite being allies until just prior.<ref name="reborn" /><ref>''“Those who were fighting as allies until just previously, attack as soon as they turn into zombies, hm? It appears that Otto-dono’s assessment is certain.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> The process that altered the mental structure of a zombie, which varied case-to-case, carried the risk of making the zombie unable to match the strength they held in their lifetime.<ref>''More or less, a process had been applied to alter the mental structure of the undead to differ from what it was during their lifetime. If not for that, the resurrected dead would likely not all assist in the destruction of the Empire. The degree to which that process had been applied varied from case-to-case, but there was a danger that, inverse to the large load being imposed upon the original form and nature in order to make them loyal to orders, they would become unable to perform at their original strength.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 2.</ref> To compensate, the load of the mental alteration process was reduced for capable individuals such as Eugard and Balleroy, giving them some degree of free will,<ref>''Therefore, it was customary for the caster to want to reduce the load in proportion to how strong any given individual was during their lifetime. In reality, considering the risk of causing severe debilitation on strong assets such as the Emperor of the Briar and the Magic Bullet Marksman by forcing that burden on them, the Witch had shifted gears to avoid that at the cost of granting them a moderate extent of free will.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 2.</ref> whereas zombies like Lamia who chose to willingly cooperate with Sphinx were spared from having their minds altered.<ref>''In any case, excluding such exceptionally strong individuals, and Lamia Godwin, who had displayed the will to take initiative in cooperating with the Witch, the souls of the undead were cruelly being toyed with.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 2.</ref> Unusually, as observed with [[Izmail]], a powerful individual with an excessive ardor for combat and fervid hatred at the moment of their death could manage to maintain their original power under the pressure of the mind control process.<ref>''Possessing the might of an elite warrior, bearing a remarkable zeal for battle within, losing no value despite being made into a subservient puppet, it had vehement regret and hatred scorched into it during its final moments. ――For that reason, that being turned undead rampaged in a ceaseless discharge of fury.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 2.</ref> This came to the detriment of the zombie's soul being stretched out, transforming into a grotesque, monstrous abomination with massive limbs that rapidly multiplied, a swelled frame larger than its original physique, and a fragile torso of skin and bone. This form was maintained after each resurrection of the zombie.<ref>''Torn to shreds, in a form that stretched out its soul as it was in the process of losing its original form, having forgotten that its body was ever in a humanoid form, it had been transformed into a repulsive, grotesque form. Even if its appearance had completely changed, with large, long arms, an exceedingly increased number of legs, and a flimsy torso of skin and bone, it could not escape the situation of being used by the Witch. Even after being killed over and over, its soul would stretch larger, and it would be revived as another monster.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 2.</ref> Among the zombies, only the exceptionally mighty were able to resist and brush aside the compulsory force, acting in accordance with their own desires.<ref>''However, among the dead were those who disregarded the Witch’s force of compulsion, acting in accordance with their own ego. And, each and every one of the deceased who retained their own will, were those who could be counted among the mighty.'' [[The Land of Nascent Wolves / Undead Busters 2]], Section 3.</ref> Despite their capabilities, individuals such as Balleroy and Eugard still fell victim to it, whereas [[Volcas]] was able to resist it outright.<ref>''His will retained, he forwent participation in the ruin of the Empire prepared by the Witch; however, neither did he fade away like those among the dead who had ceased to desire aught further, this being―― the jet-black wolfman, vocalized that name.'' [[The Land of Nascent Wolves / Undead Busters 2]], Section 3.</ref>

There were three known methods of permanently preventing a zombie from being resurrected while Muspel was actively casting restoration magic on each zombie: [[Spica]]'s “eating” of a zombie with the [[Spica#Abilities|Authority of Gluttony]], scorching a zombie's soul with the [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Volllachia|Yang Sword Volllachia]]'s flames, and returning a zombie to their original appearance they bore while alive when still an undead, either through the [[Enchanted Sword#Fiend Sword Murasame|Fiend Sword Murasame]] or by the zombie themselves managing to revert to it. Any undead who returned to their original form but was not immediately killed ran on “embers” and would accordingly “burn out”,<ref>''“Alas, these are but embers that are yet to burn out.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> lasting for only about a day at most before fading away completely.

With the blood that had long been spilled across the lands of Vollachia as a medium, a magic circle centered around [[Lupugana]] and spread out across five sites in the north, east, south, and west of Vollachia, corresponding to the settling points Muspel migrated to, was used to perpetually resurrect the undead with the Sacrament of the Immortal King.<ref>''Centered around the Imperial Capital of Lupugana, the five locations aligning with the north, east, south, and west of the Vollachia Empire―― spread out over the sites designated as the points of settlement for the ever-migrating Stone, using the blood permeated into the Vollachia Empire’s vast lands throughout the years as a medium, the magic circle had continued to resurrect the dead via the Sacrament of the Immortal King.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 5, Section 6.</ref> Towards the end of the Great Disaster, Arakiya, who had taken in Muspel, was able to assimilate with and place said spirit under her complete dominion as a result of the effects of a slash from [[Cecilus Segmunt]]'s Dream Sword Masayume in tandem with her own tenacity.<ref>''That which she had taken upon herself was an exceedingly powerful Great Spirit, and even though Arakiya was supposed to have burst asunder after taking it in, the exorcism performed by the swordsman who wielded the Dream Sword Masayume, along with her own incredible tenacity, had placed one of the Four Great Spirits under her complete dominion. By this point, the Spirit Eater, Arakiya, was already one and the same with the embodiment of the Empire's vast lands, Muspel, the Stone.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 5, Section 6.</ref> Once her consciousness returned some time after her being struck by Cecilus, she had no desire to support the Great Disaster, and as a result, she severed the mana supply from Muspel that had been utilized to resurrect the undead, making it so that, when a zombie died, they could no longer be resurrected.<ref>''The immortal army, the pack of dead wolves who could endlessly revive in their death, the prerequisite for that had collapsed. Even if the mana supply from the Stone was severed, that alone would not undo the resurrection of the undead. Only, the playing field had been leveled for both sides. ――Those alive for whom death meant the end, and those who had begun anew after the end of their lives.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 5, Section 6.</ref> As the vast majority of zombies were not returned to their original forms, they did not all fade away after Muspel's mana supply stopped being used to resurrect them. Following the Great Disaster's terminus, the zombies who escaped death, having lost the capacity to be recreated by Muspel, continued to stay alive so long as they were not destroyed.<ref>''With the Imperial Capital at its center, the hosts of undead that had deployed throughout the entire Empire lost its leadership, and fell apart; as they scattered and fled, the battle approached its curtain’s close. However, even though their commander, Sphinx, was no more, and the mana that had been provided to the Sacrament of the Immortal King by the Stone had been severed, until they were granted death once more, the resurrected undead still struggled onward with the entirety of their new lives.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Curtain's Close, Section 1.</ref> Although some of the zombies who were resurrected against their will destroyed their own bodies after Sphinx's compulsory force stopped affecting them, many others decided against destroying themselves,<ref>''The large-scale implementation of the forbidden art devised by the Witch was interrupted, and the dead who had been brought back to life by that twisted magic were all forced to remain in the land with a limited lifespan. Those who had been resurrected against their will and forced to submit to the Witch’s plans took the opportunity to turn themselves to dust and return to the whereabouts of the soul, but naturally, there were many who did not choose to do so.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 39]], Interlude, Section 1.</ref> meaning that the leftover undead could return to cause problems in the future.<ref>''It was quite possible that, from here on out within the Vollachia Empire, the undead that had managed to escape would frequently cause trouble. Even without that, even with the war itself having ended, everything that had been influenced by it would never truly be put right once and for all.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Curtain's Close, Section 1.</ref>

==Trivia==
*In the narration of [[Arc 8]], the capacity that an earthen zombie has to be destroyed and recreated anew is called '''Escape by Death''' (死に逃げ, ''Shininige'').
*In [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33|Volume 33]], Lamia said that her undead body did not seem to feel any pain. This was edited in successive volumes to allow for the zombies to feel pain.
*The Vollachia zombies were said to have an anchor.<ref>''Dispossessed of their free will, becoming a being used and discarded as tools for the sake of battle, their soul would be called down again even were they to repeatedly taste Death, their earthen vessels revived with a new anchor.'' However, Balleroy was under the impression that zombies could only be made from people who died in the Empire, and, in order to create undead outside of it, the country first needed to be destroyed, and magic circles needed to be placed in the other countries.<ref>''“…Seems like the people who get resurrected by the Witch are limited to just the people who died in the Empire. '''Zank Metley''' (ザンク・メトレイ) is a former Temple Knight of the [[Gustekan Church]].

==Appearance==
Zank is a tall man in his mid-twenties with short, brown hair and dark skin.

==Personality==
Zank at first comes off as a cold zealot who, as a Temple Knight, is willing to go to any length to eliminate heretics. However, unlike other followers of the Church, he is not as quick to condemn everyone involved with said heretic, and he has shown to be willing to work with others to accomplish his goals. He had always questioned the teachings of the Church, and when those very teachings put his [[Mikli Yulitô|fiancée]], who he cares greatly for and is willing to kill to protect, at risk of being killed by the very people she fought with, he decided to go against those teachings, even going as far as to kill other followers. This made him wary of other followers, such as [[Noelle Tuérico]], and after confronting [[Omega]], his faith in the church was gone.

==History==
===[[The Witch's After Tea Party / Omega in Wonderland Part 1|Omega in Wonderland]]===
Having grown up in the same village as Mikli, the two joined the Church together, rising in both strength and rank until eventually, the two became Temple Knights of the Church, and after meeting the [[Minor Characters#Holy King|Holy King]], they suggested for the two to marry, which they accepted. However, before the ceremony could take place, Mikli was sent to hunt a [[Shion|heretic]], which led to her going missing. Because of this, Zank decided to take other followers and retrieve Mikli from the heretic. However, after witnessing the town of Sylphoa, where Mikli had gone missing, under a sleep spell, his followers suggested to kill everyone in the town, including Mikli, claiming that it was in accordance with the teachings and Holy Will. In response, Zank killed all five followers who had traveled with him, and he set up a barrier around the town to prevent others from entering the town's vicinity.

At some point after this, Omega's [[Omega Party|party]] arrived in Sylphoa, Omega having dispelled his barrier, and Omega and [[Colette]] had passed out. Meeting with Noelle and [[Palmyra]], who had been able to ignore the spell thanks to Noelle's seal, he took their group to a large tent that only he was using. However, after explaining what was going on and finding conflict with Palmyra, who did not adhere to the Church's teachings, Colette's unconscious body turned into her beast form, a result of her [[Meteor#Beast Protection Bracelet|Beast Protection Bracelet]] detecting danger, to protect everyone, and with Zank declaring her a heretic, Colette took Palmyra and Omega out of the tent, leaving Noelle to negotiate to take care of the more pressing matter of the town's sleep spell, leading to a temporary alliance between the two.

Shortly after this, Noelle found Shion, who was partially responsible for the town falling asleep. She warned Noelle that Zank killed all of his allies, and shortly after, Zank began fighting with Noelle and the beastified Colette. However, after Palmyra awoke and claimed that Mikli was still alive, Zank spoke with Omega, who had also awoken. After Omega told him to claim that the heretic was dead to the Church, he would need to resign, and because Mikli had lost her blessing permanently, she would also likely lose her position as a Temple Knight. After being told that he couldn't chase both being a follower of the Church and his fiancée, his faith in the Church was completely broken, and he left with Mikli, deciding to resign from the Church.

==Abilities==
*'''Blessing of People Repulsion''' (人除けの祝福, ''Hito Noke no Shukufuku''): As a Temple Knight, Zank has the Blessing of People Repulsion, a red-colored spirit that creates barriers. It can create invisible small, short-range barriers, as well as a large barrier, which each make prevent people from being able to trespass beyond the barriers. It takes considerable skill to create barriers around a larger area and gives those who approach it a strange feeling. In addition, the Blessing's effects can be broken through with magic.

Glarasia |Previous Affiliation = |Occupation = Second-Class General |Previous Occupation = |Status = Alive |Relatives = Unnamed wife |Weapon = Sword |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 9]] (side story)}} '''Toledo Spiegel''' (トリド・シュピーゲル) is a Second-Class General of the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]]. ==Appearance== Toledo is a man near the age of forty with slim and nimble body, a uniform furnishes with a cloak, and a beard around his mouth that is fashioned into the shape of a sword. ==Personality== Toledo is fascinated by and in love with weapons. He is confident in his aptitude for seeing the quality of forged weapons and is uniquely able to feel their presence by “hearing” their “voices”. As a distinguished weapon collector within Vollachia, Toledo adorns the walls of his office with his weapon collection. He prevented his subordinates from using anything but excellent weapons. Toledo was also loyal to [[Vincent Vollachia]], being fully committed to removing any obstacles that could threaten his reign. ==History== ===[[Brotherhood of Pleiades Part 2|Brotherhood of Pleiades]]=== In the past, Toledo chosen to be a General due to his discerning eye for weapons and his rigorous training in utilizing all types of them. He was entrusted with the defense of Glarasia and managing the Imperial Soldiers at the Iron and Blood Fortress within the city. When [[Cecilus Segmunt]] arrived in Glarasia, he engaged in combat with Toledo and made quick work of him, easily rendering him unconscious. In due course, [[Natsuki Subaru]], [[Tanza]], and the group then known as the “Schwarnia Family” reached the Iron and Blood City. Cecilus challenged Subaru to conquer the fortress and defeat Toledo, who had no intentions of allowing him to proceed to the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]]. However, the Iron and Blood Fortress was conquered by Subaru, and he ordered Toledo to forfeit their weapons to him, leaving the weapon-loving Steel Appraiser pale. ==Abilities== '''Equipment''': As Toledo is most familiar with using a sword, he wields a treasured sword in battle. However, Toledo's proficiency in using weapons enables him to utilize other weapon types, such as spears, axes, hammers, or sickles. ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Generals]] [[Category:Imperial Army]] [[Category:Leaders]]

[[Chaosflame]] |Previous Occupation = Servant |Status = Deceased |Relatives = [[Tanza]] (younger sister) |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37|Volume 37]] (flashback)}} '''Zoey''' (ゾーイ) was a servant of [[Yorna Mishigure]] and the older sister of [[Tanza]]. ==Appearance== Zoey was a deer human girl with a pair of antlers. When she took up residence in [[Chaosflame]], she began to wear a kimono. As Zoey was Tanza's sister, it can be presumed that the two resembled each other. ==Personality== Zoey was viewed as a strong-willed and kind-hearted woman by Tanza. She scolded Tanza when she cursed the world, and was the most serious and hardworking servant that Yorna had. ==History== Zoey and Tanza's birthplace was ravaged and destroyed by bandits who sought to earn profits when the spread of a superstition claiming that boiling the antlers of deer humans could create a panacea. Their parents were murdered by the bandits, and the two of them barely escaped with their lives. From that point onward, the sisters lived a harsh life of suffering while attempting to evade those who sought to kill them for their antlers or to prey on their weakness, as has been customary for the [[Vollachia Empire]]. Zoey put herself through harsh circumstances to even obtain a plate of soup for her and Tanza. After they had continued to flee for a long time, the two of them eventually heard rumors of a paradise called Chaosflame, and Zoey led Tanza there. Yorna greeted the sisters when they arrived at Chaosflame and embraced them. Although Zoey had not cried when her parents died, when a spectacle was made of her so she could obtain soup, or when Tanza levied curses towards her, she began to sob as she embraced Yorna. Tanza, too, cried at this scene. In Chaosflame, the sisters were provided with suitable meals and a bedroom. Being the most hardworking of Yorna's servants, Zoey carried out her responsibilities dutifully. However, two years after arriving at Chaosflame, while Zoey was guiding demi-human tribes into the city, she passed a fortress of [[Imperial Army|Imperial Soldiers]] who were conducting a military exercise. They attacked the [[Demi-Human|demi-humans]] under the guise that they were potential enemies. Zoey would unfortunately be murdered and tortured for sport by the soldiers, who would then disgrace her corpse. As a result of Zoey's death, Yorna attacked the fortress and killed a majority of the soldiers there for revenge, and when a few of them escaped, she carried out a full-scale rebellion against the Empire to retrieve the escaped soldiers. ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Chaosflame]] [[Category:Servants]] [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[Category:Beast Human]] [[Category:Deceased]]

[[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of Indomitability|Divine Protection of Indomitability]] |Weapon = [[Enchanted Sword#Curse Swords Aeon|Curse Swords Aeon]] |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 22]] (mentioned) |Anime = [[Episode 72]] (mentioned)}} '''Vague Adgard''' (ヴェイグ・アドガルド) is a prince of [[Gusteko]] who is known throughout the world as the Mad Prince, one of the three people said to be on par with the [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Kingdom]]'s [[Reinhard van Astrea]] in terms of overall martial skill, alongside the [[Vollachia Empire|Empire]]'s [[Cecilus Segmunt]] and the [[Kararagi|City-States]]'s [[Halibel]]. A half-human and half-[[spirit]] hybrid, Vague strongly detests spirits, viewing them as an impurity within the world. As a result, he seeks to exterminate each and every spirit in existence. After killing a number of his siblings, he was imprisoned within the country's northernmost tower, where he is currently located. ==Appearance== Vague is a large man with a stern yet refined appearance that is described to be so unforgettable that it leaves a lasting impression in one's mind. He has long yellow-green hair that is neatly slicked back on one side and hangs over his shoulder on the other side, a small beard, a Sanskrit-like tattoo on the left side of his face, a well-trained physique, eyes that contain an unyielding resolve, and slightly-tanned dark skin. He wears a magnificent black uniform, in addition to having a white coat with a feathery collar at the top draped on his shoulders. ==Personality== The Mad Prince, perhaps befitting of his title, is considered crazed. Although Vague acts as a kind and considerate man to anyone he may encounter normally, whenever he concerns himself with spirits, he feels an intense drive to eradicate them and will not hesitate to murder others so long as it is for the purpose of killing spirits, which he absolutely despises. He is not above murdering even his own blood relatives, although it is unknown why he did so, and indicates that he even believes he should be erased, as he replied to someone else's comment that he should erase himself by saying “not yet” and it was “too soon”. Vague meticulously manages his anger and believes that, from his own experience, the full extent of one's anger lasts for six seconds. This notion, along with the mana consumption of his [[Enchanted Sword]], led to his establishment of a rule to finish a battle within six seconds so he can maximize the anger he unleashes against his opponents. ==History== Vague was born as a true descendent of the royal blood of Gusteko to a human mother and a great spirit, despite how the biology of spirits should not allow them to have the capacity to produce a child. For unknown reasons, he killed 15 or 16 of his siblings, was branded a national traitor, and was subsequently imprisoned and confined to Gusteko's northernmost tower,''“He is a true descendant of the royal blood of Gusteko. Being strong, he killed 15 or 16 of his siblings, and is now confined and imprisoned.”'' Re: Zero 10th Anniversary Space.''The Sword Saint who was bound by treaty to the Kingdom, the Mad Prince who had been branded a national traitor and confined in the northernmost tower, even the Blue Lightning whose selfishness was renowned around the world held a position.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 3, Section 2. which seals the powers of spirits. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Vague's martial skill is the greatest in Gusteko and is said to be on par with Reinhard's. Although it was in non-canon material, it was said that he was responsible for killing seven beings on the level of Great Spirits ([[Odglass]], [[Zarestia]], and the evolved forms of five of [[Julius Juukulius]]'s [[Minor Characters#Julius's Contracted Spirits|contracted spirits]]). With his Divine Protections, which allow him to progressively become stronger the longer he fights, and his Enchanted Sword, which has absorbed the power of spirits he has killed, he had amassed enough strength by that point in time to handily slay a [[Muspel]]-empowered [[Arakiya]] mere seconds after confronting her, and to fight off her, [[Madelyn Eschart]] with [[Mezoreia]]'s dragonhusk, [[Ia|Lumera Ia Juukulius]], and [[Clind]] all at once. In the present day, however, it is unclear just how powerful he is. ===[[Divine Protection]]=== Though presently unknown how many he has in total, Vague is known to possess at least five Divine Protections due to his ability to steal them from others. '''[[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of Usurpation|Divine Protection of Usurpation]]''' (簒奪の加護, ''Sandatsu no Kago''): Vague was born with the Divine Protection of Usurpation, which has the power to plunder the Divine Protections of other people. It is unknown if this power has any conditions for its activation. *'''[[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of Adaptability|Divine Protection of Adaptability]]''' (適応の加護, ''Tekiō no Kago''): This power enables Vague to adapt to any situation and environment. *'''[[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of Isolation|Divine Protection of Isolation]]''' (孤独の加護, ''Kodoku no Kago''): A power that can constantly raise Vague's battle capabilities when he is fighting people solo. *'''[[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of Repetition|Divine Protection of Repetition]]''' (反復の加護, ''Hanpaku no Kago''): This power allows for the same, repeated movements made by Vague over the course of a battle to become increasingly refined. *'''[[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of Indomitability|Divine Protection of Indomitability]]''' (不屈の加護, ''Fukutsu no Kago''): Although the exact effects of this power are unconfirmed, it normally activates at the moment of its user's death. However, due to Vague's unique constitution as the world's only spirit human, his heart does not beat, causing the Divine Protection to remain perpetually active. ===Physical Traits/Flow Method=== '''Unique Constitution''': Due to his nature as the world's only existing spirit human, Vague's physical makeup is fundamentally different from others in the world. *'''Constitution Shifting''': Vague is capable of switching his body between his physical human body and his spirit body in a manner similar to Arakiya. It is unclear how many benefits this provides him. *'''Non-Beating Heart''': Because he is a hybrid between humans and spirits, his heart does not beat, putting him in a position that can be considered neither dead nor alive. While it is unclear if this provides him any natural benefits, it is because of this that is he capable of using one of his Divine Protections to its fullest extent, as it only triggers when the user's life has come to an end. *'''Unaging Body''': Due to his spiritual nature, Vague has stopped aging, and he is known to be capable of living for centuries while appearing as a man in his prime. *'''Great Mana Pool''': Due to his spiritual nature, Vague boasts in impressive amount of mana, and he is shown to use his mana in conjunction with the Curse Swords Aeon to impressive effect. *'''Spiritual Mana Attunement''': Vague is capable of detecting where a being is utilizing magic or mana, even from across a large distance. He is able to track down spirits by using this sense. ===Equipment=== *'''[[Enchanted Sword#Curse Swords Aeon|Curse Swords Aeon]]''' (呪剣アイオーン, ''Juken Aiōn''): In the non-canon Re:Sacrificing Life In Another World from Zero IF story, Vague wields the Curse Swords Aeon, which make up one of the Enchanted Swords. They are a pair of twin swords that, when activated, transform into blades of light that drain the user's mana and manifest a sharpness that corresponds to it, which can allow them to cleave through strong defenses. However, they are unsuited for longer battles due to their energy consumption, which contributed to Vague establishing a six second rule with its usage. The ability of the Curse Swords allows them to absorb the power of an opponent. As Vague was only known to have used this power on spirits, it is unknown if it can be applied to beings besides them. Although it is unclear whether he used them before being sealed away, in the silhouetted image provided by the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (anime)|anime]], he is shown to be wielding a pair of swords that seemingly match the physical descriptions of them, so it is possible that he has used them previously. ==Trivia== *Though he has yet to appear anywhere in the main story, Vague first debuted in the Sasageru IF side story. *Before being named in the story, the author provided details regarding the Mad Prince in the 10th Anniversary Twitter Space in 2022 and at a talk show held on March 30, 2024, the latter of which revealed his name, Vague Adgard, and that he had white hair and blue or gold eyes that gave off a strong impression. His hair color was changed upon his introduction in the Sasageru IF, though his current eye color has yet to be confirmed. *According to the author, although he does not believe Vague will appear in the main story as of the 2024 talk show, it is not impossible for him to emerge in the future. **In another statement by the author in the supplement to the Sasageru IF, he would become an enemy if he appeared, and that he should not be in the main story later. *It is stated that Vague Adgard is "further distanced from death" than Reinhard van Astrea.''The Blue Lightning, Cecilus Segmunt, was faster; the Admirer, Halibel, made greater use of techniques; the Mad Prince, Vague Adgard, was further distanced from death; the Great Spirits enrolled among the Four Greats exceeded him in mana; the Sin Archbishops of the Witch Cult possessed irrational Authorities; the Witches of Sin had taken far more lives; many virtuous individuals were better at lying; and many scoundrels were more unfalteringly obstinate.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 40]], Chapter 1, Section 1. This is likely connected to his nature as a spirit human. *Vague's birthday was decided at a talk show held on April 5, 2026. The day itself, June 6 (6/6), may be a reference to Vague's fixation on expressing his anger in six seconds. *A silhouette of Vague's official design was revealed in the [[Season 4|anime]], and although he does not yet have a full design, his face is first shown among the images of [[Volume 46]]. **This technically makes Vague the first person in the series to be given a rough design in any form in the anime before the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (light novel)|light novels]]. *According to the author, if any of the world's strongest accompanied to the expedition force to the Pleiades Watchtower, the difficulty to complete the tower would increase because of [[Reid Astrea]]. This being said, Vague would have no reason to fight him.July 26, 2026 Talk Show ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Gusteko Navbox}} [[Category:Royalty]] [[Category:Human Hybrids]] [[Category:Divine Protection Holders]] [[Category:Enchanted Sword Users]] [[Category:Inactive]]

Later in life, he was killed by an unspecified young boy.''It was a sense of being overwhelmed reminiscent of the young boy who had once killed him, but what was decisively different about this, was that the flame brought about by the treasured sword of crimson, also reached beyond the bounds of death.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 66, Section 2. ==Abilities== '''Equipment''': Viva wielded a pair of curved knives. [[Stargazer]] |Status = Deceased |Relatives = [[Terriola Goldario]] (younger sister) |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero EX#Iris and the King of Thorns|Iris and the King of Thorns]]}} '''Whitaker Goldario''' (ウィテカー・ゴルダリオ) was the final head of House Goldario and a backer of [[Eugard Vollachia]] before his coronation as [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]]'s emperor. A victory contractor for the Imperial Selection Ceremony, he was the guiding figure behind Eugard's rise to the imperial throne. Having been selected to become a [[Stargazer]] at some point in time, he allied himself with the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]] and betrayed Eugard just prior to his coronation. In the end, he was executed at the hands of Eugard himself, marking the conclusion of his rebellion. ==Appearance== Whitaker was a young man in his early twenties with dark red hair and narrow amber eyes. He dressed in a formal jacket. ==Personality== Whitaker was a cunning man who utilized every means available to him to fulfill his purpose of backing an imperial family member to ensure they would become emperor, employing numerous subordinates, including [[shinobi]], who acted as his eyes and ears. Despite that, he had a reckless and childish side to him, as his schemes were rooted from a desire to bear witness to that which was “dramatic”. For this reason, he sided with Eugard in the Imperial Selection Ceremony. Furthermore, Whitaker cared deeply for the welfare of his sister, [[Terriola Goldario|Terriola]], and consistently endeavored to guarantee her a prosperous life, even after she opposed his failed rebellion. He also had a habit of using the English loan word “dramatic”, a word passed down in the Goldario family, when the situation called for it, with it being unknown who and where they learned it from. It is unclear when Whitaker became a Stargazer and what his commandment to fulfill was. Although his sister believed it was his intention from the beginning to betray the King of Thorns and install himself on his throne, he admitted that he had not always intended to betray Eugard shortly before his death. ==History== As the head of the Goldario family, despite outwardly being designated a commoner, Whitaker was entrusted with the responsibility to observe every candidate for the Imperial Selection Ceremony and determine which of contenders to be the advisor of like his predecessors before him. As the King of Thorns, Eugard Elcanti, began to show interest in involving himself in the Imperial Selection Ceremony, a move unexpected from him, Whitaker watched him and the other candidates from the sidelines with his sister, Terriola. After exerting various efforts to verify the existence of the Goldarios, Eugard Elcanti finally managed to get in contact with Whitaker over a [[Meteor#Conversation Mirror|Conversation Mirror]], introducing himself to the advisor with [[Yorna Mishigure|Iris]] at his side. Whitaker exposed his intent to regard Eugard as the successive emperor, choosing to side with him because of the response to his circumstances of his life and his curse not being rooted out of anger or lamentation, but from something else, and since siding with him granted the Goldarios the highest odds of success. With Iris's affirmation of Eugard's candidacy, Whitaker ascertained his plan to conspire with him. After their conversation ended, he spoke with Terriola about the King of Thorns and his relationship with Iris, and expressed his awareness of his sister's interest in Eugard. From then on, Whitaker began travelling around Vollachia, making preparations to ensure Eugard would acquire the imperial throne, procuring an abundance of Conversation Mirrors necessary to contact him with while doing so. During this period of preparation, he corroborated [[Volcas]]'s capabilities as being worthy of the Nine Divine Generals, attempted to ask Eugard why Iris was an exception to the binding of his [[Eugard Vollachia#Abilities|Curse of Thorns]] only to fail to receive an answer, and subsequently attempted to gauge his interest in Terriola, proposing that she could serve as a candidate for an empress consort to him, to which the King of Thorns said he would consider. Suddenly, Eugard pulled out the [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword]], signaling his father had died just then and that it was time to commence the Imperial Selection Ceremony. When it was discovered that Iris had an illness, Whitaker did research to determine it was Battle Craze Syndrome, that the healer who nursed her back to health when she was contracted it had only subdued it despite being unaware of its nature, and visited her to inform her of his findings and gifted her medicinal herbs he had quickly gathered with his influence to aid in her recovery, entrusting their use to [[Lynek]] in order to cure the disease and save her life. Once Eugard killed his final sibling, he was congratulated over a Conversation Mirror by Whitaker, who had prepared a “dramatic” gift for him. Iris, finally cured of her disease, had rushed to see Eugard; however, she was afflicted by his Curse of Thorns, triggering the emperor-to-be to repeatedly yell out Whitaker's name in horror as she was assaulted by his thorns' binding. The ensuing fallout resulted in Volcas aiming his claws over Whitaker's neck in rage, pinning him responsible for Iris having succumbed to Eugard's curse, only being stopped from taking his life by Terriola. Attributing the herbs as having produced this situation, Volcas was countered by Whitaker by mentioning Iris's preexisting illness. Volcas then left to see Iris, leaving the siblings to continue preparing for Eugard's coronation. Alone, the two spoke about the unexpectedness of Iris losing her resistance to the Curse of Thorns, with Whitaker saying that curing her had “backfired”, rousing suspicion in Terriola. Eugard's Curse of Thorns had expanded in its scope and began to pierce people through Conversation Mirrors, leaving only indirect communication as the only remaining method to viably contact him with. As Terriola left to continue preparing for the coronation, she saw Whitaker muttering to himself, wondering what the most “dramatic” plot twist from there would be. Sometime thereafter, Lynek bore news to Iris, revealing that Whitaker Goldario had launched a rebellion against Eugard, intending to murder him by setting fire to the Imperial Residence in the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]]. However, Terriola intervened before his assassination could be carried out, allowing Eugard to escape. Regarding his sister a traitor and knowing that she had loved Eugard, Whitaker imprisoned Terriola, and the siblings argued. Whitaker had come to the conclusion that Eugard needed to be dispatched because his Curse of Thorns was going haywire, believing there was no other option, which Terriola vehemently refused to accept, being under the impression he had intended to murder the King of Thorns prior to his coronation and install himself on the throne from the beginning. She expressed her abhorrence for her brother, receiving no answer in return. The rebellion caught Eugard by surprise due to both his own incompetence and Whitaker's meticulousness and shrewdness. Without the aid of Terriola, who aided him in escaping from the Imperial Residence before it could be set ablaze, he would have died. Pursued by the Nine Divine Generals, whom Whitaker had made his allies, he reasoned that the rebellion had been hastily planned and his past loyalty had not been a lie. Though he briefly considered surrendering, he was encouraged to ascend to the position of emperor by Iris, who confessed her feelings to him. Driven by love, he systematically slew the Nine Divine Generals one by one. Whitaker appeared before Eugard after the final Divine General was killed, admitting defeat. He imparted some final advice to Eugard relating to the Goldario family's dissolution and managing the water supply in the north region of the Imperial Capital, and made sure Terriola would be spared from the consequences of his actions, expressing relief once her safety was assured. He revealed that it was not his intention to rebel from the beginning, and commented on how fateful and “dramatic” it was for House Goldario to be remembered as traitors, before proceeding to kneel and bow his head, offering his neck to Eugard. Receiving final words of commend for his service, Whitaker Goldario was executed by Eugard Elcanti, putting an end to the Thief Emperor's rebellion. ==Trivia== *Despite neither the narration of Iris and the King of Thorns nor Whitaker himself outright confirming it, he was a Stargazer. The story's narration describes him as a “gazer”, a term that has been tied to Stargazers and commandments through a [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6|subsequent side story]]. Moreover, the origin of the fervent wish to reunite with Eugard that was held by Iris, reincarnated as Yorna Mishigure in the present day, was said to be “not unrelated to the Stargazers”.''Yorna could not help but feel some bitterness inside as the word “Stargazer” echoed, spoken by his mouth in such a confident tone. The existence of the Stargazer was one of Vollachia's evil practices. At least, that was the only way Yorna could describe it. The genesis of Yorna’s strong, fervent wish was not unrelated to the Stargazers.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 30]], Chapter 1, Section 4. ==References== ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Advisors]] [[Category:Stargazer]] [[Category:Deceased]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

[[Priscilla Barielle|Prisca Benedict]] (descendant) |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero EX#Iris and the King of Thorns|Iris and the King of Thorns]]}} '''Terriola Goldario''' (テリオラ・ゴルダリオ) was the advisor and first consort of [[Eugard Vollachia]], as well as a former member of House Goldario prior to its downfall. She worked alongside her brother, [[Whitaker Goldario]], to assist the King of Thorns with succeeding the imperial throne until the Imperial Selection Ceremony's conclusion, at which point he incited a rebellion. Having been smitten with Eugard, Terriola informed him of her brother's rebellious intent, allowing him to escape and suppress the revolt. After [[Yorna Mishigure|Iris]]'s death at the hands of [[Volcas]], she revealed the existence of the [[Curse#Soul Marriage Curse|Soul Marriage Curse]] to Eugard and had a child with him, becoming an ancestor to the modern imperial family after their child succeeded him. ==Appearance== Terriola was a beautiful young woman with long, lustrous red hair, narrow amber eyes, and a tall and slender figure. She wore an elegant dress. To signify her severance of the Goldario name after her brother's betrayal, she cut her hair short. According to Eugard, [[Priscilla Barielle]] bore her likeness. ==Personality== Terriola was a stern woman who had a much more serious, normal outlook on life as opposed to her brother, Whitaker. She was unable fully to mask her true feelings, yet she was also perceptive and capable of acting as an advisor in her own right, although she acted on her brother's instructions sometimes. She yearned for Eugard's affection and was staunchly loyal to him, even prioritizing him over Whitaker when he instigated a rebellion, disavowing his misdeeds. Having pined for Eugard, Terriola understood that Iris was his true love, putting the village girl's feelings over her own during her tenure as an advisor and suggesting that he employ the Soul Marriage Curse after her murder in hopes that he could one day reunite with his beloved. Her loyalty did not extend to all of Eugard's decisions, however, as she disobeyed his decree to achieve her own goal. ==History== As the King of Thorns, Eugard Elcanti, began to show interest in involving himself in the Imperial Selection Ceremony, a move unexpected from him, Terriola watched him and the other candidates from the sidelines with her brother, the head of the Goldario family, Whitaker. After Whitaker finished his introduction to Eugard, he spoke with Terriola about the King of Thorns and his relationship with Iris, and expressed awareness of his sister's interest in the man. She soon became Eugard's advisor and met Iris for the first time, informing her that the King of Thorns and Whitaker were fully confident that their victory in the Imperial Selection Ceremony was all but guaranteed. Iris also perceived the woman's feelings for Eugard and felt inferior to her, but Terriola reassured that she would provide her support because she could not be at his side, while her counterpart could. Terriola developed a positive relationship with Iris, and the often spent their free time with each other. Once the Imperial Selection Ceremony started, she continued to support Eugard's candidacy, performing deeds such such as holding negotiations with the families of opposing royals at Whitaker's instruction, using the [[shinobi]] under her command to procure information that would help eliminate the competition, or providing logistical support to the disciplinary unit to speed up the process of the ceremony. When the construction of two tents at the edge of the army's encampment was made for Eugard, she spoke to him over a [[Meteor#Conversation Mirror|Conversation Mirror]] to notify him. With the strategy being to end the Imperial Selection Ceremony as soon as possible, he prepared to attend a council of war and ended their conversation. The fallout of Iris being cured of her Battle Craze Syndrome and falling victim to Eugard's Curse of Thorns resulted in Volcas aiming his claws over Whitaker's neck in rage, pinning him responsible for Iris having succumbed to Eugard's curse, only being stopped from taking his life by Terriola. Attributing the herbs as having produced this situation, Volcas was countered by Whitaker by mentioning Iris's preexisting illness. Volcas then left to see Iris, leaving the siblings to continue preparing for Eugard's coronation. Alone, the two spoke about the unexpectedness of Iris losing her resistance to the [[Eugard Vollachia#Abilities|Curse of Thorns]], with Whitaker saying that curing her had “backfired”, rousing suspicion in Terriola. Eugard's Curse of Thorns had expanded in its scope and began to pierce people through Conversation Mirrors, leaving only indirect communication as the only remaining method to viably contact him with. As Terriola left to continue preparing for the coronation, she saw Whitaker muttering to himself, wondering what the most “dramatic” plot twist from there would be. Sometime thereafter, Whitaker launched a rebellion against Eugard, intending to murder him prior to his coronation and install himself on the throne. However, Terriola intervened before his assassination could be carried out, aiding Eugard in escaping the Imperial Residence in the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]] before it was set ablaze. Regarding his sister a traitor and knowing that she had loved Eugard, Whitaker imprisoned Terriola, and the siblings argued. Whitaker had come to the conclusion that Eugard needed to be dispatched because his Curse of Thorns was going haywire, believing there was no other option, which Terriola vehemently refused to accept, being under the impression that this was his intention from the start. She expressed her abhorrence for her brother, receiving no answer in return. Once her brother's rebellion failed and her house fell into ruin, Terriola cut her hair to signify her severance of the Goldario name. Swearing her fealty to Eugard, she gathered the shinobi that served the Goldario family to cooperate with him. However, they could not stop Volcas from murdering Iris. At Iris's funeral, Terriola revealed the existence of the Soul Marriage Curse to Eugard and implored him to use it in an attempt to ensure that he and his lover could reunite someday. To withstand Eugard's Curse of Thorns, she drank poison, imploring him to produce an heir with her to fulfill his duty as emperor while directing his true love to his one and only Iris, and that she would be the first to bear an heir. Eugard responded that he would consider her proposal, but that she would bear no responsibility in his consideration to cast the Soul Marriage Curse. From Eugard's point of view, if his love toward Iris was to produce a curse, the responsibility would be his alone, and neither Terriola nor Volcas could interfere, as it was between him and his star. Following her conversation with Eugard, she spoke with [[Lynek]], whom she had kept hidden to brew poison for her and to protect him from the imminent policy that decreed the execution of all wolf people and mole people. Despite the decree, Lynek had no words of apology for his brethren, as he and Volcas had made their decisions, and he chose to prioritize Eugard and Iris over his pack. She prepared a refuge for him at the [[Ginunhive|Gladiator Island]] surrounded by Lake Violane and considered turning it into a prison for convicts to act as a distraction for him. Affirming to him that she had not spoken of her feelings for Eugard to him so she would not be a thief like her brother, the Thief Emperor, she wished Lynek well, and he set off for Lake Violane. At some point, Eugard accepted Terriola's proposal, and the two produced a child. As a consequence of the effects of the poison she ingested multiple times to resist the Curse of Thorns, Terriola died at a young age. Before her death, she confessed her true feelings to Eugard. The child she gave birth to went on to achieve victory in the Imperial Selection Ceremony and become [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]]'s sixty-second emperor, making Terriola an ancestor to the modern imperial family. ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Advisors]] [[Category:Deceased]]
