[[The Land of Nascent Wolves / Undead Busters 2]] (side story)}} '''Volcas''' (ヴォルカス) is one of the '''[[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]]''' of the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]]. A mighty wolf person who once obeyed [[Eugard Vollachia]] after he and the pack of demi-humans he led were forced into servitude, he was the leader of the Elcanti army's main force, the disciplinary unit. After Eugard's victory in the Imperial Selection Ceremony and ascension to the imperial throne, Volcas perpetrated the murder of [[Iris]], directly instigating the emperor to decree the execution of all wolf people and mole people. He was slain by Eugard after Iris's murder, awaiting a reunion with her in death. Resurrected as a [[Undead#Zombies|zombie]] during the [[Great Disaster]], Volcas had such great strength that, rather than being forced to partake in the destruction of the Vollachia Empire, he resisted [[Sphinx]]'s compulsory force, allowing him to act according to his own desires instead.''However, among the dead were those who disregarded the Witch’s force of compulsion, acting in accordance with their own ego. And, each and every one of the deceased who retained their own will, were those who could be counted among the mighty.'' [[The Land of Nascent Wolves / Undead Busters 2]], Section 3.''His will retained, he forwent participation in the ruin of the Empire prepared by the Witch; however, neither did he fade away like those among the dead who had ceased to desire aught further, this being―― the jet-black wolfman, vocalized that name.'' [[The Land of Nascent Wolves / Undead Busters 2]], Section 3. At [[Medium O'Connell]]'s suggestion, [[Vincent Vollachia]] appointed him as one of the Nine Divine Generals. ==Appearance== Volcas is a wolf person with a muscular build covered with dark black fur whose body can be said to be a lethal weapon. He has golden-colored eyes, black bangs that droop over one of his eyes, fangs as sharp as blades that protrude from his mouth, and beastly claws at the ends of his trunk-like arms. For a wolf person, Volcas is taller than average. As a zombie, he possesses a vessel of earth, various cracks that run across his body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises differing from those he had in life. ==Personality== Volcas deeply detested Vollachia's Law of Iron and Blood for allowing for the weak to be abandoned. As a wolf person who lived and was sustained by his pack, for most of his life, his community took precedence over everything else. He valued it more than anything and would not hesitate to permit them to maraud villages in order to gather resources that guaranteed their survival or seek vengeance for members of his pack who were killed. Despite despising Vollachia's mantra, when placed in a situation where he exacted retribution for his fallen brethren and aimed to ward off the ensuing counterattack with violence, he believed he had no other choice but to kill or be killed, and to prove his pack's strength to protect them, which would ironically cause him to adhere to the Law of Iron and Blood. He had a strong sense of determination for matters relating to his pack and to achieve his own desires when he could, and confidence in his own strength and capabilities. He also spoke rudely to those he knew and frequently bantered with or hurled insults to them. After being saved by Iris, Volcas started to care for her, beginning to treat her similarly to members of his pack, and eventually, he fell in love with her. While not entirely loyal to Eugard, he was willing to serve the King of Thorns as long as it was what Iris wanted. By the time she was gradually whittling down her lifespan to stay at Eugard's side, Volcas's love for her had grown so large that he decided to prioritize his selfish feelings for her over the welfare of his pack. In order to end her suffering at the hands of poison, he chose to murder her, and to ensure that Eugard had the will to continue his reign in accordance with what he thought would be her wish, Volcas deliberately condemned his pack and their kin to persecution by asserting that they would avenge him, surmising that the King of Thorns would likely slaughter them in an act of retribution, which subjected them to the Empire's retaliation for a period of nearly 300 years. ==History== ===[[Re:Zero EX#Iris and the King of Thorns|Iris and the King of Thorns]]=== With his immense strength, Volcas became the leader of a “pack” of [[Demi-Human|demi-humans]]. Several members of their pack would attempt to maraud a village within the Elcanti Domain, and the Elcanti army, which had been directed by Eugard Elcanti to guard villages within the domain, slew the bandits and burned their bodies. Roughly twenty days later, Volcas and his pack participated in a retaliatory attack to avenge their fallen comrades. He tore apart and murdered most of the villagers, with only a number of women and children surviving the onslaught. They were captured and placed in cages within a cave the pack used as a base. Though most of the village women were sobbing and feared for their lives, one of them, Iris, stood up to Volcas, undeterred by his rage even upon learning he had murdered her parents and friends. Believing that his pack's only chance at survival was to eradicate their enemy, he rejected the girl's attempt to reason with him. Suddenly, he detected the scent of anger mixed in with the wind, emanating from a lone man who was approaching their base, and expressed confusion over what the man could accomplish by himself. With sword in hand, the man, Eugard Elcanti, arrived by himself to prevent unnecessarily sacrificing the soldiers in his army. With his [[Eugard Vollachia#Abilities|Curse of Thorns]] unilaterally binding everyone in the vicinity, besides Iris, most members of the pack were quickly defeated without a fight. Volcas used his claws and attempted to tear open his chest to remove the thorns that had imparted themselves onto it, to no avail. Ignoring his self-inflicted injuries, Volcas clashed with Eugard, attempting to kill him in one blow with his sheer physical ability and relentless assaults spanning just over than ten seconds, but was repelled with the sword techniques of the King of Thorns and stopped fighting, having exerted his efforts. Volcas believed Eugard's lack of a counterattack was an insult to him, but the man corrected that belief, saying that the wolf person was strong and that he could not risk something bad happening in order to save the hostages. Eugard then freed Iris and prepared to execute Volcas and his pack. However, rather than wishing for their execution, Iris chose to forgive Volcas and the pack, imploring Eugard to spare their lives, shocking both of the men. Despite the murder of her friends and parents, Iris wished to forgive them anyways to prevent them from perpetuating a cycle of battle and death. Listening to Iris's request, and verifying that she would not regret this result, Eugard decided to spare the pack and asked Volcas for his name. As a consequence of their defeat, the members of the pack were bound by [[Meteor#Collar of Subservience|Collars of Subservience]] and conscripted into a disciplinary unit obligated to serve the Elcanti Domain. Volcas often left the disciplinary unit's training sessions to disturb Iris while she was being taught by Lynek, chiming in by bantering with the village girl. After [[Whitaker Goldario]] joined their faction, the man gauged Volcas as having the power to the ascend to the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]] under Eugard's reign. As he began moving with the disciplinary unit when it came time to act in the Imperial Selection Ceremony, he spoke with Eugard over a [[Meteor#Conversation Mirror|Conversation Mirror]], being given the instruction to have the soldiers refrain from marauding as they had done before to limit bloodshed. In return, Volcas told Eugard he did not need to be on the front lines and to stay by Iris's side. He said he would not act for their sake, requesting that he receive proper treatment in exchange for fulfilling his duties, to which Eugard replied by evaluating he was more than worthy of receiving the treatment of a General. When it was discovered that Iris lost her ability to stay in close proximity to Eugard upon being cured of her Battle Craze Syndrome, Volcas aimed his claws over Whitaker's neck in rage, pinning him responsible for her having succumbed to the Curse of Thorns, and he was only stopped from taking the man's life by Terriola. Attributing the herbs used to cure her as having produced this situation, Volcas was countered by Whitaker by mentioning Iris's preexisting illness. Volcas then left to see Iris, leaving the siblings to continue preparing for Eugard's coronation alone. Some time later, he entered the Musik Castle where Iris had been briefly staying at and spoke with her. Believing he was indebted to her due to her decision to spare him and that he could not repay her with his life, Volcas declared to Iris that she could treat and use him however she wished. Shedding tears in response, he licked her tears in accordance with tradition for an adult from his pack to lick the tears of the young to comfort them. Just afterwards, Lynek appeared to inform Iris that Whitaker Goldario had launched a rebellion in tandem with the Nine Divine Generals against Eugard, intending to murder him by setting fire to the Imperial Residence in the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]]. To return to Eugard's side and encourage him to take arms against Whitaker, who planned to install himself on the throne once the King of Thorns was killed, Iris requested Lynek to use the herbs he had been gifted to create a medicine that would simulate the effects of Battle Craze Syndrome, which he reluctantly accepted after Volcas demanded an explanation from her. With Iris's encouragement, Eugard swiftly extinguished the lives of the Nine Divine Generals and Whitaker, putting a stop to the revolt, and his coronation proceeded as planned, being crowned as emperor by his beloved. Having been within the range of the Curse of Thorns for an extended period of time, Iris began to cough up blood when she returned to her quarters. Lynek warned her that she was pushing herself too hard, feeling guilty for creating a poison that was whittling down her life. Volcas, who was with the two, told Iris he was siding with her above all else, rather than with the Vollachia Empire, and that Eugard had no issue with his loyalties, giving her a cup of water after saying this. Though tolerating her selfishness despite the risk to her life, Volcas expressed genuine concern for her mind and body. Lynek rejected her proposal to teach her how to brew it herself, as she would not have been able to make it even if she had learned how to, yet he also had the responsibility of complying with her selfish request in order to remain with Eugard, placing him in a predicament where he would have had to continue bestowing her with poison out of obligation. Volcas delivered her a gentle insult, and Iris proceeded to rest in order to conserve her energy in order to interact with her beloved Eugard. Iris's poisoning of herself troubled Volcas, who did not wish to see her suffer. In his mind, he was left with only two decisions to end her suffering. The first would be to take away her reason from using the poison, and the second was to physically stop her from using it outright. The first option, kill Eugard, would send Vollachia in disarray, something that neither he nor anyone else wished to see come to fruition. Thus, to prevent Iris from having to suffer the effects of the poison, Volcas made the decision to brandish his claws and tore into her back, removed her heart, and clutched it within his hand, performing this in the garden of the Crystal Palace to allow Eugard to witness it. With Iris's collapsed body lying by Volcas's feet in a pool of blood, being held in his arms, Eugard discovered the scene. His Curse of Thorns activated and bound themselves to Volcas, producing an immense, agonizing pain within him, as well as Iris's heart, which became entwined with thorns. Eugard only pronounced a single word, why, upon observing Volcas's actions. He then opened his mouth and ate Iris's heart, swallowing it whole, making Eugard repeat his question. Volcas claimed it was a wolf person's nature, and that he had been waiting for this moment from the beginning. The emperor proceeded to shout Volcas's name, unsheathing the [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword Vollachia]] from the air, incinerating his enemy's arm at the elbow instantly with the flames quickly spreading to his whole body. Although Volcas had always valued and prioritized his pack, in his last moments, he instead chose to prioritize his star, Iris, whom he had fell in love with. With his last breaths, he told Eugard to not think this was the end, and that his brethren would turn their fangs against him, to which he replied, suppressing the urge to yell and unleash his rage, by saying he would repel and eradicate anyone with ill intentions who came his way. Swinging the Yang Sword once more, Volcas pronounced once more that, in the end, Eugard was just a normal man, given his reaction to Iris's death. Though Volcas felt guilty for bringing his pack into his selfish whims, he did not regret it, and told Eugard to take his time, believing that he would have the woman he loved all to himself in death. As a result of Iris's murder at the hands of Volcas, when Eugard publicly announced her death, he also began the decree that ordered the extermination of wolf people, the race the murderer of his beloved had belonged to, as well as the mole people, the race that Lynek, who had been perceived as a collaborator in her death, belonged to. While Volcas's plan of giving Eugard a reason to live by eradicating the two races had succeeded, his single miscalculation had been that the King of Thorns loved Iris far more than he could have imagined. Rather than performing the policy out of a desire for vengeance, which had been Volcas's goal, after learning of the existence of the [[Curse#Soul Marriage Curse|Soul Marriage Curse]] from Terriola, he chose to bind the lives of the slaughtered wolf people and mole people as a means of preventing Iris's soul from being forfeit to [[Od Lagna]], perpetually forcing her to reincarnate anew into vessel after vessel, with this eventually starting sometime after Eugard's reign. In the meantime, the soul of Volcas waited in vain in the [[Od Lagna#Corridor of Memories|Corridor]] until he could achieve a reunion with the one he sought. ===[[The Land of Nascent Wolves / Undead Busters 2|Undead Busters]]=== Resurrected in an [[Undead|undead]] form during the Great Disaster, Volcas's great strength allowed him to resist the compulsory force Sphinx used to place most zombies under her command. As such, he refrained from taking part in any battles during the disaster. Following [[Arakiya]]'s assimilation with [[Muspel]], limiting the lingering undead to have only one more life, he persisted afterwards unlike those who were killed or had ceased to desire anything and faded away, desiring to reunite with Iris, whose name he spoke. He encountered an undead weaponkin by the name of [[Minor Characters#Breznon|Breznon]] and quickly disarmed and dispatched the man with his claws and fangs. This sight was witnessed by [[Cecilus Segmunt]], who introduced himself to Volcas and in turn asked for his name. Recognizing Volcas from the tale of Iris and the King of Thorns and as a warrior whose name was spoken throughout Vollachia's history, the two Generals clashed in battle, which ended in the Blue Lightning's victory. However, as they were near [[Chaosflame]] and Yorna, rather than seeking to have [[Spica]] eat Volcas's name, Cecilus tried reasoning with [[Arakiya]] to let the wolf person stick around for the time being. While Cecilus and Arakiya were quarreling, Spica patted Volcas's head, causing him to reminisce back to when Iris had done so to him. Upon reaching the location that the emperor and the Nine Divine Generals were staying at, Yorna Mishigure engaged in combat with Volcas. However, he did not make any attempt to fight back during their battle, and he stated that she smelled like Iris, to which she affirmed that she had gotten stronger since they last met. Although her appearance, expressions, voice, and presentation were completely different to Volcas, he recognized her laughter, which was the same as it was 300 years ago. Following the events of the battle, Volcas sought to be executed by the emperor, Vincent Vollachia, with the Yang Sword, whereas Yorna obstinately did not want to accept that outcome. Realizing that there was a possibility Yorna could revolt again, the new empress consort, Medium O'Connell, suggested to Vincent that Volcas should be chosen to fill the vacancy in the Nine Divine Generals. She believed her proposal would not only cater to Yorna and fill the vacancy left by [[Chisha Gold]], but with Volcas being the direct cause behind Eugard's decree to execute the wolf people and mole people, forgiving him and having him join their side would show that Vincent was serious about keeping the decree rescinded. After hearing Medium out, Vincent proceeded to meet with Volcas in person to discuss her proposal with him. At some point afterwards, Volcas accepted the proposition, becoming a member of the Nine Divine Generals.[[The Land of Nascent Wolves / The Magnificence of the Eminent Emperor of Vollachia]]. ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Volcas possesses strength far beyond that of even an ordinary wolf person. In terms of pure might, Volcas was described as the pinnacle of strength in Vollachia during his time,''The moment that voice so cold it chilled him to his core was uttered, Volcas's beastly claws wrapped themselves around Whitaker's neck. Truly, it was a deed so swift it ought to even be said to be as fast as the blink of an eye. Whitaker, who had not even studied the art of self-defense, was unable to even follow the movements of the Empire's pinnacle of strength, whom he had enraged.'' Iris and the King of Thorns Part 2, Section 10. and he was only outclassed by Eugard Vollachia, whose prowess and technique with the sword was able to counter him even without the Curse of Thorns. Likewise, his strength was enough to allow him to resist the influence of Sphinx's compulsory force so that he could act on his own. ===Physical Traits/Flow Method=== Among the wolf people, Volcas is particularly powerful, possessing a muscular body and large arms he can move at such swift speeds that his relentless assault of an opponent can be compared to the speed of a tornado, while his movements seem as quick as the blink of an eye. '''Powerful Jaw''': As a wolf human, Volcas has sharp fangs rather than teeth. That, combined with his jaw strength, allow him to easily crush the iron legs of a powerful weaponkin like Breznon. '''Powerful Claws''': Volcas has sharp, blade-like claws capable of tearing through iron and piercing into someone's body or reducing them to a clump of blood in a single blow. With them, he is easily able to rip a person's heart out of their body or sever the legs of his enemies with ease. '''Heightened Olfaction''': As a wolf person, Volcas has a strong, keen sense of smell, allowing him to detect the amount of people in a given area by their scent. From his many experiences in combat, he is also able to distinguish the smell of anger emanating from those who were preparing to do battle. ==References== {{References}} ==Navigation== {{Vollachia Navbox}} [[Category:Leaders]] [[Category:Soldiers]] [[Category:Generals]] [[Category:Demi-Human]] [[Category:Deceased]] [[Category:Undead]] [[Category:Zombies]] [[Category:Imperial Army]] [[Category:Nine Divine Generals]] [[Category:Side Story Antagonists]]

[[Filore Camp]] |Previous Affiliation = |Occupation = |Previous Occupation = |Status = Alive |Magic = Fire Magic |Weapon = Shamshir |Divine Protection = |Light Novel = [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 44|Volume 44]] |Game = [[Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World: The Prophecy of the Throne]] |Japanese Voice = [[Wikipedia:Toshiyuki Toyonaga|Toyonaga Toshiyuki]] |English Voice = [[Wikipedia:Aleks Le|Aleks Le]]}} '''Tiga Rauleon''' (ティーガ・ラウレオン) is an emissary of the [[Divine Dragon Church]]. He plays an antagonistic role in [[Arc 10]]. ==Appearance== Tiga is a gentle-looking and handsome man with bright-green colored hair and distinctive yellow eyes, whose affective gestures suit him.''A gentle-looking man with bright-green colored hair, and a beautiful woman with short purple hair, reminiscent of flowers blooming in the rainy season. Despite the circumstances, the two of them stood dignified, not at all overwhelmed by their surroundings.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 3, Section 1.''As he spoke, the gentle-looking man―― Tiga bowed with a distinct style, and, closing one of those yellow eyes he had turned toward Felt, he was a handsome man whose affected gestures truly suited.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 3, Section 1. Tiga's attire consists of a long violet suit with gold highlights and black pants and boots. He adorns himself with a jet-black wide-brimmed, bowl-shape hat, a purple rose on his coat, and a gold pendant that is in the shape of the [[Volcanica|Divine Dragon]].''Then, turning himself towards Felt and Reinhard, he removed the wide-brimmed hat that had been pulled low over his head, and placing it against the chest of his dark purple cloak, "And so, my companion has been terribly rude, Felt-sama. I am Tiga Rauleon, and this is Sakura Element. We look forward to making your acquaintance."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 3, Section 1. ==Personality== Tiga is a friendly young man who is able to get along with others rather easily. He also acts with a sense of responsibility as a member of the Divine Dragon Church, especially concerning matters of [[Filore]] and her reckless behavior, and he is quick to chide both her and his other coworkers for their behavior should he believe it necessary. He does seem to have a slightly competitive side as well, as upon seeing Filore's triumphant expression at gaining a new friend in [[Emilia]], he said such an expression was unacceptable before looking toward [[Natsuki Subaru]] and asking him to be his friend.''"I see. I’m also glad you were able to make a friend. However, the way you’re making a triumphant face at me is unacceptable. For instance… say, would you be my friend?"'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 7, Section 2. Despite his usual demeanor, Tiga is easily capable of making cruel and harsh decisions when necessary. Though not unwilling to give an ultimatum to his opponents according to the wishes of a friend,''In reality, that was so. Beatrice and the others had directly witnessed the tragedy of the McMahon manor, and in the chain of events following their confrontation against its perpetrator, Crusch, there had been no errors in Tiga’s actions. To the maximum extent, he had acted in accordance with Subaru’s intent, and had tried to help subdue Crusch, with the only one refusing that judgment altogether being unmistakably Crusch herself.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 15, Section 1. he can ruthlessly attack said opponent even if it means burning away said friend and even himself in the process.''In order to defend himself from such a dangerous individual, Tiga did have the right to make a callous decision. Even if it was a decision that caused collateral damage to Subaru, with whom he had been fighting alongside, it was morally unacceptable to blame him for the matter without even asking for the reasons behind his judgment.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 15, Section 1. At the same time, however, he declares that his doing so is due to needing to reclaim his life.''"I just do what’s necessary. ――So that I may reclaim my own life."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 15, Section 1. His ruthlessness has been described by [[Beatrice]] as akin to [[Roswaal L. Mathers|Roswaal]]'s.''An aberrant tenacity that far exceeded a mere sense of duty―― Beatrice knew of people who operated with such resolve. Tiga’s tenacity, was of the same nature as Roswaal’s.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 15, Section 1. ==History== ==Abilities== ===Overall Power=== Tiga is a considerably strong combatant capable of going toe to toe with the likes of someone on the level of [[Crusch Karsten]], and his willingness to bring harm to his own body and fight dirty make him far more dangerous. This being said, both he and [[Heinkel Astrea]] believe that his skill do not reach the likes of [[Wilhelm van Astrea]]'s, as they both believed that if they confronted each other, Tiga would most certainly lose.''The comment about Wilhelm not having been present there, it was something he could have figured out even if it had not been expressly stated. If Wilhelm had been there, and Tiga had ended up crossing swords with him, Tiga would no longer exist in this world today.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 26, Section 2. ===Physical Traits/Flow Method=== '''Expert Swordsman''': Tiga is an excellent swordsman with enough skill to fight evenly with someone on the level of Crusch. His attacks are brutal and efficient, aiming for limbs with his strikes and weaving spins into his swordsmanship, reminiscent of a spinning top.''If their swordsmanship could be called orthodox, then Tiga’s would be considered an unorthodox article―― it did not cut down his foes straightforwardly, but mercilessly targeted the hands and feet, mixed artifice and honesty, and gave priority to catching his opponents off guard: the technique of someone avariciously coveting victory――, "Seyah――!"'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 13, Section 1.''At that rapid combo attack reminiscent of a spinning top, Crusch’s countenance remained unchanged, and, keeping her distance with nimble and precise footwork, she aimed to seize the initiative in the blisteringly fast exchange with a single swing of her sword.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 13, Section 1. He is also shown to be able to seamlessly weave in kicks while he attacks without breaking his momentum.''Holding the shamshir in a reverse grip, the strike of his sword, together with a rending shout, flashed forth towards his opponent from an unusual trajectory. When Crusch bent her body to evade it, it was followed up by Tiga’s long and flexible leg, unleashed like a whip.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 13, Section 1. ===[[Magic]]=== Tiga is capable of using fire magic. However, as he had previously claimed to be incapable of using magic,''"I can’t use it in the first place, my friend!"'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 13, Section 2. Beatrice suspects that either that was a bluff or that there was some other reason he was able to cast magic.''"Unmistakably, I suppose. Either what he said about not being able to use magic in the middle of the battle was a bluff, or possibly… mm-mm, it’s nothing, in fact."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 15, Section 2. ===Intelligence=== '''Keen Observation''': Tiga is rather perceptive in combat. After only being exposed to it for a mere few moments, he was able to come up with a countermeasure to use magic when under the influence of EMT. ===Equipment=== *'''Shamshir''': Tiga wields a curved sword called a shamshir as his primary weapon.''Keeping low to the ground and erasing the sound of his footsteps as he walked, within Tiga’s hand was a sword he had drawn in one smooth, soundless motion―― a silver crescent that carved deep, sharp arcs: that which he grasped was a shamshir.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 12, Section 2. ==Trivia== *Tiga originally debuted as an exclusive character in [[Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World: The Prophecy of the Throne|The Prophecy of the Throne]]. title: Witch Era Party
wikitext:
The '''Witch Era Party''' (''unofficial name'')<ref group="Note">Witch Era Party is an unofficial name that has been derived from [[Omega Party]], which itself was coined by the author in an afterword and is not an in-world name used by any character.</ref> is a group of people who set out on a journey to seemingly save the world.

==Information==
The party was formed four centuries ago, prior to the [[Great Calamity]]. It was filled with figures who not only had the capability to shape the fate of the world, but whose legacies would go on to entirely reshape it. Their home base seemed to be a floating palace created and maintained by the [[magic]] of the [[Witch]] [[Echidna]].

The Witch Era Party was described as a tight-knit group composed of people with mostly good hearts. They were often claimed to have roughly six people at all times, but there were other people who would join them at times and then leave just as another person joined them, meaning the exact number of people involved was never fixed to a specific number. Regardless, the core members of the party were described as people who had such power that, if they chose, they could supposedly split the world in two: a man who reached the Heavenly Sword, whose physical might was unrivaled and was capable of not only wiping out entire towns with ease, but also pushing the strongest race in the world, [[Dragon]]s, to the brink of extinction; a prince who was the living embodiment of "the fine line between genius and madness"; a merchant with a silver tongue so fine that he could achieve results equal to [[Authority|Authorities]]; a Witch who was rejected by her Witch Factor; a half-elf who had mastered Yin Magic to an unparalleled degree who also became a Witch; and a man who was described to be the one most likely to die among the group, yet was recognized as a Sage.

Although information on the Witch Era Party is limited, they were known to have had caused major incidents and had made enemies out of powerful figures and factions. Thus far, it is known that they ventured to the nation of [[Magrizza]] and were at odds with a group led by [[Pandora]], the [[Saintess Sect]], which had spread across the world. Echidna has also mentioned that there was a possibility that they were being pursued by the [[Black Serpent]].

==History==
''Note: Due to the limited amount of information, it is likely that some of the events here will be listed out of order.''
----

It is unknown exactly how the group formed. However, [[Alec Hoshin]] proclaimed that they went on a journey to save the world. According to [[Shaula]], a [[witchbeast]] who referred to Echidna as her mother, the people there were brought together by Flugel and had the same glint in their eyes with their own ambitions. During their travels, during their travels, the group became responsible for or were involved in several different incidents. In one case, Shaula and [[Reid Astrea]], the first Sword Saint, besieged a fort together. In another, Reid and Echidna hastily built a fortress wall to protect a town from destruction. Though unknown when the Pleiades Watchtower was constructed, it is possible that it existed while the six of them travelled together.

At some point, they found themselves in the country of Magrizza, where, despite supposing to be hiding their identities, they were discovered thanks to the naive earnestness of [[Farsale Lugunica]]. Thanks to this, the country's [[Minor Characters#Magrizza's Crown Prince|crown prince]], who had fallen for Echidna due to her unrivaled mastery of magic, attempted to arrange a marriage between them. However, due to a rampage by Reid and [[Volcanica]], which had an unknown trigger, the party was ultimately exiled from the country. Soon after, the Black Serpent, which was possibly pursuing the party, appeared and destroyed Magrizza.

Eventually, [[Satella]] took in the Witch Factor of Envy, allowing her to manifest an Authority. Her intentions were unclear, but thanks to this, a rift in her personality began to emerge, and for unknown reasons, a trap was laid for [[Minerva]], where Satella ultimately devoured her after she went mad. For reasons unknown, Satella, now the Witch of Envy, began to lay waste to the world.

Because of her rampage, numerous people have tried to stop her. Echidna, who had separated from her friends, rose up and taught [[Al|Aldebaran]], fighting against the Witch of Envy alongside her student. Ultimately, however, he lost his arm and she was heavily injured, and she chose to seal him away. At some point, Echidna's soul was attached to the [[Sanctuary]]'s tomb, and she presided over the trials for the next four centuries from the [[Castle of Dreams]], accompanied by the souls of the other deceased [[Witch#Witches of Sin|Witches of Sin]].

Whether at an earlier or later point in relation to Echidna and Al's attempt to defeat Satella, [[Flugel]], Reid, and Volcanica met in the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]'s city of [[Flanders]], and they united to bring down the Witch of Envy. In the end, Satella was sealed away within a shrine at the [[Augria Sand Dunes]]. Volcanica would come to regret hesitating on something unknown related to Satella, though it has not been clarified whether or not it is in reference to her taking in the Witch Factor of Envy, her sealing, or something else.

At an unknown point, Farsale made a covenant with Volcanica to protect Lugunica, and Farsale ultimately became the country's king. Reid continued to live his life as the strongest man of the era, until he was eventually recorded to have died of old age. It is unknown if he was ever given a noble title, but his [[Toska Astrea|brother]]'s descendants became the Lugunican nobles famous for producing Sword Saints, [[House Astrea]]. Meanwhile, Alec went on to continue acting as the overall leader of [[Kararagi]]. Volcanica stayed atop the Pleiades Watchtower as one of the examiners, and Shaula, who had had all of Flugel's achievements forced upon her, became the keeper of the tower. Meanwhile, Flugel, having entrusted the Witch Factor of Sloth to [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti]], vanished from history.

As for Satella, the [[Witch Cult]], partially made by Petelgeuse, was created with an unspecified goal. Over time, they were corrupted from within due to being subsumed by the Saintess Sect, and they eventually became a terrorist organization feared throughout the world. During this time, information on the Witches were actively suppressed and associated with Satella alone, until eventually, they were forgotten and Satella became even more feared by the world at large. For four centuries, she remained quiet within the Evil Sealing Stone Shrine, until eventually, when [[Natsuki Subaru]] found himself in the [[Royal Capital]], she granted him [[Natsuki Subaru#Authorities|Return by Death]].

'''Tornel''' (トルネル) is a member of the [[Beloved Children]]. He plays an antagonistic role in [[Arc 10]].

==Appearance==
Tornel is a young boy in his early to mid-teens with chestnut colored hair and light blue eyes, and his bangs cover his right eye. He carries around a large yellow lamp that contains Lagmite ore within it.<ref name="sorry">''It came from the person sitting on the other side of Reborn opposite Arbalest―― a young boy with chestnut colored hair who looked to be in his early to mid teens. The boy had tears filling his eyes, and as he clutched a large lamp containing Lagmite ore with both his hands, "I-I’m sorry, I’m sorry! I’m apologizing so please don’t be mad. When people get mad at me, my head starts spinning. So please stop. I’m apologizing. I said I’m sorry… hk."'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref> He wears a light tan robe that is a little longer than his body, and a similarly colored beret. He has on a darker tan button-up shirt with a white collar and light purple tie, a light purple sash that hangs from his shoulder to his waist, brown shorts, brown boots, light purple socks that almost come up to his knees, and bandages on one knee.

==Personality==
Tornel has a tendency to constantly apologize, whether for simply speaking or in response to others' actions. He is afraid of people being mad at him and will apologize when someone is angry, even if he is not the target of their anger.<ref name="sorry" /> He often appears nervous around others and seems to have a habit of clutching his head when he is overwhelmed.

==Abilities==
===Techniques===
'''Detour''' (遠回り, ''Tōmawari''): Tornel has the capacity to make people unable to reach their intended destination, resulting in them becoming lost in the process of attempting to reach it. When someone subject to Tornel's Detour attempts to travel to another place, such as from one point of a building to another, they will repeatedly go through the same rooms, and the distance between them and their destination will not shrink. However, it is possible for other abilities, like [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]]'s [[Natsuki Subaru#Authorities|Cor Leonis]], to surpass the effects of Detour, allowing someone who is subjected to its power to reach a destination. Upon deactivating his power, a blue light will coalesce in the area before returning everything to normal.

title: Royal Army
wikitext:
[[File:Kingdom_Knights.png|thumb|300px]]
The '''Royal Army''' (王国軍 ''Ōkoku-gun'') are the armed forces of the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]. The Royal Army is responsible for guarding its borders, maintaining order over unruly territory, and participating in its wars. Much of the military generally consist of common soldiers, armored guards, knights, and military officers.

Though the army has had major presences during the side stories centering around the [[Demi-Human War]], for the most part, it has gone unseen throughout the main story, and it is mostly involved in endeavors unrelated to the [[Witch Cult]]. 

==Information==
The Royal Army is tasked with defending the Kingdom of Lugunica and its territories from danger, from [[witchbeast]]s to foreign nations. Many aspects of the army are unknown. It can be presumed that it is very similar in nature to a typical fantasy army, with sword-wielding infantry, magic casters, and armored knights all marching alongside. However, despite the medieval nature of the military, the Lugunican army is able to field magic artillery resembling [https://godzilla.fandom.com/wiki/Maser_Cannon Maser cannons], and for battles that might take place at nighttime, they have a Night Banisher, which is a cannon that fires a magical, artificial sun that makes it appear as though night has turned into day. It also has a secondary effect of creating illusions.

[[Crusch Karsten]] has been circulating iron products such as weapons and armor to the knights as a means to strengthen the army, and she has begun making improvements on the knights’ training.

==Royal Knights==
Within the Royal Army are the '''Royal Knights''' (王国騎士 ''Ōkokukishi''), whose total number is around 2000 strong. They are a class of dragon-mounted cavalry riders and form the professional core of the Armed Forces. The two ways for someone to become a knight are by birth or by merit. As such, a large portion of the knights are made up of the children of nobility, and as a result, the Royal Knights presumably have an inclusive in-group court culture that follows strict chivalric principals. Having said that, several people who were not of noble descent, such as [[Reiner Wahrheit]] and [[Natsuki Subaru]], have also been accepted as knights due to merit. Being entwined with the history of the country, its monarchy, and its politics, the Royal Knights hold considerable prestige and influence in the government. The Royal Knights are by far the most distinguished and showcased members of the Lugunican army. Although they are not common, women can also become knights,<ref>''"They can, but there aren’t very many."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref> and it is said that the knight uniform provided to women comes with a skirt.<ref>''It was the messenger girl who had triggered their trip to the Royal Capital. Subaru was a little surprised to see her standing with the knights, dressed in a female uniform for the Royal Guard, complete with a skirt.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 4]], Chapter 3, Section 6.</ref>

The knight corps consists of the "most skilled" and "most capable" members of society. The average Knight most likely receives much more training in all arts of combat and magics alike than the average soldier, as is expected of the nobility. Their weapon of choice seems to be a type of straight-edged, one-handed short-sword with the hilt of a rapier. The swords are shown to be effectively weightless. Unfortunately, it is not known if the pommels can be unscrewed in order to end opponents rightly.

On the other hand, their style of swordplay is defined by quick, decisive strikes, wide angle swings, lots of movement with heavy amounts of footwork, and a focus on clean cuts designed to slice straight through both animals and the magical arts alike. Such is the art of swordplay in a magical world.

There are a total of four divisions, with their members distinguishable by the color of the cape they wear. Starting from the first division, the cape colors are red, blue, green, and black. The Royal Guard wears white capes. The Royal Knights seem to have an unspoken agreement when it comes to the knights' garrison's dining hall, being that the lower divisions always sit closest to the entrance, with the farthest tables reserved for members of the Royal Guard. Members of each division tend to group and socialize with other members of their own division.

===Royal Guard===
Within the Royal Knights are the '''Royal Guard''' (近衛騎士団 ''Konoe Kishidan''), an elite group dedicated solely to the security and wellbeing of the [[Royal Family]]. The Royal Guard is currently led by Commander [[Marcos Gildark]], and although [[Julius Juukulius]] is unofficially considered the second-in-command, the real Deputy Commander is [[Heinkel Astrea]], though because of this, the role is seen as ceremonial and holds no weight. The Royal Guard is described to be a group that anyone involved with the Royal Knights dreams of entering. They are traditionally tasked with protecting the king and the members of the royal family. All members of the Royal Guard are handpicked by their Commander and wear a white cape.

Following the [[Royal Abduction Incident]], in which [[Ford Lugunica]]'s daughter Filore was apparently kidnapped, the group was almost disbanded after the former Commander of the Royal Guard, [[Wilhelm van Astrea]], left their ranks following the death of his wife, the previous generation's Sword Saint, [[Theresia van Astrea]]. It was only thanks to Marcos Gildark that the Royal Guard managed to get back to their former glory. Formerly, those of a notable household or those with a strong backer had a large say in the entrance process, making the Royal Guard the most influential (and arguably most corruptible) power within the Kingdom. However, those practices have long since been abolished.

In the present day, the Royal Guard bears several members of true importance and power, and their names are recognized among the nation as the true elite: Marcos Gildark, the commander and one of the strongest people in the nation after [[Reinhard van Astrea]]; Julius Juukulius, the Spirit Knight and one of the most powerful warriors among the Royal Army; [[Ferris]], the Blue and the foremost greatest healer in the world; and Reinhard van Astrea, the most powerful person in both the country and the world.

===Sword Saint===
The army also often employs each generation of '''Sword Saint''' (剣聖, ''Kensei'') in their army. Following the transference of the respective [[Divine Protection#Divine Protection of the Sword Saint|Divine Protection of the Sword Saint]], once the person in question decides to take up their arms for the country, the king grants them the title of Sword Saint, and they become a part of the army in an official stance. The previous Sword Saints were [[Fribal van Astrea]] and his niece, Theresia van Astrea, while the current generation Sword Saint is Reinhard van Astrea.

While Theresia did take up her arms and fight alongside the army at times, particularly during the Demi-Human War, she did not maintain title for the country, as during the ceremony to award her for her achievements, Wilhelm challenged and defeated her, proving his might as one superior to the Sword Saint, and after further proving his might against the country's most elite Zergev Squadron, he replaced her as the country's most powerful warrior, the Sword Demon. While she would at times still assist them when her husband could not or was otherwise busy, the official title was not truly reused until the aftermath of the [[Great Conquest]].

At present, the current generation Sword Saint, Reinhard, is famous across the world as the strongest man in the world, and he is recognized as the strongest possible unit for the Lugunican military to send, to the point that the '''Reinhard Law''' was made specifically to bind him to Lugunica alone.

===Zergev Squadron===
[[File:Zergev Squadron Early Civil War Members.png|thumb|right|200px|The Zergev Squadron's principal members in the early years of the Demi-Human War.]]
The '''Zergev Squadron''' (ツェルゲフ隊, ''Tsuerugefu-tai'') was an elite unit of soldiers personally picked out by its commander, [[Bordeaux Zergev]], and the deputy commander, [[Pivot Arnancy]]. Though originally a small unit, they were powerful, and during the Demi-Human War, they were often sent to the front lines of the battlefield, bringing with them many victories. Following the first [[Battle of Castour Field]], in which the Kingdom lost a vast portion of its soldiers, Bordeaux scouted the young Wilhelm, shortly after he was first dubbed the Sword Demon, and [[Grimm Fauzen]], who was the only other survivor alongside Wilhelm in their squadron at the decisive battle of Castour Field. As the Demi-Human War dragged on, though the squadron saw its fair share of losses, it expanded its numbers upwards of 100, and throughout the battles they waged, they were often seen alongside the warriors [[Roswaal J. Mathers]] and [[Carol Remendis]].

During the [[Battle of Aihiya Swamp]], however, the majority of the Zergev Squadron, including Pivot, was slain by [[Libre Fermi]] after they fell victim to one of [[Rom|Valga Cromwell]]'s and the [[Witch]] [[Sphinx]]'s traps. Because of this, their numbers were reduced to a mere 11. In the aftermath, the Zergev Squadron did increase their numbers again, and when the Demi-Human Alliance managed to [[Invasion of the Royal Castle|sneak into the castle]], it was the Zergev Squadron who prevented them from attaining victory and ultimately succeeding in bringing down the Demi-Human Alliance's leadership.

Over the following years, the Zergev Squadron continued their battles throughout the war, and Wilhelm became the next deputy commander. However, following the [[Battle of the Trias Domain]], when Theresia decided to join the war, Wilhelm abandoned the Zergev Squadron to train himself, and the Zergev Squadron continued to fight alongside Theresia for the following two years, and in the end, finally managed to bring the war to a close.

Following Wilhelm's return and his battle with Theresia, the [[Gionis Lugunica|King]] allowed Wilhelm to rejoin the Royal Army and Theresia to retire, and after Wilhelm's victory over the Zergev Squadron in combat to prove his might, Bordeaux accepted a promotion that involved him joining the country's politics, and Wilhelm became the Zergev Squadron's commander, taking Grimm as his deputy commander, and they continued to be an instrumental unit to the country, even taking part in the battles during the campaigns led by [[Stride Vollachia]]. Eventually, the Zergev Squadron was folded into the Royal Guard, which was led by Wilhelm and his new deputy commander [[Conwood Melahau]].

AskFM Q&A.</ref>

title: Vollachia Empire
wikitext:
[[File:Flag of the Sacred Vollachia Empire.svg|thumb|170x170px]]
The '''Sacred Vollachia Empire''' (神聖ヴォラキア帝国, ''Shinsei Vorakia Teikoku''), usually referred to as the '''Vollachia Empire''' (ヴォラキア帝国, ''Vorakia Teikoku''), is one of the [[world]]’s Four Great Nations. It is where the events of the seventh and eighth arcs in the main story take place. As explained in its name, the Vollachian state is an Empire, ruled by the Vollachian Imperial Family, though importantly, no single bloodline within the extended family controls succession. 

Vollachia is the largest known country in the world. Though its geography and boundaries are, for the most part, unspecified, it shares a large northern border with the [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica]], whom it has historically quarreled with for over a millennium.

In [[Arc 7]], Emperor [[Vincent Vollachia]] was temporarily deposed from the Imperial Throne by Imperial Prime Minister [[Berstetz Fondalfon]] and Fourth ranking Divine General [[Chisha Gold]], the latter of whom only chose to rebel in an attempt to prevent both the emperor's death and the [[Great Disaster]], a disaster foretold to commence with the death of "Vincent Vollachia". After Chisha's self-sacrifice and the beginning of the Great Disaster, Vincent reclaimed his position as Vollachia's emperor, taking [[Medium O'Connell]] as the Imperial Empress Consort.

==Information==
===Geography===
The Sacred Vollachia Empire is blessed with fertile soil, mild weather, and the temperature remains relatively the same throughout the year, making it one of the more hospitable regions for a person to live. To the country's east is the massive Buddheim Jungle, which shares a large border with Lugunica, while the northernmost and western sections of the country have mountain ranges.

Due to the country's connection to the [[Spirit|Great Spirit]] [[Muspel]], the lands receive benefits such as fertile soil while its people receive greater recuperative capabilities.<ref>''"To put it plainly, the Stone is a Great Spirit that governs the Earth attribute. Therefore, the land it uses as a resting place naturally receives the protection of its special qualities. In addition to cultivating fertile soil, it also yields a positive impact on the recuperation of those who live on that land."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 31, Section 1.</ref> However, this also makes the lands vulnerable to destruction should something happen to the Stone, and thus, should such a scenario occur, the land will become fragile and uninhabitable.<ref>''"That is why we made use of our relationship with it, but… at the same time, it continued to move into the Empire’s bowels, spreading its roots."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 31, Section 1.</ref><ref>''"Think of it as the roots of a tree. A tree with thick, long branches may strengthen the ground it is affixed to, but conversely, if that tree were to be uprooted, what shall become of the land?"'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 31, Section 1.</ref><ref>''"Wait, so when you say that it would be the end of the line for Vollachia if Muspel were to die, you mean it would literally be the end of Vollachia!?"'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 31, Section 1.</ref> Because of this, the current emperor is working on slowly removing the spirit from the land so that the Empire can eventually survive without its influence.<ref>''"Of course, the process of decoupling the roots of the Stone from this country had been underway."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 31. Section 1.</ref>

===Population===
As with the other Four Great Nations, a sizable portion of the population is human. However, the Empire is known for being home to a large population of various [[Demi-Human|demi-humans]], which form different tribes. Some of these tribes are world renowned for their physical attributes, such as the Multi-Arm Tribe, which is notorious for their brute strength and thirst for battle.

Spirits, not including the Stone, are also rather scarce in Vollachia. This is likely due to the creation of the Crystal Palace several centuries in the past, which required the usage of a great many magic crystals, crystals born of deceased spirits, to create. Upon seeing this palace, the Great Spirit [[Beatrice]] immediately recognized the materials required to make the palace and deduced that spirits were hunted down to gather so much of the material.

In the present, [[Witchbeast|witchbeasts]] are a rare sight in the Empire, most likely due to local extermination. That said, there do exist witchbeasts such as the Elgina within the Buddheim Jungle, and numerous others are used at the [[Ginunhive|Gladiator Island Ginunhive]], both for Sparka events and to act as guards alongside the soldiers.

In the Sacred Vollachia Empire, nobles belong to one of the three following ranks: '''Low Counts''' (下級伯), '''Mid Counts''' (中級伯), and '''High Counts''' (上級伯). With a higher class or rank, a count has considerably more influence, with High Counts even being able to influence the state of the nation itself, while Low Counts barely hold any authority outside of their domains. More than 300 years ago, in recognition of the Elcanti family's political influence and connections, the leader of House Elcanti was granted the position of '''Special High Count''' (特別上級伯), with the final person to hold this title being [[Eugard Vollachia|Eugard Elcanti]], prior to his ascension to emperor.

===Government===
The Imperial government is an autocratic Imperial monarchy led by an emperor, though it is not a monarchy in the traditional sense. While not seen in the story, there also exists a legislative branch of the government known as the '''Imperial Parliament''' (帝国議会, ''Teikoku Gikai''). The emperor is ordinarily chosen from among the Imperial Family via the '''Imperial Selection Ceremony''', which begins once the siblings of the Imperial Family decide whether to take up the [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword Vollachia]]. Should one not pick up the sword, they do not qualify to participate to become the next emperor; if the sword deems them unworthy of wielding it, they burn to death and are disqualified; if they are chosen by the sword, then those siblings are qualified to participate in the ceremony, and they enter a large-scale battle with each other, usually involving assassinations and battles between personal armies until there is only one wielder of the sword left. The final sibling left becomes the next emperor, and it is the norm for new emperors to completely change the reforms made by the previous emperor.<ref>''“According to the way things are done in the Empire, it is the norm to negate whatever the previous government did, so his speculation is no laughing matter.”'' [[The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint: The Lion's Ferocity Chronicle 3]], Section 2.</ref>

Their flag is a defiant wolf impaled by three swords, known as the '''Sword Wolf''' (剣狼, ''Kenrou''). Because it is a meritocracy, it doesn't place as much weight on race or status compared to other nations, making it arguably one of the better places for demi-humans to live in. Because of its emphasis on strength above all else, the weak and disabled are often crushed or left behind by society.

Vollachia typically has bad relations with its neighboring nation Lugunica, resulting in skirmishes between the two countries. Currently, Vollachia's borders with the Kingdom are closed, not permitting a single citizen of the Kingdom or the Empire to pass. However, due to the effects of the [[Imperial Civil War]] and the Great Disaster, the possibility of a continued alliance or improving relations has opened up.

Following the coronation of Vincent Vollachia, the nobility who maintained their positions only by clinging to their family name and history in the distant past despite having merely become a shell of themselves were purged of their positions. Likewise, Vincent completely scrubbed clean the corruption that infested the Empire that was caused due to the previous emperor's, his [[Drizen Vollachia|father]]'s, beliefs, and the unwritten rule that the strong were absolutely right and to be respected was completely disavowed.<ref>''By purging those who had become a mere shell of their former selves and enjoyed high status because of history alone, the way of the Vollachian Empire, which flew the national flag of a “wolf pierced by swords”, was enforced inside and outside its borders without exception. The way of doing things that had lasted till the previous Emperor, who had unthinkingly believed the unwritten rule that the strong were absolutely right and had let the Empire fall to ruin internally, was completely disavowed and the initial principle that the strong were to be respected was scrubbed out.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 6.</ref> Later, following the Great Disaster, the Vincent made the decision to completely abolish the Imperial Selection Ceremony, making the ceremony he participated in the last of its kind.

===Mages===
The Empire has an unknown number of skilled [[Magic|magic]] stone craftsmen. It's also worth noting that, contrary to Lugunica, there are only a few mages and Spirit Users spread across the Empire. Magic is relatively scarce in the Empire, with presently only [[Balleroy Temeglyph|one known person]] to have utilized it. As such, magic is severely underdeveloped in Vollachia compared to the other countries.<ref>''In the Vollachian Empire, “magic” had hardly developed at all.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 98, Section 1.</ref> It is because of this that, rather than healing magic, people are forced to use crude and dirty methods when patching up injuries, thus making said healers highly valuable.

That said, magic is not looked highly upon in the Empire either. After an emperor of the past attempted and failed to utilize the buffing effects of Yang Magic on an entire army, the military shied away from magic.<ref>''In the past, the Vollachian Empire had also focused its attention on the power of magic, and it’d had an Emperor who had intended to amass the most powerful army. The Thirty-First Emperor of the Vollachian Empire, Murkia Vollachia, had planned to utilize Yang Magic to turn a powerful army into an even more powerful one. Taking into account the aforementioned shortcomings, he had enlisted Yang Magic users into his powerful army, training them so that their enhanced state would become their natural state, and then went into actual battle. However, the results that had unfolded had been disastrous; the powerful army became dependent on the enhancements, being defeated before any Yang Magic could be applied. The skills of the casters, so essential they were, varied; and being unable to function in a cohesive fashion, the army had been sent packing by forces superior in numbers. Even the Emperor’s life had been in jeopardy.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 98, Section 2.</ref><ref>''Because of this precedent, the value of Yang Magic, and thus the value of magic as a whole, was reduced in Vollachia, leading to the spread of the idea that mastery of martial arts was the mark of a strong soldier.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 98, Section 2.</ref>

===Religion===
The Empire does not follow a set religion, such as their neighboring Kingdom of Lugunica. Instead, the Vollachian people are taught to be strong through the principle of "The strong rule over the weak". This point of view is so prevalent that anyone who has died is considered a loser whereas those who live are Sword Wolves.<ref>''"Huh? By the looks of it, you’re a part of the Vollachian Imperial Family, but what does it matter when you’re dead? Those who die a dog’s death are losers, and those who live are Sword Wolves! That’s it! That’s the way of the Empire!"'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 27, Section 5.</ref> While this only meant raw power in the past, strength itself has been redefined under the reign of Vincent Vollachia.

In the Empire, there are select individuals known as [[Stargazer]]s, who are able to peer into the future and predict future events. The Stargazers are seemingly forced into following set commandments by forces they call the "stars", otherwise known as "observers", to a select few.

===Economics & Currency===
Vollachia maintains their own currency based solely on gold, or more specifically, gold coins. 

Despite the Empire having a rather hostile relationship with its neighboring nations, especially with the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica, they actively engage in trading with all kinds of goods that are scarce or unavailable in the Empire. Cities, such as one of the Kingdom's Five Great Cities, [[Picoutatte]], are widely known as the Kingdom's largest trading hubs with the Empire, for example.

===Military===
The nation highly prides itself in having a strong military and has a national creed saying that "the people of the Empire are strong", resulting even in lower ranked soldiers being exceptionally strong. Throughout the centuries, the Empire was constantly at war with the other nations, specifically with the neighboring Kingdom of Lugunica. However, during Vincent Vollachia's reign, no major conflicts with the other nations have spurred. Thanks to his actions, unnecessary bloodshed and conflict ceased, fights to the death were no longer applauded, and proof of strength was no longer determined solely by the person's respective overall strength, giving those with ambitions the drive to strive with their lives to achieve them.<ref>''Useless conflicts would cease, and absurd fights to the death would no longer be applauded. Proof of strength was no longer based on an individual’s military prowess, and those who held ambitions not suitable for their stature would prove with their lives the difficulty of truly fulfilling those ambitions. It was as if they were watching the process of completely painting over the criteria for what was “strong”.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 107, Section 6.</ref> According to [[Zikr Osman]], the Empire has been in its most peaceful years during the aforementioned emperor's leadership, something that had never happened ever since the Empire's foundation over a millennium before the main story. Due to their militaristic society, Vollachia's [[Imperial Army]] is the strongest standing army out of the Four Great Nations. In Arc 7, Vollachian soldiers can be heard using "Vive Vollachia", or "Long Live Vollachia", as a rallying cry.

It should be noted that Vollachia specializes in using various different types of techniques and physical abilities rather than magic when it comes to combat.<ref>''Compared to the technological prowess of the Kararagi City-States, the Spiritual Arts and Curse Arts of the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko, and the magical disciplines of the Kingdom of Lugunica, the Vollachian Empire excelled in the martial arts.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 98, Section 1.</ref> Aside from the users of magic being rather scarce in Vollachia to begin with, following the failure of a past emperor, people began to shy away from magic in favor of discovering, perfecting, and creating various techniques and abilities to use in fights. Demi-humans would even utilize the unique aspects that they were born with or were part of their culture to advance their skills; prominent examples include the Multi-Arm Tribe and the [[Insect Cage Tribe]].

Throughout the years, the various emperors have both removed and revived the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]] system, which displays the nation’s most powerful warriors. Under the rule of Vincent Vollachia, this system was revived yet again, and it is by far the most powerful generation in Vollachian history.

A common belief for Vollachian soldiers who have family or loved ones is that once they die, those loved ones will be given compensation equivalent to the contributions of the soldier who died in combat.<ref>''"Katya crying ’cause of my death? I don’t care about that. What’s important is how useful I am to His Excellency and the country when I die, and whether there’ll be a reward for it."'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 35, Section 1.</ref><ref>''"What a thick-headed brat! She can’t even stand up or bear any children! If that guy, Todd, ain’t here, then there’s no man that would take her as a wife! Katya needs the money to live!"'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 35, Section 1.</ref><ref>''Jamal’s opinion made sense. From the viewpoint of the people of the Empire, it was a shared belief.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 35, Section 1.</ref> As such, these soldiers will fight harder and will have no hesitation to die, using their achievements to make sure their family can live in peace, in spite of said loved ones' feelings.<ref>''"Right now, I’m a General Third-Class. If I can be of use to His Excellency in this, then I can look forward to being treated as a General Second-Class when I die. That way, Katya can live in peace. I’m able to do my job as her big brother if I’m dead, more than if I stay alive!"'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 35, Section 1.</ref>

Following the [[Battle for the Imperial Capital]] and the Great Disaster, a large portion of the country’s military was lost, including one of their Nine Divine Generals, Chisha Gold.

Shortly thereafter, one of Eugard's allies, a wolf human named [[Volcas]], kills Iris, and as a result, he orders the execution of all wolf people and mole people, a decree that would persist for 300 years.

==Locations==
[[File:Empire of Vollachia v2.jpg|thumb|350px|The land of the Sacred Vollachia Empire]]
'''[[Lupugana]]''' (ルプガナ, ''Rupugana''): Lupugana, also known as the '''Imperial Capital of Lupugana''' (帝都ルプガナ, ''Teito Rupugana'') or simply the '''Imperial Capital''', is the capital city of the Vollachia Empire. It is administered by the emperor of Vollachia, Vincent Vollachia. It is a large star-shaped city located near the center of the Empire. It is surrounded by a five-sided bastion fort with high city walls, a moat, and various forests situated in between each bastion. The city can normally be accessed through a bridge located at the first bastion, which gives a direct path to the center of the city. Each bastion is numbered, with the first bastion located in the south, the second bastion located in the southeast, the third bastion located in the northeast, the fourth bastion located in the northwest, and the fifth bastion located in the southwest. To the city's north is a reservoir, which was formerly an area of the Imperial Capital. The architecture within the city itself varies little in quality from one part of the city to another. At the heart of Lupugana lies the Crystal Palace, which is considered to be the city's symbol.

'''[[Chaosflame]]''' (カオスフレーム, ''Kaosufurēmu''): Chaosflame, also known as the '''Demon City of Chaosflame''' (魔都カオスフレーム, ''Mato Kaosufurēmu''), is an Imperial City located west of the massive Buddheim Jungle. It got its title as the Demon City due to various different races living there, which has resulted in the city not having any conventional laws, as it's known as the place where people live in disorderly harmony. It was governed by the Seventh ranking Divine General, Yorna Mishigure, until the Destruction of Chaosflame.
*'''Crimson Lapis Castle''' (紅瑠璃城, ''Beniruri-jō''): At the center of the city, a giant red castle sprouts forth. The castle vaguely resembles a traditional Japanese castle, though the building materials are different. Its foundations and framework are built out of lapis lazuli, which constantly switches between a deep blue hue and a blood red color, hence its name. The Crimson Lapis Castle was used as private residence for the 7th ranking Divine General, Yorna Mishigure, until its destruction during the Destruction of Chaosflame.

'''[[Garkla]]''' (ガークラ, ''Gākura''): Garkla, also known as the '''Fortified City of Garkla''' (城塞都市ガークラ, ''Jōsai Toshi Gākura''), is a border city located north of the Imperial Capital. It lies on an unnamed larger hill that overlooks the Gairahal Tropics. The fortress city was known for its importance in trading between the Empire and the Kingdom. Despite being one of the most fortified cities alongside the nation's borders and manned with thousands and thousands of extremely well-trained and battle-hardened troops, it was single-handedly destroyed 15 years prior to the story by Regulus Corneas, when items that were associated with the witch were put up for sale. It is rumored that the auctioned item was Eridna. The city was later rebuilt after Greed's rampage.

'''Glarasia''' (グララシア, ''Gurarashia''): Glarasia, also known as the '''Iron and Blood City of Glarasia''' (鉄血都市グララシア, ''Tekketsu Toshi Gurarashia''), is an Imperial City situated relatively close to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive and lies directly under the Gariu Heights mountain range. It lies on the far western part of the Empre.

'''Mezoreia''' (メゾレイア, ''Mezoreia''): Mezoreia, also known as the '''Cloud Sea City of Mezoreia''' (雲海都市メゾレイア, ''Unkai Toshi Mezoreia''), is an Imperial City situated east of Ginunhive and the home of many flying dragons. It is said to contain the nest of [[Mezoreia|a dragon]] and areas close to the city experience year-round overcast skies.

'''[[Guaral]]''' (グァラル, ''Guararu''): Guaral, also known as the '''Fortress City of Guaral''' (城郭都市グァラル, ''Jōkaku Toshi Guararu'') is a heavily fortified Vollachian city, located somewhere near the Buddheim Jungle. According to Subaru, its large walls makes one think that the city's inhabitants are trying to protect themselves from titans.

'''[[Ginunhive]]''' (ギヌンハイブ, ''Ginunhaibu''): Ginunhave, also known as the '''Gladiator Island Ginunhive''' (剣奴孤島ギヌンハイブ, ''Kendo Kotō Ginunhaibu''), is a relatively large island located on a larger lake that's situated on the south-west side on the Empire's territory. The island is infamous for its arena, where gladiators are pitted against each other or against witchbeasts.
*'''Lake Violane''' (ヴィオラーヌ湖水, ''Viorānu Kosui''): The Gladiator Island is surrounded by a black lake, known as Lake Violane. It is filled with various aquatic witchbeasts, which, next to the deathmatches, are the second most common causes of death in the area.

'''Gairahal Tropics''' (ガイラハル温帯, ''Gairaharu Ontai''): Gairahal Tropics is a massive lake situated at the Imperial border with the Kingdom of Lugunica, lying east of Garkla and west of the Barielle Domain.

'''Mount Gildray''' (ギルドレイ山, ''Girudorei Yama''): A mountain range that is directly adjacent to the city of Garkla. The large fortress within the city is carved into the mountainside.

'''Mount Palzoa''' (パルゾア山, ''Paruzoa Yama''): A mountain where the Cloud Dragon Mezoreia resided. It is also a habitat for flying dragons. Flying Dragon Riders often test their mettle here by attempting to fly as high as they can with their respective flying dragons.

'''Gariu Heights''' (ガリウ高地, ''Gariu Kouchi''): Gariu Heights is a mountain range located on the west of the Empire's territory. The Cloud Sea City of Mezoreia is located on it and the mountain range itself is located somewhat close to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive and the lake surrounding the island.

'''Buddheim Jungle''' (バドハイム密林, ''Badohaimu Mitsurin''): A vast jungle located in the far east territory of the Empire. It has a thick flora, making it extremely tough to maneuver through and nigh impossible to unravel all its secrets and hidden places. Geographically, it borders the Kingdom's Aihiya Swamp to its northeast and Kraukraun Grasslands to its northwest. 
*'''Shudrak Village''' (シュドラクの集落): Deep in the forest is a settlement belonging to the [[Terminology#Races|People of Shudrak]]. This settlement is inhabited solely by dark-skinned women.
*'''Graveyard of Nameless Monarchs''' (名もなき王の墓所, ''Na mo naki Ō no Bosho''): At the edge of the Buddgeim Jungle, overlooking the Great Waterfall, a single cliff is located, where the remains of emperors past, as well as tombstones dedicated to them, are located. The location of this place is unknown even to the imperial family and is only known by the emperor and their select and trusted aides.

'''Faradar''' (ファラダー, ''Faradā''): A small village located in the south of Vollachia where the Evil Eye Tribe once lived and where [[Melty Pristis]] and [[Salum Pristis]] lived. However, the village was destroyed, and the Evil Eye Tribe migrated elsewhere. Rumors say that there are still living Evil Eye members existing.

'''Godlait Waterfall''' (ゴドレート瀑布, ''Godorēto Bakufu''): Godlait Waterfall is a massive waterfall situated on the far east of the Empire near Lake Penelope. The water from the waterfall flows directly off of the world into the uncharted depths underneath. The area is inhabited by aquatic witchbeasts.

'''Lake Penelope''' (ペネロープ湖, ''Penerōpu Mizūmi''): Lake Penelope, also known as '''My Beloved Lake Penelope''' (我が愛しのペネロープ湖, ''Waga Itoshi no Penerōpu Mizūmi'') is a large lake situated at the south of the Empire, halfway between Godlait Waterfall and the Imperial Capital of Lupugana. It was named after a woman that a previous emperor of Vollachia loved dearly.

'''Kraukraun Grasslands''' (クラウクラウン草原, ''Kuraukuraun Sōgen''): Kraukraun Grasslands is a large grassy area in the Vollachia Empire located northwest of the Buddheim Jungle and east of Picoutatte. The area was inhabited by nomads, whose ruling class was prone to change throughout history, since they would constantly develop new techniques to outperform each other.

'''Averyk''' (エイブリーク, ''Eiburīku''): Averyk is a very small town located west of Chaosflame.

'''Mozotto''' (モーゾット, ''Mōzotto''): Mozotto is a town near the northeastern border with Lugunica and Shamrock Valley.

'''Insect Cage Tribe's Village''': A village in southern Vollachia where the members of the Insect Cage Tribe reside.
*'''Abyss''': A cave near the Insect Cage Tribe's village. Its name comes from the deformed creatures that live within it and the poisonous air that pervades it. This is where the tribe's "insects" live.<ref>''In the southern region of the Vollachian Empire, deep within the village where the Insect Cage Tribe lived, there was a cave where “insects” lived, and the cave was called the “Abyss” because of the deformed creatures and poisonous air that pervaded it. The “insects” inhabiting the cave had a strange appearance and were fundamentally different from the insects that were commonly thought of.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref>

'''Shinobi Village''' (シノビの里, ''Shinobi no Sato''): A village in an unknown location in Kararagi. The village is home to Kararagi's shinobi, and this village is where all shinobi are trained.

title: Iron Fang
wikitext:
[[File:Hoshin_logo.jpg|thumb|250px]]
The '''Iron Fang''' (鉄の牙 ''Tetsu no Kiba'') is a private mercenary group from [[Kararagi]]. They are currently owned by [[Anastasia Hoshin]] and led by the captain of the Iron Fang, [[Ricardo Welkin]] and his vice-captains [[Mimi Pearlbaton]], [[Hetaro Pearlbaton]], and [[Tivey Pearlbaton]]. It is generally considered the most popular military force in Kararagi. They are tasked to transfer valuable goods and weapons to different locations that are ordered by the '''Hoshin Company''' or battle in the front lines.

The Iron Fang has a large number of [[Demi-Human|demi-humans]] in their ranks, and while there are humans who do work with the Iron Fang, the majority of the force are beast humans. They consist of both sword wielders and magic casters.

==Information==
<gallery type="slideshow">
Fang of Iron Anime.jpg|The leaders of the Iron Fang.
Pearlbaton twins & The Fang of Iron.jpg|Iron Fang's official uniforms.
</gallery>
As mercenaries, they can be hired for various duties such as being hired as a bodyguard or volunteering to fight in the war. Although most of their services tend to be used by the Hoshin Company, their services can be bought by others, like [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]], who hired them in his effort to gather an army to fight the [[White Whale]] and the [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti|Sin Archbishop of Sloth]]. The majority of members wear a white robe with yellow highlights with the Hoshin Company's logo written on the sleeves of the robes, and there are animal ears on the hoods for beast humans. Other members, such as Ricardo Welkin, were given a black shoulder guard with a red logo.

[[File:Agility and Speed Liger.gif|thumb|250px|The Iron Fang riding on their Ligers onto the White Whale.]]
Members of the Iron Fang ride on wolf-like creatures called Ligers. They are often used to transport supplies from long distances. Although they are similar to Earth Dragons, Ligers lack strength, but they are more agile and have higher speed and endurance. They have a high chance of winning if the two were to ever be needed to fight in melee combat. They are a somewhat rare type of species, and they are often seen in Kararagi, but not anywhere else, especially not in [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Lugunica]]. Ligers are very territorial, so they can be difficult to raise.
