Five of the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]] |forces2 = Rebel Army |forces3 = Pleiades Battalion |forces4 = |casual1 = Unknown |casual2 = Unknown |casual3 = Unknown, likely minimal |casual 4 = |civilian =}} The '''Battle for the Imperial Capital''' (帝都攻防戦) is the name given to a major battle that took place in the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]] approximately one year and eight months after [[Natsuki Subaru]] was summoned to the [[world]]. It was a crucial conflict during the latter part of [[Arc 7]], revolving around a battle for control over Imperial Capital of Lupugana by the [[Imperial Army]], Subaru’s Pleiades Battalion, and a loose collection of individuals that included the [[Emilia Camp]], the [[Priscilla Camp]], [[Serena Dracroy]]'s Flying Dragon Squadron, members of the Imperial Army, and numerous rebels who began uprisings all throughout the Empire, colloquially known together as the Rebel Army. The battle was [[Vincent Vollachia|Vincent Abellux's]] apparent attempt to reclaim his throne after he was deposed by [[Chisha Gold]] and [[Berstetz Fondalfon]]. In actuality, however, it was a precursor to the [[Great Disaster]], a predestined disaster said to bring ruin to Vollachia after the death of “Vincent Vollachia”. With the help of the Stargazer, [[Ubilk]], Abel confronted Chisha in an attempt to fulfill the prophecy and end his own life, but the Fourth ranking Divine General, who was posing as Vincent Vollachia, took the then-former emperor's place to realize the forecast of Vincent Vollachia's death. The Great Disaster begins immediately following this. ==Background== Though the entire civil war following the Imperial Coup was leading towards this major battle, preparations for it didn’t truly begin until the conclusion of the [[Destruction of Chaosflame]]. With [[Olbart Dunkelkenn]]’s infantilization technique having been used on Natsuki Subaru, Vincent, using the alias Abel, decided to use his appearance as an instigating factor to drive the country into a civil war, dubbing him the black-haired crown prince. This, of course, was a massive success, causing numerous riots and uprisings all across the nation, using a black-haired figurehead of their own as an excuse to go to war. Meanwhile, Vincent had many of his allies gather in Guaral, including the People of Shudrak, General Second Class [[Zikr Osman]] and his soldiers, Divine General [[Yorna Mishigure]], Private First Class [[Jamal Aurélie]], various members of the Emilia Camp, and even members of the Priscilla Camp. Simultaneously, [[Roswaal L. Mathers]] of the Emilia Camp, using the name Dudley, was together with Serena Dracroy, where she decided to also take part in the war at the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]], offering her Flying Dragon Squadron. Lastly, unbeknownst to them all, Subaru, who had been teleported to [[Ginunhive]], was busy making an ally of every single gladiator and soldier on the island, instigating even the stalwart [[Gustav Morello]] and the bizarre, infantilized [[Cecilus Segmunt|Blue Lightning]] to march as one to the Imperial Capital, gathering allies along the way. Though many riots were forced to be quelled by the Imperial Army, they were incapable of bringing an end to all of them, and eventually, every force across the nation that was ready for war all gathered at the Imperial Capital. Utilizing the forces of the Divine Generals [[Arakiya]], Olbart Dunkelkenn, [[Moguro Hagane]], and [[Madelyn Eschart]], and Second-Class General [[Kafma Irulux]], alongside their respective armies, they defended the bastions of the Imperial Capital, thus starting the Decisive Battle for the Imperial Capital. ==Battle== ===First Battle for the Fifth Bastion=== [[File:Re Zero Light Novel 32 2.png|thumb|250px|Garfiel facing off with Kafma.]] The battle at the fifth bastion started between a large army of centaur people and the Second-Class General Kafma Irulux. Despite such a large army, Kafma had great ease in defending his bastion, and he was prepared to annihilate the rest. However, before he could, another fighter appeared on the battlefield: [[Garfiel Tinzel]]. With Garfiel telling the others to stand back, he avoided all of Kafma’s attacks and met him atop the fifth bastion, and he challenged the general. The ensuing battle between them was incredibly vicious, with Garfiel destroying and dodging a large number of Kafma’s attacks. Kafma was even forced to release his wings and take flight in an effort to keep Garfiel from reaching him. However, armed with the strength of his Divine Protection of Earth Spirits, Garfiel still managed to reach him and even drag him across the ground of the bastion. Though Kafma began to respect the boy, due to the role he had to play as a general, he was forced to use an underhanded technique that was all but guaranteed to kill his enemy: placing a large number of his insects directly within Garfiel’s body. Unable to pry Kafma’s hand away from his mouth, he was eventually pushed off of the bastion, leaving Kafma appearing to be victorious. Kafma soon realized that he did not come out victorious, as soon after, Garfiel transformed into his beast form and appeared atop the bastion. Having basically gutted himself to remove the insects as well as devouring fire stones to burn and kill them, Garfiel came back to fight Kafma once more, something that left Kafma rather elated. Kafma and Garfiel then began throwing hands up close and personal, both sides taking severe injuries. Deciding to use his strongest attack against Garfiel, he ended up revealing an extra organ he held within his body, and he ended up unleashing a laser-like attack against Garfiel that could very easily leave him as nothing more than a red mist. However, Garfiel not only withstands it, but he heals and fights against it, and he ends up attacking Kafma with an attack so strong that he not only defeats the general, but he also tears a hole through the bastion. ===Battle for the Second Bastion=== The battle started out with the weaponkin launching their attack on the second bastion. Its guardian, Divine General Madelyn Eschart, stood in their way, using her might as a dragonkin and her boomerang-like weapon to repel all of them. During the raid, however, the battlefield became cold as [[Emilia]] arrived. Due to the cold’s negative effects on the weaponkin, they became unable to properly fight, and because Madelyn outclassed them anyway, Emilia asked them to retreat while she dropped a glacier on her opponent. With Madelyn destroying the glacier, she engaged in battle with Emilia. [[File:Re Zero Light Novel 32 9.png|thumb|left|180px|Mezoreia's arrival to the battlefield.]] The battle remained mostly even, with Madelyn withstanding and shattering every attack that Emilia used, while Emilia mostly avoided every attack thrown at her, using her Ice Soldiers for assistance. She even managed to separate Madelyn from her weapon and create a wall of ice to keep her from it. Attempting to negotiate with her and learn why she fought, she stated her own reason for fighting: for her knight. However, Madelyn did not give her an answer, shattering the ice wall and taking back her weapon. Summoning the Cloud Dragon [[Mezoreia]], she had it unleash its breath, which Emilia just barely managed to deflect. This ultimately led to Emilia being forced to use the strongest attack in her arsenal, Absolute Zero, to freeze Madelyn solid. Unfortunately, this backfired. Madelyn took over Mezoreia and proceeded to unleash attacks in its body. That said, with the arrival of Cecilus Segmunt, she was spared from a fatal attack. Cecilus challenged the Dragon while entrusting Madelyn’s body to Emilia, and in return, she offered him innumerable weapons of ice to use against the Dragon. That said, with something strange taking place in the Imperial Capital, Mezoreia flew to the Crystal Palace, with a disgruntled Cecilus following behind. It wouldn’t be long after that Emilia made her way into Lupugana as well. ===Battle for the First Bastion=== In this battle, the cyclops tribe attempted to punch their way through the walls. However, Divine General Arakiya, directed by Private First Class [[Todd Fang]], easily wiped them all out with a flash of her fire. However, with the arrival of Divine General Yorna Mishigure and [[Priscilla Barielle]], Todd left the scene, and a massive battle took place, one with Arakiya’s goal to incapacitate Priscilla and put her on the imperial throne. As she utilized her vast flames, immensely pressurized water, and scorching winds, Arakiya managed to continuously repel the two, leaving them in a position difficult to even get near her. This became tougher when, upon managing to reach her, her body either turned into flame or light and counterattacked. In fact, if not for the usage of the two’s respective Soul Marriage Techniques, they would have been severely injured. Deciding to take the fight to the next stage, Priscilla and Yorna shared the Soul Marriage Technique with each other, igniting Arakiya’s confusion and fury enough that she revealed her covered eye. As the fight progressed, both Yorna and Priscilla’s attacks managed to reach her, bypassing the Spirit Eater’s intangibility. Eventually, Priscilla finally managed to strike Arakiya with her [[Enchanted Sword#Yang Sword Vollachia|Yang Sword]], granting her and her mother victory. Shortly after this however, they were encountered with something else. ===Battle for the Third Bastion=== Appearing to be the least defended of the five bastions, the winged people attempted to fight off the large number of golems that were used to defend the bastion seemingly in place of a Divine General. Soon after, the People of Shudrak, being led by their chieftain, [[Taritta Shudrak]], as well as [[Heinkel Astrea]], began making their assault as well. Realizing the intentions of the supposed weakness of the third bastion, Abel decided to send reinforcements through Zikr Osman and his troops, including Jamal Aurélie, realizing they would be being sent to their deaths. The golems were handled with incredible ease, and eventually, Heinkel managed to reach the top of the third bastion. However, waiting there was the hidden Divine General Moguro Hagane who decided to attack Heinkel for having slain so many golems on his own. After striking down Heinkel from atop the bastion, Moguro took on a massive form that surpassed even the bastion in height, and they sent off more golems. As they made their way forward, the residents of Chaosflame, with a flame burning in their eyes, launched house-sized boulders at them. Neither side was discouraged, and Zikr led his men forward in a charge against the Divine General. Meanwhile, having already gained permission from Chisha prior to the battle, Berstetz decided to take advantage of the uniqueness of Moguro’s constitution to fire the Magic Crystal Cannon against the massive Rebel Army. However, thanks to the nearly self-sacrificing efforts of [[Beatrice]] and the handiness of [[Spica|Rui’s]] teleportation, Beatrice was able to use Al Shamak to send the blast into another dimension, shocking both sides. However, Abel managed to overcome this shock quickly, and he ordered his troops to move forward while summoning the Flying Dragon Squadron brought by Serena Dracroy. As the People of Shudrak moved forward, they gained assistance in the form of [[Ram]], who used her Wind Magic to amplify their arrows’ damage, retrieve their arrows, and even fire off attacks of her own. That said, upon receiving a command from the emperor at the Crystal Palace, Moguro retreated, leaving the Rebel Army behind. ===Second Battle for the Fifth Bastion=== [[File:Re Zero Light Novel 32 10.png|thumb|right|180px|Olbart's surprise attack.]] Shortly after Kafma’s defeat, the centaur people offered Garfiel, as the victor who was responsible for opening up the hole in the bastion, to be the first one to pass through the walls. However, Garfiel did not accept and prepared to move onto the next battlefield. However, having already stopped the enemy at the fourth bastion, Divine General Olbart Dunkelkenn appeared before Garfiel and prevented anyone from moving forward, killing some of the centaur people who tried to push forward while handling Garfiel one-to-one. Despite Garfiel’s feat of defeating Kafma, Olbart merely toyed with him, using misdirection and other [[shinobi]] techniques to thrash him. He made a point to show that he could very easily kill everyone there. However, because he was focusing on preventing anyone from breaching the wall, he couldn’t move forward to kill the enemy himself, leaving him to keep his focus on repelling Garfiel. Before long, he was ready to kill him. Before he could however, a man going by the name of Dudley stepped forward to protect Garfiel, easily handling the shinobi’s misdirecting techniques. With his own knowledge of shinobi and some guidance for Garfiel, Olbart prepared to fight both of them seriously, coming to see even Garfiel as a considerable threat. As the fight progressed, Olbart eventually caught sight of an infantilized Cecilus, leaving the Vicious Old Man bewildered and annoyed, realizing that it must have been Chisha’s doing. Soon after, he had to cut the battle short, sensing something very wrong, and he retreated to the Crystal Palace. Left behind, Garfiel noticed something else was coming with his Divine Protection, and he warned Dudley about it. ===Attack on the Support Group=== Throughout the battle, [[Otto Suwen]], with the assistance of [[Petra Leyte]]’s Yang Magic, used his Divine Protection of Soul of Language to listen to the channels of the war, allowing him to accurately determine the direction of the battle. With the help of [[Medium O'Connell]] and her escorting soldiers, they were able to convey this information to Abel, allowing him to make decisions that could direct the war. Furthermore, [[Frederica Baumann]], using her leopard form, conveyed these orders across the battlefield and returned with other pieces of valuable information. Essentially, the support group made up the most important part of the Rebel Army’s forces. Realizing that the flow of the battlefield was moving oddly, Todd Fang began moving around, until he eventually reached the support group that was situated away from the main camp. Successfully managing to slaughter the soldier entourage that accompanied Medium, Todd confronted Otto, Petra, and Medium in an attempt to kill them and end the battle faster. Utilizing the spirits that he terrified to work under him, he cast some fire spells in combination with his axe in order to try and kill them. On the other hand, while Medium distracted him at points, utilizing the buried fire stones that they had secretly placed around themselves in case of emergency, Petra and Otto attempted to scare the soldier off. This ultimately failed as, combined with the spirits, he was able to sniff out the locations of each mine and trigger them prematurely, leaving the support group mostly defenseless. [[File:Re Zero Light Novel 33 12.png|thumb|left|180px|Otto, Petra, Medium, and Al holding off Todd.]] Right as he was ready to kill them, assistance came in the form of [[Al]], whose presence on the battlefield made no difference anywhere else. Because of him, Todd was completely unable to land any decisive blows, making him wary and leading him into creating a wall of flame to surround the group. Making it seem as though he was using it for cover for his own retreat, he made one final swipe at Otto. Once again, however, he failed, as Otto used his Divine Protection to dodge him. Ultimately, Todd retreated for good, leaving for another battlefield. With their enemy gone, the support group was forced to leave before they were burned, but not before Otto muttered about a problem he sensed with his Divine Protection. {{Clear}} ===Battle for the Fourth Bastion=== The battle initially began with the glow people combatting the shinobi and Olbart Dunkelkenn. The glow people were presumably defeated, and Olbart decided to move to the fifth bastion to strike the opponent that defeated Kafma there, leaving Second-Class General [[Gudda Dialmo]] and his army as the defenders in his and the shinobi's places. With Beatrice saved thanks to Rui and Subaru's efforts, the two girls who prevented Berstetz from using the Magic Crystal Cannon to decimate the battlefront of the third bastion meet and ally themselves with the Pleiades Battalion. The group sets their sights on conquering the fourth bastion being defended by General Gudda Dialmo and his troops. Subaru's [[Natsuki Subaru#Abilities|Cor Leonis]] and the Pleiades Battalion's war cries managed to recreate a lost technique of old that forcibly manifested the Flow Method and used the body's internal mana to strengthen a group, inducing an effect reminiscent of yang magic trigged by the war cries, heightening the abilities of everyone in the battalion. Intending to destroy the fighting spirit of his enemies by swiftly defeating them, Gudda attempted to attack the Galewind Horse that Subaru was riding on, but was met with Gustav Morello's shield, and blown away by a hammer attack from [[Weitz Rogen]]. The entire defense force at fourth bastion was uprooted and pulverized with not even a single fatality caused by the Pleiades Battalion. Under Subaru's orders, Gustav, Hiain, and half of the battalion went to support the other invaders at the bastions, whereas Weitz and the other half held their position at the fourth bastion. The remaining five, a unit comprised of Subaru, Beatrice, Rui, Tanza, and Idra, proceeded to enter Lupugana. Coinciding with the arrival of the Pleiades Battalion to the battlefield was the entrance of Scorching Lady Serena Dracroy, her Flying Dragon Squadron, and the two members of the Emilia Camp who visited her, Roswaal and Ram, to the war front. ===Conclusion=== With the arrival of the [[Stargazer]] [[Ubilk]] in the main tent of the Rebel Army, he decided to assist their leader, Vincent, in reaching the Crystal Palace, where he would encounter the commander of the Imperial Army and his former aide, Chisha Gold, under the appearance of Vincent. After one last conversation, Chisha used his iron fan to push Vincent out of the way, while he himself took a fatal strike from the [[Undead|undead]] [[Balleroy Temeglyph]], thus triggering the start of the Great Disaster. ==Aftermath== Directly after Chisha's death, Moguro arrived in the Crystal Palace to protect Vincent per the false emperor's orders. A short time later, Vincent unmasked himself and revealed his true identity, casting aside the name Abel and taking charge of the forces at his command to commence an evacuation of Lupugana when the reality of the Great Disaster's form became clear, ordering Moguro to hold back Balleroy and the ally who had suddenly taken his side, Mezoreia, controlled by Madelyn. At the same time, Subaru, who was within the Imperial Capital, also decided to retreat once he found and saved [[Rem]]. A majority of the living forces evacuated the city; however, Priscilla, Yorna, and Arakiya were ambushed and captured by undead at the first bastion. As a result of Priscilla's disappearance, Al stayed behind in Lupugana. Moreover, Cecilus remained in the area to hunt for the Great Disaster's ringleader, and Heinkel's breakdown following his defeat at the hands of Moguro demoralized him from acting until [[Rowan Segmunt|a man]] found him and brought him outside the city's vicinity by force. The battle ended without a proper conclusion, as the circumstances had transformed from a battlefront where living armies fought each other to a crucible of chaos in which the living clashed with an army of the undead. The battle itself, the blood spilled because of it, and the lives lost during it were all in vain, as many who had died in the hours prior to the Great Disaster rose one after another. Aside from the deaths of Chisha Gold and the soldiers or combatants who engaged in the conflict, the full repercussions that the battle has left on the Empire have not been fully comprehended by reason of the ongoing effort to terminate the Great Disaster taking more precedence in the minds of Vollachia's occupants. ==Navigation== {{Battles & Events Navbox}} [[Category:Vollachia Empire]] [[Category:Lupugana]] [[Category:Terminology]]

title: Stargazer
wikitext:
{{Construction|Page to be heavily revised}}
'''Stargazers''' (星詠み, ''Hoshiyomi'') are people in the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]] who have the ability to peer into the future. They exist to preserve Vollachia's continued existence. 

==Information==
[[Vincent Vollachia]] has said that the purpose of Stargazers are for the wellbeing of Vollachia, not for the emperor themselves.<ref>''"――. Not too far from all of your perception. Because the power of the Stargazers is to peer into the future, to preserve the Empire."'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 28]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref><ref>''"As I told you before. The Stargazer’s power is for the preservation of the Empire. ――It does not necessarily coincide with my safety."'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 28]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref> Based on [[Ubilk]]'s own description,<ref name="twofive">''“It’s about something which can be described as the alignment of the stars, or their guidance. It’s like, about people having their own destiniiies~? I’m in the business of gazing at them.” [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 30]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> they were able to tell the future from seeing the “stars”, otherwise known as the Observers,<ref>''"Your Excellency, by Observers, do you mean the “stars” Ubilk-dono speaks of?"'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 4, Section 6.</ref><ref>''"…I share the same perception. What Ubilk has recited is a type of announcement, of what the Observers had peered at." [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 4, Section 6.</ref> metaphysical beings claimed to observe the world from outside and manipulate every living thing. For this reason, Vincent refers to Stargazers as pawns of the Observers.<ref>''A convenient being who had foreseen the coming threat, yet refused to be asked for more. Or should he call said being, a pawn of the Observers?'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 30]], Chapter 1, Section 5.</ref> The Stargazers cannot be eliminated, because once a Stargazer is killed, there are countless people who can become new Stargazers, and it is unknown the standard of Observers for choosing new Stargazers. Thus, unless one is able to kill everyone inside Vollachia, it is impossible to eliminate the Stargazers. In addition, the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]'s [[Dragon History Stone]] has been compared to Vollachia's Stargazers due to their similar purposes.<ref>''It could be argued that the Stone and the Stargazer, two objects with similar roles, had both overlooked the plight of what should be the most noble position in their respective countries.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 28]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref>

The knowledge of Stargazers is shared between each other. One such example is how [[Mariuli Shudrak]] knows of songs and knowledge she would not have had the chance to learn of in her village. Another method for them to gain knowledge is through the "stars". As noted by [[Olbart Dunkelkenn]], some Stargazers can be different from one another.<ref name="twoeight">''“It’d be pointless if the other Stargazers were all tha same as it, but I’ve tortured enough of ‘em ta understand that ain’t the case.”'' [[The Land of Wolves / Death unto the Weak, No Mercy ZERO Nine Divine Generals]], Section 3.</ref> Just like the fundamental differences between Taritta and Ubilk, their knowledge is not shared. Currently, it is known that at least 27 Stargazers can coexist at the same time,<ref>''“Let’s see, within the range where our voices can be heard, there are twenty-seven of uuus~.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 34]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> though with the exception of Ubilk and [[Cecilus Segmunt]], nothing about any of the others in the present are known.

===Commandments===
The Stargazers take their instructions from a '''commandment''' (天命, ''tenmei'') passed down to them by the Observers. A commandment is often referred to as fate itself, and is regarded by many as unchangeable fate, and this has been emphasized by Ubilk many times. The method of obtaining commandments is different between Stargazers. For Ubilk, it is mostly through dreams.<ref>''“It varies. More often than not, I receive them in something like a dream.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 4, Section 8.</ref> When a person became a Stargazer, they become completely different people; a puppet that only lives to fulfill their commandment<ref>''A Stargazer is a commandment’s puppet in human form. No matter how much they could possibly have pretended to be likable or accommodating, what lay inside was naught but an obsession with their commandment and a fanatical desire to fulfill it.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 5, Section 6.</ref><ref name="twoeight" /> until they die. Based on Vincent's knowledge, it's hard for the Stargazers to resist their Commandment, and there will be cases where multiple Stargazers share the same commandment. Fortunately, there is only one Commandment at a time, and no new commandment is passed down before the previous one is fulfilled.<ref name="twenty">''“――Yes. I, for one, wouldn’t lie. No new commandment has been handed down. In the first place, without completing the previously passed down commandment, one wouldn’t try for a new commandment to be passed down, however…”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 32]], Chapter 4, Section 3.</ref>

Another thing of note is that the purposes of commandments may not necessarily align with each other, and they may even apparently contradict with each other. One example is that the commandment of Mariuli is to kill the "black-haired and black-eyed traveler" to stop the [[Great Disaster]] from happening, while the commandment of Ubilk is to kill "Vincent Vollachia" to make the Great Disaster happen and minimize the damage afterwards.

==Stargazers in History==
*[[Rowan Segmunt]] was tasked with searching for a way to reach the Heavenly Sword. This resulted in the births and murders of his numerous children, until Cecilus’s birth. Following his birth, Rowan was abandoned by the Observers after being deemed to have completed his commandment by producing Cecilus.
*At some point, Cecilus discovered Vincent Vollachia and decided to serve him. This resulted in him becoming one of Vincent’s most loyal servants, and later, the First of the reinstated Nine Divine Generals system.
*At some point, Ubilk became a Stargazer. With his prophecies, his position was cemented in the Crystal Palace, and his role was critical for quelling numerous disasters and events in Vollachia.
*During his time in the palace, Ubilk informed the emperor of the trigger that would kick off the Great Disaster: the demise of Vincent Vollachia.
*Mariuli Shudrak became a Stargazer in her youth. On her deathbed, she passed on her commandment, to kill the “black-haired and black-eyed traveler”, to [[Taritta Shudrak]] in order to prevent the stop the Great Disaster. Because of this, Taritta successfully killed [[Natsuki Subaru]] in his first failed loop in [[Arc 7]], which led to Subaru’s eventual meeting with Vincent, and his subsequent involvement with the [[Imperial Civil War]].
*After speaking to [[Chisha Gold]] about the signal for the beginning of the commandment regarding the Great Disaster, being the death of "Vincent Vollachia", he unintentionally triggered the start of the Imperial Coup, which would later result in the Imperial Civil War. Likewise, this resulted in Cecilus becoming infantilized, temporarily losing his memory, and being sent to [[Ginunhive]] as a gladiator.
*Ubilk appears in [[Chaosflame]] and assists Subaru’s and [[Spica|Rui]]’s escape from the city’s citizens. He later appears in front of Taritta Shudrak and speaks with her, shortly before the [[Satella|shadow]] burst from the Crimson Lapis Palace, which Ubilk claimed was out of his jurisdiction as it was Lugunica’s problem.
*After Subaru finds himself in Ginunhive, he stumbles onto Cecilus, who later joins Subaru’s Pleiades Battalion on the march towards the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]].
*Towards the end of the [[Battle for the Imperial Capital]], Ubilk led Vincent towards the disguised Chisha. Shortly after their meeting, Chisha pushed Vincent out of the way of a lethal attack by the [[undead]] [[Balleroy Temeglyph]]. With Chisha taking the shot while still transformed into Vincent, the Great Disaster began.
*During the escape from the Imperial Capital, Ubilk reveals that the four major nations have their own disasters: the Empire’s Great Disaster; the [[Gusteko|Holy Kingdom]]’s Collapse; the [[Kararagi|City-States]]’ Night Weeping; and the Kingdom’s Witch(es).
*During the retreat to [[Garkla]], Ubilk is given a prophecy. He is told that the keys to defeating the Great Disaster are Rui, with her Authority of Gluttony, and [[Groovy Gumlet]], with his knowledge of curses and curse tools. At some point after this, Ubilk, fulfilling his commandment by doing all he could to help end the Great Disaster, loses his position as a Stargazer.

==List of Stargazers==
===Current===
*[[Cecilus Segmunt]]

===Former===
*[[Whitaker Goldario]]
*[[Stride Vollachia]]
*[[Mariuli Shudrak]]
*[[Rowan Segmunt]]
*[[Ubilk]]

==Trivia==
*Despite being a Stargazer, Cecilus is unable to hear the voices of the Observers. On the contrary, he considers them his “audience”, and he seems to be able to convey his voice to them.
*Ubilk has referred to Subaru as a “Stargazer of the Kingdom”. Likewise, Vincent has also mistaken Subaru as a Stargazer due to the sudden future knowledge he obtained via his [[Authority]].
*The term '''gazer''' (詠み人, ''yomibito'') has been used as a substitute for “Stargazer”. In Iris and the King of Thorns, [[Whitaker Goldario]] is described as a gazer in the story's narration, and in [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6|Sword Demon Battle Ballad]], Stride Vollachia voiced that the Observers were averse to a gazer deviating from their commandment,<ref>''“…Indeed, you do not find it to your liking when a gazer deviates from their commandment, accursed Observers!”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 5, Section 2.</ref> implying that he was not adhering to his own commandment.

title: Ginunhive
wikitext:
'''Ginunhive''' (ギヌンハイブ, ''Ginunhaibu''), also known as the '''Gladiator Island Ginunhive''' (剣奴孤島ギヌンハイブ, ''Kendo Kotō Ginunhaibu''), is a large island located in the southwestern part of the [[Vollachia Empire|Sacred Vollachia Empire]]. It is where many of the Empire’s criminals and slaves are forced to become gladiators.

==Information==
For many years, the Gladiator Island has been a place where slaves or criminals became gladiators in order to fight for the entertainment of the Empire’s citizenry.<ref>''Most of the gladiators were either criminals or people who had been left with no choice but to sell themselves into this life when they had been unable to repay a debt. Every once in a great while, though, some unlucky person with nowhere to go would be caught and brought here.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 3.</ref><ref>''And this, the so-called Gladiator Island, where these fights to the death passed for entertainment, was the perfect place for the awful crowds of Imperial Citizens to slake their bloodlust.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 1.</ref> Admission to and departure from the island is strictly controlled, and the island is isolated in the middle of a black lake filled with various aquatic [[Witchbeast|witchbeasts]] in order to prevent gladiators from leaving.<ref>''Admittance to the island—as well as departure from it—was strictly controlled, and the reason for this near-total isolation of those on the island was quite simple: The gladiators could not be allowed to leave.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 2.</ref>

Before [[Gustav Morello]] became the Island Chief, Ginunhive most often featured deathmatches between gladiators, including one-on-one fights, three-on-three battles, five-on-five bouts, or even a clash between multiple gladiators and a witchbeast.<ref>''The island of Ginunhive offered a variety of entertainments featuring its gladiators. The simplest was a straightforward one-on-one deathmatch. Sometimes, there might be team battles, three-on-three or five-on-five. Sometimes, a massive Witchbeast might be brought in, and the gladiators would be forced to fight it in a “raid”-style battle. Anything to sate the spectators’ lust for blood and gore. On the Gladiator Island, any battle could be permitted if it would slake the audience’s thirst for violence.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 3|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 21.</ref> There were also some cases where special events would happen, such as the celebration of a new emperor’s coronation. These special events did away with the typical rules, and in one case, ten gladiators were pitted against a massive witchbeast.<ref>''Reflecting on examples from his past, Al knew that the celebration of a new Emperor was likely to involve death matches of some “special” variety. The usual one-on-one rules would be modified or done away with. In at least one case, ten slaves had been pitted against a massive Witchbeast caught especially for the spectacle.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 3.</ref> The only way to reach the island was through a drawbridge that was usually kept raised,<ref>''The only way to reach the island was a single bridge—specifically, a drawbridge that was usually kept raised and impassable. '' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 2.</ref> making it an impassable method for gladiators to escape through. The gladiators themselves were treated contemptibly by many of the guards,<ref>''Many of the guards treated the slaves with contempt, but this one, Auran, was unusual in that he was almost friendly with the fighters.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 2.</ref> prevented from carrying weapons outside of the arena, and they were always forced to wear handcuffs outside of the fighting grounds.<ref>''The gladiators were not allowed to carry weapons except in the arena proper, and everywhere outside the fighting grounds, they were required to wear handcuffs.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 2.</ref> In order to survive, some gladiators took up other positions like healing or prostitution, and in return, they were usually not forced to fight in the arena.<ref>''They were women in provocative clothing, and though they were officially sword slaves themselves, they served as the island’s prostitutes. They were never—well, almost never—summoned to fight in the arena, but instead, they were expected to make themselves available as an outlet for the other gladiators.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 3.</ref><ref>''Hornet might have been the most noted of the female gladiators, but no small number of women proved capable fighters in the ring. Ubilk’s job was to keep a number of them fulfilled, just as the female prostitutes did for many of the male gladiators.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 3.</ref> If a gladiator were to die, their bodies would usually be thrown into the lake from the island's waste disposal site, though in some rare cases, a spectator would purchase a corpse.<ref>''“’Course, you get the occasional spectator with, uh, funny tastes who’ll buy one of the corpses.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 2.5|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 16.</ref>

The deathmatch system was revised when Gustav Morello took over as the Island Chief. Gladiators were organized into units, which were comprised of five people.<ref>''“In the first place, since there are five people per unit, if that girl didn’t wake up, they’d have to do it while lacking in people, it was Gustav-san who said that, you know.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 64, Section 9.</ref> The people that made up a unit were selected at random upon their entry to Ginunhive,<ref>''In addition, the unit assembled for Sparka would be determined at random, composed of a selection of people who entered Gladiator Island at the time of the Sparka.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 67, Section 2.</ref> depending on its performance, it could be broken up.<ref>''“I’ve heard that every gladiator here joins a unit for Sparka at some point or another. After that, depending on their success, they may break up the unit depending on their performance, but your unit is…”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 65, Section 2.</ref> The units were formed for an event that served as a rite of passage to become a gladiator, called '''Sparka''' (スパルカ, ''Suparuka''),<ref>''“Sparka is a rite of passage for people who are going to become new gladiators, and those who have already become gladiators don’t participate.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 67, Section 2.</ref> which was unanimously regarded by gladiators as the toughest deathmatch they could face at the Gladiator Island.<ref>''It was unanimous among the gladiators’ statements, Sparka had been their toughest deathmatch on the Gladiator Island.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 67, Section 2.</ref> units could also be forced into Sparka as a punishment.<ref>''Everyone seemed to know Gustav’s desire to not waste gladiators and have their numbers reduced as much as possible, and there was a common understanding of the rules laid out. Punishment―― in other words, forced participation in a Sparka performed by an unrelated unit.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 67, Section 2.</ref> In Sparka, units face off against various types of witchbeasts, known on the island as '''Gladiator Beasts''' (剣闘獣, ''Kentō Kemono''), which were trained for use in deathmatches and had their horns broken off by the island’s guards. There were one hundred guards assigned to Ginunhive.<ref>''There were also one hundred guards assigned to the island, but it was impossible for them to stop all of the gladiators from operating in such an organized and systematic manner.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 9]], [[Brotherhood of Pleiades Part 2|Brotherhood of Pleiades Part 1]], Section 9.</ref>

Although the conditions of being a gladiator were improved in the time since Al’s escape, there were two ways that made it near impossible for other gladiators to follow in his footsteps. The first change involved the drawbridge. It was altered to be composed of two main drawbridges, one on the side of the island and the other on the opposite bank. To open the path to Ginunhive, multiple interconnected bridges connected to one of the banks were structured to form a single bridge when being lifted to the same level, the water within them was drained, and the same process occurred on the opposite bank, ultimately creating a single bridge when the procedure was finished.<ref>''In precise terms, it was not one singular bridge that was brought up, but multiple connected bridges that emerged from the bottom of the lake, apparently structured to form a single bridge. Once the bridge, divided into multiple sections, was lifted to the same level, it was then connected together to become one, which was completed while a large quantity of water was drained from it. That very mechanism was also in operation on the riverbank side, and so the drawbridge would also rise on the opposite bank. The two drawbridges raised in that way would then become one, releasing the Gladiator Island from its isolation for a limited time.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 66, Section 1.</ref> The second change involved the curse rule. When a gladiator entered the island, a curse mark was bestowed onto them.<ref>''A curse mark was bestowed upon all the gladiators on the Gladiator Island, and it was activated on those who broke the curse rule, dispossessing them of their lives.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 66, Section 1.</ref> The curse rule could be invoked whenever a gladiator broke the island's rules, and it took the lives of anyone who was engraved with a curse mark.<ref>''The curse rule was invoked when someone who had been engraved with the curse mark from Gustav violated the rules. That life would then be taken without any room for argument.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 75, Section 7.</ref> However, the curse rule could not be utilized freely. The curse rule was tied to [[Meteor#Orb-Shaped Curse Tool|a black orb-shaped curse tool]] created by [[Groovy Gumlet]], and it could only go into effect on the gladiators if they surpassed the orb's fixed range.<ref>''“――At a fixed distance, those who go too far from the curse tool will die.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 75, Section 7.</ref> Due to the curse tool's range, it was effectively impossible for gladiators to escape the Gladiator Island Ginunhive without removing the curse mark's effects. In addition to the gladiators, the guards were also subject to the curse rule and given curse marks.

==History==
The Gladiator Island has been active for at least four centuries. In the distant past, [[Reid Astrea]] visited Ginunhive for an extended period of time and achieved 6,000 recorded undefeated victories.<ref>''“Certainly, there is no time to recite the legend Reid Astrea etched into posterity in all parts of the world. Speaking of things he was famous for… the fight where he slayed a hundred Dragons, or his battle achievement of six thousand undefeated victories recorded in the arena of the Gladiator Island. The victor of a drinking competition with the existence known as the Oni God, such varieties are also there.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 24]], Chapter 2, Section 6.</ref> Another individual known as the Gladiator King visited the island at one point in time, and he became heralded as a hero. A statue and a custom-built replica of his helmet were eventually created and displayed in the island’s Colosseum to honor his legacy.

Eighteen years before [[Natsuki Subaru|Subaru]] was summoned, [[Al|Aldebaran]] appeared on Ginunhive, where he would stay for over a decade.<ref>''“Yes, I was a gladiator, a ten-odd-years vet at that.”''' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 4]], Chapter 4, Section 3.</ref> During Al’s tenure as a gladiator, he gained an assortment of scars from cuts and burns on his face. Coincidentally, a man named [[Null]] once put a cloth over the wound of a gladiator who lost their arm,<ref>''It had all started when he did nothing more but to apply a dirty cloth on an open wound of a gladiator who had lost their arm.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 67, Section 1.</ref> which eventually allowed him to officially act as a healer in the island's healing room, despite still being enslaved. Around five years into Al's stay, a man named [[Ubilk]] was sent to the Gladiator Island. For another five years, he acted as a male prostitute in order to survive and spent his time slowly trying to convince other gladiators to participate in a rebellion with him.<ref>''“I know how you must feel, I really do. I spent five years convincing them to stop dragging their feet.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 2.5|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 15.</ref> A year after Ubilk’s arrival, ten gladiators were pitted against a large witchbeast. Eight of them died, and the only two who survived were Al and a woman named [[Hornet]], who took interest in the one-armed man after he managed to survive the deathmatch.

Around the time of [[Vincent Vollachia]]'s coronation, Ubilk began the [[Ginunhive Armed Rebellion|rebellion]] he had been planning for five years by murdering [[Minor Characters#Auran|Auran]], the assigned guard of Al, the only gladiator who had not joined him. When Al refused to join in an act of sedition, Ubilk ordered Hornet to kill him shortly afterwards, though the one-armed man would barely escape certain death. The gladiators sought to take a countess who was visiting Ginunhive by the name of [[Serena Dracroy]] hostage. However, they instead captured [[Priscilla Barielle|Priscilla Pendleton]], who feigned being Serena and was taken captive to the room of the murdered master of the island, where Ubilk was. He chose to reveal his heritage as a member of the Evil Eye Tribe and spoke of his plans with Priscilla. Rather than seeking independence from the Empire, which was what all of the gladiators besides Hornet sought to achieve, Ubilk's true plan involved buying time for something; Priscilla speculated that he intended to send some of the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]] to the Gladiator Island as a distraction so that the emperor could be killed while the Generals were dispatched elsewhere. As a consequence of the uprising, [[Olbart Dunkelkenn]], the Third ranking Divine General, was dispatched to the island along with [[Arakiya]].

While trying to enter the island, Arakiya found a severely injured Al. She made the decision to heal him, and after a brief period of conversation, the two went onto the island to figure out how to open the drawbridge in order to send in her reinforcements. However, Hornet found the two of them and began to duel Al. Meanwhile, Priscilla saved her husband [[Jorah Pendleton|Jorah]] with the help of [[Balleroy Temeglyph]] and a gladiator called [[Ghajit]], though the gladiator was swiftly subdued by [[Miles]] after he began panicking. Shortly afterwards, Priscilla used a broadcast to reveal Ubilk's plan, splitting the gladiators into two factions that either sought to ensure their survival or to be free.

Priscilla’s message had no effect on Hornet, as her goal was to fall gloriously in battle at the hands of a strong opponent. Al used [[Al#Abilities|his ability]] to continue distracting Hornet and buy enough time for Arakiya to burn the body of a [[shinobi]] who used a technique known as the Poison Hand, causing the Gladiator Empress to die a death without honor. Olbart confronted Al after the drawbridge was lowered and asked if he wanted a reward, but the man declined the offer and said his goodbyes to Arakiya. Before Ubilk, the instigator of the rebellion, could be apprehended and questioned for his motivations, he was thought to have escaped Ginunhive via a teleportation mechanism within the murdered island head’s room. In the end, the ways of the Gladiator Island generally remained the same as they were before the insurgence.

When Al escaped the Gladiator Island at an unknown point in time after the revolt, he was given the jet-black replica of the Gladiator King’s helmet while leaving.<ref>''“It’s from the gladiators’ Colosseum that I was in a long time ago――! But, it’s not like I stole it! It’s just that when I was running away from that place, a kind hearted guy gave it to me. It was being displayed in the Colosseum, so I think it’s a pretty decently made helmet. Maybe.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 3]], [[Sunlight Illuminating the Water's Surface]], Section 2.</ref><ref>''“You were one of the gladiators at Vollachia, indeed. If that is so, then you must be from somewhere on the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. That helmet would be an item associated with the Gladiator King, or more accurately, a replica.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 3]], [[Sunlight Illuminating the Water's Surface]], Section 2.</ref> After his escape, the head of the island at that time was promptly fired. To fill up the position, Vincent Vollachia appointed Gustav Morello as the new Island Chief.<ref>''“I heard it was because of what happened with that person, the previous Chief was fired, and Gustav-san was chosen as the new Chief.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 69, Section 1.</ref> Under Gustav's leadership, the Gladiator Island was remade from its previous lawlessness into a more orderly place where there were less unnecessary deaths. As a result, the number of people who died from injuries or illnesses decreased.<ref>''“I asked Old Man Null, the geezer gladiator who’s been living here for a long time. He said that, before Gustav-san’s arrival, the Gladiator Island was a lawless place, and more people died from injuries or illnesses. But things have changed a lot since Gustav-san arrived. Fewer people die.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 68, Section 2.</ref>

Later on, an infantilized Natsuki Subaru, using the name of Natsuki Schwartz, arrived on the island with [[Tanza]]. In order to save everyone on the island, he befriended and allied with every gladiator and soldier on the island, including Gustav and the infantilized [[Cecilus Segmunt]]. With everyone gathered, they successfully prevented a slaughter by the hands of Arakiya and [[Todd Fang]], and they marched to the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]].

==Locations==
*'''Lake Violane''' (ヴィオラーヌ湖水, ''Viorānu Kosui''): The Gladiator Island is surrounded by a black lake, known as Lake Violane. It is filled with various aquatic witchbeasts, which, next to the deathmatches, are the second most common causes of death in the area.<ref>''By fish food, he was talking about the aquatic witchbeasts that inhabited the lake. Rather savage ones were loose there seemingly; the most common causes of death on Gladiator Island were deathmatches, but the second most common cause of death was falling prey to the witchbeasts, whether by accident or by trying to escape.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 69, Section 1.</ref>
*'''Gladiatorial Arena''': The arena is a circular field with high walls, located at the very center of Ginunhive. It is where the Gladiator Island’s deathmatches and Sparkas are held. There is a passageway for gladiators that leads into the arena, which is lowered by an iron gate whenever no events are held there. Additionally, a separate iron gate and passageway are used to bring Gladiator Beasts into the arena.
*'''Seating''': On the other side of the walls surrounding the arena, there is staircase-like seating where spectators can view ongoing deathmatches or Sparkas.
*'''Healing Room''': The healing room is located in the lower stratum of the island. The room was once occupied by Null, who used his amateur healing skills to treat other gladiators to the best of his abilities. It is also known as the corpse room, as it is where many who fall in the arena become corpses.<ref>''“This is the healing room. It’s also called the corpse room. Many people become corpses here after failing to die in the arena.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 61, Section 3.</ref>
*'''Office''': The office of the Island Chief is located in the upper stratum of the island. It is a spacious but mostly empty room, only containing a desk, a guest sofa, a bookshelf, and a toolbox, which are all used for Gustav’s work.
*'''Common Rooms''': The common rooms serve as the living quarters for the gladiators. There are usually multiple gladiators assigned to a given room.
*'''Dining Hall''': The dining hall is a space where the gladiators usually eat their meals together.
*'''Library''': A library was formed when Gustav Morello decided to start accepting books to the island. It is a place where the gladiators often spend their relaxation time together.<ref>''“It is said that they began taking in books ever since Governor Gustav became the Island Chief. Surprisingly, I hear that it has become the place where everyone spends their relaxation time together.”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 69, Section 1.</ref>
*'''Waste Disposal Site''': A place on the lower stratum of Ginunhive where anything deemed unnecessary, including human corpses, are thrown into the lake to serve as food for the aquatic witchbeasts residing there.<ref>''He and Arakiya had made landfall at the waste-disposal site on the lower part of the island—a simple landing from which trash, garbage, and anything else unnecessary that was generated on the island was thrown into the lake to feed the witchbeasts.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 2.5|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 16.</ref>
*'''Observation Decks''': There are a few balconies that serve as observation decks around the island. They overlook both the island itself and the lake that surrounds it.
*'''Control Tower''': The drawbridge used to enter the island raised and lowered at a control tower. The large metal door at its entrance is sealed by an impressive lock.
