[[File:Julius Quasi Spirits.gif|thumb|250px]]
'''Spirits''' (精霊, ''Seirei'') are beings that materialize in the [[world]] through mana and manipulate it as they please.

==Information==
===Overview===
Regarded as supernatural beings, spirits are given life by [[Od Lagna]], tied to [[magic]] by nature, and manifest through mana, which they have the aptitude to control.<ref name="born">''Spirit is the term used to refer to supernatural beings who are given life by Od Lagna, manifest in this world through the power of mana, and meddle with it as they please. They are born as lesser spirits, become quasi-spirits, and finally reach the status of spirit.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref><ref>''Beatrice, as a spirit, was closely tied with magic by nature.'' [[Beatrice's Everyone is Troublesome, I Suppose]], Section 2.</ref> For example, spirits can utilize mana in the atmosphere to form and dissolve their bodies.<ref>''Spirits could freely control the formation and disintegration of their bodies from atmospheric mana.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> In contrast, if a spirit’s Od were to receive fatal damage, it will perish.<ref>''Unless the attack penetrated the defenses of the mana composing their body and harmed their Od, the spirit would appear to be in perfect condition. However, if their Od were to sustain fatal damage, the spirit’s existence would crumble away like sand.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref> Moreover, spirits need an '''[[Terminology#Magic Related|anchor]]''' (依り代, ''yorishiro'') in order to remain in the world and store their mana.<ref>''For spirits, who form their bodies by using mana, a stone was necessary in order to remain in the world――, “――An anchor! An anchor is needed so that a spirit can remain in this world!”'' [[Re:IF]], Chapter 5, Section 6.</ref><ref>''Mana was necessary for a spirit to materialize and act. If it were a great spirit, a vast amount of mana would be needed. An anchor, something that was needed to store it, was exactly what Tia’s Light Sphere was.'' [[Re:IF]], Chapter 5, Section 6.</ref> A spirit's anchor is almost always a crystal, and because they use up mana by materializing, they return to their crystals to recover what they used.<ref>''“I use a lot of mana just by materializing. When night falls, I return to the crystal that is my anchor and prepare for when the sun is out again.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 1]], Chapter 1, Section 5.</ref> Most spirits have a limit to how long they can maintain a physical form, but they usually do not reach this limit and return to their crystal when they have no need to manifest themselves.<ref>''“There is, but in their case, there’s usually no reason to keep them in a physical form to their limit, so when there’s no need for them, they’re in hiding.”'' May 7, 2015 AskFM Q&A</ref> Some spirits have used human bodies as anchors in exceptionally rare cases, such as [[Melakuera]], who used [[Chap]] as an anchor,<ref>''“You were just used as an anchor, but I don’t really pity you in the slightest.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 4, Section 4.</ref> and [[Muspel]], which was offered [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachian]] convicts that were sentenced to death.<ref>''“After all, Natsuki Subaru and the half-elf spiritual arts user are both utterly opposed to even the appearance of injustice. ――It would be troublesome if they knew that we have been using convicts sentenced to death as the Stone’s contractors, disposing of them upon their deaths.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> 

===Grades===
There are multiple grades of spirits, and they develop not through time or age, but with accumulated power,<ref name="timeandgs">''“If no one interferes, and they grow vigorously, a spirit can, in the end, grow into a great spirit. There are rankings amongst the great spirits too, so please think of it being like the way that although all humans can, after enough years, become adults, there are individual differences in adults too, due to differing abilities. Having said that, spirits develop not by age, but by accumulated power, so time isn't everything.”'' [https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/1015643296108982272 July 8, 2018 Twitter Q&A]</ref> among other things, such as a sense of self and knowledge. Once a spirit accumulates enough of these qualities, it advances into the next grade.

Spirits begin their lives as '''lesser spirits''' (微精霊, ''bi seirei''), beings that, prior to growing into spirits, are essentially balls of mana.<ref>''Lesser spirits were beings who hadn’t yet become spirits, essentially balls of mana.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 2, Section 10.</ref> Although they cannot communicate with words, lesser spirits can transmit and receive feelings with mana.<ref>''Fundamentally speaking, lesser spirits were unable to communicate with words. At best they could transmit and receive feelings via mana, but the lesser spirits were still very fond of this crude form of communication.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> They can start to develop knowledge, and if they gain strength and a sense of self over time, they can grow into normal spirits.<ref>''“Lesser spirits are beings that, in a state prior to becoming spirits, start to develop some knowledge. If, over time, they gain power and self-awareness, they’ll become spirits like me.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 1]], Chapter 1, Section 6.</ref> Between spirits and lesser spirits are '''quasi-spirits''' (準精霊, ''jun seirei''), which also retain an inability to comprehend words and an ability to transmit emotions.<ref>''“They don't understand words, but they are at the level where emotions can be sent. His good or bad impressions of other people and such, that can be sent as well.”'' [https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/1015644274883420160 July 8, 2018 Twitter Q&A]</ref> They have a sense of self and can fulfill tasks assigned to them by a contractor. As spirits develop by their accumulated power, quasi-spirits naturally have more strength than lesser spirits.<ref>''In contrast, Julius had contracts with multiple quasi-spirits more powerful than lesser spirits, which meant he was a powerful practitioner himself.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 15]], Interlude, Section 6.</ref>

Once a spiritual being that is born as a lesser spirit and becomes a quasi-spirit accumulates enough power, it finally attains the grade of '''spirit'''.<ref name="born" /> A spirit tends to have a developed mind of its own, can communicate itself, and has the ability to guess the emotions and tell surface thoughts on humans’ minds by sensing them within mana.<ref>''The emotions of humans dwelled within mana. For that reason, those who excelled at perceiving such mana could easily guess the emotions of others. The ability spirits had to read minds was said to be corollary to this.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> Despite the fact that spirits generally have liberal principles,<ref name="principles">''Anyway, even among spirits who generally had fairly liberal principles, Melakuera was a spirit who followed extremely rigid rules.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 3, Section 3.</ref> they are self-centered beings who prioritize their own wills and desires in nearly all cases.<ref name="self">''It could be said that it was very much like a spirit to be so extremely self-centered. The natural beings known as spirits did not need any reason besides their own will for their actions and their results. The only exception being a contract with a spiritual arts user, in which case they may prioritize the will of their contractor. In any other situation, a spirit would place its own convenience above all else.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 3, Section 3.</ref> It is well-known that provoking a spirit will invite disaster.<ref>''But even so, it was a fact that spirits were beings of incredible power, and it was well known that to provoke one was to invite disaster.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 2, Section 1.</ref> If spirits were to come into contact with one another and have a conflict caused by their different aims, the only result and solution is for one to wipe out the other.<ref>''If fellow spirits came into conflict due to their differing goals, it would only result in battle. When this happened, the only solution was for one to wipe out the other, and thus it could probably be said that spirits were savage beings much more simplistic than humans.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 3, Section 3.</ref> A majority of them take on animal-like forms, but on some occasions, they can specialize in taking a human form.<ref>''“Though on instances there are also some who specialize in taking the forms of humans, a great deal of spirits’ original forms are animal-esque forms.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> That being said, they prefer not to take on a human form, hence why a majority of spirits that can change their forms do not choose to appear as one.<ref name="formandnecessity">''“There aren’t many spirits that deliberately take human shape, so probably not. In the same way that Puck has the form of a cat, those who can chose the form they prefer don’t often want to take human form. Petelgeuse attached himself to humans out of necessity, and Beako was designed by Echidna, as well.”'' August 13, 2014 AskFM Q&A</ref> With enough time and accumulated power, they become '''great spirits''' (大精霊, ''dai seirei'') in the end.<ref name="timeandgs" /> Even among great spirits, manifesting in a detailed human form signifies that a spirit wields extraordinary power.<ref>''“Anastasia-sama, to manifest herself in such a detailed human form means that even among great spirits, Tia-sama possesses extraordinary power.”'' [[Kararagi Reaper Incident 3]], Section 2.</ref>

===Variants===
A rare variant of spirits designated as enemies of mankind and hostile to life around them are '''evil spirits''' (邪精霊, ''yokoshima seirei'').<ref>''On the other hand, it was a rare occurrence, but spirits that evidently bore ill will towards those around it, such as what was inside of the Water Mirror, were born. They were called evil spirits and were given the same treatment as witchbeasts, designated as the harmful enemies of humanity.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 3]], [[Sunlight Illuminating the Water's Surface]], Section 5.</ref> They are alternatively known as '''fairies''' (妖精, ''yōsei'').<ref>''Echidna’s teasing statement also seemed to express pity that she called the lesser spirit a fairy. That was a term for an evil spirit. No spirit would be pleased to be referred to as a detestable, abominable fairy.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 14]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> There are no differences between evil spirits and regular spirits in a strict sense.<ref>''Evil spirits were a species of spirits, but there were no differences between the two in a strict sense.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 3]], [[Sunlight Illuminating the Water's Surface]], Section 5.</ref> They can hold malicious intent to humans and animals, and while it is speculated that they were corrupted in the process of becoming a spirit, the cause or causes behind their birth as well as their true natures are unclear.<ref>''Evil spirits, while originating from the same source as spirits, harbored malicious intent to harm people and animals. They were an evolution of lesser spirits, just like spirits, but popular belief described them as the result of corruption occurring amid this process, while their cause of birth and essential nature were shrouded in mystery.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 5]], [[The Three Idiots Set Out! Earth Spider Episode Part 3|The Three Idiots Set Out! Earth Spider Episode]], Section 13.</ref> It is presumed that evil spirits cannot suddenly shift their natures and they have no reason for their malevolence as mankind’s enemies,<ref>''Evil spirits were evil spirits; their nature would not warp into something else so abruptly. There was no reason for their malignity either, as they were purely an enemy against humanity.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 3]], [[Sunlight Illuminating the Water's Surface]], Section 5.</ref> though the [[Earth Spider]]’s inclination to change contradicts this claim. In addition, because their origins are the same as a normal spirit’s, evil spirits communicate with people who possess a high affinity with spirits in unusual ways.<ref>''Nevertheless, since their roots remained identical to spirits', it was not impossible for them to come into contact with humans possessing great affinity for spirits in strange ways.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 5]], [[The Three Idiots Set Out! Earth Spider Episode Part 3|The Three Idiots Set Out! Earth Spider Episode]], Section 13.</ref>

When the [[Witch#Witch of Greed, Echidna|Witch of Greed]], [[Echidna]], was alive, she created three man-made '''artificial spirits''' (人工精霊, ''jinkou seirei''). Of the three total artificial spirits that were ever successfully created,<ref>''There have only been three successful attempts. Where are these three now, and what are they doing?'' [[Re:Zero Visual Complete Vol.3 Rem]], Character Visual “Beatrice”.</ref> the first of them was [[Puck]], and the last was [[Beatrice]].<ref>''Of the artificial spirits that were created by the Witch Echidna, in which Beatrice was included, only three existed in this world. The first of which was Puck, and the last was Beatrice.'' [[Beatrice's Everyone is Troublesome, I Suppose]], Section 2.</ref> The three artificial spirits were forged with unspecified mechanisms.<ref>''Constructed using mechanisms similar to the artificial spirits, each one was a brand new life.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 35]], Chapter 1, Section 5.</ref> They differ from normal spirits in some respects. Puck and Beatrice were born as great spirits and wield extreme power at the cost of having a large mana consumption rate and being incapable of absorbing mana from the atmosphere, instead needing it from humans or their contractors. In contrast, [[Eridna|Echidna]] does not consume much mana and is skilled in concealing herself, but she cannot contract with humans and has difficulties using magic. To Puck and Beatrice, the concept of a duty and the meaning of their births carry an incredibly significant weight to them.<ref>''Duty; that word, to spirits―― to the artificial spirits Beatrice and Puck, that word carried weight. A weight so incredibly heavy that it was beyond any possible comparison, constituting the core of their selves.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref><ref>''For the crafted lives that were artificial spirits, the meaning for being born was the weightiest, most precious thing of all.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 2, Section 3.</ref> If something concerned the duty that one of them had, the other would not impede them from carrying it out.<ref>''One day, Puck would depart from that palace and leave to search for something solely his own. She had heard about that before, and as long as it was concerned with Puck’s duty, Beatrice could not impede him.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By]], Chapter 2, Section 3.</ref>

Spirits are unable to have children.<ref>''“They can’t.”'' [https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/495524631156391936 August 2, 2014 AskFM Q&A]</ref> In spite of their biology normally making this impossible, there is a single known exception where a spirit has had a child. Although a spirit and a human should not be able to have a child together, as the mana body of a spirit is fundamentally different in structure from that of a human body, the Mad Prince of [[Gusteko]], [[Vague Adgard]], was born to a great spirit parent and a human mother through unknown means, making him the only '''spirit human''' (精霊人, ''seireijin'') in the world. He was granted a body that does not age past a certain point, and his heart does not beat. In a similar vein, he can switch between a physical body and a mana body at will, which effectively grants him a form of immortality.

===Contracts===
Contracts, a type of promise between two parties, carry great meaning for spirits.<ref>''In this world, contracts bore enormous weight to the beings known as spirits.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 15]], Chapter 1, Section 3.</ref> It is uncommon for someone to naturally have an affinity for spirits and form a contract with them, and it is even rarer for one to do so with powerful spirits.<ref>''“The predisposition needed to form contracts with spirits is rare to begin with, and powerful spirits are even rarer.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 3]], Chapter 2, Section 4.</ref> Contracted spirits tend to reflect their contractor’s magic affinity. There are, however, rare cases where someone with high ability can form a contract with spirits without regard to affinity.<ref>''“More or less, the spirits that can be contracted will tend to have the contractor’s affinity. Someone with really high ability might be able to contract a spirit without regard to affinity, but it feels like that would be rare.”'' July 28, 2014 AskFM Q&A</ref> Individual spirits desire different conditions to fulfill a contract. Simple requirements, like contact with their contractor, are typically all that lesser spirits ask for,<ref>''“So individual spirits want different things… But lesser spirits like that just want contracts with simple conditions like contact with the caster.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 2]], Chapter 1, Section 5.</ref> but it can be more challenging to fulfill a contract with a normal spirit.<ref>''“Right, it’s a bit harder to satisfy a spirit with a mind of his own, like me.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 2]], Chapter 1, Section 5.</ref> While spirits tend to be self-centered beings who follow their own wishes in most scenarios, they may prioritize the will of a spiritual arts user who they are contracted with.<ref name="self" />

A person who conveys themselves to spirits by forming a contract with one and borrowing their powers is a '''spiritual arts users''' (精霊術師, ''seirei-jutsushi'').<ref>''“A spiritual arts user is one who can convey their heart to them, borrowing the spirits’ power through forming a contract.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 14]], Chapter 1, Section 8.</ref> Spirits and spiritual arts users utilize '''[[Magic#Spiritual Arts|spiritual arts]]''' (精霊術, ''seirei-jutsu''), which uses mana in the atmosphere around them. The process is different from normal magic, which takes mana from within a human, though the principles of the magic and the effects are the same.<ref>''“In contrast, spiritual arts users use the mana in the air around them. The process is fairly different, even when the effects are the same.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 3]], Chapter 2, Section 4.</ref><ref>''“It’s spiritual arts, using magic that uses mana from the atmosphere. It’s a difference between using mana from inside or outside, and the principle of the magic is the same.”'' [https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/477843319448698880 June 15, 2014 AskFM Q&A]</ref> The strength of a spell that spiritual arts users can cast is dependent on the power of the spirit they are contracted with.<ref>''“And the strength of the spells a spiritual arts user can use is dependent on the spirit you’ve formed a contract with.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 3]], Chapter 2, Section 4.</ref> While spiritual arts users can form contracts with multiple spirits, an extraordinary talent is necessary for them to even borrow the abilities of passing lesser spirits.<ref>''“It is a rare talent to be able to borrow strength from passing lesser spirits like Lady Emilia does.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 21]], Chapter 2, Section 1.</ref> While spiritual arts users are the only people spirits tend to use their powers for, they can lend the spirits they are contracted with to other people as long as the spirit itself gives them permission.<ref>''“If the spirit itself gives permission, it’s not impossible.”'' August 6, 2014 AskFM Q&A</ref> Uniquely, if a person has had their name devoured by the [[Authority#Authority of Gluttony|Authority of Gluttony]], as in the case of [[Julius Juukulius]], the name connected to the contract will cease to exist while the contract itself can potentially remain intact. Should this happen, the spirits involved in the contract may not offer their assistance to their contractor. However, by breaking that contract and renewing it, not only can said person use their power again, but it is even possible for the spirits involved, if they are of lower grades, to evolve one grade higher.

===Possession===
Although not commonly seen, spirits are capable of possessing people, though the exact limitations to this are unknown. As the majority of spirits have no need to do so, they are rarely seen possessing people. However, there are a few notable examples. In one case, the artificial spirit Echidna possessed [[Anastasia Hoshin]]’s body after she locked herself away in her Od. In this state, Echidna could control her body as if it were her own, and she was capable of using magic by way of Anastasia’s Od. In another case, the evil spirit [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti]], for reasons as of yet still unknown, needed to use the bodies of humans as his vessels out of necessity.<ref name="formandnecessity" /> He could only take control of humans that were compatible with spirits and had no preexisting contracts with them. Like Echidna, he could control their bodies as his own, and he was also still able to use his [[Authority]] in each host he possessed. Said hosts were beings compatible with spirits and capable of making contracts with them, and in the event that a spirit is residing within the target, Petelgeuse can forcefully eject them and make a one-sided contract in order to hijack the body for himself. However, he could only take control of humans that were compatible with spirits and had no preexisting contracts with them.<ref>''“Forcing a contract onto a human being qualified to be a spiritual arts user and taking over their bodies. That’s the truth behind your possession. Sin Archbishop… no, spirit, Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti!”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 9]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref>

Although not quite the same as typical possession, there is a unique case in which a “core” of a spirit’s power can directly influence and change whomever holds it in their possession. The great spirit [[Zarestia]]’s Light Sphere, which contains the vast majority of her power and bloodlust, is capable of granting the one who holds it her power. However, it also gives them her bloodlust and certain other quirks, such as her fear of alcohol (at least in [[Re:IF]]). Likewise, their bodies may also begin to take on Zarestia’s appearance as well. However, despite this, the person holding the Light Sphere is not actually being possessed directly by Zarestia, as Zarestia will continue acting of her own will in her own body.

==Four Great Spirits==
The '''Four Great Spirits''' (四大精霊, ''Shi Dai Seirei''), also simply known as the '''Four Greats''' (四大, ''Shi Dai''), are a group of great spirits that possess exceptional and unparalleled power among spirits of their grade.<ref>''Particularly powerful spirits are known as great spirits, but even among them there are four who possess exceptional power, the ones known as the Four Great Spirits, and these four spread dread, reverence, blessings, and menace across all the land.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref> Their existences are widely known throughout the world, as handling them is a matter of grave importance for the world’s countries.<ref>''Their existence and names are known far and wide, and the matter of how to deal with them is considered to be of grave importance in all the world’s countries.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref> They each reside in a great nation and govern one of the four main magic attributes. With the exception of [[Odglass]], the Sacred Beast, the Four Greats are often not friendly with mankind, and their actions are predominantly self-righteous.<ref>''Setting aside the Sacred Beast, the Four Greats cannot be said to be friendly to mankind, and their actions for the most part are entirely self-righteous.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref>

===Current===
====The Beast of the End, Puck====
{{Main|Puck}}
Puck is the first artificial spirit created by Echidna. In the past, he lived with Beatrice at Echidna's palace until he departed to fulfill the mission he was born with. An indeterminate number of years later, he found a frozen [[Emilia]] in the [[Elior Forest|Great Elior Forest]] and watched over her for many years to come until, one day, he freed her. He began to live with Emilia in Elior Forest until Melakuera, the great spirit who then governed fire mana, made an attempt to eliminate her. Emilia and Puck made a contract as a result, and together, they successfully vanquished Melakuera. After the Arbitrator's death, Puck took his position as the great spirit that governs fire mana.<ref>''“I spent a long time in the Great Elior Forest, a world of permafrost, am served by the great spirit Puck, who governs fire mana, and am a silver-haired half-elf.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 4]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref><ref>''“The Arbitrator Melakuera has been absent ever since. It is said that his now empty position among the Four Greats is filled by the being known as the Beast of the End.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Epilogue, Section 2.</ref>

Currently, Puck is trapped in a crystal after having broken his contract with Emilia, spending his power to delay [[Roswaal L. Mathers]]'s weather-changing spell, and saving everyone who was within the [[Sanctuary]].<ref>''Having broken his contract and pushed himself several times over, this was the sealed bed in which Puck had fallen into a deep sleep.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 15]], Interlude, Section 3.</ref><ref>''“The great spirit preceded your arrival, destroyed the seals, and apparently delayed the spell’s activation. He used all his strength to save the people in the settlement.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 15]], Chapter 6, Section 6.</ref> After receiving a high-purity crystal for her efforts during the [[Battle for Priestella]], Emilia is currently waiting for enough mana to be stored within the crystal for Puck to return.<ref>''“There’s not enough mana stored up yet for Puck to come out, but I just have to be patient for a little while longer.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 20]], Chapter 7, Section 7.</ref>

====The Stone, Muspel====
{{Main|Muspel}}
Muspel is a spirit that does not possess intentions, words, or a philosophy; it simply exists.<ref>''The Stone, Muspel, a sanctum that merely exists, possessing no will, words, or ideology.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref> It resides and wanders in the Sacred Vollachia Empire. Unlike its fellow Great Spirits, Muspel has not left any voluntary actions or claims in the annals of history, making it seem like the most spirit-like of spirits.<ref>''Unlike the Sacred Beast, the Slasher, and the Arbitrator of the other countries, it was a being that had not left any voluntary actions or claims in the annals of history. Though it was known to exist in Vollachia, no further information or observations of it had surfaced; one could even say it was the most spirit-like Sspirit.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 36]], Chapter 1, Section 3.</ref> Records from Vollachia rule that Muspel moves on a grand scale every 12 years, leading to various earthquakes after its movements.<ref>''“And given that the records of major activity were twelve years apart, we can anticipate a large-scale earthquake in six years.”'' [[The Land of Wolves / Death unto the Weak, No Mercy 8]].</ref>

Muspel and its mana were used in the [[Great Disaster]] by [[Sphinx]] to revive [[undead]] throughout Vollachia. Presently, however, the Spirit Eater [[Arakiya]] has fully devoured and assimilated with the Stone.

====The Slasher, Zarestia====
{{Main|Zarestia}}
Zarestia is a spirit that indulges in everlasting tranquility at her dwelling.<ref>''The Slasher, Zarestia, the most beautiful slaughterer who indulges in eternal peace in her bed.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref> Predating the [[Satella|Witch]] and the [[Volcanica|Dragon]], she once exerted mastery over the four main affinities, but after nearly being killed by humans, she was left with control over wind magic and developed an intense bloodlust that compelled her to kill everything, no matter the circumstances. She lives in Zarestia's Bed on the far western side of the [[Kararagi|Kararagi City-States]].

====The Sacred Beast, Odglass====
{{Main|Odglass}}
Odglass is a spirit who, unlike most other spirits, interferes with the way of the world by watching over the human populace in the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko, where she resides, with affection and benevolence from her abode, the Sacred Mountain Paradochia.<ref>''The Sacred Beast, Odglass, who watches over mankind with affection and benevolence from atop the Sacred Mountain.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref><ref>''Normally, spirits didn’t interfere with the way of the world, but Odglass was an exception among them, and she continued to take a friendly position toward humans. The Great Spirit called all the lives in the harsh land of Gusteko her own children, yet she spared little mercy for them.'' [[Red Snowfall on the Orcos Domain Part 1]], Section 3.</ref> She is a powerful great spirit who has scores of spirits and lesser spirits under her control, which she uses to help humans live in the permafrost-covered nation.<ref>''The simple fact that humans were able to live in Gusteko, which was covered by permafrost, was primarily due to the help of the myriad of spirits and lesser spirits under the control of Odglass.'' [[Red Snowfall on the Orcos Domain Part 1]], Section 3.</ref>

The ruling entity of Gusteko is a theocracy known as the [[Gustekan Church]], which has a doctrine that centers on both her and spirits in general. At the country's founding, she exchanged a contract with a spiritual arts user who followed her, bestowed the title of Holy King onto them, and from then on, she was involved in choosing successive Holy Kings, who were selected out of the citizens regardless of their bloodline or origin.<ref>''At the founding of the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko, Odglass bestowed the name Holy King and exchanged a contract with a spiritual arts user who followed her, and since then she has always been involved in choosing the Holy King, who is the head of the nation. The Holy King who leads the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko is determined, regardless of bloodline or origin, by being chosen by the Sacred Beast Odglass from one selected out of the citizens to lead the next generation.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 1]], [[The Day I Gave Up on Being a Following Star]], Section 1.</ref> This process created an established and long relationship with Odglass and Gusteko, as the tradition to select the Holy King is something she has held from the beginning of the country’s history. Because of this, she is heralded as the Church’s Benevolent Mother.<ref>''Due to this, Odglass and the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko had a long and profound friendship. The authority to decide the head of the Holy Kingdom and the Church, the Holy King, had been delegated to Odglass, and this tradition had been passed down from the beginning of the history of the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko. That format was unbreakable. Odglass had always been, and would always be, the Benevolent Mother of the Church.'' [[Red Snowfall on the Orcos Domain Part 1]], Section 3.</ref>

===Former===
====The Arbitrator, Melakuera====
{{Main|Melakuera}}
Melakuera was a spirit who acted to protect the balance of the world and arbitrate unnatural threats who could jeopardize its safety.<ref>''The self-appointed Arbitrator, Melakuera, who acts in order to preserve the balance of the world.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Prologue.</ref><ref>''The flaming horse’s goal was as he stated, to protect the balance of the world, and to deliver arbitration upon any unnatural distortions.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 3, Section 3.</ref> Initially born as a lesser spirit from the spark of a campfire, he lived alongside a man named Melakuera until his death and resolved to protect the world and save all others from suffering to fulfill the wishes of his friend by following a rigid set of self-appointed rules.<ref name="principles" /><ref>''It would fulfill its friend’s prayer. It would fulfill Melakuera’s hope, he who had entrusted it with maintaining peace and tranquility. It would protect the world from all dangers. It would save others from all suffering.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 4, Section 6.</ref> After taking the name of its friend and developing power, Melakuera eventually became a great spirit. He divided his existence into seven parts, each of which he controlled individually and used to monitor the world as an arbitrator who deterred any signs of a potential calamity.<ref>''The great spirit Melakuera had divided his existence into seven parts, and was controlling each of them individually. Possessing seven bodies, each of which was on par with Puck, he used this overwhelming power to monitor threats to the world, secretly acting as a force to deter any potential causes of calamity.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 4, Section 5.</ref>

Seven years before the events of the main story, the Arbitrator set his sights on Elior Forest and discovered Emilia there. He regarded her existence as a threat and a sin solely because of her resemblance to the Witch of Envy.<ref>''“Don’t play dumb, half-devil! No, half-elf! You who bear the same appearance as the Witch! Born from the same cursed blood as the Witch, descendant of the Witch! Reincarnation of the Witch! Danger to the world!”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 4, Section 3.</ref><ref>''“Your very existence in this world is a sin. That is unforgivable.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: Bonds of Ice]], Chapter 4, Section 3.</ref> Melakuera perished when Puck, the Beast of the End, made a contract with Emilia, and worked together with her to defeat him.

This allowed a spirit eater to take the abilities of a spirit for themselves until it was consumed.<ref>''As a spirit eater, Arakiya could ingest the spirits in the atmosphere around her and make their power her own. [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 2|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 12.</ref> They were created in the distant past to oppose an unnamed [[Witch]] who charmed everything.<ref>''Created in ancient times to oppose a lone Witch who charmed all, whom even the wordless great spirit obeyed, they were beings devised for the purpose of fighting, much like the Oni Clan that could sense miasma.'' '''Lugunica''' (ルグニカ, ''Rugunika''), also known as the '''Royal Capital of Lugunica''' (王都ルグニカ, ''Ōto Rugunika''), or simply the '''Royal Capital''', is the capital city of the [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica]]. It is where the Lugunican [[Royal Family]] traditionally ruled the Kingdom of Lugunica from, until their purported extinction. The Council of Wise Men is currently regulating the country as its provisional government, holding the [[Royal Selection]] to choose a new monarch. It is a primary setting for the events of [[Arc 1]], [[Arc 3]], and [[Arc 10]].

==Information==
===Overview===
Lugunica is a large circular city in the heart of the Kingdom, surrounded by high outer walls. It can be accessed from the gate in front of the city that goes along the main street and directly leads to its center. The Royal Capital is divided into five layers, with the topmast layer being the core of the city, containing the Royal Lugunica Castle and the areas surrounding it, including the knights’ garrison, the Prison Tower, and the Royal Magic Research Institute. Under the castle layer is the elegant Noble District where the country’s nobility resides, and below it is the Commercial District, home to a variety of shops. The Commoner District and the slums are on the lowest layer. The city is characterized by a disparity between the wealthy and the destitute, who could be said to live in completely contrasting worlds.

The capital has a population of 300,000, although when accounting for merchants and adventurers, as well as for festivals, there are more people within it at any given time.<ref>''──The Royal Capital of Lugunica, the center of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica. The biggest capital of the Dragon Kingdom, a diverse melting pot with a population of over 300,000. That was the name and title of the land Rem and Ram were standing on.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref><ref>''“It’s not an unusual scene for the Royal Capital… is what I’d like to say. But today is just speciaaal~. Today is the day of the Tammuz Festival, one of the monthly festivals that happen once a month.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 1.</ref> The districts on the lower layers are abundant with a great number of [[Demi-Human|demi-human]] races across them, making the Royal Capital a melting pot. However, as a possible result of the prejudice they face, demi-humans are almost always commoners, so they are usually unseen in the Noble District and the Royal Castle. A number of guard stations are scattered around the city to maintain law and order.

The Royal Capital is protected by a force simply referred to as the guards. The guards, who are recruited annually even from among the commoners and checked for their physical and magical aptitude, education, work experience, qualifications, and enthusiasm,<ref>''"Guards are recruited annually, so please apply. Even a commoner is just fine. They’ll check your education and work experience, qualifications and enthusiasm. If you pass the magical strength and physical fitness exams, you’ll be selected. Knights will be shaken off by their family background first."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref> are based in numerous stations across the capital and act similar to a police force. They are also responsible for dealing with the entry and exit of the Royal Capital. All this being said, the guards are beneath the knights in the hierarchy.<ref name="guards">''"Even within the capital there are multiple guard stations, but basically, when people say ‘guard station’, they mean the one on the edge of the nobles’ section of town, where Julius dropped by. There’s the same sort of differences as between a police officer and a police chief, but it’s fine to basically think of them all as below the knights."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref>

===Royal Castle===
<gallery type="slideshow">
Royal Castle Daisanshou.png|The Royal Castle as seen in the Arc 3 manga.
Royal Castle Outside.png|The Royal Castle seen from the distant streets of the capital.
</gallery>
As of the present day, the Royal Capital is effectively run by the Council of Wise Men in the '''Royal Lugunica Castle''' (ルグニカ王城, ''Rugunika Ōjō''). In everyday conversation, the government is synonymous with the Royal Castle, and people will mention the castle whether to refer to the government or to the building itself. Although it is true that the King, who was technically the leader of the country, and the royal family resided in the Royal Castle and had influence over certain matters in the Royal Capital and the nation, governance was mostly left to the council both before and after the demise of the royal family. Because of the separation between the powers of the Royal Castle and the [[Divine Dragon Church]], the church and the castle maintain a certain distance from each other, and because of this, the church has no sway at all with the castle and its leaders, something which may have led to their hesitation to act when the royal family [[Royal Plague|fell ill]].

Although they have used Royal Castle's throne room in public matters, the council carries out meetings in a specified room, and those involved in said meetings or those qualified to be there can usually freely come and go as they please. The meetings they hold typically vary, but they are usually held to deal with important matters, such as how to handle the liberated [[Pleiades Watchtower]] or to determine whether to acquit the deeds of an [[Meili Portroute|assassin]]. When dealing with matters that involve the possible crimes of those who are connected to or have particularly high standing in governmental matters, such as the Royal Selection candidates, interrogations will be held in a private meeting room where the Council of Wise Men are already present. The one being interrogated will be escorted by the knights, and behind them, every door they pass through will be shut while the knights keep their scrutinizing gazes on the one being judged. In the room where they are to be interrogated, they are effectively at the center of the room with all eyes on them. The knights will be placed at evenly spaced points in the room, the door will be shut, and they will all be armed. Although attendants can be allowed during such interrogations at the whims of the council, the only ones allowed to speak freely are the interrogators and the interrogated, and speaking out can result in punishment.

Although it is unclear if there are specific parts of the castle meant for this, a certain section of the castle can be used to place certain people on house arrest. If there is no reason to place the suspected person in prison or there is reason to isolate someone from the world outside the castle, the person will be given a room in a specified wing of the castle. There, numerous knights will be put in place to prevent the person's escape. The person will be given wooden utensils in place of regular ones in order to prevent them from being used as weapons, and in the case that one of the people they are isolating is a capable magic user, they will take measures to seal off the person's magic as well.<ref>''"Seems like it’ll be a headache later on, but it’s fine for now. In that case, follow behind me. Emilia-sama’s locked up on a higher floor. They’ve done the appropriate arrangements in order to seal her magic――"'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 27, Section 3.</ref> When the Royal Selection candidates were restricted this way, they were placed in the castle's East Wing, and the rotation of the patrolling knights was left to the commander, [[Marcos Gildark]]. Furthermore, the council can also choose whether to allow outside visits through official queries or prevent others from visiting the isolated person to keep said person trapped with no chance to plan an escape.

As of the [[Lugunican Subversive Conspiracy|events]] of Arc 10, the current state of the Royal Castle is one of corruption. Various members of both the Council of Wise Men, the knights, and other unspecified people have been replaced with members of the [[Beloved Children]], putting the castle, as well as the country at large, under the direct command of [[Capella Emerada Lugunica]]'s forces.

==History==
*Note: The characters within the story rarely describe historical events within helpful context, so the unit BA, “Before Arrival”, and AA, “After Arrival”, will be used to place moments in time with the best available knowledge. Both are in reference to Natsuki Subaru’s arrival in the new world. Also note that the units are not official.

===Before 400 BA===
*Years before the covenant with [[Volcanica]] was formed, demi-humans had a role in constructing the Royal Castle.<ref>''“Back before the covenant with the Dragon… demi-human tribes were among those who helped construct this castle. Trying to speculate about the relations between humans and demi-humans in those days is a fool’s errand, but it is rather ironic. It was those times that allowed this moment of reprisal.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 2]], Sixth Stanza, Section 4.</ref> The castle’s hidden passageways were created at this time.

===Approximately 50 BA===
*[[Emerada Lugunica]], a princess known for her beauty, wisdom, and cruelty, suddenly succumbs to an illness at a young age. The news of her death was suppressed for a period of time because she was branded a heretic for having an unfathomable darkness within her. Emerada was ultimately denied a state funeral, with the claimed reason being that the circumstances were too dire to give her one. However, in actuality, the Kingdom’s people were against holding one for her.

===48-40 BA===
*The Demi-Human War begins. As the war drags on, the bustle in the Royal Capital gradually fades over time.

*[[Roswaal J. Mathers]] becomes involved in the war when [[Sphinx]] appears at Castour Field to gather [[Undead#Corpse Soldiers|corpse soldiers]]. Following a brief encounter at Castour Field, Roswaal and the members of the Zergev Squadron who accompanied her give a report on Sphinx’s activity at the assembly hall within the Royal Castle. Afterwards, Sphinx is branded a [[Witch]].

*In 43 BA, Sphinx, [[Rom|Valga Cromwell]], and an [[undead]] [[Libre Fermi]] launch an [[Invasion of the Royal Castle|attack]] on the Royal Castle. They are all confronted and defeated by [[Wilhelm van Astrea|Wilhelm Trias]], [[Grimm Fauzen]], [[Bordeaux Zergev]], [[Carol Remendis]], and Roswaal J. Mathers. Libre is reduced to ash and the other two attackers are presumed dead, but in truth, Valga was covertly taken prisoner and was sent to the McMahon Manor outside the Royal Capital, while Sphinx was left limbless and taken captive by [[Leip Barielle]], who sought to further his plan to take the Kingdom for himself.

*In 42 BA, the Sword Demon abandons his knighthood and leaves his post at the Royal Capital to return to his home, the Trias Domain, when he discovers that it is under attack. He was cornered by demi-humans until [[Theresia van Astrea]] saved him. When he returns to his and Theresia’s meeting spot in the slums, he has a falling out with her and spends the next few years improving his sword skills.

*Two years after the Sword Saint's arrival on the battlefield, the war ends, and [[Cragrell Dawson]], the last remaining leader of the Demi-Human Alliance and the demi-human representative, signs a peace treaty with King [[Gionis Lugunica]], ending the war.

*A ceremony to commemorate Theresia’s wartime achievements is held at the ceremony hall in the Royal Castle. Wilhelm interrupts the proceedings and faces off against Theresia in a sword battle, which results in his victory.

*Following his duel with Theresia, Wilhelm is imprisoned in a cell with "Six Tongues" [[Orphe]] at the Prison Tower but is released shortly after thanks to the Sword Saint pleading to King Gionis and receiving his compassion.

*Wilhelm spars with forty combatants handpicked by King Gionis, including Bordeaux, Grimm, Carol, and [[Conwood Melahau]], in order to prove that the Sword Devil replace the role of the Sword Saint. He is victorious and gains his knighthood once again. He also puts in a good word for Orphe and recommends Bordeaux to have the con artist work for him.

*Theresia and Wilhelm get married, which officially allows the former to retire from the [[Royal Army]].

===39-38 BA===
*In the wake of the Demi-Human War, Roswaal founds the Magic Research Institute, and Orphe gains subordinates to monitor various places and gather intelligence for Bordeaux as part of a trial period of sorts.

*Wilhelm makes a report concerning [[Stride Vollachia]] and [[Kurgan]]'s appearances at the Royal Castle’s assembly hall. A short time later, Stride barges into the Astrea Manor to place a curse on Carol and meets Wilhelm once again.

*Stride breaks into the Astrea Manor for a second time to kidnap Theresia, force Carol to murder [[Veltol Astrea]] with her curse, cast a curse on [[Tishua Astrea]] that stripped her of her will, and leave the widow with a message for Wilhelm, informing the Sword Demon that he will be awaiting the conclusion of their story in [[Picoutatte]].

*A subjugation force is assembled and dispatched to Picoutatte to defeat Stride Vollachia, rescue the two hostages he took, and [[Subjugation of the Blight Dragon|save the city]] from his madness.

*Grimm retires from the Zergev Squadron after the successful defeat of Stride to marry Carol. The remaining members of the Zergev Squadron are promoted to become members of the Royal Guard. Wilhelm is appointed as commander of the Royal Guard, and Conwood becomes their vice commander.

*Around this time, the [[Six Tongues]], a defense organization dedicated to protecting Lugunica from the shadows, is created. Its namesake came from Orphe’s nickname.

===17 BA===
*Two years after [[Reinhard van Astrea|Reinhard]]'s birth, when [[Heinkel Astrea]] is 21 years old, his wife [[Louanna Astrea|Louanna]] falls victim to the Sleeping Beauty disease and is confined to a room of the Astrea Manor.

===15 BA===
*Marcos Gildark quits the knights and founds The Brotherhood, which seeks to benefit the people of the slums. Around the same time, [[Russell Fellow]] subtly persuades [[Fareed Impusen]] to found the Golden Wing Faction, a gathering of nobles without a cause.

*[[Roswaal K. Mathers]] dies and a ceremony is held to commence the succession of his son, [[Roswaal L. Mathers]], to be the new head of [[House Mathers]].

*Roswaal has his family crest stolen by [[Belmont]] and is knocked out by Marcos upon attempting to retrieve it. Russell encounters Roswaal and joins his search for his missing crest. Around the same time, Heinkel Astrea attempts to convince Marcos to rejoin the knights, but ultimately fails, leaving with Reinhard, who accompanied him, back to their manor. Roswaal and Marcos fight shortly afterwards. The fight results in Roswaal’s victory, but only because Reinhard utilized the Divine Protection of Mind-Changing to convince Marcos to rejoin the knights. After the battle, Roswaal gets Russell’s help to host a meeting between The Brotherhood and the Golden Wing Party, resulting in both groups deciding to leave the Royal Capital and move to [[Costuul]], while Marcos resigns to rejoin the knights, appointing [[Leno Rex]] as his replacement. That night, Russell sends people to the Astrea Manor upon discovering the source of the interference in Marcos’s fight, threatening the young Reinhard to protect the Kingdom for his family.

===14 BA===
*The [[Royal Abduction Incident]], in which [[Ford Lugunica]]'s daughter Filore was kidnapped from the Royal Castle by “thieves”, occurs. Wilhelm is tasked with recovering Ford’s daughter. On the night of the incident, Heinkel perpetrates a betrayal, as well as a mistake that rendered said betrayal pointless. The repercussions of this caused Heinkel's body to become immeasurably durable.

*An operation to subjugate the [[White Whale]] dubbed the [[Great Conquest]] is organized. Heinkel Astrea declines to join the operation and recommends that his mother, Theresia, participate instead. It ultimately results in the transfer of the Divine Protection of the Sword Saint to Reinhard, Theresia’s death, and a disastrous defeat to the knights.

*With the search for Ford Lugunica’s daughter ending in failure and the presumed death of his wife to the White Whale, Wilhelm resigns from the Royal Guard.

===10 BA===
*On the day of the Tanmuz Festival, Roswaal, [[Ram]], [[Rem]], and [[Frederica Baumann|Frederica]] visit the Royal Capital. However, their trip was interrupted by [[Witch Cult]]ists whose aims were unknown. Reinhard captured the surviving cultists and took them in.

===7 BA===
*[[Felt]] and Rom acquire a tavern formerly inhabited by thugs for themselves and decide to repurpose it into the Loot House.

===6 BA===
*At [[Fourier Lugunica]]'s suggestion, [[Ferris]] begins training under [[Garitch Fabless]] at the Royal Treatment Center.

===4 BA===
*Before Ferris’s training officially ends, Garitch was murdered by a student of his who wanted to become the next Blue. At Garitch’s state funeral, the student, who attempted to utilize curse arts to kill Ferris, was himself killed by Marcos Gildark. When Ferris was offered to succeed Garitch as the next Blue, he denied the offer, leaving the seat unfilled for a few years.

===2 BA to 8-9 months BA===
*At the suggestion of the Royal Treatment Center and Fourier’s insistence, Ferris becomes a member of the Royal Guard.

*One by one, the members of the royal family begin contracting an incurable disease of unknown origin.

*Ferris’s probationary period ended close to the time that Fourier collapsed and was confirmed to be afflicted by the very same disease himself.

*[[Zabinel Lugunica]], the first confirmed royal to have contracted the disease, dies a month after the disease was discovered.

*For several months, the royals continue to die out. When Fourier reaches death’s door, he has one last conversation with Ferris and passes away on Crusch’s lap in the garden where he first laid eyes on her. Fourier’s death is treated as a footnote in comparison to King [[Randohal Lugunica]]'s death.

===8-9 months BA to 0 AA===
*The Council of Wise Men, with [[Miklotov McMahon]] as their representative, assume control of the country as a provisional government after the royal family perishes. They express more concern over the termination of the country’s covenant with Volcanica than the end of the Lugunica family.

*Baron Leip Barielle announces that the [[Dragon History Stone]] foretold of a process to select a new monarch, the Royal Selection. They begin to test nobility to see if any of them can make the Dragon Insignia light up to become a candidate, and Duchess [[Crusch Karsten]] is discovered as the first candidate in this way.

*Sometime later, Leip confirms this his wife, [[Priscilla Barielle]], can make the Dragon Insignia shine, thereby making her the second candidate. 

*After witnessing an argument between Wilhelm and Bordeaux about the White Whale, Ferris and Crusch visit Wilhelm when he is briefly held at the Prison Tower. In due time, he joins their [[Crusch Camp|camp]] once Crusch accepts his request to assist him in subjugating the White Whale. 

*Following a diplomatic trip to the [[Vollachia Empire]] that resulted in a non-aggression pact between both nations, [[Cecilus Segmunt]] illegally crosses the border to engage in a duel with Reinhard and to kill [[Gramdart Holstoy]], the escaped viscount who orchestrated a rebellion while the Lugunican diplomats were in the Empire, although he keeps his second reason private. He is allowed to remain under a few select conditions. He stays at House Juukulius for an extended period of time to wait for Reinhard. A few days pass, and [[Chisha Gold]] arrives in Lugunica to retrieve Gramdart. The viscount attempted to seek asylum in Lugunica by bestowing the flying dragon taming technique to the Six Tongues, but he ultimately failed when Cecilus captured him. Before the two of the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]] brought Gramdart back to Vollachia, Cecilus was able to engage in the duel he sought with Reinhard. Their match ends in a draw.

*[[Anastasia Hoshin]] visits House Juukulius as part of a business trip and discovers that she meets the criteria to become the third candidate. Later, she has a meeting with the Council of Wise Men, who are hesitant to allow her entry into the Royal Selection due to her status as a foreigner. [[Julius Juukulius]] recommends Reinhard to become her knight, but she decides that she will not participate. Julius attempts to convince her otherwise but fails. After visiting the inn she was staying at, he pledges that he will offer to become her knight instead, which Anastasia accepts, having only held out because she wanted Julius as her knight.

*Roswaal confirms that [[Emilia]] can make the Dragon Insignia shine, thereby making her the fourth candidate.

*One day, Emilia and Ram embark on a trip to the Royal Capital.

===0 AA===
*[[Natsuki Subaru]] is summoned to the middle of a plaza within the Royal Capital and discovers his ability, [[Natsuki Subaru#Authorities|Return by Death]].

*Emilia’s insignia is stolen by a thief named Felt. She was hired to steal the insignia by [[Elsa Granhiert]], who herself was hired by Roswaal to carry out this task.

*While searching for the respective candidates they served, Ram and [[Al|Aldebaran]] briefly met one another. The helmeted man proceeded to wish his farewells to Ram and said her name despite her not telling him what it was.

*Subaru visits the Loot House in an attempt to negotiate the insignia back from Felt and Rom. However, Emilia manages to find the building, and Elsa follows in her wake, beginning a confrontation. The fight ends after Felt escapes from the building and brings back Reinhard, who forces the Bowel Hunter to retreat.

*Reinhard inadvertently discovers Felt’s qualifications as a candidate and brings her to the Astrea Manor for the following two months. Subaru is taken to [[Roswaal Manor]] for his treatment.

===2 months AA===
*The Royal Selection Ceremony commences the 3-year period of the Royal Selection.

*After Subaru challenges and brutally loses to Julius at the knights’ garrison’s training grounds, Emilia leaves him at the Karsten Manor for the treatment of his gate.

*Felt recruits [[Gaston]], [[Rachins Hoffman]], and [[Camberley]] to her [[Felt Camp|camp]] a day before leaving the Royal Capital.

*On behalf of Roswaal, Subaru makes an alliance with the Crusch Camp to play a part in slaying the White Whale. Anastasia Hoshin and Russell Fellow also play a part in the negotiations. 

*A subjugation force is assembled and dispatched to [[Flugel's Tree]] to slay the White Whale.

*After successfully slaying the White Whale and the Sin Archbishop of Sloth, [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti]], Subaru returns to the Royal Capital to find that the [[Lye Batenkaitos|Sin Archbishop of Gluttony]] had taken Crusch’s memories and that Rem’s existence was erased to everyone but himself.

*The claim ceremony for slaying the White Whale held in the Royal Castle occurs sometime after the incident at the [[Sanctuary]]. Each of the primary contributors to the White Whale’s fall are in attendance.

===1 year and 4 months AA===
*After an arduous two month-long journey from [[Priestella]], the [[Witch Cult#Sin Archbishops|Sin Archbishop of Wrath]], [[Sirius Romanée-Conti]], is successfully delivered to the Royal Capital by Felt and Reinhard. She is sealed with Evil Sealing Stones at the Prison Tower. As Reinhard took Sirius into the tower, Felt was greeted by Russell Fellow, who briefly engaged in a conversation about how the world was going through a time of change with her and invited her and her knight to dinner at his mansion.

*That evening, Felt and Reinhard have dinner at Russell’s mansion, where they resume their earlier conversation and talk about how the changes are comparable to what was occurring in the world 400 years ago. In addition, they also discussed then-recent signs of civil unrest in the Vollachia Empire, heretic hunts of [[Gusteko]], and actions of the mayors of [[Kararagi]].

===1 year and 5 months AA===
*Following the [[Emilia Camp]]'s decision to covertly enter Vollachia in search of Subaru and Rem, [[Clind]] uses [[Clind#Authority|his Authority]] to instantly teleport Meili Portroute and [[Annerose Miload]] to the garden within the Royal Castle, shortly thereafter being confused for invaders by Marcos and members of the Royal Guard.

*With Clind in tow, Annerose and Meili have a meeting with the Council of Wise Men regarding the Pleiades Watchtower. Felt and Reinhard interrupt the meeting and join in the talks, ultimately resulting in the two of them, [[Flam Remendis|Flam]] and [[Grassis Remendis]], and [[Ezzo Cadner]] accompanying Meili to the Pleiades Watchtower.

*The [[Anastasia Camp]] takes the sealed [[Roy Alphard]] to be imprisoned in the Prison Tower before setting off for [[Kararagi]].

===1 year and 8 months AA===
*The second expedition ends, and Meili is forgiven for her past as an assassin, with credit going to her camp.

*Emilia and [[Otto Suwen]] arrive in the Royal Capital to report to the Council of Wise Men about the death of Priscilla Barielle and the disbandment of her [[Priscilla Camp|camp]]. Felt was present for the report.

*A woman from the Divine Dragon Church, claiming her name to be [[Filore]], met with the Council of Wise Men with the statement that the Divine Dragon Church intended to help regarding the Priestella victims.

*Filore uses her Sacraments to restore Crusch's memories and remove her [[curse]]. This results in Ferris resigning as her knight and later being retrieved by Russell Fellow.

*Filore is determined to have the qualities to join the Royal Selection.

*Upon returning to the capital and entering the Prison Tower, Subaru, [[Beatrice]], and Reinhard discover seemingly discovered the mangled corpse of Roy Alphard.

*After speaking to members of the Emilia Camp, Filore accepts her position as a Royal Selection candidate, and during the conversation with Miklotov that followed, she chose Heinkel as her knight.

*In Miklotov's manor, Crusch intended to speak with him regarding her suspicions of traitors in the country, but due to Miklotov's heavily suspicious behavior and the reaction of Crusch's Divine Protection, she cut down Miklotov and his men, resulting in the following battle with Subaru, Beatrice, and [[Tiga Rauleon]], as well as Crusch's escape with Subaru and Beatrice after Tiga nearly killed them.

*The Royal Selection candidates are called in for questioning, and the Emilia Camp flees to find Subaru, obtaining Wilhelm's assistance when they were faced with the coerced Reinhard.

*Following the escape from the Royal Army and one of the Beloved Children, Subaru's group finds themselves in Russell's manor, where they discuss their enemy.

*During their attempt to escape from the capital, Subaru's group is involved in helping to save people from an accident, being witnessed by both the citizens and the knights in the process. With help from the citizens and the guards, the knights were fended off once everyone was healed, and everyone managed to escape the capital.

*Filore took Heinkel as her knight, and afterward, helped to calm the people of the capital as the Saintess, as well as made numerous pleas to visit the isolated candidates.

===1 year and 10 months AA===
*Filore and Heinkel perpetrate an escape plan for the isolated candidates. Despite Heinkel coming to blows with Marcos, who also intended to help the candidates, everyone managed to flee from the castle.

==Locations==
*'''Castle Layer''': The highest of the layers in the Royal Capital holds the grounds of the Royal Castle and several adjacent locations. Only the royal family, the Council of Wise Men’s members, and the most important nobles are allowed to reside here.
**'''Royal Lugunica Castle''' (ルグニカ王城, ''Rugunika Ōjō''): The Royal Castle is the castle where the monarch of Lugunica reigns from. It is the very center of the Royal Capital, sitting atop its very summit, making it visible from everywhere in the city. It is a large castle made of white stone, filled with a countless number of rooms. The premises and surroundings are protected by hundreds of members of the Royal Guard. Before perishing, the royal family lived in the upper regions of the castle. They were in the possession of a Dragon’s blood, granted to them by Volcanica. Throughout the castle are a multitude of hidden passageways leading underground, although the passageways were forgotten about by the humans residing there until the Demi-Human War.
***'''Throne Room''': [[File:Royal Castle.png|thumb|250px]] An enormous room in the upstairs area of the castle with glittering adornments spread across the walls, illuminated by extravagant lighting hanging atop the ceiling. The furthermost part of the room has the monarch's Dragon-fashioned throne, with a red carpet leading up to it, as well as ten seats found toward the back of the room meant for the Council of Wise Men, with five on either side of the throne. The room is incredibly large, enough so that it can simultaneously hold every member of the Royal Guard and an equally large number of nobles, and there will still be room inside for more. As such, the throne room has been used for special occasions, such as the Royal Selection Ceremony.
***'''Assembly Hall''': A conference room where most of the meetings in the Royal Castle are held.
***'''Ceremony Hall''': A room where ceremonies for achievements are held.
***'''Anteroom''': A small waiting room with several comfortable furnishings.
***'''Chapel''': A large chapel in the basement of the Royal Castle. The large door at its entrance leads into a splendor room with blue-white lights, rows of benches on either side, the crest of the Divine Dragon engraved in the back wall, and an altar in front of the Dragon engraving where prayers are offered.
***'''Courtyard Garden''': An indoor courtyard garden that features an open-air gallery. The garden, adorned with a rich tapestry of flowers and different blossoms for each season, is maintained by court gardeners that exercise all of their knowledge and talent into their work.
***'''Bordeaux Zergev’s Office''': A luxuriously structured room prepared for Bordeaux, a member of the Council of Wise Men. In contrast to the room's appearance, the furnishings within are basic, complimenting Bordeaux’s lack of interest in conveying influence or vanity.
**'''Knights’ Garrison''' (騎士団詰所, ''Kishi-dan Tsumesho''): Adjacent to the Royal Castle is the knights’ garrison, where the knights who serve the Kingdom are stationed.
***'''Training Grounds''': A circular-shaped arena area where knights hone their skills by training. It is normally filled with the sound of clashing swords. There are observation seats in the higher areas of the training grounds where fights can be viewed from. 
***'''Dining Hall''': A dining hall that is usually crowded at lunchtime. The seating in the dining hall is divided by which of the four divisions a normal knight is in, with the lowest ranked red-caped division sitting the closest to the entrance and the highest ranked black-caped division sitting farthest away. According to customs, the Royal Guard, whose members wear white capes, sit further away than the black division.
***'''Commander’s Room''': The innermost chamber of the knights’ garrison, serving as Marcos Gildark’s office.
**'''Prison Tower''' (監獄塔, ''Kangoku-tō''): The location where heinous criminals who await their punishments are imprisoned. The guards there are just as frightening as the prisoners, who receive worse treatment than the residents of the slums.<ref>''Viewed from the castle, the tower appeared to be extremely high up, but the people there were treated worse than those who lived in the slums.'' [[The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint: The Lion's Ferocity Chronicle 2]].</ref> Most notably, the Witch Cult's Sin Archbishop of Wrath, Sirius Romanée-Conti, is currently being held there.
**'''Royal Magic Research Institute''' (王立魔法研究所, ''Ōritsu Mahō Kenkyūjo''): An institute founded by Roswaal J. Mathers in the wake of the Demi-Human War, which caused the importance of [[magic]] to be reevaluated. It is located in a stone tower that was built as a counterpart to the Prison Tower, although the prison was ultimately closed down more than a decade before Roswaal was allowed to work there and use it as a research facility.

*'''Noble District''' (貴族街, ''Kizokumai''): A high-layer district that gives off the impression of being the height of class, containing dazzling, elegant buildings. Chock-full of the homes of nobles with status who are permitted to have homes in the Royal Capital, it contains the main mansions of the lower-ranked nobles and the secondary residences of higher-ranked nobles. In addition, there is a guard station that checks the identities of those who enter the district.
**'''Royal Treatment Center''' (王立治療院, ''Ōritsu Chiryō-in''): A facility where the most talented healers in the Kingdom are gathered or dispatched to other locations whenever necessary. They also tutor those who have a talent with healing magic. It is divided between a research building, where only healers are allowed and an infirmary building, where patients visit healers or corpses are laid in the building's morgue.
**'''Royal Cemetery''' (王立霊園, ''Ōritsu Reien''): A location where those who have been given state funerals, such as a royal or a person of great importance to Lugunica, are buried.
**'''Royal Residence''' (王侯館, ''Ōkō-kan''): A residence akin to a guest house where nobles and other important people in the Kingdom are permitted to stay or reside in.
**'''Rendezvous Street''' (逢引通り, ''Aibiki-dōri''): A clean, tidy street lined with the auxiliary residences of nobles, lived in by caretakers when the owners are not there. It received its name due to the presence of women in jobs and positions who do not want to be seen by others in public. 
**'''Juukulius Manor''' (ユークリウス邸, ''Yūkuriusu-tei''): The residence of the Juukulius family of knights, currently headed by [[Alviero Juukulius]].
**'''Nico Olsen’s Mansion''': The residence of Baron [[Nico Olsen]].
**'''Auxiliary Astrea Manor''': The auxiliary residence of [[House Astrea]], away from its main residence in the Astrea Domain. It was gifted to Theresia van Astrea by Gionis Lugunica in honor of her achievements during the Demi-Human War.
**'''Auxiliary Karsten Manor''': The auxiliary residence of [[House Karsten]], away from its main residence in the Karsten Duchy.
**'''Auxiliary Barielle Manor''': The auxiliary residence of House Barielle, away from its main residence in the Barielle Domain. Though it was originally made and furnished for Leip Barielle, after his death, and was refurnished to Priscilla's liking. The building took severe damage during the events of Aldebaran's scheme.
**'''Miklotov's Manor''': A residence of Miklotov McMahon which sits on the outskirts of the Noble District.<ref>''Then, at the outskirts of the Noble District, finding the designated address and a large mansion with the matching roof color he had been told, he fathomed a guess that this must be Miklotov’s residence.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 12, Section 1.</ref>

*'''Commercial District''' (商業街, ''Shōgyōmai''): The heart of commerce in the Royal Capital. Home to countless stalls that provide a variety of imported goods, it is a major contributor to the city’s activity, as the low-layer district is busy and crowded with customers and merchants that spend their time conversing and negotiating.
**'''Trading Street''' (商い通り, ''Akinai-Dōri''): A street filled to the brim with countless stalls that vend an assortment of goods. The changes in the exchange rates of currency are posted on a sign at the entrance to the street.
***'''Kadomon''' (カドモン, ''Kadomon''): A fruit store ran by [[Kadomon Risch]]. It sells multiple types of colorful produce, including appas.
**'''Russell Fellow’s Mansion''': A mansion in the possession of Russell Fellow. It is the largest building in the Commercial District, having more luxurious qualities than the average mansion in the Noble District.

*'''Commoner District''' (平民街, ''Heiminmai''): The Commoner District is where more than half of the population of the Royal Capital resides. Compared to the Commercial District and the slums, most commoners live here. Along with the slums and the Commercial District, the Commoner District is on the lower layers of the Royal Capital.
**'''Silver Shield''' (銀の盾, ''Shirogane no Tate''): A tavern owned by Conwood Melahau. It is commonly frequented by members of the Kingdom Knights.
**'''Cascus''': (カスクス, ''Kasukusu''): A tavern in the Royal Capital. It is a tavern Heinkel Astrea is known to visit.
**'''Roswaal’s Tavern''': A tavern in the Royal Capital that is currently owned by Roswaal L. Mathers as a property of the Mathers family. Roswaal J. Mathers bought it and lined the walls with her collection of liquor. When she passed away and Roswaal K. Mathers inherited the tavern, it was abandoned, and Clind preserved the building in the following decades.
**'''The Dragon Times’ Headquarters''': The headquarters of the Dragon Times, a newspaper that covers news in the Kingdom of Lugunica.
**'''[[Minor Characters#Azla Eastern|Azla Eastern]]’s Residence''': A small house in a corner of the Commoner District where the lively bustle of the Royal Capital can be heard. It is part of a housing complex where each house has no gaps with one another.
**'''Church''': A church of the Divine Dragon Church located within a corner of the Commoner District.

*'''Slums''' (貧民街, ''Hinminmai''): The slums are areas in the lower district where the destitute who lack proper jobs or homes live. They are scattered in three locations across the lower layers of the Royal Capital, with at least one connected to the Commercial District and another filled with warehouses.<ref>''The place known as the Slums was scattered throughout the large royal capital’s lower district, and there were three of them. Felt lived in a place that was connected to the commercial district, but the area she was in now mainly contained warehouses, and thus wasn’t her turf.'' [[Lone Wolf of the Slums, Felt-chan's Noisy Days]], Section 2.</ref> More often than not, its residents struggle with living by the day and are required to turn to crime for survival. Because the country’s leadership do not wish to get involved with the slums, lawlessness reigns freely there.
**'''Loot House''' (盗品蔵, ''Tōhin Zō''): A shop in the deepest part of the slums where goods that were stolen or found by Felt were appraised and resold by Rom. It was originally a tavern used as a hideout by several thugs until Felt and Rom managed to gain ownership of it, seven years before it was eventually blown away by Reinhard van Astrea during his fight with Elsa Granhiert.
**'''Plaza''': The small plaza with a flower garden where Theresia and Wilhelm met each other during the Demi-Human War. During Arc 1, Felt met Reinhard in this general area.<ref>[https://twitter.com/nezumiironyanko/status/768186205120794624 August 24, 2016 Author's Comment]</ref>

*'''Guard Stations''': There are multiple guard stations across the Royal Capital, the most prominent of which is found on the edge of the Noble District. These stations act as bases for the Royal Capital's guards.<ref name="guards" />

*'''Underground''': The underground area of the Royal Capital. It has multiple passageways leading in and out of it. Some of them connect to the Royal Castle, which has a stream that runs directly below it. Additionally, the underground is currently plagued by an infestation of giant rats. Although not explicitly stated outright, it is implied the sewers beneath the city are divided between districts, and even if one traversed through the sewers, they cannot bypass the checkpoints that control the passage between districts.<ref>''"We are in the sewers, a short distance away from Miklotov McMahon’s residence. Based on our travel distance, this must be about midway between the Noble and Commercial Districts. Even through use of the sewer system, we cannot slip through the checkpoints that control entering and exiting the upper stratum. At present, that is the obstacle that stands in our path."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 14, Section 2.</ref>

*'''Walls''': The Royal Capital has multiple walls within it. There are walls that can be seen in the slums, and there is also a wall that divides the Noble District from the Commoner District.<ref>''At Otto’s call, Garfiel scooped up Petra and Meili from beside him, and tucking one under each arm, he kicked off the wall in front of him―― the sturdy bulwark that separated the Royal Capital’s Noble District from the Commoner District, and vaulted over to the other side.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 16, Section 3.</ref>

*The Royal Lugunica Castle is depicted on the copper coins exchanged within the Kingdom of Lugunica.
*The Silver Shield tavern was said to be within the Commercial District during the events of [[Re:Zero Prequel: Camp Formation Stories]]. However, in [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12|Tanpenshuu Volume 12]]'s [[First Mission Part 2|First Mission]] story, the tavern was within the Commoner District. *Although newspapers do exist, there is no system to circulate them nation-wide. Even in the Royal Capital, important information is often posted on signboards.<ref>''"They have it around the level of newspaper extras, but there’s no system that could circulate a newspaper nation-wide, you see. Even in the capital, important information is posted on signboards."'' August 2, 2014 AskFM Q&A.</ref>
*According to the author, after the White Whale's head was used to confirm its death, it was rendered to bone and stored away in a corner of the Royal Castle.<ref>''"The head was used when their claim was evaluated, and afterwards it was rendered to bone and stored in a corner of the royal castle. After a while, if they make a museum, it might get put on display. The main body was burned, and the great tree became lumber."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref>
