title: House Remendis
wikitext:
'''House Remendis''' (レメンディス家, ''Remendisu-ke'') is a noble house in the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]] that is well known for producing generations of servants and bodyguards for the members of [[House Astrea]]. Its most recently known patriarch is the brother of [[Carol Remendis]].

==Information==
Although it is unknown how ancient of a family this house is, nor how long they have been serving House Astrea, House Remendis is a powerful house that has produced warriors capable of fighting alongside or in the place of House Astrea, with at least one of their heirlooms, [[Grimm Fauzen]]'s greatshield, being made specifically for combat. From a young age, its members are trained in combat, learning the Flow Method as well as a unique style of swordsmanship that is unlike any other. As of yet, Carol Remendis is the only known practitioner of the Remendis-style swordsmanship that allows mid-air combat by kicking off of the sky. Even in the present, House Remendis continues to produce strong warriors. The twins, [[Flam Remendis|Flam]] and [[Grassis Remendis|Grassis]], are each a master of the Flow Method, giving them power contradictory to their small frames, and likewise, they are excellent practitioners of stealth. Even their aunt, [[Raksha Risch|Raksha]], seems to be capable of combat, having been the one to give her [[Kadomon Risch|husband]] his scar.

However, it is unknown what kind of position they have in the royal court. Nobles though they might be, they have yet to partake in the politics of the Kingdom. Likewise, their court rank is also unknown. This being said, their house does seem to be involved somewhat in the [[Royal Selection]]. Despite the major members of House Astrea being split apart into different camps, Carol and her husband Grimm continue to serve House Astrea, particularly [[Reinhard van Astrea]]. Meanwhile, their grandchildren Flam and Grassis not only act as direct servants to Reinhard, but they are also members of the [[Felt Camp]], and they can be seen taking part in the camp’s conflicts. As of yet, the only major points of the house to be shown in the series are the actions of a few solitary members of their family taking part in the [[Demi-Human War]] or in conflicts revolving around the Royal Selection.

At present, House Remendis seems to be somewhat divided. Although there is no confirmation of any internal conflicts within the house, there are a few members of the house that do not seem to be part of the primary household or have seen to bear different surnames. Raksha, for example, and her daughter [[Plum Risch|Plum]], both carry the surnames of Risch and do not seem to be involved with noble affairs. Likewise, compared to her cousins, Plum does not seem to have been trained in the same way, living a relatively normal life. Carol, who married Grimm, also seems to have taken the surname Fauzen, although in their case, Grimm still technically married into House Remendis. Their involvement with the house’s internal affairs is unknown. Meanwhile, while the current whereabouts of Carol and Grimm’s other child is unknown, Flam and Grassis both carry the Remendis name, despite their grandparents each bearing the name Fauzen.

==History==
===48-40 BA===
*A young Carol Remendis, who was recognized as having displayed the greatest skill among her generation of her house, was assigned to be [[Theresia van Astrea]]’s attendant. Miffed about her pacifism despite being the supposed Sword Saint, she challenged Theresia repeatedly and was turned down. After eventually deciding to sneak attack her, she was promptly defeated, and after witnessing her skill, her tears at having caused her harm, and learning of Theresia’s [[Divine Protection]], Carol became devoted to following Theresia for the rest of her life.
*When Theresia was initially assigned to guard [[Roswaal J. Mathers]] during the Demi-Human War, Carol decided to take her place so she wouldn’t have to take part in the war.
*Following the [[Battle of Castour Field]], Carol and Roswaal visited Castour Field, alongside the [[Royal Army#Zergev Squadron|Zergev Squadron]], so that Roswaal could investigate the magic circles. Here, Carol met Grimm for the first time.
*During the investigation, the group learned of the existence of [[Sphinx]], and they were forced to contend with a small army of [[undead]]. However, they were able to stop it thanks to Grimm cutting down the undead [[Tholter Weasily]].
*At an unknown point after this, due to Theresia’s continued feeling of confinement and sadness, Carol suggested leaving her home at time, leading the girl to visit what becomes her flower field in the slums.
*In the following years, Carol accompanied Roswaal and the Zergev Squadron to the frontlines of the war.
*At some point, Carol learned of Theresia and [[Wilhelm van Astrea|Wilhelm Trias]]’s meetings and started to watch over them.
*[[Battle of Aihiya Swamp]]. Assigned to protect Roswaal, they visited the main magic circle employed by Sphinx that had been placed on the field, and they encountered the [[Witch]] herself as well. Despite nearly meeting her demise, Carol was saved by Roswaal, and Sphinx was repelled.
*After meeting with a hospitalized Grimm, the two kissed and became lovers. At some point after this, she retrieved her house’s heirloom greatshield and gifted it to Grimm.
*[[Invasion of the Royal Castle]]. Alongside the newly rebuilt Zergev Squadron and Roswaal, they went to fight off the Demi-Human Alliance’s leaders who invaded the Royal Castle. Fighting alongside Roswaal and Grimm, they were able to corner and nearly kill Sphinx.
*[[Battle of the Trias Domain]]. After Wilhelm left everything behind to go save his home, Carol reported this to Theresia, and alongside the Zergev Squadron, they went to fight to save Wilhelm. This marked Theresia’s first battle in the war and the turning point for the entire war, with Carol conflicted over her newfound will to fight and Wilhelm vanishing for the following two years.
*After accompanying Theresia and the Zergev Squadron, the war finally came to an end after the Second Battle of Castour Field.
*Carol attended the ceremony to commend Theresia’s achievements, and she witnesses Wilhelm’s return and his battle with Theresia.
*After Wilhelm was given his ultimatum to rejoin the [[Royal Army]], he was tasked with battling the entire Zergev Squadron and Carol all at the same time. In the end, Wilhelm won.
*A few months later, Carol attended Wilhelm’s and Theresia’s wedding.
*Carol accompanied the two on their honeymoon, acting as their guardian. During their trip to [[Picoutatte]], she went to search for the one who assaulted [[Veltol Astrea]] and failed, and afterward, she bore witness to the [[Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte]].

===39-38 BA===
*Carol took part in subduing the conflicts created by the campaigns of [[Stride Vollachia]], and at some point, she was cursed by his [[Authority]].
*After the confirmation of Theresia’s pregnancy, Stride initiated an attack on House Astrea, activating his curse on Carol and forcing her to kill Veltol. Afterward, he takes her along with him to Picoutatte.
*[[Subjugation of the Blight Dragon]]. Carol was forced to act as Stride’s bodyguard due to the curse, leading to her fighting against Grimm. Eventually, one of Stride’s other subordinates is tasked with killing Carol, resulting in Roswaal jumping in the way to save her. After the curse on Carol was broken, she held Roswaal in her arms as she died.
*Carol attended Roswaal’s funeral, and despite crying over her death, Roswaal’s son, [[Roswaal K. Mathers|Karl]], the next head of [[House Mathers]], comforted her.
*With the Zergev Squadron being folded into the [[Royal Army#Royal Guard|Royal Guard]], Wilhelm, the new commander, takes [[Conwood Melahau]] as his deputy commander, allowing Grimm to marry Carol and become attendants to House Astrea together.

===12 BA===
*Carol and Grimm’s unnamed child had Flam and Grassis.

===Between 38 BA-0 AA===
*At some point, Carol's younger brother became the head of House Remendis.
*At some point, Grimm and Carol had children.
*At some point, Flam and Grassis, having gone through training, became servants to House Astrea.

===0 AA===
*Carol and Grimm watched over [[Felt]] during her time in Astrea Manor.

===2 Months AA===
*Flam and Grassis accompanied Felt to the Royal Selection Ceremony.

===1 Year, 5 Months AA===
*Shortly after the successful [[Pleiades Watchtower Expedition]], Flam and Grassis accompanied the Felt Camp and [[Meili Portroute]] to the [[Pleiades Watchtower]] to investigate it.
*After Reinhard and [[Ezzo Cadner]] discovered that the birds that appeared there were being used to spy, they destroyed them, and the majority of the camp left the tower, leaving Ezzo and Flam behind.

===1 Year, 8 Months AA===
*Flam and Ezzo greeted members of the [[Emilia Camp]] after they arrived at the tower. After a peaceful day, [[Al|Aldebaran]] attempted to start his [[Pleiades Sealing Conflict|scheme]], but he failed and was sealed. Flam and Ezzo later watched the Emilia Camp off as they stayed behind at the tower.

==Members==
*[[Carol Remendis|Carol Fauzen]]
*Carol’s unnamed younger brother
*[[Flam Remendis]]
*[[Grassis Remendis]]

==Trivia==
*At present, it is unknown whether or not Raksha and her sibling are considered members of House Remendis due to likely having carried the surname Fauzen after their birth. Likewise, if they were, it is unknown if Raksha left the house after marrying and having a child with Kadomon.
*Despite the house being confirmed to have its own crest and the fact that it has been carved on one of their heirlooms, as the crest was left undescribed and lacks an illustration displaying it, it is unknown what the crest is or what it is meant to represent.
**Despite [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 2|Sword Demon Love Song]] stating Grimm's new greatshield bears the House Remendis crest on it, its depiction in the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (manga)|Sword Demon manga]] does not illustrate the crest, instead continuing to display the crest of the Kingdom that was on his previous shield.

[[Hornet]] killed |casual3 = |casual4 = |civilian =}} The '''Ginunhive Armed Rebellion''' (''unofficial name'') is an event in which numerous gladiators led by [[Ubilk]] rose up and rebelled all across the [[Ginunhive|Gladiator Island Ginunhive]]. The event took place approximately 7 years before the arrival of [[Natsuki Subaru]] into the world, and it is the primary conflict of [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], later adapted into [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5|The Tale of the Scarlet Princess]]. With the Imperial Selection Ceremony over and a new emperor crowned, a grand event was held on Ginunhive for the many nobles who wished to visit. However, due to the machinations of one of the island’s slaves, [[Ubilk]], and his supposed intent to slay the new emperor, a revolution was staged in order for the gladiators and other slaves to supposedly vie for their freedoms. Ultimately, thanks to [[Priscilla Barielle|Priscilla Pendleton]] discovering Ubilk's apparent goals and revealing them to the gladiator, as well as [[Al|Aldebaran]] lowering the drawbridge, they were able to free the hostages and end the rebellion. However, Ubilk still escaped, and this event marked the prelude to Priscilla's life in the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]]. ==Background== ===The One-Armed Gladiator=== Approximately 18 years prior to Subaru’s arrival, Aldebaran appeared on Ginunhive. Becoming a gladiator, Al became one of the oldest fighters on the island, always achieving victory despite the odds almost always being against him. During one such battle, six years after his appearance on the island, his feats were witnessed by the Gladiator Empress known as [[Hornet]] when they took on a gladiator [[witchbeast]] together and were the only survivors against it. ===Imperial Selection Ceremony=== Approximately 7 years before Subaru’s arrival into the world, the [[Vollachia Empire]] held the Imperial Selection Ceremony, in which the siblings of the Imperial Family were to fight and kill one another to become the next emperor. In the end, among the siblings who took part in the ceremony, the final two siblings left to compete were [[Vincent Vollachia|Vincent Abellux]] and Prisca Benedict. However, thanks to Vincent and his aide [[Chisha Gold]] essentially threatening Prisca’s life, Prisca’s own attendant, [[Arakiya]] trapped Prisca into draining the poison that Arakiya had imbibed, allowing for the two parties to fake Prisca’s death, resulting in Vincent’s ultimate victory in the Imperial Selection Ceremony. With her death faked, Prisca decided to take on the name Priscilla, after a [[Minor Characters#Priscilla|body double]] who had died in her place some time ago, and she found herself married to [[Jorah Pendleton]]. Vincent, meanwhile, revived the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]] system and named Arakiya, who lost her eye from the poison, Chisha, and [[Cecilus Segmunt]] three of them before going on to promote several others to the position, including [[Olbart Dunkelkenn]] and [[Balleroy Temeglyph]]. ===Coronation Celebration=== For a long time, Ubilk, a male prostitute on the island, had gone around convincing other gladiators to join his cause in obtaining their freedom. One day, after defeating a [[shinobi]] using the Poison Hand technique and speaking to Hornet, Al spoke with Ubilk, who informed him of a major event taking place to celebrate the coronation of a new emperor. Believing this to be a chance to take a hostage to demand their freedom, Ubilk attempted to sway Al into taking part in the rebellion. However, Al ultimately declined the offer. Elsewhere, [[Serena Dracroy]] sent her attendants [[Miles]] and Balleroy to deliver a letter and invite Jorah and his wife Priscilla to Ginunhive. Although Jorah was hesitant due to Priscilla’s identity potentially being exposed, because of her own insistence, they decided to accept the invitation. Sometime later, Serena arrived after receiving a report from her messengers, and they accompanied Priscilla and Jorah to Ginunhive, gifting them a flying dragon carriage to take them to the island. ==Revolution== ===The Offer=== [[File:Re Zero Ex Volume 5 10.png|thumb|right|180x|Hornet appears to confront Al for the first time.]] On the day of the event, Al, as well as other gladiators, fought for the crowd that came to watch, which included Priscilla’s group. After Al won his match and returned to the living quarters, he found Ubilk standing above the corpse of the guard he’d befriended, [[Minor Characters#Auran|Auran]], who Ublik had killed. With Ubilk claiming a revolution was needed and aware that he was a criminal and no match for Al, Ubilk tried once more to convince Al to assist his revolution, which he declined again. Not wanting to kill him, Al decided to sever one of Ubilk’s arms and hand him to the guards, but his attempt was blocked by Hornet, who was convinced to help Ubilk for her chance to fight various people, including Al. Using his [[Authority]] to escape Hornet, he ran for the arena, Ubilk still calling out to him to join him. However, when he reached the arena, he found the gladiators taking arms against the spectators and taking them hostage. Afterward, he was defeated by Hornet, and he was tossed into the lake and left to die. ===Hostages=== After Al’s match, Priscilla and Balleroy accompanied Jorah for fresh air, where they noticed that the drawbridge had been raised without anyone noticing. Deciding to return to Serena, they instead found that the gladiators had taken up arms and began taking the audience hostage, demanding for Serena to show herself in exchange for the other people’s lives. Interested, despite Jorah and Balleroy intending to protect her, Priscilla decided to proclaim herself Serena. Despite the skepticism of her due to her age, she managed to convince the man who spoke to her, [[Ghajit]], of her identity and went along with him, bringing Jorah along as well when he spoke up. Soon, Al appeared in the arena, where he was defeated by Hornet. As for Balleroy, Miles knocked him out to prevent him from acting on his own and ruining whatever Priscilla had planned. After Priscilla was taken away, Miles and Balleroy met back up with Serena and began planning their next move. ===The Mastermind=== They took Priscilla and Jorah to the office of the island chief, whose corpse stained the floor. Afterward, they met with Ubilk, who claimed his goal was to free the slaves on the island and give the island independence. However, Priscilla noted that Ubilk realized that such a rebellion would not work and that the emperor would send the Nine Divine Generals to the island instead. Though the gladiators were frustrated, Ubilk quickly calmed them. Talking with Jorah, Priscilla came to the conclusion that Ubilk was too smart not to realize what they had and that he had a different goal in mind. After some time, Ghajit questioned the truth of her claim of the Nine Divine Generals coming, to which she agreed and told the men of the options that they carried. Afterward, she joined Ubilk on the balcony of the building at his invitation, where he pointed out the encampment of soldiers beyond the raised drawbridge, discussed his men, revealed himself as a member of the Evil Eye Tribe, and realized her identity was not Serena. Soon enough, deciding the best course of action was to keep her somewhere separate from Jorah, he had her escorted away, mentioning the trump card of his forces in passing. ===Mutiny=== After some more time, Priscilla waited for her reinforcements to arrive, to which Ghajit, accompanied by Balleroy, appeared and killed the gladiators guarding her. Deciding to make her own move, they escorted and cleared paths for Priscilla after she left the room, explaining Ubilk’s most likely goal being the emperor’s head and his likely strategy of bypassing the Nine Divine Generals to reach him. This angered Ghajit, who realized he would have become an accomplice to an attempt on the emperor’s life and essentially receiving a death sentence, and he decided to attack Priscilla for it, only to be defeated swiftly by the newly arrived Miles. Afterward, deciding to quell the rebellion, Priscilla moved to inform the gladiators of their situation via a broadcasting device, inciting the rebellious gladiators to prevent their own executions by turning on Ubilk. Following the announcement she made, the gladiators split into two groups and began arguing and fighting against each other. Deciding to retrieve Jorah, Balleroy and Miles cleared any enemies in their path on the way to the room he was being held in. After arriving, she tossed a vase hard enough to move Jorah out of the way, allowing for Balleroy to attack the rebellious gladiators and slay most of them with ease. While the last gladiator attempted to take Jorah hostage, Miles called for his [[Dragon#Flying Dragons|flying dragon]] [[Minor Characters#Gaius|Gaius]], who burst through the ceiling and killed him. Realizing that Ubilk was nowhere to be seen, Priscilla speculated that he had escaped the island via some unknown teleportation device. ===Suppression=== Learning of the incident on the island, the emperor sent a force of approximately 2000 soldiers sent to exterminate the gladiators. After arriving at the island, Olbart and Arakiya, their commanders, discussed how to get onto the island with the drawbridge raised. Deciding to bypass the aquatic witchbeasts in the water, Arakiya devoured a lesser water [[spirit]], stripped down, and turned her body into water to cross the lake, intent on lowering the drawbridge. Along the way, however, she discovered Al, bloody and defeated, lying on was little more than an island-like patch of rocks. Deciding to get information from him to better understand the situation, Arakiya decided to give Al first aid, even if it was rather crude and inexperienced. Deciding to assist each other, Arakiya used her abilities to take Al to the island with her. After returning to the island’s waste disposal site and giving Arakiya something to cover herself with, they confirmed where they needed to go to lower the drawbridge, and they discussed how they should handle Hornet. Because of Al’s insistence on Hornet’s strength being too much for the two to handle, Arakiya devoured a lesser wind spirit to become invisible, figuring it would be best to avoid fighting her. Before leaving, at Al’s suggestion, Arakiya crushed the body of a shinobi that he killed, allowing the poison within it to carry in the wind. Then, deciding to make their way through the island, they passed through several gladiators which Al promptly silenced, picking up a dagger along the way. Eventually, they made it to the control tower, where Hornet was waiting. Believing there was nothing he could do about her, he told Arakiya as much, to which she thanked him for his assistance, baffling him. Attempting to bypass her, Arakiya moved forward, only for Hornet to notice her and attack her. Realizing that she was quickly becoming cornered, Al began to question whether he would simply abandon her. As she managed to strike down Arakiya, making her visible, Al, disgusted by seeing her silver hair stained in her blood, decided to step forward and prevent Arakiya’s death. After a short conversation, their battle began, and Al was quickly forced to use his Authority repetitively. [[File:Re Zero Ex Volume 5 11.png|thumb|left|180x|Priscilla speaks to the gladiators.]] Amazed by Al’s surprising handling of Hornet, Arakiya attempted to put strength into her limbs, using the powers of a water spirit to speed up her self-healing, though Hornet kept an eye on her as well. As the fight progressed, the voice of Priscilla could be heard across the island, informing everyone of the situation they were in and inciting them to rebel against Ubilk. With a lull in the battle, Al questioned Hornet’s motives and came to the conclusion that she wanted to challenge the Nine Divine Generals, to which she did not deny and even claimed to want to fight everyone else on the island, regardless of their status. Picking herself up, Arakiya decided to assist Al in the fight, having healed herself into considerably better shape than before. Avoiding a combo attack from Hornet, Al used earth magic to catch her off guard while Arakiya attempted to charge her while clad in flames. Dodging, Hornet spun with her large weapons embedded in the ground, tearing it up and destroying her opponents’ footing. Arakiya avoided falling by kicking off of the wall, grabbing Al, and stabilizing themselves at the deepest depths of the island. Confronting Hornet who was in front of them, Al began talking about his experiences in the battle thus far and that she managed to kill him 792 times that day. Excited, Hornet tried to lunge, only to fall, succumbing to poison from the dead shinobi’s Poison Hand. After explaining that to her, she felt genuine fear of him and asked him to finish her, though he declined to do so in the event that she had another trick up her sleeve. Before long, she finally died. Afterward, Al and Arakiya lowered the drawbridge, allowing Olbart and the rest of the Vollachian forces to enter the island and clean up the situation. ==Aftermath== In the direct aftermath of the rebellion, Al met Olbart with Arakiya, where Olbart mentioned a possible reward for Al, though he decided not to take him up on it, instead deciding to remain on Ginunhive. Sometime later, he faced off against Ghajit, slaying him. At an unknown point after this, having been inspired by saving Arakiya and the words spoken by Priscilla to the gladiators, Al gained the courage to leave the island. After being given his signature helm by one of the jailers, he used his Authority to swim through the witchbeast-infested lake, and, becoming the first person to escape the island, he set about chasing the trail of the [[Witch]]es. Numerous uprisings appeared around Vollachia after the rebellion, and each one was quelled by the Nine Divine Generals, thus providing Ginunhive with new gladiators. However, Ubilk had seemingly vanished, apparently never intending to target Vincent’s head. However, at some point, he became a [[Stargazer]], and he eventually strolled into the Crystal Palace, where he proved himself valuable to the emperor and was given an official position. This would eventually lead to his speaking with Vincent about the coming [[Great Disaster]]. Priscilla’s group ultimately left the island, and having met with Serena, it was pointed out that Serena owed Priscilla a favor. After Priscilla returned to the Pendleton Estate with Jorah, [[Goz Ralfon]] was sent to eliminate her and Jorah, who were framed to have been conspiring against the Empire. With Jorah giving his life to protect Priscilla, she ultimately escaped, and with the assistance of Serena and her men, they were able to smuggle her into the Kingdom of Lugunica, where she would go on to have seven more marriages and eventually become one of the [[Royal Selection]] candidates. ==Navigation== {{Battles & Events Navbox}} [[Category:Vollachia Empire]] [[Category:Ginunhive]]

title: Shinobi
wikitext:
'''Shinobi''' (シノビ, ''Shinobi'') are a secretive group of people hidden from public view who hail from villages in the [[Kararagi|Kararagi City-States]] and the [[Vollachia Empire]]. They are employed or tasked by influential figures to carry out deeds such as infiltration and assassination.

==Information==
Originating from Kararagi, the shinobi are a people of the shadows who specialize in carrying out dirty work away from public view in secrecy.<ref name="native">''“I’m not sure if it proves that theory, but there's something that can be discerned from the shinobi who committed suicide. As I said, the shinobi are originally native to Kararagi; they’re a people of the shadows, so to speak. Whether it’s tasks that can't be revealed to the public or matters that need to be covertly taken care of, they’re professionals who specialize in dirty work.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref> They handle tasks such as assassinations and infiltration,<ref>''“These shinobi… Do they use ninjutsu, or do they go undercover in the darkness of night to spy on or assassinate people?”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 1, Section 1.</ref><ref>''“I know not what ninjutsu means, but that is indeed the main function of the shinobi. …How do you know that?”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 1, Section 1.</ref> as well as torture,<ref>''Stargazers―― they were those who devoted themselves to the fulfillment of the commandment that they received from the stars; Ubilk, who frequently visited the Crystal Palace, was one of them. Aside from him, there were some other Stargazers here and there, and in order to question them about the authenticity of Ubilk’s words, many were imprisoned and put through the hardship of torture by the hands of the shinobi.'' [[The Land of Wolves / Death unto the Weak, No Mercy ZERO Nine Divine Generals]], Section 3.</ref> among other similar work. They can also be hired by influential people as troops dispatched to carry out their duties, whether they involve assassination or other tasks.<ref name="hired">''They were hired by the great and powerful as elite soldiers in the game of kill-or-be-killed that such people lived in, but since this one had ended up here, he could not be much more than a prisoner now.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 1.</ref> Even at the cost of death, a shinobi will exhaust every effort to succeed in a task they are assigned.<ref>''So long as they did not experience an instant death, it was in a shinobi’s nature to get the job done, even if it meant letting their head fly.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 6, Section 3.</ref> Because the existence of the shinobi is generally kept a secret, they are expected to operate in the shadows of history, almost never leaving a major mark on the world.<ref>''As the chieftain of the shinobi, who were expected to operate in the shadows of history, his ambition was to leave his grand mark on the history of the Empire and to destroy the very concept of shinobi.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 3.</ref><ref>''Was it truly possible for one such as himself, a shinobi, chased into hiding amidst the shadows of history and the world, behind the curtain of the story, condemned to a fate of rotting in the darkness, to be risen up to center stage in such a manner?'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref>

The village where trainees are taken to undergo a brutal training process to be made into shinobi and the place of residence for most of the shinobi is known as a '''shinobi village''' (シノビの里, ''shinobi no sato''). The original village was founded in Kararagi, and a second village was eventually established in Vollachia, whereas there are no villages in [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Lugunica]] or [[Gusteko]].<ref name="2025talkshow">April 6, 2025 Talk Show</ref> After advancing beyond the position of a trainee, shinobi are divided between three ranks. The lowest rank is '''genin''' (下忍, ''genin''), the middle rank is '''chunin''' (中忍, ''chunin''), and the highest rank is '''jonin''' (上忍, ''jonin''). It is not simple for anyone to become a shinobi; the process of advancing to a subsequent rank is so ruthless and difficult that it has created a warranted yet exaggerated expression that only one of a thousand trainees will become genin, only one of a thousand genin will become chunin, and only one of a thousand chunin will become jonin.<ref>''To begin with, the path walked by the shinobi was a steep one; not just anyone could become one. Only one of a thousand trainees would become a genin, only one out of a thousand genin would become a chunin, and only one out of a thousand chunin would finally become a jonin―― such sentiments were commonly repeated due to how high the hurdles were. To this day, whenever Yae heard that example, she would think about how it would require a billion shinobi candidates. In any case, the selection was ruthless enough to warrant that expression, no doubt.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> When a shinobi deserts their village without intending to return ever again, they are referred to as '''runaway shinobi''' (抜けシノビ, ''nuke shinobi''). One such case of runaway shinobi was observed with the Twin Shura, [[Shasuke]] and [[Raizo]], who fled the village in Vollachia and became runaway shinobi after they were deemed incomplete shinobi.<ref>''As a consequence, the Twin Shura, once called the village's masterpiece, slayed all the adults who took everything from them, along with their brethren, and thus became runaway ninja.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref>

The shinobi push their minds and bodies to extreme levels, with only a few being able to reach the state of becoming one.<ref>''“Old age is not enough for your ambition to dry up. ――The shinobi push their bodies and minds to the extreme, and merely a scant few can reach such a state. Even if the day of your death arrives, you shall never be complete.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 2, Section 1.</ref> To eliminate an opponent, they utilize their entire being as a weapon. Proficient in swiftness and agility,<ref>''“Agility and swiftness are the specialties of a shinobi. Fulfill your duty without indecision.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 34]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> shinobi fight by setting up trap after trap for an opponent,<ref>''Meanwhile, the true skill of a shinobi lay in setting trap upon trap, like the web of a spider, ten layers, then twenty, until――, “Four moves.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 2, Section 5.</ref> and become between five to ten times more dangerous foes if they manage to escape someone's sight.<ref>''The moment they slipped out of sight, a shinobi would become five or even ten times as troublesome than they would have been while visible.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 2, Section 6.</ref> By taking an opponent's attention and obfuscating their mind, they can immobilize them and promptly finish them off.<ref>''The ultimate technique of a shinobi was to steal their opponent’s attention, cloud their mind, immobilize them, and take their life. Yae was an excellent student in the art of clouding the mind, but she knew that she was no match for the village chief’s years of experience.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 2, Section 7.</ref> In situations where a shinobi is weaker than their opponent, they may still manage to successfully kill an opponent by depriving them of the ability to fight at their best.<ref>''“That’s the thing, even I’ve ended up on the verge of death many times quarrellin’ wit’ those above myself, ya see? But, I’m the one who’s still kickin’ when all’s said ‘n done, so it means we gotta get sneaky ‘n bridge the gap between us ‘n those monsters bit by bit ta succeed in life. If ya can rob yer opponent of their ability ta perform flawlessly, the opportunity ta chop off the heads of those above ya will come around. ――And it goes both ways, y’see? Kakakakka!”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> Furthermore, shinobi utilize a variety of techniques known aptly as '''shinobi techniques''' (シノビの術技, ''shinobi no jutsugi''). Used for the ultimate goal of taking an opponent's life, they tend to focus on exploiting their openings.<ref>''――Most shinobi techniques specialized in exploiting an opponent’s openings. That was why, unlike the fighting techniques of warriors utilized in battle, the techniques of the shinobi utilized for killing were called jutsu. Yae’s Steel Thread Technique was a prime example of that distinction.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 2, Section 5.</ref> The strength of these techniques resides in their applicability and their diversity. For a shinobi who excels at being adaptable, there is an untold number of strategies they can implement with their countless techniques.<ref>''Only for the shinobi, utility players who could adapt to any situation, was the number of possibilities for plans which could utilize their techniques and abilities a value that rivaled the number of stars in the night sky. For example, the poison coating the short sword Al had been using to dispose of the assassins behind closed doors, was something that had been concocted by Yae.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12]], [[Guardians of the Crimson Flame]], Section 2.</ref>

The total number of shinobi techniques that exist in the world is innumerable. Only a handful of them have been shown, with known ones including a technique allowing its user to cross through shadows,<ref>''The shadow had flickered, just as it had done when Stride had escaped. Crossing through shadows was a shinobi technique. It had blended in with the chaos of the battle and carried Roswaal away.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 5, Section 4.</ref> a technique that hardens the body to the point that it reaches the caliber of steel,<ref>''Facing her head-on, Shasuke channeled a shinobi technique throughout his whole body, hardening his body to the caliber of steel.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref> a technique that completely eliminates one's presence and allows its user to evade the effects of a distance-based [[curse]],<ref>''The invisibility that eliminated the shinobi’s presence, rather than serving as a precaution against the castle’s guards, was a countermeasure to elude being counted as a target of the Curse of Thorns, which had been dispersed across a wide area in the Imperial Capital.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 1.</ref> unspecified interrogation techniques,<ref>''That would be, the interrogation techniques passed down in his shinobi village―― With Olbart’s reflection on his dark eyes, Subaru felt a surge of fear, suspecting that the method the menacing old man had suggested could lead to torture.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 2, Section 4.</ref> a survival technique that transmits what its user wills to their muscles and internal organs,<ref>''Receiving a direct kick from the horned girl named Rem, Yae maneuvered her creaking body to disperse the impact through her arms and legs, a shinobi survival technique that transmitted one’s will down even to their muscles and internal organs.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> and a technique that makes it difficult for others to tell when an object has been thrown.<ref>''The next instant, an endless deluge of shuriken rained upon Yorna in the air from all directions. The shinobi technique made it impossible to discern when he had thrown them. The rotating blades drew a different trajectory each as they closed in on Yorna, threatening to brutally lacerate her maidenly skin in their wake.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29]], Chapter 6, Section 1.</ref> Two notable techniques include Infantilization, which interferes with the Ods of others, causing their bodies to shrink, and the Steel Thread Technique, a killing technique that utilizes thin steel wires to bind or kill people, though the wires can be used for other purposes as well. It is unknown if some techniques employed by shinobi are classified as shinobi techniques, like a combat technique that [[Roswaal L. Mathers]] was taught by a shinobi from the west, which unleashes shockwaves from a palm strike that bypasses an opponent's defenses while injuring them. Some shinobi may opt to utilize [[Magic|magic]] or curse arts as part of their shinobi techniques, such as an unnamed shinobi eaten by [[Lye Batenkaitos]], who made use of a magic technique that installed invisible blades of wind in a fixed space of their choosing,<ref>''The art of installing blades of invisibility in space was a legendary shinobi technique, but it did not matter whose Memories they were from since he had already thrown them away.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 25]], Chapter 7, Section 8.</ref> whereas another shinobi, [[Hamayal Wesmi]], was a Phantom Wolf user. In addition to their varied techniques, when engaging in battle, shinobi often employ kunai, throwing knives that originate from Kararagi,<ref>''“Correct. This is a kunai, a weapon that can be used for throwing. It’s one of the famed shinobi’s preferred tools in Kararagi to our west.”'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 1, Section 4.</ref><ref>''A black knife―― the same kunai that was sticking up in the man’s forehead, was held firmly in her hand. Kunai were daggers that were unique to the west, and she had many more weapons that were hidden under her red maid uniform.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 4]], [[Pride and Prejudice and Zombies Part 1|Pride and Prejudice and Zombies]], Section 4.</ref> as well as other weapons such as shuriken and bombs.

===Kararagi Shinobi===
Kararagi is the country that shinobi and the original shinobi village are native to.<ref name="native" /> It is unknown how they came to be, and why their name and culture bears similarities to the concept of shinobi from Japan. Similarly to Vollachia's shinobi village, it is said that the training of Kararagi's shinobi village is inhumane,<ref name="2025talkshow" /> but the extent to which the practices and cultures of Kararagi's village and Vollachia's village resemble each other is unclear. Likewise, the identity of the shinobi chieftain in Kararagi, if one exists, is unknown. The mightiest individual in the country, [[Halibel]], is considered the strongest shinobi of the City-States as well as the strongest shinobi in the world.

===Vollachia Shinobi===
At some point in time, shinobi from Kararagi who either escaped the shinobi village there or were sent to the Empire on assassination missions founded a shinobi village in Vollachia.<ref name="2025talkshow" /><ref group=Note>The talk show summaries provided by official sources are confirmed by eventgoers to sometimes forego or paraphrase details revealed by the author. As opposed to previous years in the 2020s, there is an inability to verify the author's exact wording for statements from the 2025 talk show. Although there are conflicting accounts of this statement, since there are no means to verify what the author truly said, the details taken from the talk show's summary, the closest official source, have been included here.</ref> Shinobi have been present in the country for at least 300 years, dating back to their employment and use by House Goldario, led by [[Whitaker Goldario]]. Under the command of Whitaker's sister, [[Terriola Goldario|Terriola]], they provided information that led to the elimination of a number of [[Eugard Vollachia|Eugard Elcanti]]'s opponents during the Imperial Selection Ceremony. Following the circumstances of Whitaker's death and the downfall of the Goldario family's influence, the shinobi employed by the family were inherited by Terriola, and they began to serve the Vollachia Empire's interests.

The current chieftain of the shinobi in Vollachia is [[Olbart Dunkelkenn]]. While he served as a member of the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]], Olbart leveraged his position as the leader of the shinobi to use them as an emergency force for the [[Imperial Army]] if they are needed in times of crises. Furthermore, the army's former military advisor, [[Chisha Gold]], was able to task shinobi with duties that he assigned to them and had a method to stay in touch with them while they were away in order to pass on new orders. Since then, however, Olbart has retired from the army.

In Vollachia's village, shinobi are assassins created through a rigorous training regimen and unimaginable, tortuous modifications to the body.<ref>''That Poison Hand, and an unflinching readiness to kill, were enough to guess at the opponent’s background. Shinobi were assassins who had undergone the most rigorous possible training and submitted to unimaginable augmentation of their bodies. Some people doubted they really existed, but they were an urban legend worth believing in.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 5]], [[The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame Part 1|The Sword Wolf of the Scintillating Flame]], Section 1.</ref><ref>''――The shinobi were shura that were birthed as a result of “modifications” akin to the tortures of hell.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref> To begin with, shinobi begin their training process by indoctrinating young children, most of whom are abducted from outside of the shinobi village once they reach a suitable age in order to efficiently fill the places of the large number of candidates who die during training.<ref>''First of all, shinobi indoctrination began around the age of consciousness acquisition, targeting mostly children who had been abducted from other places. Since many candidates ended up dying in cold blood due to the inhumane and unreasonable drills, it proved more efficient to abduct toddlers of a suitable age from the outside.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> Once the children arrive at the shinobi village, their original names, families, and lives are deprived from them in order to prepare them as a shinobi candidate.<ref>''In the beginning, their names were taken away. Then their family, their possessions, their past, their future, and everything they had before becoming a shinobi; only after having their life bleached like this, were they recognized as a shinobi prototype.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref> They are subjected to a process of memory erasure using drugs, signals, and techniques to interfere with their memories in order to make them forget about their families and hometowns, and then given a substitute name, such as “Red Number 8”, a name given to a trainee because of their hair color.<ref>''Of course, the abducted children were subjected to drugs or signals, techniques that interfered with memory, to make them forget about their families and hometowns completely. Yae did not remember her parents’ faces either, nor did she even know her own real name. “Yae”, it was a name that she had only received later on, and until then she had simply been called “Red Number 8” in accordance with her hair color.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> The memory disposal process can vary depending on a trainee's aptitude for it; those who lack an aptitude will fail to have their memories disposed, those whom it functions too efficiently on become husks, and others experience differing levels of challenge when facing the process, with some seemingly losing their memories normally while others have their memories disposed with ease.<ref name="namingparent">''Those without aptitude would fail first at this memory disposal. For some, the memory erasure would not function effectively enough, and conversely, for others, it would function too effectively, leaving them as useless husks; as for Yae, she forgot everything with cold-hearted ease. It had been so unchallenging that even the one in charge of her memory disposal, Fujirou Tenzen, had been left speechless. ――Incidentally, this Fujirou would later go on to be Yae’s naming parent, and was the previous Tenzen whose family name she inherited.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref>

After the memory disposal process is completed and a trainee is readied as a canvas to be painted over by the shinobi, they commence the village's training, which aims to achieve the restructuring of the body.<ref>''Regardless, forcibly robbed of their heart’s foundations, they would become a white canvas to be painted at the mercy of the black brush known as the shinobi―― once the children stripped of their past were prepared, the true essence of the inhuman training facility that was the shinobi village would begin: not merely strengthening of the flesh and muscles, but the very restructuring of the human body.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> Trainees have their bones destroyed and reconstructed to pick up mastery over a soft body and superhuman acrobatics, gradually go from intaking small doses to fatal doses of poison to build a resistance to it, and experience a daily routine of learning of how martial arts and shinobi tools perform by feeling the pain they deliver to the body, all while fulfilling a quota of experiencing broken bones, torn flesh, and blood loss during the process.<ref>''Destruction and correction of the bones in order to achieve mastery over a soft body and acrobatics surpassing human understanding; training to build up a resistance to poison by gradually advancing from small doses to lethal ones; daily routines comprised of learning the dangers of martial arts and shinobi tools by the pain they inflicted upon the body; and being tasked with meeting a quota of broken bones, torn-up flesh, and shed blood.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> It is prohibited to bury the bodies of trainees who died so that their corpses could aid them in becoming acclimatized to death, and the smell of the rotting corpses is carved into the minds of the remaining trainees, which would make some of them lose their grasp on sanity.<ref>''Were people to die, it would be forbidden to bury them, so that their corpses could serve as material in their training to grow accustomed to death, and instead the putrid odor of those bodies rotting day after day on their beds was drilled into their minds, causing some to lose their sanity.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> They are forced to be on the receiving end of training, drugs, curse marks, and all sorts of heresies from across the world; there is an expression that one in a hundred of trainees refrain from suicide, one of those hundred would manage to prevent their mind from being broken, one of a hundred from those survived the training regimen, and one from the remaining hundred would become a complete shinobi.<ref>''Once readied, these nameless beings would not be granted mercy of any kind. Be it training, be it drugs, be it curse marks, they were subjected to subjected to all kinds of heresy from every land and every time―― One in a hundred of them would resist suicide, one in a hundred from those would keep their mind unbroken, and from those hundred, one would survive the regimen. Finally, one from those hundred would become a complete shinobi.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref> Once a trainee qualifies to become a genin, they are granted a given name by a naming parent, whose family name they inherit.<ref name="namingparent" /> Despite being naming parent and child, a relationship between them is closer to that of an instructor and their student, and a child could regard their naming parent as someone in the village whom they contact frequently.<ref>''But even if they could be called naming parent and child, their relationship was emotionless, closer to that between an instructor and his pupil. From Yae’s perspective, her impression of Fujirou more or less amounted to someone in the village with whom she had a high frequency of contact.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref>

Shinobi are subject to a number of other forms of training. They are taught to suppress their emotions to develop a mentality to reveal anything to anyone else regardless of any torture they may face.<ref>''Shasuke, who had been instructed from childhood to lose his heart and throw away his emotions, the same Shasuke who had turned into a runaway ninja after failing to become a shinobi along with his brother Raizo, laughed for the first time in ages.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref><ref>''Even if she was of an unserious disposition, Yae had received the shinobi training of suppressing emotions, having acquired a spirit that would never reveal anything, no matter the level of torture; thus, her statement was bloodcurdling, and by no means could it be taken as a falsehood.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12]], [[Guardians of the Crimson Flame]], Section 2.</ref> Unless it concerns false information that is manufactured with the intent of deceiving and manipulating their opponents, shinobi usually do not reveal any details to someone else,<ref>''Shinobi would never relinquish information to their opponents. If they did, it would have been fabricated information for the purpose of manipulation.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 1, Section 2.</ref> and in the event that they fail, it is engraved into their soul to commit suicide to prevent leaks of information from Vollachia.<ref>''――She was an unparalleled genius of a ninja produced by the Vollachia Empire’s shinobi village, granted a mission of utmost importance, an existence promised to carry it through to fruition. In the one in ten thousand possibility that she were to fail, it was engraved into her soul to commit suicide without leaking any bit of the Empire’s information whatsoever.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12]], [[Guardians of the Crimson Flame]], Section 2.</ref> Their minds are trained to stay unfazed by most circumstances that come their way, and although there can be exceptions in particularly daunting situations,<ref>''Her mind had been trained to remain unshaken by most situations, but even when considering circumstances in which the unexpected and unforeseen might occur in rapid succession, a scenario such as this would be considered an anomaly, demanding to be deemed as an exception.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 2, Section 5.</ref> it is considered unbecoming for a shinobi to lose their composure.<ref>''To lose one’s composure, was of a shinobi.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 9.</ref> By learning how to alter the blood  flow around their eyeballs, shinobi can acquire a form of night vision.<ref>''This was the result of training to become accustomed to the darkness of night, a type of physical manipulation that altered her blood flow around the eyeballs to adjust vision.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 41]], Chapter 2, Section 7.</ref> They are also made to embark on a constant run from the [[Lupugana|Imperial Capital]] to their shinobi village with a lone bamboo cylinder of water in their possession, without sleeping or resting for more than half a month.<ref>''“Shinobi training is crazy, y’know. They make us run nonstop from the Imperial Capital back to the village with no sleep or rest for over half a month, with just a single bamboo cylinder of water.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 40]], Chapter 2, Section 4.</ref> While shinobi undergo training to resist the effects of poisons, they are vulnerable to Jiranme, an especially lethal poison.<ref>''“A super lethal poison which can kill even the shinobi who are trained to resist poison, Yae-chan’s special Jiranme mixture.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12]], [[Guardians of the Crimson Flame]], Section 2.</ref> As a possible result of their training, a shinobi may develop a strong mental fortitude.<ref>''Perhaps being the result of her shinobi training, her well-honed mental strength was admirable.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 40]], Chapter 3, Section 2.</ref> In addition, the modifications made to a shinobi's body allows them to shift the positioning of their organs.<ref>''But, she had avoided damage to her vital organs by shifting them aside. Through the inhumane shinobi modifications to her flesh, Yae could shift the positioning of her internal organs.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 9.</ref>

In Vollachia's shinobi village, there is an ironclad law that a shinobi must never yield their heart to anything.<ref>''――A shinobi must never give their heart to anything. In the shinobi village of the Vollachia Empire, that was an absolute teaching imparted upon those forbidden to lead any way of life other than that of a shinobi; it was an ironclad rule that demanded absolute obedience even more so than the Law of Iron and Blood rooted in the vast lands of the Empire.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 1.</ref> Those who assume the role of shinobi strictly follow this tenet and engrave it into their souls, since if they were to disobey the ironclad law, it is believed that they would be weakened.<ref>''If they were to yield their heart to something, the honed blade known as shinobi would easily come to rust. Therefore, any and all who took on the mantle of shinobi, without exception, etched that ironclad rule into their soul, abiding by it no matter the cost.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 1.</ref> Because he adheres to this law as a core philosophy, Olbart's thoughts are not influenced by anyone, and he has presided as Vollachia's strongest shinobi as someone who does not hold anything or anyone dear.<ref>''――Without a doubt, Olbart’s thoughts were dictated by no one. For that reason, this man, Olbart Dunkelkenn, reigned as the strongest shinobi. He was a shinobi who had been completed with him not holding anything as precious, or having anyone to whom he devoted his heart.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 30]], Chapter 2, Section 1.</ref> Having said that, Olbart once told Yae, who he saw as as a remarkable person who would outlive most ordinary shinobi like he has, that there may be a time when she has to break the shinobi's ironclad rule.<ref>''“Ya don’t wanna? Listen, I’ve been there myself. Remarkable folk like the two of us end up livin’ longer than most ordinary shinobi without even realizin’ it, ‘n we end up seein’ tons’a things. So occasionally, there’ll be times. Times when you’ll hafta end up breakin’ the ironclad law of the shinobi.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 10.</ref> Therefore, he proposed to her that it would be fine for her to break the ironclad rule and hold at least one thing in her heart.<ref>''“Hey, yer like that, ain’t’cha? Same as me, ya can do just about anythin’ without so much as a second thought, ‘n so life kinda loses its spark, don’t it? Wouldn’t it be fine ta keep at least a single somethin’ in yer heart, then?”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 1.</ref>

While in the past, the shinobi were commonly driven to specialize in a single technique, in Olbart's view, doing so was only feasible for a privileged few people powerful enough to fight anyone with a lone skill, whereas ordinary people had to adapt or face death; as such, the doctrine of single-skill specialization once he became chieftain.<ref>''Prior to Olbart becoming the chieftain, the shinobi were generally encouraged to specialize in a singular technique. However, the idealized conception of single-skill specialization was only for the privileged few like Cecilus and Arakiya, who possessed a single technique that could be effective against anyone, while those with ordinary abilities must be adaptable or they would simply die. Thus, when Olbart became the chieftain, he immediately abandoned the doctrine of single-technique specialization.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7.</ref> In contrast to the village's old ideology, Olbart's basis for his fighting style as a shinobi is his belief that the essence of a battle was for one to impose their own strengths onto the weaknesses of their opponent. Therefore, to adjust to an opponent and fight them while accounting for their unique weaknesses, he shied away from focusing on using specialized skills.<ref>''A battle, in essence, was about imposing one’s strengths upon the weaknesses of the other. This was the basis of Olbart’s fighting style as a shinobi. To strike according to the weaknesses of all sorts of opponents, Olbart had avoided honing any specialized skills.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7.</ref> Although this style of aiming to counter an opponent's strengths, accompanied by techniques to aid in accomplishing this, was what Olbart sought to teach the other shinobi in the village, the implementation of his ideology did not yield favorable results so easily.<ref>''Rather than blindly honing one’s own special skill, they would thoroughly forge a combat style that thwarted the opponent’s strong points, and learn techniques to bring about that situation. But then again, this change did not readily bear fruit.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7.</ref> In all, the number of shinobi who had properly molded by it were few in number, with the last one being [[Yae Tenzen]], who developed a reputation in the village as a genius.<ref>''Those who had been properly shaped by it were few, with the last being a genius girl who had appeared in the village four or five years prior. It seemed like that genius girl had also died, so the cultivation of talented individuals was nothing more than a lost cause.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 3, Section 7.</ref>

The path of a shinobi involves walking over a mountain of corpses. A shinobi who has been completed as a puppet will not question the orders given to them,<ref>''Hamayal knew not of the aim or the objective of this assassination, but he did not think to question it. Having received such an upbringing, Hamayal, now surpassing forty years of age, had been completed as a puppet devoid of any free will, bearing no superfluous questions in regards to this duty.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12]], [[Guardians of the Crimson Flame]], Section 6.</ref> and will voluntarily accept being killed if it means fulfilling their duty.<ref>''For Hamayal, past the age of forty, no longer would an important duty greater than this come about. Ergo, the very end of the footsteps he had tread, living as a shinobi, was something Hamayal would adorn alongside his other half.'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12]], [[Guardians of the Crimson Flame]], Section 6.</ref> As such, shinobi are prone to being used up and discarded before they ever get the opportunity to approach old age.<ref>''Many shinobi would have their lives used and discarded, never to achieve a long life. Yet, Olbart had lived to a point where the age of one-hundred was now close at hand.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 37]], Chapter 7, Section 1.</ref> In the case that a shinobi reaches advanced age and loses their utility, they may use a magic stone in order to blow themselves up while taking the life of an enemy caught in an explosion with them.<ref>''“For the old folks who can’t possibly be useful anymore, makin’ ‘em carry a magic stone and blow themselves up along with the enemy is the shinobi style.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 5, Section 8.</ref> As a result, shinobi do not die of old age, and the only known shinobi who has come near doing so is Olbart.<ref>''“Oh, geez, that was a real close one. At this point, I’m thinkin’ the only thing I’m able ta do that the other shinobi can’t is dyin’ of old age.”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 38]], Chapter 5, Section 8.</ref>

The culture of the shinobi village outside of its training practices is not well-known. If a shinobi is tasked to kill someone and fails to to do, the village is notified, and shinobi are dispatched one after another to fight the other person until they are successfully killed,<ref>''“The basic rule of fightin’ a shinobi’s ta lose yer life. In the case the shinobi’s killed durin’ their attempt, the village’s notified, and the next one’s dispatched, and this happens ’til the other person croaks. So, how’re ya still alive?”'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 33]], Chapter 3, Section 4.</ref> with the only known exceptions to this rule either being with runaway shinobi or in the case of [[Priscilla Barielle]], whose guardians managed to defeat a ten-person shinobi suicide squad that was tasked to kill her. From the experience of Yae Tenzen, who is the youngest person to have ever attained the rank of jonin,<ref>''As the youngest to ever be promoted to jonin, that perception of her had become widely known as something unshakeable, so Yae’s “special” allergy had worsened to a point beyond any help.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 4.</ref> the people of the shinobi village have an idealized image of what a shinobi ought to be.<ref>''“I get that Hamayal-san and everyone else at the village has an idealized image of shinobi, y’know? But, I just never fit that image, and it was troubling for people to expect that I would. For the most part, I just do what I can, so isn’t it the people who can’t do that who are worse?”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 12]], [[Guardians of the Crimson Flame]], Section 6.</ref> It was believed by the shinobi of the village that she possessed the greatest talents seen in the village since its founding, and that she may have the potential to one day rival Halibel.<ref>''Those around her had lauded her as possessing the greatest talents the shinobi village had seen since its founding, loudly voicing their admiration that her potential might even rival that of the Admirer of the Kararagi City-States.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 2.</ref> Furthermore, in the village, it is possible for two shinobi candidates to be deemed incomplete shinobi simply on account of being twins, as in the case of Shasuke and Raizo, who were considered incomplete despite initially being appraised highly and having great expectations placed on them by other shinobi.<ref>''Therefore, when the twin brothers Raizo and Shasuke were completed, the shinobi village met this unprecedented feat with earnest expectations for their growth and achievements. However, the village’s adults should have realized earlier. ――By virtue of being twin brothers, Raizo and Shasuke had already been deemed incomplete shinobi since the initial selection of prototypes.'' [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6]], Chapter 6, Section 7.</ref>

There are two symbols associated with shinobi who hail from Vollachia's shinobi village. Shasuke, Raizo, and Olbart have each possessed a scarf with a lightning bolt symbol at its end. Moreover, the three of them also have circle symbols on their garb. In Olbart's case, the circle symbol is on his sleeves, whereas for Shasuke and Raizo, it was on their scarves. The colors of both the lightning bolt symbol and the circle symbol vary between Olbart and the twins. Because neither of these symbols are mentioned in the text, it is unknown why they are associated with shinobi from Vollachia's shinobi village.

==Trivia==
*Rather than being named with the typical word used for shinobi (忍び), the term “shinobi” in the world of the series has a katakana name, similarly to the Japanese words and loan words spread throughout the world by characters who originate from Japan. Likewise, the word for “kunai”, the throwing knives employed by shinobi, is written in katakana instead of its hiragana or kanji counterparts, whereas in contrast, the word “ninja” is not recognized by those familiar with or who are themselves shinobi.
*A number of statements related to the shinobi were stated exclusively within the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (web novel)|web novel]].
**Olbart once stated that control over one's body, which enables them to do different things with each of their limbs, is foundational for the shinobi.<ref>''“Kakakakka! Body control’s the foundation of the shinobi. Ya can’t be a shinobi unless ya can do different things with yer right hand and left hand, and yer right foot and left foot. What of it?”'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 51, Section 1.</ref>
**In a section with Olbart, he mentions the existence of a shinobi technique that makes someone self-destruct at the moment they die to send information based on the color of the explosion's smoke,<ref>''“Well, shinobi techniques’ve also got somethin’ that makes ya self-destruct upon death, sendin’ information through the color of its smoke, so we’re in the same boat, the same boat, I tell ya.”'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 58, Section 1.</ref> and the narration also communicates that flawlessly grasping an area from a map alone and never forgetting a location after visiting it once are fundamental shinobi skills.<ref>''Being able to perfectly grasp a scene simply by looking at a map, and absolutely never forgetting a location upon a single visit, were fundamental skills of the shinobi, and for Olbart, the Crystal Palace was a place of work that he visited frequently.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 58, Section 1.</ref>
**Halibel has compared the bloody histories of Vollachia and the shinobi, claiming that they were just as bad as each other.<ref>''“Now, now, there’s no need for ya to say nothin’, the kid gets it just right. Ya see, Vollachia’s history’s bloody ‘n unequaled, but the shinobi‘re just as bad in retrospect.”'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 66, Section 1.</ref>
**The strength of shinobi techniques is said to reside in applicability and variety, and that the techniques are designed to bring an end to an opponent's life.<ref>''The strength of the techniques employed by the shinobi lay in their variety and applicability. Although developed to enable the fulfillment of the mission in any environment, all the various techniques had the ultimate goal of reaping the life of the opponent.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 68, Section 2.</ref>
**The essence of the shinobi is said to be to obey commands from someone else without asking too much, and Olbart is the only shinobi in Vollachia who would disobey that practice.<ref>''The essence of the shinobi was to obey commands without asking too much, and Yae considered that a preferable trait. **Vollachia shinobi are said to go through training to engage in battle while they are in a near-death state and have had a large quantity of blood drained from their bodies.<ref>''She had already surmounted the training to fight in a near-death state, with vast amounts of blood drained from her body.'' [[Arc 9]], Chapter 51, Section 9.</ref>

[[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 43]], Chapter 2, Section 3.</ref> while Yae concealed that he had not been killed along with the other shinobi who participated in the deathmatch. title: Royal Plague
wikitext:
{{Infobox Events |Name = Royal Plague |Image = |Kanji = |Rōmaji = |Date = 1 BA |Place = [[Royal Capital]], [[Kingdom of Lugunica]] |Result = The [[Royal Family|royal family]] perished
The [[Royal Selection]] began}} The '''Royal Plague''' (''unofficial name'') is a major event that shook the entirety of the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]] and changed it forever, and it paved way for the course of the main story. It took place approximately one year before the arrival of [[Natsuki Subaru]] into the world and was a major event in [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 1|The Dream the Lion King Saw]]. The [[Royal Family|royal family]] of Lugunica was a one beloved by the populace, but one day, they faced an unprecedented tragedy: one by one, every member of the royal family fell ill. Slowly, the royal family succumbed and perished to the illness of unknown origin. Eventually, on the final day of this tragedy, the fourth prince, [[Fourier Lugunica]], and the king, [[Randohal Lugunica]], died on the same day, effectively bringing an end to the royal family, and in response to the possible severing of the covenant with the [[Volcanica|Dragon]], the [[Royal Selection]], foretold by the [[Dragon History Stone]], began. ==Background== One day, [[Leip Barielle]], the caretaker responsible for the Dragon History Stone, discovered that the royal family would one day fall ill and die, and after, the Royal Selection would begin. Keeping this information to himself, Leip prepared for the day that he could make his ambition of ruling the Kingdom in the shadows through a puppet ruler. ==Tragedy== An unspecified amount of time later, the members of the royal family were quietly infected by a disease. Though it started as a small cough, the symptoms slowly got worse, but nobody truly noticed the problem. At the end of the [[Raid of Argyle Manor]], however, things changed. Fourier, who was there to witness the end to the event, collapsed. Around the same time, the other members of the royal family dropped, and all of them were left bedridden. In the following months, the royal family deteriorated in their beds. In an attempt to save them, [[Reinhard van Astrea]] was tasked with heading to the [[Pleiades Watchtower]] in order to obtain the assistance of the [[Flugel|Sage]]. However, Reinhard was unable to overcome the Sand Time barrier that spanned the [[Augria Sand Dunes]], and unable to come close to the tower, he returned to the [[Royal Capital]] in failure. [[File:Re Zero Ex Volume 1 3.png|thumb|right|250px|Fourier imagining a future that would never come as he died in Crusch's lap.]] Eventually, starting with the first prince, [[Zabinel Lugunica]], the royal family began to die. As Fourier was dying, [[Ferris]] had brought with him a book containing information on the Sacrament of the Immortal King, which he had received from Argyle Manor on the day of the raid. His intention was, even if Fourier died, he could perfect this imperfect forbidden art to bring him back to life. However, it was Fourier who convinced him not to use the technique. Eventually, Fourier found himself in the castle's garden with the woman he loved, [[Crusch Karsten]], who had been incredibly busy as a result of the plague. In that garden, he laid his head on her lap, talking with her. However, as he confessed his feelings for her Fourier died. The same day, his father, Randohal, followed him into the afterlife. ==Aftermath== Following the demise of the royal family, the Kingdom felt it, especially those of the governing bodies. Although Crusch, sad as she was, resolved to make the nation prosper in Fourier's will, she became disillusioned as those of the governing body were more concerned by the covenant with Volcanica rather than by the death of their leading figures. Because of this, Crusch began to harbor negative feelings toward to covenant and started to think of the Kingdom as having become weak. Shortly after, Leip, who was ready for this day, informed everyone of the Royal Selection that was foretold by the Dragon History Stone, presenting a Dragon Insignia that would signify who could become one of the five candidates. As it was passed around the room, it eventually reached Crusch's hands, and the Dragon Jewel within shined brightly, marking her as the very first candidate. After the meeting ended, Crusch, accompanied by Ferris, made a vow to Fourier that she would win the Royal Selection, severing the covenant with Volcanica and strengthening the nation once more, and after knighting Ferris, they left to prepare themselves for the selection. Meanwhile, Leip, who had intended to present [[Priscilla Barielle]], his wife, as the first candidate, instead revealed her as the second, and he attempted to start his scheme. However, it was thanks to Priscilla and the knight she chose, [[Al|Aldebaran]], that his schemes were thwarted. After being put through Al's Aggressor, Leip lost his mind, and eventually, he passed away, taking the secret foretold by the Dragon History Stone to his grave. It is unknown who became responsible for the stone after his demise. Sometime after the Royal Selection started, as a result of the method by which her [[curse]], which she obtained during the [[Battle for Priestella]], was removed and the [[Pleiades Sealing Conflict|failed attempt to seal him away]] by Aldebaran, Crusch and Subaru respectively started to harbor doubts about the demise of the royal family and the Dragon History Stone itself. While this would end up leading Subaru to want to speak with the head of the Council of Wise Men, [[Miklotov McMahon]], about it, Crusch came to the conclusion that he was responsible, leading to her staining her hands in his and his retainers' blood for treason and the [[Lugunican Subversive Conspiracy|conspiracy]] that the two became involved in afterward. ==Navigation== {{Battles & Events Navbox}} [[Category:Kingdom of Lugunica]] [[Category:Royal Capital]] [[Category:Events]]
