title: Insect Cage Tribe
wikitext:
[[File:Kafma Irulux LN character design clean.png|thumb|Insect Cage Tribe]]
The '''Insect Cage Tribe''' (虫籠族, ''Mushiko-zoku'') is a tribe of heretical [[Vollachia]]n [[Demi-Human|demi-humans]] who take on insect-like traits after merging with special "insects" after birth. The current chief of the tribe is the uncle of [[Kafma Irulux]].

==Information==
The Insect Cage Tribe is a minority group of various demi-humans existing only in Vollachia, considered strange, heterodox, and even heretics within their own nation.<ref>''――Even in the land of the Empire, where a wide variety of demi-human people lived, there were those who were regarded as heretics. The “Insect Cage Tribe” was exactly that, and even in an empire where demi-humans of various species were intermingled, the reality was that they weren’t free from being seen as strange and heterodox.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> Ordinarily, the members of the tribe have brown skin and a custom of tattooing, but in terms of appearance, they would not be all that different from ordinary human.<ref>''In appearance, the Insect Cage Tribe did not differ significantly from the human race. Many of them were brown-skinned and they had a custom of tattooing, but did not have any other obvious characteristics like the “Cyclops Tribe” and “Evil Eye Tribe” with their distinctive eyes, or the “Multi-Arm Tribe” and “Long-Leg Tribe” with their distinctive arms and legs, or especially the “Beastman Tribe” and “Halfbeast Tribe” who could not be any more distinctive.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> The tribe consists of different people who, at a young age, take in a special type of insect with magical properties and gain demi-human qualities after birth, allowing them to eventually adopt their powers.<ref>''It was, so to speak, the acquisition of characteristics of demi-humans after birth, and the forbidden art of transforming the body in which one was born――That was the primary reason they were shunned by other demi-humans.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> 

From birth, the child's body is altered in preparation to take in their insect, and until twelve years have passed for the child, it is forbidden to take in an insect, else they risk death.<ref>''The ritual of inserting “insects” into the body was the culmination of careful preparation, even for the Insect Cage Tribe. From the time they were newborn babies, their bodies were altered in preparation for the future insertion of “insects,” but the ritual was forbidden until they reached the age of twelve. That was to say, it took at least twelve years of preparation before an “insect” could be inserted into the body. If the process was skipped and an insect was implanted, the subject’s body would not be able to withstand it.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 87, Section 4.</ref> Until they reach age twelve, the members of the clan train their bodies and minds to become suitable vessels for the insects and proper hosts upon the time of the ceremony.<ref>''Returning back to the original topic. ――The Insect Cage Tribe waited until they were twelve years old to receive their first “insect”. Until that age, they trained their bodies and minds to be suitable vessels for the “insects” so they were recognized as an “insects” host during the actual ceremony and the time of hatching could be appropriately arranged.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> Although tribesmen cannot undergo the ritual until they turn twelve, so long as one's vessel was not prepared, then they could extend the age to fifteen before taking in an insect. However, if by this age the individual is unable to undergo the ritual, they will be tossed into "Abyss" to become food for the insects.<ref>''Those who challenged the ritual before they were physically and mentally ready would be eaten alive by the incorporated “insects”. The minimum age to challenge the ritual was twelve, but as long as the vessel was not ready, the age was allowed to be extended to fifteen. If the vessel was not ready by then, they would be deemed unqualified to be considered a member of the Insect Cage Tribe and thrown into the “Abyss” as food for the “insects”.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> The ritual to take in the insect is incredibly painful compared to attempting to take in a blood type incompatible with one's own, the sensation of which is like one's own blood has become poison, rotting the organs and burning the brain.<ref>''The suffering associated with the ritual of taking in those essential “insects” was indescribable. There were different types of blood among the human race, and trying to compensate for a lack of blood via the transfusion of a different blood type could endanger one’s life. The suffering of the “insect” ceremony was similar to that. The feeling that all of the blood flowing through one’s body was poison, rotting one’s organs and burning one’s brain.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> During the ritual, the insect grows a chrysalis that tests the host for three days and nights to see whether or not they will use the vessel as a host or dissolve it and eat it.<ref>''The “insect” grew into a chrysalis that tested the host to see if it was worthy of being its vessel, and then spent three days and three nights deciding whether to use it as its vessel or to dissolve and devour it.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> 

Should the insect decide to use its new vessel as a host, the individual's Od synchronizes with the insect's Od, allowing them to share their souls, merging them into a single living being. By doing so, the person's external appearance can drastically change to incorporate insect-like body parts, giving them a gruesome appearance most people fear and, more importantly, a means of attacking.<ref name="change">''When the chrysalis finally hatched, if the human form was still intact, the ritual succeeded and the “insect” became a symbiote. The first physical change occurred in the Insect Cage Tribe when an “insect” was taken into the body and hatched from out of their chrysalis. Some acquired antennae and wings, some developed compound eyes, others grew multiple arms and legs, and others covered their fingers and bodies with a shell.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> This being said, some members of the clan do not have a major change in their appearance, and they can otherwise pass as a regular human in such cases. The abilities possessed by the members of this clan can vary dramatically from one individual to the next; some are encased in a bug-like shell, while other have wings. Others possess sickle-like appendages, large compound eyes on their heads in place of regular eyes, and in one unique case, a brand new and unique organ as a result of taking in multiple insects.<ref name="change" /> Because of how unique the insects are, the abilities that the individual tribesmen can hold have an infinite range, and no two members of the tribe will be the same.<ref>''The “insects” that they put inside their bodies had evolved and grown beyond the bounds of human imagination, and their abilities could be said to be of an infinite variety. In addition, if they harmonize with the “insects” bred within their own bodies, and hasten the development of their skills even further, then the Insect Cage Tribe did not yield two warriors who were the same.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 87, Section 4.</ref> It is even possible for the members of this clan to weaponize their insects, whether by using unique traits such as vine and thorn like appendages or directly implanting an insect into another person's body, forcing them to either face the deadly traits of the insect or attempt to adapt to the insect merging with their body. However, the insect would only give its obedience if its host showed mastery over it, and only then would the host be recognized as a true member of the tribe.<ref>''After that, the symbiotic “insect” would only recognize its obedience towards the host if they had complete mastery over it, thus they were then allowed to call themselves a full-fledged member of the Insect Cage Tribe.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> As time passes, they can eventually take on more insects. The more insects one takes into their body, the stronger they become. Even among the tribe, its best warriors carried at least three insects.<ref>''In order to be recognized as a member of the Insect Cage Tribe, a person must take in a single “insect”. However, the more “insects” one took in, the more powerful one became as a warrior. Therefore, the best warriors of the Insect Cage Tribe had taken in at least three “insects”.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> However, taking in more insects increases the risk of the insects cannibalizing each other and endangering the host,<ref>''However, with more integrated “insects” the risk of them cannibalizing each other inside the body and endangering the life of the host increases. Therefore, the number of symbiotic “insects” is directly related to the quality of the warrior.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> which is why the tribe's current chief, who has taken in eight insects, is revered as a hero.<ref>''The current chief of the Insect Cage Tribe was known as a warrior among warriors, and was revered and respected as the hero of his tribe for having taken eight “insects” into his body.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> 

The clan is known throughout the Empire for their deadliness and effectiveness, and coupled with their large numbers, they are very effective assassins for dispatching groups of powerful foes threatening the emperor. Because their way of life is shrouded in mystery, there have been many rumors spread about them that they have not had the chance to correct, and as such, the misunderstandings surrounding the tribe have not been cleared,<ref>''The way of life of the Insect Cage Tribe, who did not mingle with others and never left their homeland, was shrouded in mystery. Since falsified knowledge was often spread with prejudice, some of the rumors would be hard for the Insect Cage Tribe to avoid laughing at if they had the opportunity to hear them. However, there were few opportunities for the rumors to be corrected, and there were again no opportunities for the misunderstandings to be cleared.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> with the most common misconception being about when they take the insect into their bodies or the connections between the tribesmen and the way of life of the insect.<ref>''The most common misconceptions were the timing of when the insects were introduced into the body, as well as the connection between the insects’ way of living and the Insect Cage Tribe――In other words, it was about the history of the Insect Cage Tribe.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref>

In the tribe's village in the far south of the country is a cave known as "Abyss". This cave, called as it is because of the deformed creatures that live within it and the poisonous air that pervades it, is where the insects, which are fundamentally different from typical insects, live.<ref>''In the southern region of the Vollachian Empire, deep within the village where the Insect Cage Tribe lived, there was a cave where “insects” lived, and the cave was called the “Abyss” because of the deformed creatures and poisonous air that pervaded it. The “insects” inhabiting the cave had a strange appearance and were fundamentally different from the insects that were commonly thought of.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> It is unknown who came up with the idea to take in these insects, but the consensus is that it was an extraordinary method thought up by a [[curse]] arts user, [[shinobi]], or other aberrants with abnormal principles.<ref>''Just who had come up with the idea of taking in these mysterious creatures, was unknown. The tribe’s point of view was that it was probably an extraordinary method discovered by curse arts users, shinobi, and other deviants with abnormal principles in order to gain power that could not be obtained through conventional methods.'' [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 32]], Chapter 6, Section 1.</ref> Regardless, the Insect Cage Tribe was created as a byproduct of this method, and the ancestors of the tribe who wished to live in symbiosis with their powers and the insects passed down the method to the present day.<ref>''In any case, given their existence, the existence of the Insect Cage Tribe was merely a byproduct. The ancestors of the Insect Cage Tribe were the ones who wished to live in symbiosis with their natural powers by implanting mysterious “insects” into their bodies, and this madness had been passed down to the present day.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref>

title: Beloved Children
wikitext:
[[File:Mark of the Beloved Children.png|thumb|165px|The Mark of the Beloved Children, as worn by [[Clarissa]].]]
The '''Beloved Children''' (愛し子, ''Itoshigo'') are a collection of people who serve an individual known to them as Mama, whose true identity is the Sin Archbishop of Lust, [[Capella Emerada Lugunica]].

==Information==
The Beloved Children are a group of people who Capella Emerada Lugunica has taken in as her "children" and are forced to call her Mama or Mother.<ref>''"――The Sin Archbishop of Lust, Capella Emerada Lugunica. She is the evildoer who compelled us Beloved Children to call her Mama, and obey her."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> Rather than being members of the [[Witch Cult]], they are primarily made up of people who have been coerced into obeying her every command.<ref>''"Is that, so… is the nuance something like a squad detached from the Witch Cultists, or a private army that includes the Sin Archbishop? Either way, calling them something like her beloved children just rubs me the wrong way."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> A number of her children appear to be unaware of her position as a [[Witch Cult#Sin Archbishops|Sin Archbishop]], instead only knowing her as Mother or Mama. Having said that, the seven currently known children who serve under her, led by [[Dandon]], have shown awareness of her appearance in [[Priestella]].<ref>''“In the Watergate City… the Sword Saint… cooperated with the other camps… that’s the story. I heard that he also got in Mama’s way there… did he let them go on purpose?”'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref>. Although people such as [[Elsa Granhiert]] and [[Meili Portroute]] are known to have been children under Capella, it is unknown if they could be considered part of the Beloved Children or held special positions within the organization. The duties of Capella's children are known to have spanned from retrieving certain items, such as a legacy of a Witch, to assassination jobs. The only known Witch Cultist among these children is Capella's fellow Sin Archbishop, [[Roy Alphard]].<ref>''“E~h, then condolences to this town’s people. If it were just us, that’d still be something, but if guys like Regulus or Sirius, and even Mama on top of that have shown up, hell would be more preferable anywa~y.”'' [[Malice Before the Theater]], Section 3.</ref>

The criteria that Capella uses to adopt someone into the Beloved Children is unclear, but she is known to gather them from various places, treat them as her own children, and direct them to think of her as their mother.<ref>''"Mama… Capella, she gathers all kinds of children from all kinds of places, and treats every one of those children as her own little ones. Bidding us to think of her as our mother. But…"'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> According to [[Melty Pristis]], one of the requirements for being picked out to join the Beloved Children is to have a unique ability that nobody else has. As such, many of the Beloved Children are either capable combatants or may provide versatile utility with their strange abilities, even if said abilities are seemingly inconsequential on their own. Whenever they are given missions to accomplish, They are sent in groups of at least two or more in order to prevent them from escaping her. Considering that Melty and [[Black Dog]] ran away when they got the opportunity to and that two other members, [[Clarissa]] and [[Tornel]], are fearful of Capella's wrath, it is likely that several of the members do not share true loyalty to the organization. Likewise, it seems as though internal fighting is not allowed, and it comes with the undesirable risk of being labeled a dropout or problem child, which seems to imply an appropriate punishment and will dissuade even the likes of the aggressive [[Reborn]].<ref>''"Hm? What’s the matter, Bellaris? You’re always so full of passion, so you hardly strike me as the type to give a silent welcome… hahaa, I take it this is your doing, Reborn? You mustn’t, oh you really mustn’t. Do make sure to follow what Mama says! You don’t wish to be branded a “Dropout” or a “Problem Child”, now do you?"'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref>

[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 46 3.png|thumb|right|250px|Dandon's unit within the Beloved Children.]]
While the group's total number of members are unspecified, Capella's children do not all work together, and they are often assigned to take care of different duties. One subgroup of the Beloved Children is led by Dandon, who Mama tasked with being in charge of keeping the others in order.<ref>''“My dear brother and honored grandfather, I told you to take your seats, did I not? It is I, after all, whom Mama placed in charge of keeping everyone in line. I should so hate to brand you an ‘encumbrance’, grandfather.”'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref> Each member of this group can be seen donning the mark of the Beloved Children, whether it is imprinted into their clothes or an accessory they wear. Although the members of this subgroup are completely out of sync, have wildly different personalities, and are misaligned in their respective principles, each of them adhere to Mama will without question. When they have meetings, they have a ritual to thank her and express that they love her more than anything else.<ref>''“――Mama, thank you for everything. I love you more than anything in the world.”'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref> Moreover, it is Dandon's belief that discerning Mama's wishes is a requirement for being among her dutiful children.<ref>''“After all, discerning our dear Mama’s wishes is a prerequisite for being dutiful Beloved Sons and Beloved Daughters.”'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref> Besides this group, Dandon has also mentioned the existence of another group, which he refers to as the "Supporters",<ref>''"――Deploy the “Supporters”. Why, this is no cause for panic."'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref> which, although their specific purpose is presently unknown, they were ordered for deployment in response to Beloved Children's "prisoners" escaping from their confinement, implying that they may be a retrieval or disposal group of some sort. Furthermore, they also have what Reborn has referred to as "Executors", and it is known that [[Tiga Rauleon]] is one, though his specific role with the Beloved Children is unknown.

The Beloved Children have been at odds with the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]] and the [[Six Tongues]] for over 30 years, posing a threat to the country for unknown reasons.<ref>''"That is correct. According to our records… they have been documented as operating behind the scenes starting over thirty years ago."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> The members of the Beloved Children regards the Six Tongues as their longstanding nemesis,<ref>''“They must have a collaborator who makes such a feat possible, it is the only logical conclusion. A yet unidentified entity has aided in their escape, provided them with food and shelter, and concealed them from watchful eyes. ――In all likelihood, it is our longstanding nemesis, the Six Tongues.”'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref> and as they have worsened Capella's mood on numerous occasions, the organization's very name has a profound, loathsome meaning to them.<ref>''For all the people present here, the name Six Tongues bore an immense, loathsome meaning. ――Just how many times had that opposing organization spoiled Mother’s mood with their interference?'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref>

With the presumptive aid of Capella's [[Capella Emerada Lugunica#Authority|Authority of Lust]], the Beloved Children have infiltrated the Kingdom by repeatedly replacing Lugunican nobles and other people who have wielded considerable influence in the nation.<ref>''"――The enemy’s aim is a silent, thorough invasion of the Kingdom. The very core of the Kingdom has already fallen into the hands of our long-sworn enemy, verging on a crisis of total downfall."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 20, Section 3.</ref> To achieve their goal of subverting the Kingdom, the Beloved Children have made use of what the Six Tongues refers to as '''Replacement Dolls'''. It is unclear if they are people whose forms are altered by Capella's Authority or something else entirely, but they are capable of seamlessly taking the place of a desired target.<ref>''――After all, none of them had any way of knowing that Disken Moreau had been replaced with another person, his position completely uprooted and usurped.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 29, Section 1.</ref> This being said, these Replacement Dolls do not seem to be able to replicate the memories or immediately understand the meaning of various things involving their histories or connections. As such, they must keep the target of whom they are replacing alive so that they can retrieve the necessary information from them whenever they need it.<ref>''Four days ago, a letter from that very retainer had arrived inscribed with the same wording. On that same day, “Viscount Moreau” had confirmed its meaning with the real one, and filled the gaps in their memory.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 29, Section 1.</ref><ref>''"Unfortunately, there were no signs of anything like that anywhere in the mansion, in fact. As expected, it must be assumed that the real one is being held captive in some other location, I suppose."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 29, Section 2.</ref> Even then, their similar yet differing behaviors will still stick out to those who have known the person who has been replaced, which can risk the exposure of said Replacement Doll, and as such, the Replacement Dolls are likely to kill such people to maintain their appearance.<ref>''In preparation for that destined moment, they had an obligation to remove every obstacle standing in the way. ――For this reason, despite being a perfectly identical existence in shape, the long-time retainers and servants who might doubt the authenticity of their inner character needed to all be removed at once.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 29, Section 1.</ref> Presently, these Replacement Dolls have been used to replace people of importance, such as some nobles, and their goal is to spread their "poison", effectively corrupting the nation from within, until the right time comes.<ref>''If it was to be put into words, the “poison” would have been none other than their own self, falsifying their position as they assumed the identity of Disken Moreau. Gradually gnawing away at the surrounding persons, those lives would be imperilled before they could even realize it. “Viscount Moreau” had heard that by now, the “poison” administered for this objective would have spread all throughout the Kingdom.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 29, Section 1.</ref><ref>''In all likelihood, the time for the “poison” to display its true efficacy was nigh.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 29, Section 1.</ref> Furthermore, while they are aware that there are other Replacement Dolls active throughout the nation, they are fully unaware who are among their allies.<ref>''The reason for the hearsay, was because even they were unenlightened as to the details of the plan to spread the “poison”. But, it was impossible that they were the only one, as the collective influence could be subtly perceived when observing the state of the nation.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 29, Section 1.</ref>

[[File:Episode 76 Beloved Children Castle.png|thumb|300px|A castle where Elsa and Meili met with Capella.]]
While the members of the Beloved Children spread across the world have not been stated to have a singular headquarters to use as a gathering place, there are various hideouts that have been prepared for Capella's children, such as a safe house that existed in the [[Royal Capital|Royal Capital of Lugunica]], in addition to several other hideouts scattered across the towns and villages in its vicinity.<ref>[[Elsa and Meili, Assassin Sisters' Dark Diary]], Section 2.</ref> One such hideout includes an octagonal table made of ancient yet sturdy wood made by [[Arbalest]] specifically for meetings between the group. In [[Episode 76]] of the anime adaptation, Elsa and Meili were shown to have met Capella at a castle within an unspecified snowy region.

==History==
The Beloved Children were formed at an unspecified time in the past. They have been noted by the records of Lugunica's intelligence and spy agency, the Six Tongues, to be operating in the shadows for over 30 years. For most of said period of time, the Six Tongues struggled with opposing the Beloved Children due to their true nature being uncertain to the agency, which was narrowly able to prevent them from having their way with the country.<ref>''"Indeed. As such, the history of the Six Tongues can be said to be a history of its hidden conflict against the Beloved Children. However, the Beloved Children were an opponent of whom we knew little, whereas we were always one step behind… in a constant state of having our hands full just barely containing them from doing as they pleased within these borders."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> While the Six Tongues had trouble with countering the Beloved Children, innumerable examples of nobles or influential people having abrupt changes of heart and acts of sabotage such as information leaks to other nations took place.<ref>''"I have no retort. In fact, throughout the Kingdom, there have been numerous abrupt changes of heart by nobles and people of influence, as well as some of them acting against our interests by providing intelligence to the other nations, too many to count in fact. Even in the decade or so since I took over as Director, lacking any decisive blow to end this deadlock, we have continued with such stopgap measures. ――However, the situation has changed."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref>

In light of [[Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti]]'s death, Capella was left in a frenzy. Two of the Beloved Children took advantage of the circumstances and escaped from Capella's grasp.<ref>''"Fing…? That is incorrect, but, it did cause Mama to be rattled, and we slipped out amidst the kerfuffle… and here we are."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> They were discovered by the current director of the Six Tongues, [[Russell Fellow]], who learned the truth about the Beloved Children from them.<ref>''"――Hk! You got members of the enemy to switch sides!?"'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref><ref>''"It was a situation where several coincidences aligned in our favor. Nevertheless, as a result, regarding the Beloved Children whom we had opposed for so long… we were blessed with the opportunity to learn of their true nature."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> Taking on the aliases White Sheep and Black Dog, they aligned themselves with the Six Tongues and won the trust of Russell, who took measures to prevent any possible betrayal by them. For over a year after Melty became a member of the Six Tongues, they successfully foiled a handful of the Beloved Children's plans.<ref>''"If that were true, it would have made far more sense for us to have been crushed long ago. It has already been over a year since White Sheep and Black Dog joined us… during that time, we have thwarted the Beloved Children’s intrigues on more occasions than can be counted on a single hand. There would be no purpose to contribute so much.'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref>

With the [[Battle for Priestella]], Capella brazenly made an appearance in the Watergate City alongside the other Sin Archbishops. When the description of Capella Emerada Lugunica corresponded to the “Mama” who Melty knew, it was determined that they were the same person. Russell came to believe that Capella's strike on Priestella was intended to reveal her existence to the Six Tongues. For some time after this, they dealt with seven fakes who matched Capella's description. However, while Russell was preoccupied with them and the Beloved Children, the Council of Wise Men and many of the high-ranking nobles were presumably replaced by Capella,<ref>''"It is highly feared that the Kingdom’s Council of Wise Men, as well as the majority of its upper nobles, have been replaced by Capella Emerada Lugunica, matriarch of the Beloved Children, and that the Dragon History Stone now lies in the hands of the aforementioned Lust."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 21, Section 2.</ref> causing the Royal Capital, as well as the Dragon History Stone, to fall into the hands of her and her children.

Following the return of the [[Emilia Camp]] to the Royal Capital, the movement of the [[Divine Dragon Church]], and [[Crusch Karsten]]'s murder of [[Miklotov McMahon]] and his retainers, who had likely already been replaced by Capella's forces, Capella started to set her plan into motion, having her Beloved Children isolate, apprehend, and attempt to kill different members of the various camps of the [[Royal Selection]]. [[Emilia]], [[Ram]], and [[Felt]] were put under house arrest within the castle, Crusch, [[Natsuki Subaru]], [[Beatrice]], and [[Rachins Hoffman]] were forced to seek the assistance of the Six Tongues after managing to escape from Clarissa, [[Reinhard van Astrea]] was effectively coerced into cooperating with the corrupted government to arrest the other camps, and the remaining members of the Emilia, [[Felt Camp|Felt]], and [[Crusch Camp]]s were all forced to flee from the Royal Capital, leaving the Beloved Children, seemingly led by Dandon, free reign over the city and the nation.<ref>''“Right then, ‘scuse me, ‘scuse us, we ended up running a tad late! Terribly sorry for gathering you all today. Mind you, governing a nation’s a proper busy job, amirite!?”'' [[Arc 10]], Interlude 2.</ref>

title: Dragon History Stone
wikitext:
[[File:Dragon Stone ep.12.png|thumb|right|250px]]
The '''Dragon History Stone''' (竜歴石, ''Ryūrekiseki'') is a large stone lithograph bequeathed by [[Volcanica]] to the late [[Royal Family]] of the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]] that could foretell the fate of the country. Its current caretaker is unknown.

==Information==
The Dragon History Stone is a permanent fixture of the Lugunican culture, alongside the [[Dragon]] and the covenant. The stone is capable of telling the future of the Kingdom, making note of numerous tragedies that the Kingdom can either prepare for or avoid. Because of its accuracy, the populace has come to rely on it very heavily, to the point that almost nobody questions it, especially those in the highest positions of power. Similarly, if the stone states that certain national events must occur, then the government will almost immediately come to the consensus to act on or prepare a response to said event. Such is the case with the [[Royal Selection]], and despite some of the people involved being chosen as candidates and both the government's and populace's discontent that has been brought about by that decision, such as in the case of [[Anastasia Hoshin]], [[Emilia]], and [[Felt]], the will of the stone will remain prioritized. At present, the exact functions that make the stone capable of determining the future are currently unknown.

Although its abilities are highly accurate, there are times when certain futures have seemingly not been predicted. Namely, the [[Royal Abduction Incident]]. In a similar manner, as the stone is merely an object, it is easy for it to be taken advantage of by those who watch over it. Previously, the Dragon History Stone was overseen by the previous head of House Barielle, Baron [[Leip Barielle]]. This man, corrupt as he was, had witnessed certain prophecies from the stone and chose not to inform anybody, allowing the caretaker to hide knowledge from those who needed to know it.

Because nobody questions the stone, this makes it very easy to fool the very people who rely on it. Despite the tragedies surrounding the royal family, both of which had tremendous repercussions and even threatened the nation's survival, nobody has thought to question why the stone seemingly did not foresee the tragedies, instead making those in power focus on entirely separate matters. At present, there are only two people who have questioned the veracity of the Dragon History Stone: [[Crusch Karsten]] and [[Natsuki Subaru]], the former of which only realized something was wrong after meeting with a possible impostor of [[Miklotov McMahon]], and the latter of which was originally a foreign entity who had knowledge of the questionable nature of being able to see the future.

Ordinarily, the care of the safety and location of the stone is known only to its caretaker and the '''Safeguarding Chamber''' (守護室, ''Shugo-shitsu''), a group of people who are permitted to know of and protect the location of the Dragon History Stone. Each member must swear allegiance to Lugunica and are thoroughly vetted before being accepted to ensure that there are no problems with appointing them to such a crucial role. Presently, it is unclear who the current caretaker of the Dragon History Stone is, as it was never stated following the death of Leip. However, it can be assumed that its care was entrusted to the government, as during the [[Lugunican Subversive Conspiracy]], with [[Capella Emerada Lugunica]]'s use of the [[Beloved Children]] to replace government officials, [[Russell Fellow]] believed that the stone had fallen into their hands. As such, the current state and present location of the stone is also unknown.

==Prophecies==
*Great Famine of Cudegra
*[[Royal Plague]]<ref>''Having grasped the fact that the prophetic tablet had been inscribed with information about a calamity that would soon strike the Kingdom of Lugunica―― a disease that would spread through the Royal Family, Leip blazed with aspirations towards the next battle for the throne that would follow thereafter.'' [[Arc 8]], Chapter 72, Section 1.</ref><ref group=Note>Despite the belief that the deaths of the Royal Family was not foretold by the Dragon History Stone, this is actually false. Leip Barielle, who was the stone's caretaker, had seen that the Dragon History Stone foretold of their demise and took advantage of it to suit his own purposes. With his death, the secret went down with him.</ref>
*[[Royal Selection]]

==Trivia==
*The Dragon History Stone is strikingly similar to the [[Vollachia Empire]]'s [[Stargazer]]s in its purpose to see the future and prevent the collapse of the country.
**The stone also bears similarity to [[Echidna]]'s Book of Wisdom and the Gospels used by the [[Witch Cult]], [[Beatrice]], and [[Roswaal L. Mathers]]. If it is connected to them, however, is unknown.
*Presently, although the [[Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (anime)|anime]] has provided a makeshift image of the stone, its physical description has not been provided in the novels.
*It has supposedly been claimed that the "nightmare of the blight dragon [[Valgren]]" (邪竜バルグレンの悪夢, ''jyaryū Baruguren no akumu'') was foretold by the Dragon History Stone. However, given that it was never mentioned in the events of [[Re:Zero Ex Light Novel Volume 6|Sword Demon Battle Ballad]], it is unknown if this is truly the case.

title: Demi-Human
wikitext:
'''Demi-Humans''' (亜人, ''Ajin'') are a number of various humanoid races besides human that have traits and abilities that separate them from ordinary humans.

==Information==
<gallery type="slideshow">
LiM Lilac V2.png|An elf, a type of demi human.
Halibel LN character design clean.png|A wolf human, a type of demi-human.
Kurgan LN character design.png|A member of the Multi-Arm Tribe, a type of demi-human.
Ezzo Cadner LN character design.png|A dwarf, a type of demi-human.
Groovy Gumlet Without Sample.jpg|A hyena human, a type of demi-human.
</gallery>
In the world of Re:Zero, there are many different races, and the majority of the various races of people that are not human are colloquially referred to as demi-humans. Demi-humans often carry traits that humans do not have, including extra organs, horns, animal traits, longer life spans, excessive physical sizes, extra body parts, unique abilities, etc. Apparently, demi-humans have been said to have greater strength in order to make up for their fewer numbers.<ref>''In this world, demi-humans were called the race that was powerful to make up for the lack of numbers they had in comparison to people.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Prologue.</ref> For a long time, due to the fear that humans have had over beings that were different than them, demi-humans have been consistently persecuted throughout history, resulting in various slaughters and enslavement. Even as time passed and discrimination has lessened in the present day, it is still a consistent problem witnessed in present society.

===Present Day Treatment of Demi-Humans===
====Overview====
During the era of the [[Great Calamity]], demi-humans still faced heavy discrimination, but after [[Satella]] became the Witch of Envy and was responsible for the destruction of half of the world, persecution became even harsher, and demi-humans were forced to bear hellish consequences. The overall hatred towards demi-humans continued to last for centuries, and in the [[Kingdom of Lugunica]], it has resulted in what has become known as the [[Demi-Human War]], an event that, although started out as a more scattered and disorganized affair with smaller albeit bloody skirmishes, quickly devolved into a decade-spanning civil war between humans and demi-humans. Because of this war, demi-humans have been both positively and negatively influenced, and although discrimination overall has been reduced, the war was one in which the might of the demi-humans was left permanently branded into the minds of humans.

In particular, demi-humans who have horns have also been despised and compared to [[witchbeast]]s, who had been created around that time by [[Daphne]] and were mistaken as Satella's creations, while elves and half-elves face some of the harshest discrimination across the world, as they are immediately associated with Satella, who was a half-elf. Although there have been very few showings of elves in general, the few times they have been seen, they were hiding somewhere away from society. At present, due to the [[Permafrost of Elior Forest]], many elves were frozen. It is unknown if there were any other settlements of elves besides the one in [[Elior Forest]], but at present, the only other likely place for one to be is in the Forest of the Elves in southern Lugunica, though this is unknown. As for half-elves, their persecution is even worse. Historically, the [[Witch Cult]] has killed any half-elves they have found while believing that the only half-elf that could be allowed to exist was Satella. Likewise, thanks to the Great Calamity, half-elves, especially ones with silver hair, are deeply despised by the populace.

Each country is still affected by the events of the Great Calamity. However, each country handles their respective demi-humans differently.

====Lugunica====
The Kingdom of Lugunica still remembers the blood spilled during the Demi-Human War, as compared to the Great Calamity, it is much fresher in their minds. However, thanks to the war, the discrimination towards the country's demi-humans has still lessened compared to prior to the war. It is unknown when the Kingdom abolished slavery, but because of this, demi-humans no longer face slavery while within the Kingdom. They are allowed to have jobs, and as part of the Kingdom's laws, they are to be given fair wages.

Presently, the nobility of the country has scattered views towards demi-humans. Thanks to the Demi-Human War, there are still some nobles who hold deep-seated grudges against demi-humans, with one particular person, [[Bordeaux Zergev]], being a prime example. Even younger members of nobility, such as [[Joshua Juukulius]], held some minor prejudice at one time, though in cases like his, exposure to demi-humans and influence by other non-prejudiced people have eliminated such prejudice. On the opposite end of the spectrum are nobles like Margrave [[Roswaal L. Mathers]], although he is considered eccentric, who is called the Demi-Human Lover due to his favoritism towards demi-humans and the fact that he often hires them to work for [[House Mathers]] or House Miload. There are also almost no demi-humans in the [[Royal Army]]. In the past, just like the common folk, there was scattered prejudice towards demi-humans among the knights' ranks. However, thanks to the presence of [[Ferris|Felix Argyle]], a demi-human member of the Royal Guard, as well as the other popular members of the army, [[Julius Juukulius]], [[Reinhard van Astrea]], and [[Marcos Gildark]], treating him like an equal, prejudice towards demi-humans among the knights has also reduced.

This being said, the discrimination towards half-elves is still deep-seated. However, thanks to the efforts of the [[Emilia Camp]] in the [[Royal Selection]], and their achievements while participating for the throne, at least towards her, such discrimination is vanishing from the minds of the people. Slowly but surely, she is becoming recognized not as a silver-haired half elf, but as the Royal Selection Candidate [[Emilia]], and her popularity with the public eye is beginning to increase, due also in part to [[Shorty Megan]] and [[Lululala]] and their reports on them in the Dragon Times newspaper.

====Vollachia====
[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 28 1.png|thumb|left|250px|The Nine Divine Generals' diverse makeup]]
As [[Vollachia Empire|Vollachia]] holds a might above all stance and a heavily meritocratic government, prejudice towards demi-humans as a whole is practically non-existent. As might makes right, it can become very simple for a demi-human to rise in the ranks and even obtain noble or general status. In fact, even among the [[Imperial Army#Nine Divine Generals|Nine Divine Generals]], four of their current ranks are demi-human, while two others are neither human nor demi-human. Even in the past, a demi-human, [[Kurgan]], was hailed as the country's hero and War God.

However, this does not prevent some people from turning their enmity towards specific demi-humans, though this is less discrimination than it is either fear of an attack or a simple personal grudge. Such issues have led to attack and traps for the Multi-Arm Tribe and the near annihilation of the Evil Eye Tribe. This being said, Vollachia still holds an abnormally high number of demi-humans within its borders, and numerous skirmishes involve them. In fact, thanks to [[Yorna Mishigure]], who created the [[Chaosflame|Demon City of Chaosflame]], Vollachian demi-humans, especially horned demi-humans have been given a safe haven from which to reside and are heavily protected by the Divine General.

Approximately three centuries prior, however, due to the betrayal of [[Volcas]], a wolf human, and the misunderstanding with [[Lynek]], a mole human, revolving around the murder of Iris, the wolf and mole humans have since suffered merciless persecution, and by the decree of [[Eugard Vollachia]], the emperor of the time, the genocide of the wolf and mole humans was ordered, resulting in the deaths of many of their races. Their deaths fueled the [[Curse#Soul Marriage Curse|Soul Marriage Curse]] placed on Iris's soul, and for three centuries, this decree was not released. Thanks to this, wolf and mole humans have been in hiding across all of the nations, as Vollachia will not hesitate to send one of their own soldiers to slay any other known members of their races. Ultimately, this led to the creation of the wolf humans' hidden village and Everlasting Darkness, an underground passage that connects Vollachia and Lugunica and is inhabited by the mole humans. It wasn't until the end of the [[Great Disaster]], when Eugard was revived as a [[Undead#Zombies|zombie]], that the decree for the deaths of the mole and wolf humans was finally repealed. The aftereffects of the repeal have yet to be seen.

====Kararagi====
The [[Kararagi|Kararagi City-States]] have a high number of demi-humans within its borders, likely the highest among the Four Great Nations. Although slavery is still a legal practice, it is not made specifically for demi-humans, as either race can be involved in either the trade or becoming a slave. Demi-humans, like any other human, have been involved with the mercantilist ways of the nation, creating their own businesses or even creating their own mercenary group, with the [[Iron Fang]] being one of the most well-known mercenary groups.

At present, however, it is unknown the general consensus of demi-humans. While it is an unspoken secret that the wolf human village exists in Kararagi and that their strongest warrior is [[Halibel]], a wolf human, nobody seems to mind, and it is not uncommon for his services to be bought even by the League of Cities. However, it has been said that hairless demi-humans are considered unfortunate. This being said, it is unknown if this leads towards discrimination.

====Gusteko====
Among all of the four countries, [[Gusteko]] is the vaguest about their stance toward demi-humans. Although the country has a public stance of equality, the people who reside within the country are actually very prejudiced and insular. Slavery exists as an open secret, and both humans and demi-humans are subject to it, in a way making them "equal". This being said, however, elves, in particular, are seen as a heretical race, and the [[Gustekan Church]] would have no qualms in eliminating any that they found, as in the attempted case of [[Shion]] and [[Lilac]], who were merely traveling in the country at the time.

===Abilities===
As has been stated, demi-humans have often been attacked or enslaved for their abilities. One such example of this is the Evil Eye Tribe, whose members bear either an extra eye or uniquely shaped eyes with an ability claimed to be like a [[Divine Protection]], refused to join the forces of various Vollachian nobles, and as such, they were attacked numerous times, with the tribe as a whole being pushed nearly to extinction as a result. Another is the [[Oni]] Tribe, which has been recognized as the strongest of demi-humans and was systematically slaughtered for it. As such, despite having faced persecution, the various races have been recognized for their different strengths and abilities.

It has been said that [[magic]] was once the domain of demi-humans and [[spirit]]s,<ref>''“The world was a tough place for humans to live four hundred years ago. Magic was an exclusive strong suit that demi-humans and spirits had, regardless of which country you were in.”'' [[Re:Zero Tanpenshuu Volume 6]], [[The Witch's After Tea Party / The Requirements to be a Witch]], Section 3.</ref> although in time, humans eventually became capable of it as well. This being said, there is one race of demi-humans, the Multi-Arm Tribe, who lack such affinity for magic. In their case, they are given extra arms, larger builds, and increased physical might to make up for their lack of magic. Other demi-human races also bear increased physical strength. In particular, beast person races. While not all of them have increased strength, there are still a good number of beast people whose physical strength and durability, at a basic level, are greater than humans'. Likewise, their bodies are physically tougher as well, which grants them resistances to things such as certain Divine Protections that would ordinarily force humans to suffer from drawbacks. Sometimes, depending on the animal, they can even gain abilities unique to that animal, such as how snake humans can have regeneration or poison glands. Of course, beast humans also have their own problems; for example, their fang-like teeth and claws continue to grow, forcing them to gnaw and file them.

Although it is unknown if it is limited to half- or quarter-blooded beast people, there are some beast people who are able to tap into their more bestial traits and change their physical make-up to become stronger.<ref>''“It’s my beast form, characteristic of half-beasts.”'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Chapter 4, Section 3.</ref> In [[Garfiel Tinzel]]'s case, a quarter-blood tiger human, he is capable of becoming a large bipedal tiger with incredible physical might and toughness, albeit with the chance to go berserk. In his sister [[Frederica Baumann]]'s case, she can become a quadrupedal leopard with greater speed and apparently no chance of her going berserk. For particularly skilled beast people, they can even partially transform their bodies, giving them access to increased strength than they ordinarily bear without exerting their full bestial might.

Melinda Evil Eye Design.png|Melinda's Evil Eyes

When it comes to Divine Protections, there are actually other races with a greater chance of receiving them, whereas there are others whose every member is born with a Divine Protection. The Uruha Tribe, a tribe native to Gusteko, is one such tribe in which every member has a Divine Protection. The dwarves, on the other hand, who are born with smaller bodies, weak physical strength, and a lower capacity for magic, all have a greater chance of being given a Divine Protection. The ten siblings of [[Ezzo Cadner]], for example, were all given a Divine Protection, with Ezzo being the odd one out. Uniquely, half-blooded wolf humans, referred to as werewolves, have all been given the Divine Protection of Ambushing, which makes it nearly impossible for someone to locate them while hiding. This being said, it should be noted that the Evil Eye Tribe, despite the abilities granted to them by their eyes, may not truly be Divine Protections, and instead, the abilities are unique to each person's specific eye.

There are also some races born with abilities and physical traits that set them apart from any other races. The weaponkin, for example, are a race that have different parts of their body made out of metal, which they eventually fashion into their own weapons. Some of them are even born with a tail with this trait. Steelfolk have bodies made entirely of minerals, and as such, they have significantly greater physical strength and durability compared to others, though they also have unique mindsets as well.<ref name="steelfolk">''She only knew of them from rumors, but Moguro Hagane was a special kind of demi-human called a “Steelfolk”. Unlike the Weaponkin, whose bodies were only partially made of metal, she had heard that they were existences whose bodies were entirely made out of minerals.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 93, Section 1.</ref> Glow people have [[Mana#Mana-Related Natural Resources|glintstones]] on their forehead which are said to carry the souls of anyone they kill,<ref name="distinguish" /> and the cyclops tribe have a singular eye which give them greater eyesight and the ability to read emotions through color. Of course, as there are numerous types of these demi-humans, it is unknown just how many unique and various people may exist in the world.

===Artificial Races===
For reasons unknown, there have been races that were artificially made for specific reasons. As of yet, only the Oni Tribe has been confirmed to be like this. Having been made to counter the [[Witch]]es, smell the scent of the Witch, and bear strength claimed to be the strongest of all demi-humans, their might has been highly recognized by the world. However, their insular and secluded ways eventually led to their ultimate demise, and now the race has very few survivors.

There is one tribe of humans, the Insect Cage Tribe, that can also artificially become demi-humans. It is unknown the reason for the tribe's existence, but they have displayed to ability to house various types of insects in their bodies. The process by which this is done is unknown, but it is said to be extremely dangerous and can even threaten the life of anyone who attempts it. For those that succeed in taking in such an insect, the person will obtain various types of insect traits and abilities, including compound eyes or exoskeletons. In the case of [[Kafma Irulux]], he even developed a special organ that is unique to him and provides him abilities that nobody else in his clan is capable of reproducing.

===Traditions===
As each race and tribe is unique, each one carries its own traditions. The Multi-Arm Tribe, for example, following in the footsteps of their hero, Kurgan, became a warring tribe, in which the men would train to fight while the women and children remained behind to take care of their homes. However, because of their beliefs, any man to stay behind or to hold more pacifistic beliefs was considered an outcast and shunned by the rest of the tribe. This is especially the case for one such as [[Gustav Morello]], whose pacifistic nature even led him away from the path of vengeance despite been given the chance to kill the man responsible for the slaughter of his people.

The Oni Tribe have a bloody tradition of their own. Due to the heavy belief that they carry the greatest strength among demi-humans, they believe in purity. Because their horns can provide the onis with strength, if twins, who are born with only one horn, are born, they are quickly put to death in order to preserve the purity of the Oni Tribe's might.

==Types of Demi-Humans==
===Closest to Humans in Shape===
Demi-humans that fall under this category are those that can be indistinguishable from humans if not for a few noticeable traits, such as extra eyes, long ears, extra organs, etc. Beast humans will not fall under this category.

[[File:Elves of Elior Forest ep.42.png|thumb|250px|Elves]]
*'''Elf''' (エルフ, ''Erufu''): Elves are a race of demi-humans known for their longevity and beauty, and their signifying traits are their pointed ears. It is stated that elves are the longest-lived race, unaging after reaching a certain point in their life, and not dying unless killed. Because of the Witch of Envy, elves were also the target of prejudice from others. Currently, the only known elven community to appear in the story are frozen in the Great Elior Forest.

[[File:Re Zero Light Novel 3 3.png|thumb|250px|Oni]]
*'''Oni Tribe''' (鬼族, ''Onizoku''): A race of demi-humans that, while mostly identical to humans, were distinguished by their special mana-absorbing retractable horns. Among the numerous humanoid races that existed in the world, the Oni Tribe were considered the mightiest. Their powerful bodies and the potency of the mana quality they employed, both granted the onis peerless combat strength. However, as the members of the race had an elitist mindset, in order to preserve their purity and pride, enacted strict taboos and lived in villages in the mountains, away from others. For more details, see [[Oni]].

[[File:Valga.png|thumb|Giants]]
*'''Giant''' (巨人, ''Kyojin''): Giants are a demi-human race of massive people with tremendous strength and a lifespan of around 150 years. In fact, giants are the next longest-lived species of demi-humans after elves. They fought in various places during wartime, and because of that, their numbers dwindled. Furthermore, they faced persecution in a similar manner to the elves and onis.<ref>''For many people, the Oni Clan’s power that overwhelmed other races became something to fear and drive out. To put it appropriately, for the people afraid of the return of the Witch of Envy, it seemed really close to how the Elves became persecuted. Similarly, it’s said that in ancient times there was also a similar type of rejection towards giants.'' [[Re:Zero Prequel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village]], Prologue.</ref> The only known giant to live in the present day lives in the [[Royal Capital]] of Lugunica, [[Rom|Valga Cromwell]]. It is mentioned that in the earlier days, it was common for giants to reach about 4-5 meters in terms of height, though [[Sekhmet]], a giant herself, killed most other giants, pushing them toward the verge of extinction. Those that remain have their blood continuously mixed with that of other races, and thus, their sizes have become much smaller. Because of this, the average size of a giant in the present is a little over 2 meters in height.<ref>''"In earlier days, it was common for them to reach four or five meters, but Sekhmet killed most of them, and other bloodlines began to mix in, so they’re gradually getting smaller. Currently, if there was a three-meter-tall one, that would be pretty big. The average is a bit over two meters, and Old Man Rom is average."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref> According to Valga, he himself may be the final living giant.<ref>''"Unfortunately, never’ve I happened ta meet another Giant ‘side from myself. It’s possible that I’m the last of the Giants still kickin’ in this world."'' [[Arc 10]], Chapter 4, Section 2.</ref>

[[File:Kan 3 Star.png|thumb|Dwarves]]
*'''Dwarf Tribe''' (小人族, ''Kobito-zoku''): The Dwarf Tribe are a common type of demi-human that are shorter than normal humans. Many dwarves tend to look like children, even in adulthood. [[Arc 8]], Chapter 61, Section 1.</ref>

*'''Weaponkin''' (刃金人, ''Hakane Hito''): A race of demi-humans born with parts of their bodies metallized which they reshape into any weapon of their choosing as they grow up.<ref>''In the vicinity, ceasing their movements and exhaling white breaths, were the people equipped with one part of their body as an eye-catching feature. [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref> They may also be born with a body part that a normal human lacks that carries this metallic trait, such as a tail. ===Beastman & Halfbeast Tribes===
The races that fall under this category are those who bear traits that are shared with animals. Beast people that share traits with animals typically only share things like ears, noses, or tails, while beast humans with that are linked to more carnivorous animals will also have sharp fangs or claws. However, there are other types of beast humans that exhibit a more animal than human appearance, such as the mole or snake humans. In such cases, they typically take on the appearance of anthropomorphic animals that vary in size. No matter what kind of beast they take after, beast humans tend to possess enhanced senses, such as smell, hearing, or eyesight. However, depending on the animal, beast people may be born with other traits unique to their specific animal, such as poison, regeneration, or camouflage.

===Unique Demi-Humans===
Demi-humans in this section are those who are clearly distinguishable from other races.

Kurgan's fame changed their position, yet the tribe remained a force to be reckoned with, causing the local feudal lord of one settlement, believing the men had been slain in combat, to dress his subordinates as bandits to indiscriminately kill the women and children remaining there. If not for the pacifistic Gustav Morello taking a stand and [[Cecilus Segmunt]]'s interference, the settlement may have faced complete destruction. The locations of other Multi-Arm Tribe settlements are unknown.

==Trivia==
*Due to having a different physical make-up on the molecular level, [[Dragon#Dragonkin|Dragonkin]] are not considered demi-humans.
**It has been said that Dragonkin have pushed ten races to extinction. It is unknown if this means ten races of demi-humans or otherwise.
**Despite not being considered demi-humans due to being different from them at a fundamental level, dragonkin have been called demi-humans in the story. It is unknown if this was a mistake in narration or if they were referred to as such from the perspective of the characters.<ref>''The guardian of the second bastion was Madelyn Eschart, the dragonkin who had almost plunged the Fortress City into a state of total destruction――and was part of a demi-human race so exceedingly rare, people questioned its very existence.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 95, Section 3.</ref>
*Like dragonkin, since [[Shaula]] was born as a [[witchbeast]] and has a different physical make-up, she cannot be considered a demi-human.
*Although particularly powerful spirits can take a humanoid shape while others, like [[Beatrice]], are purposefully made that way, they are not considered demi-humans.
*Before their reveal as a [[meteor]], [[Moguro Hagane]] was claimed to be a steel human.<ref name="steelfolk" />
*There are a number of demi-humans that have yet to be classified, including [[Minor Characters#Tokaku|Tokaku]] and Frederica.
*The Demon City of Chaosflame's populace was filled with demi-humans that have yet to be classified, including demi-humans with horns like rhinos or rams, as seen through some of the images provided with [[Re:Zero Light Novel Volume 29|Volume 29]].
*The entire population of the Sanctuary, except for Garfiel and Frederica, were half-blooded demi-humans.
*The game [[Re:Zero Lost in Memories]] introduces bear humans through [[Madara]] and chameleon humans through [[Melio]]. However, as there have been no bear or chameleon humans revealed in any main or side story, they are both presently non-canon.
*Uniquely, the eyes of the Witch of Gluttony, Daphne, are strangely shaped, similar to how the Evil Eyes held by [[Melinda]] are shaped differently from other people's eyes. However, it is unknown if these are Evil Eyes, and as such, makes it unknown if Daphne was born a member of the Evil Eye Tribe.
*When asked in a Q&A if there would be fish type demi-humans, merfolk, or turtle type demi-humans, the author claimed there would not be.<ref>''"There’s something similar to lizardmen, but there’s nothing like mermen. Perhaps it’s because there’s no ocean."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref><ref>''"There’s no mermen, so maybe not…"'' AskFM Q&A.</ref>
*Although not canon, [[Tarco Ulrat]] is the only wolf human to possess a human appearance, wolf ears, and a tail. Since werewolves can pass as human in appearance and other wolf humans have been shown to be mostly anthropomorphic, it is unknown if wolf humans of any kind can exhibit traits like Tarco's.
*When asked about there being races with extra legs, heads, or eyes, though the author claimed there might be some with extra eyes, there likely would not be races with extra legs or heads, as it would be difficult to picture races the further from human they appeared.<ref>''"Probably not legs and heads. Eyes, maybe. It’s tough when the visual gets too far from human-shaped."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref> However, the Multi-Leg Tribe was later introduced within the story.
*Although mentioned in the web novel, the long leg tribe were removed from the light novel and thus made non-canon.<ref>''In appearance, the Insect Cage Tribe did not differ significantly from the human race. Many of them were brown-skinned and they had a custom of tattooing, but did not have any other obvious characteristics like the “Cyclops Tribe” and “Evil Eye Tribe” with their distinctive eyes, or the “Multi-Arm Tribe” and “Long-Leg Tribe” with their distinctive arms and legs, or especially the “Beastman Tribe” and “Halfbeast Tribe” who could not be any more distinctive.'' [[Arc 7]], Chapter 89, Section 1.</ref>
*Thus far, the lizard humans are the only known race of demi-humans known to have a subspecies, and [[Cragrell Dawson]] is the only person to be a member of said subspecies.
*Uniquely, [[Vague Adgard]] is a "spirit human", someone born of both humans and spirits. However, as spirits are not demi-humans, it is unclear if spirit humans can be classified as demi-humans.
*According to the author, excluding Ferris, as a member of the Royal Guard, and Cragrell Dawson, who was given a noble title to prevent him from assassination and the resurgence of war, there are no demi-humans in positions of importance within Lugunica.<ref>''"There are no demi-humans in important positions."'' Q&A.</ref>
*According to the author, it is not uncommon for demi-humans to build settlements in secluded areas in Lugunica, as relations between them and humans were bad.<ref>''"With the capital in the center, there are large cities placed like a six-pointed star, with populations around 200,000 to 300,000 people. Aside from those, small cities are scattered about, and it continues down through towns, villages, and settlements, you see. If you only look at humans, they mostly live in villages, but there are cases where demihumans create settlements in the mountains and woods and live there. Relations are quite bad."'' Q&A.</ref>
*According to the author, due to the atavistic nature of his demi-human traits, Ferris does not experience cat-like instincts.<ref>''"Unfortunately, he doesn't manifest cat-like instincts that much. Ferris' demi-human blood is a throwback to earlier generations, so he mostly doesn't have those characteristics aside from his external appearance. He had a terrible time as a child due to that appearance, so it was quite a nuisance.''" Felix Birthday Q&A 2018.</ref> It is unclear if this means that other cat humans do experience these instincts.
*When asked if dark elves exist, the author claimed that there might be a similar race with black skin, but they would be mostly unrelated to elves.<ref>''"They might exist, as a species that is simply black-skinned, and mostly unrelated to elves."'' AskFM Q&A.</ref>

[[Tiga Rauleon]] |forces3 = |casual1 = |casual2 = |casual3 = |civilian = }} The '''Emergence of Kugelschreiber Castle''' (''unofficial name'') is a battle that took place approximately one year and ten months after the arrival of [[Natsuki Subaru]] into the world, and it is one of the earlier conflicts in [[Arc 10]]. It is a battle that takes place early in the [[Lugunican Subversive Conspiracy]], in which Subaru's group traveled to Kugelschreiber Castle in order learn of a way to undo [[Capella Emerada Lugunica]]'s [[Authority#Authority of Lust|Authority of Lust]]. After two months of fighting against the [[Beloved Children]]'s forces, Subaru's group decides to focus on a way to counter Capella's Authority, setting their sights on the legacies of a [[Echidna|Witch]]. At [[Beatrice]]'s lead, the group made their way to Kugelschreiber Castle, where her laboratory was. However, shortly after their arrival, the group found themselves at odds with elite members of the Beloved Children. ==Background== ===Echidna's Soul Experiments=== During the era of the [[Great Calamity]], the [[Witch|Witch of Wisdom]] Echidna performed various experiments during her research into immortality, leading her to researching the soul in Kugelschreiber Castle. Because of the battle between Echidna's group and the Warlock of Melancholy, [[Hector]], in the [[Sanctuary]], Echidna chose to leave her records of her soul experiments within the castle rather than in the [[Forbidden Library]], either due to their importance or for the sake of Beatrice, who had lost her [[Ryuzu Meyer (original)|friend]] during that battle, so she would not be forced to remember what happened. Eventually, however, for reasons unknown, Hector found Kugelschreiber Castle, and he began dealing tremendous damage to it, forcing Echidna to flee and abandon the castle. Ever since, the castle remained untouched for four centuries. ===[[Great Escape]]=== At the start of the Lugunican Subversive Conspiracy, many members of the [[Royal Selection]] were falsely accused with charges after the Beloved Children corrupted the [[Kingdom of Lugunica|Lugunican]] government, forcing them all to flee from the [[Royal Capital]]. Subaru, who was accompanied by [[Crusch Karsten]], Beatrice, and [[Rachins Hoffman]], found their way to members of the [[Six Tongues]], who had already recruited [[Ferris]] for assistance. Together, the group escaped from the capital and started working to fight the Beloved Children. ===The Return to Flugel's Tree=== After two months of removing false members of the Lugunican nobility, Subaru's group met in a cabin deep in the forest where they discussed how to proceed. There, [[Russell Fellow]] chose to focus on finding a way to undo the Authority of the Sin Archbishop of Lust, wishing to avoid using the Sacraments of the [[Divine Dragon Church]]. To this end, he asked Subaru for a way to contact [[Roswaal L. Mathers]], having been unable to find a way to reach him himself, so that they could find the soul experiments of Echidna. After a short private conversation between Subaru and Beatrice, Beatrice recalled that there were no records within the Forbidden Library but that there might have been some at Kugelschreiber Castle. Afterward, the group made their way to the stump of [[Flugel's Tree]], where the secret entrance was located, and which had become a tourist attraction due to the [[Subjugation of the White Whale]] resulted in the tree's felling. After Russell and [[Melty Pristis]] managed to remove the tourists from the area, Beatrice found the entrance and opened it with Door Crossing. After arriving at the castle, the group quickly found their way to Echidna's laboratory and records room. After collecting everything, Beatrice, accompanied by most of the group, chose to retrieve something that she had left behind when she was forced to flee the castle. ==Battle== ===Separated=== [[File:Re Zero Light Novel 46 8.png|thumb|right|180x|Subaru's group under the effects of Bellaris's ability.]] As the group made their way through the half-destroyed castle, Subaru found himself subjected to the effects of multiple abilities and was forced to use [[Natsuki Subaru#Authorities|Return by Death]] twice. Upon recovering, he warned the group about enemies but realized that Ferris had gone missing. Unable to properly contain their emotions due to the effects of the ability of the Beloved Children's [[Bellaris]], Crusch drew her sword and questioned her allies, and when she decided to go find Ferris, [[Black Dog]], not intending to let her do that, resorted to violence, resulting in Subaru's irritation at him, Black Dog's defeat, and Melty breaking down in panicked tears. After Crusch left and Subaru realized that something was off, Beatrice had gone to heal Black Dog. Shortly after, however, as silence started to take over, Subaru noticed the collapsing roof, and after using his [[Natsuki Subaru#Authorities|Invisible Providence]] to move Black Dog and Beatrice out of the way, he picked up Melty, who had clung to him, and started running. Separated from the others, Crusch, her negative feelings amplified, found herself fighting against [[Reborn]], who used his silencing technique and swordsmanship to corner her. Despite her Dragon Eye being open, she struggled against him. As their fight continued, the effects of the ability of [[Tornel]] came undone, distracting both of them. With his silence also coming undone, Crusch could hear the sound of Ferris beneath them crying out for someone not to die. Becoming desperate, Crusch carved through the ground, where she found Subaru bleeding on the floor, Ferris pinned to the wall, and Melty holding hands with the enemy, Bellaris, causing her to see red. ===Natsuki Subaru Faked Murder Mystery=== After running for some time, Subaru and Melty eventually stopped, now back to normal. Discussing what had happened to them all, Melty revealed that the Beloved Children might have been at the castle. Because of this, Subaru used [[Natsuki Subaru#Authorities|Cor Leonis]] to locate his allies. After deciding that they'd just get in Crusch's way, that Ferris was the closest, and that he was the one best suited toward their continued survival, they decided to chase after him. However, they found themselves under the effects of Tornel's abilities, forcing them to go in circles. Realizing that he could overcome the ability with his Cor Leonis, the two discussed the Beloved Children's reason for taking Ferris, with Melty concluding it was likely to have him work for them. Then, they strategized about how they would handle Ferris's captor, and though Melty was at first heavily against the idea and believed it to be a product of her ability influencing him, he was able to refute and convince her to go along with the plan. After arriving at Ferris's location, where he had his arms stabbed into the wall by one of Reborn's blades, the two put their plan in action. Subaru used Cor Leonis to gather the excess emotions of his allies into himself, and after distracting Bellaris by talking to her, Melty stabbed him from behind in front of both Bellaris and Ferris. As Subaru was on the ground, Melty convinced Lycoris that she was a member of the Beloved Children sent to work as a spy to gather information on the Six Tongues. Although Ferris also fell for her act, after looking into Subaru's eyes, he realized it was a farce. After Melty managed to get close and shake hands, her ability activated on Bellaris, causing her to listen, give them information, and call out to Tornel to undo his ability. ===Squabble with Children=== Shortly after Tornel released his power and Ferris cried out to Subaru, the roof above them collapsed, and Crusch and Reborn fell through it, still clashing. Seeing what was happening, both Crusch and Reborn questioned Melty's allegiance, and after positioning herself properly and drawing a staff, Melty claimed that she was one of the Beloved Children, catching Reborn off guard and signaling to Crusch with her [[Divine Protection]] that she was lying. Afterward, the two simultaneously attacked Bellaris, sending her flying. Realizing that she had interrupted Subaru and Melty's plan, Crusch entered battle with Reborn again. However, she was put on the back foot as she was still under the effects of Bellaris's ability. Melty was also injured by Reborn and sent flying away. As the battle began to digress towards Reborn's favor due to Crusch's self-deprecation and Reborn's skill and silence, Ferris called out to Crusch, taking a page from Subaru's book, claiming that she was aware that Crusch had not recovered her memories and still claimed to believe that she would win. Reinvigorated, after being told to do as such by Ferris, Crusch severed Ferris's arms, allowing him to move freely and heal Subaru. Healed from his injury, Subaru took Ferris onto his back. Entrusting the injured Melty to him, Crusch threw her toward him, and he caught her with Invisible Providence, allowing Ferris to heal her and Crusch to continue fighting. At the same time, Subaru used Cor Leonis to take in all of the emotional turmoil from everyone nearby. As the two fought, Reborn told Bellaris, who was injured nearby, to light them up, causing her to cause an explosion of colorful fire. Subaru quickly thought about her ability and realized through the scent of sulfur that Bellaris was using chemicals as her primary ability and told Crusch to use her wind to protect herself, leading to her blowing the flames away and directly toward Reborn. Realizing Subaru was the one who discovered Bellaris's ability, Reborn chose to attack him, using his silence on him. However, Subaru used Invisible Providence to open the door behind him, allowing Beatrice and the healed Black Dog to appear through Door Crossing. Black Dog used green flame to attack, providing an opening for the healed Melty to hit Reborn with her staff and Crusch to slash his eyes, sending him flying and defeating him. [[File:Re Zero Light Novel 46 12.png|thumb|left|180x|Tiga arrives to assist the Beloved Children.]] With Tornel not appearing and Bellaris unconscious, the blinded Reborn attempted to get up and fight again, only for [[Tiga Rauleon]], who recognized Tiga as an Enforcer, and the and a squirrel-shaped [[spirit]] to appear, much to the shock of Melty, who called out Tiga's name, though he didn't recognize her. Meanwhile, the spirit recognized Black Dog as her contractor. Questioning why they were there, Tiga claimed that things had turned into a mess and that the castle had emerged in the real world. {{Clear}} ==Trivia== *The Natsuki Subaru Faked Murder Mystery, which was coined by Subaru during the battle, may be a reference to a quote once given by [[Rui Arneb]] during the [[Pleiades Watchtower Expedition]]. ==Navigation== {{Battles & Events Navbox}} [[Category:Alternate Spaces]] [[Category:Kingdom of Lugunica]]
